author: 0xdeafcafe
body:
ADR-092 stage B, reshaped as decided: the system migrates its own authorization data **in place** — no scripts, no operator steps. One PR for the whole stage, per the one-PR-per-stage restructure recorded in the delivery plan amendment included here.

Spec: `specs/rbac/in-place-authz-migration.feature` (19 scenarios, all tagged and bound).

## What this builds

**`@langwatch/system-migrations` (new package).** A generic in-place migration runner: per-tenant state machine (`pending → migrated → finalized`, `parked` on error, `rolled_back` for the operator), one driver fleet-wide under a Redis lease, level-triggered from worker boot — every boot re-attempts held and parked tenants, so a fixed blocker heals itself. Storage-engine-free; the app implements the state repository (Prisma), lease (Redis `SET NX PX` + compare-and-renew Lua) and tenant source (Organization table). The identity-platform program is the expected second consumer (D01 Account backfill, D09 per-customer migrations).

**The M1 rider (`TeamUserBackfillMigration`, in `@langwatch/authz-server`).** Per organization: every legacy `TeamUser` row gains an equivalent TEAM-scoped `RoleBinding` (role → role, `assignedRoleId` → `customRoleId`), batch-inserted under the partial unique indexes so re-runs create nothing, one audit event (`source: backfill-b`) and one epoch bump per org (M7 discipline). Binding identity mirrors those indexes exactly — built-in bindings key on `role`, custom bindings on `customRoleId` — so an existing custom binding can never read as missing and have its insert silently dropped by `skipDuplicates`.

**Finalization is a parity proof, not an assumption.** The rider collects each member's grants once and runs the pure engine twice per (permission × scope) — with the legacy rows and without. Zero disagreements → `finalized`; any disagreement → the org is **held** (`migrated`) with the diffs stored in its report, behaviour unchanged. This is the plan's "refuses to finalise any org with a diff", made per-organization and self-healing. Held is the *expected* steady state for orgs whose members lean on the legacy org-level union quirk (a team-ADMIN `TeamUser` row grants ~95 org-scope permissions a TEAM binding never will — verified empirically against the engine); those orgs finalize after remediation or after stage C's re-key, per the M2 observed-zero gate.

A proof that does not finish is not a proof: a pass interrupted by shutdown throws rather than returning a short diff list, so the org parks and is verified again from the start rather than finalizing on a partial sweep.

**The per-organization switch.** Once (and only once) an org is `finalized`, its legacy fallback reads stop: all three `rbac.ts` fallback branches and the engine collector's legacy-row fetch consult one gate (`server/authz/legacy-fallback-gate.ts`). Gating the collector too keeps the shadow comparison agreeing with the legacy path it wraps. Answers are cached per organization — 15 minutes for "switched off", 5 minutes for "not yet", and any storage error fails safe to "fallback on".

**Rollback is a status, not a deploy.** Writing `rolled_back` on an organization's state row returns it to its legacy path fleet-wide within the gate's cache bound, with no restart. It is the only status the runner refuses to act on, which is what makes it stick: blanking the row or moving it back to `migrated` does *not* roll an organization back, because the next pass re-runs a migration whose proof still passes and re-finalizes it minutes later. Bindings are additive and stay either way.

**Rollout control.**
- Self-hosted: every organization, automatically, silently. No configuration, no announcement, no visible change — held orgs just keep their legacy behaviour.
- Cloud: `SYSTEM_MIGRATIONS_COHORT` (read per pass, same internal-knob posture as `AUTHZ_V2_SHADOW`): unset/`none` = nothing (default), a comma-separated org list, or `all`.
- **Ops → Migrations** (new ops dashboard page, `ops:view`/`ops:manage`): per-migration status rollup, the held/parked organizations with their full reports, and a "Run a pass now" action (safe verb — the lease guarantees a single driver; there is deliberately no force-finalize, since that would bypass the parity proof).

**Where it runs.** The pass is a worker-only background loop, so the app layer owns it: `presets.ts` starts it behind `roleRunsWorkers()` exactly like the ADR-044 scheduler, and the App's graceful closeables stop it. It never blocks boot and never throws out of that seam — a failed pass is a logged no-op the next boot repeats. The lease is held by a heartbeat for the duration of the pass rather than renewed between tenants, because one large organization's parity sweep can outlive a lease term by itself.

**What deliberately did not change.** `TeamUser` rows are never deleted (stage E). The personal-workspace dual-write stays — it is the expand-phase posture while legacy readers live. Invites/SCIM/groups already write bindings only, so the plan's B3 was already true; the reader migrations (`virtualKey.authz.ts` etc.) ride stage E once every org is finalized.

## Verification

- `@langwatch/system-migrations`: 10 unit tests (lease race, cohort filter, park-and-retry, finalized skip, operator rollback stays rolled back, previous-record hand-off, lease lost mid-tenant, held-and-reverify, abort, pagination). Package typecheck clean.
- `@langwatch/authz-server`: 94 tests (11 new rider tests: equivalence, idempotency, personal teams, epoch/audit once, custom-role identity, resumed epoch bump after a parked attempt, aborted-sweep parking, parity-clean finalize, quirk-diff hold with report, heal-on-regrant, empty-org fast path). Package typecheck clean. Quirk fixtures verified against the real engine, not hand-asserted.
- App: authz + rbac suites green with the gate wired; gate tests (finalized skips fallback and never reads `TeamUser`; pending/migrated/parked keep today's behaviour exactly; unreadable state table fails safe); cohort tests; `SystemMigrationTenantState` classified in `dbMultiTenancyProtection` as a scoped model, so a query naming neither a tenant nor a migration still throws.

## Deployment Impact

- New Prisma migration `20260817000000_system_migration_tenant_state` — additive table, no backfill, safe to deploy in any order relative to pods.
- Workers kick one background migration pass at boot. On cloud this is a no-op until `SYSTEM_MIGRATIONS_COHORT` is set (separate saas PR when we start the rollout): every organization is skipped, no state rows are written, and every permission check behaves exactly as it does today. Self-hosted installs migrate silently in the background starting with the release that ships this; behaviour changes only for organizations that pass the parity proof, and for them "change" means answers come from bindings that provably agree.
- No new required environment variables, no chart changes.

  * Added an Operations Migrations page to monitor progress, review attention records, and start migration passes.
  * Added background, resumable authorization migrations with staged cohorts, retries, lease protection, and safe shutdown.
  * Migrated legacy team memberships into team-scoped permissions while preserving roles and audit history.
  * Organizations are finalized only after permissions match and then no longer rely on legacy authorization data.
* **Documentation**
  * Added guidance for rollout, verification, monitoring, and rollback.
* **Tests**
  * Expanded coverage for migration reliability, retries, fallback behavior, and parity verification.

author: aphoristicartist
body:
## What changed

- treat complete `prog run` stream text as complete evidence instead of confusing bounded `head`/`tail` disclosure fields with derivation windows
- preserve already-captured stdout and stderr in their canonical fields when a run times out or is cancelled
- classify canonical stream text per semantic line, keep moved findings stable across reruns, and stop reclassifying derived `head`, `tail`, `combined`, and failure-section representations
- make verification readback return success only for `verified`; `pending` now fails the process gate
- regenerate deterministic finding goldens and the replay report through their sanctioned update commands

## Why

Three trust-boundary bugs made machine-readable outcomes disagree with persisted evidence:

1. a fully stored long run was marked unable to prove absence because its preview fields were bounded
2. timeout output existed in `combined` but canonical stdout/stderr were replaced with empty captures
3. a pending readback exited zero even though only verified outcomes may pass

Once full text became provable, duplicate and context-wide generic fingerprints could also turn an unchanged error that moved lines into a false new/resolved pair. Canonical per-line identity fixes that without adding a provider/plugin framework.

## Impact

- full, unredacted, untruncated run captures can participate in conservative resolved/persisting deltas
- moved unchanged errors remain `persisting`
- distinct error lines remain distinct occurrences while derived representations no longer inflate counts
- partial timeout evidence remains navigable at `/stdout/text` and `/stderr/text`
- shell/CI gates cannot treat eventual-consistency `pending` as success
- replay coverage improves from 5/11 to 7/11 provable comparison pairs, while compared findings fall from 49 to 35 and all 57 correctness checks retain zero false decisions

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features`
- `cargo run -- --help`
- focused timeout, moved-finding, delta-budget, verification, golden, and replay tests

author: jayson-odoo
body:
## Intent Backend half of multi-company reply clarity for sorento-crm: every company-scoped MCP presenter tool must label results per company whenever the lookup or the returned entities actually span more than one company. Source of truth is the firstmate scout report multicompany-response-clarity/report.md (reproduced defect: list_stock queries all the caller's companies with one IN predicate but rows carry no company identity, so n8n cannot attribute rows or name the companies searched). Captain decisions 2026-08-16: (1) rollout scope (c) = ALL company-scoped presenter tools in this one PR: crm_inventory_stock_balance_list, crm_incoming_stock_list, crm_incoming_stock_by_product, crm_incoming_stock_shipments, crm_master_products_list, crm_master_product_attachments_list, crm_certificates_list, crm_marketing_promotions_list, crm_marketing_promotion_products_list, crm_order_management_orders_list, crm_order_management_orders_by_product_list. (2) Labelling rule: label ONLY when the set of companies actually queried for the resolved product ids/entities, unioned with the companies present in returned rows, has size > 1. Do NOT key it on the caller's access list: a two-company caller asking for a code that exists in one company only gets a plain, byte-identical single-company answer (byte-identical at the MCP render envelope level; the raw ListResponse JSON gains lookup_companies: null / company_name: null the same way resolved_entities already does). (3) Simplest thing that works, mirroring existing patterns (attachments company stamp precedent, resources_service.company_name_map, _PASSTHROUGH_KEYS, _Builder.item None-dropping); no new service module, no abstraction, no config knob. Deliverables: app/schemas/common.py ListResponse gains optional lookup_companies (list of {id,name}, sorted by name; ONE name everywhere, matching the report and the n8n follow-up); affected row schemas gain optional company_id/company_name; ONE shared helper stamp_lookup_companies in app/services/company_scope.py (scoped Product.company_id query for the requested ids UNION row companies; if > 1, one batched Company id/name query, stamp company_name per row, set payload lookup_companies; else emit nothing extra; best-effort under a SAVEPOINT so a failure never aborts the caller's transaction; single-company scope short-circuits before any query) called by every service on with-data AND empty payload paths, including resolver-miss early returns where the requested product set is already known; MCP presenters.py: lookup_companies in _PASSTHROUGH_KEYS, a leading Company field on each affected row presenter (auto-dropped when None), and an empty result with lookup_companies gets the intro 'No matching results found for Mocha or Sorento.' (only when every entry has a name); MCP sanitizer strips row company_id for exactly those eleven tools (no UUIDs in agent-facing rows; crm_resource_attachments_list deliberately keeps its company_id). Deliberate decisions: rows-only tools (incoming_stock_shipments, and free-text axes like list_orders product_query / list_stock entities that resolve to codes not ids) label from the current page's rows; company_id on the eight Pydantic row schemas fills from the mixin via from_attributes (harmless for the FE, stripped by the MCP); certificate rows are pre-built Pydantic objects so the helper takes a row_company_id callable for that one caller; incoming-stock endpoints return raw dicts and set lookup_companies directly. Tests: Postgres-only, own seed chains, per tool: two-company lookup -> rows stamped + lookup_companies present; empty result -> lookup_companies present; single-company lookup under a two-company scope -> neither; out-of-scope product id contributes nothing; one batched companies query; presenter tests with/without company_name plus the byte-identical proof. Known baseline: the full backend suite has 152 pre-existing failures that reproduce on the clean origin/main tree (env / borrowed-row tests), unrelated to this diff; the targeted suites (60 backend + 290 MCP) are green. Deploy note for the PR body: the FastMCP process registers presenters and sanitizers at startup, restart it after merge (same gotcha as sorento_crm_mcp PR #109). The n8n half is a separate follow-up task; this PR does not touch n8n. Do not merge; the captain merges. ## What Changed - Backend: `ListResponse` gains optional `lookup_companies` (`{id,name}` sorted by name) and the stock, incoming-stock, product, product-attachment, certificate, promotion, promotion-product and order row schemas gain optional `company_id` / `company_name`; one shared `stamp_lookup_companies` helper in `app/services/company_scope.py` (scoped `Product.company_id` for the requested ids UNION row companies, one batched `Company` id/name query when the set exceeds one, best-effort under a SAVEPOINT, single-company scope short-circuits) is called by inventory, incoming-stock, product, certificate, marketing and order services on with-data, empty and resolver-miss paths, so a single-company lookup emits nothing extra. - MCP: `lookup_companies` added to `_PASSTHROUGH_KEYS`, a leading `Company` field on each affected row presenter (dropped when `None`), empty results with fully-named `lookup_companies` render `No matching results found for Mocha or Sorento.`, and `_sanitize_tool_response` strips row `company_id` for exactly the eleven labelled tools (`crm_resource_attachments_list` keeps its stamp). - Tests and docs: Postgres-only pytest suites with a shared `_mc_lookup_seed.py` seed chain per tool (two-company stamped, empty-with-companies, single-company byte-identical, out-of-scope product, one batched query), MCP presenter/sanitizer tests, plus the PLAN and acceptance-criteria docs under `documentation/plans/multi-company/`. Deploy note: the FastMCP process registers presenters and sanitizers at startup, restart it after merge (same as sorento_crm_mcp PR #109); the n8n half is a separate follow-up. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Additive, best-effort labelling behind a savepoint with single-scope short-circuit; every intent-listed tool, schema, presenter, sanitizer and empty/early-return path is covered, the raw-JSON changes are the ones the intent explicitly accepts, and the new tests exercise behaviour rather than source text. ## Testing Ran the targeted backend (54) and MCP (80) suites for this change using the main checkout's venv/.env since the worktree carries neither; all green. Then produced product-level evidence with a script that drives the real FastAPI routes and the real MCP sanitizer + presenter: two-company hit shows a "Company" field on every row plus lookup_companies and no company_id UUIDs in agent-facing rows; empty two-company result reads "No matching results found for Mocha or Sorento."; a Sorento-only code under a two-company caller renders byte-identically to a single-company caller. No failures, no findings. Note: full-suite baseline not run per targeted-validation rule.
Evidence: E2E transcript: HTTP route -> MCP sanitizer -> MCP presenter (stock + products, 4 scenarios) 1. two-company hit: lookup_companies=[Mocha, Sorento]; MCP rows: {"key":"company_name","label":"Company","value":"Mocha"} / "Sorento"; sanitized rows carry company_id? False 2. two-company empty: intro "No matching results found for Mocha or Sorento.", lookup_companies present 3. Sorento-only code, two-company caller: lookup_companies None, row company_name None; MCP render two-company-scope == single-company-scope: True 4. products list two-company hit: rows [('ZZT-BOTH-M','Mocha'),('ZZT-SORENTO-ONLY','Sorento'),('ZZT-BOTH-S','Sorento')], Company field leading, company_id stripped ```text ============================================================================== 1. Two-company caller, stock lookup for a code presen

author: vyncint
body:
## Summary

All four hand-maintained inventories on `cuda-oxide-book/compiler/mlir-dialects.md` are stale, and nothing checks any of them. Every count below was recomputed from the tree at `a766fc26`.

### 1. dialect-mir types: "seven" → **nine**

`mir.union` and `mir.fp16` both have `#[pliron_type(...)]` declarations in `dialect-mir/src/types.rs` and no row. `mir.union` is not a corner case — #857 and #927 are both about union constants.

### 2. dialect-mir operations: 54 across 11 categories → **62 across 12**

| Category | Book | Tree | Missing |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|
| control flow | 5 | 6 | `mir.unroll_hint` |
| memory | 9 | 11 | `mir.memcpy`, `mir.memmove` |
| comparison | 6 | 7 | `mir.cmp` |
| aggregate | 8 | 10 | `mir.construct_slice`, `mir.construct_disjoint_slice` |
| enum | 3 | 4 | `mir.set_discriminant` |
| **debug** | — | 1 | `mir.dbg_value` — no row at all |

### 3. LLVM dialect: 62 → **69**

Counted at the pinned `pliron` revision `8447aa42`, where `pliron-llvm/src/ops.rs` declares 51 ops with `#[pliron_op(` plus 18 through its binop macros. The table gains `indirectbr`, `insert_element`, `shuffle_vector`, `poison`, and a row for the four with no existing category (`freeze`, `va_arg`, `blockaddress`, `blocktag`).

Two names are wrong rather than merely missing:

- **`inline_asm_multi` does not exist.** Not in any version of `pliron-llvm`, and nowhere in this repository — this page is the only place the string appears anywhere. Same shape as the fictional `shuffle_xor_{f32,i32}` rows #815 removed from the API quick reference.
- `extractelement` is spelled `llvm.extract_element`.

Also records that `llvm-export` contributes one op of its own (`llvm.dbg_value`), which the surrounding prose did not mention, and that this table tracks an upstream crate — so it moves when the pin moves (as it did in #919), not when this repository changes.

### 4. dialect-nvvm: 123 → **543**

Not so much drift as a different tree. **Six of the twelve modules listed no longer exist**: `thread` and `warp` are gone (the warp ops now live in `warp_shuffle`, `redux`, `vote`, `warp_match`, `warp_barrier`, `active_mask`, `elect`), and `mbarrier` split into `mbarrier_basic` / `mbarrier_extended`. The ones that do exist are 4×–9× low — `tcgen05` is listed at 24 and has **210**, `tma` at 15 and has **111**. Eighteen modules are missing outright, including `sreg` at 44 ops.

Rewritten around the split `adding-new-intrinsics.md` already documents — 7 hand-written modules (18 ops) against 34 generated ones (525 ops, resolved from 986 catalog entries, since several intrinsics share one structural op). That is what decides where a contributor would add an op, and a table saying `warp` when the file is `ops/generated/warp_shuffle.rs` sends them to the wrong place.

The per-module "Minimum SM / GPU Family" columns go with it. Those requirements are per intrinsic, not per module, and the catalog already records them: `intrinsics/generated-reference.md` renders the PTX version and minimum SM for each of the 986 entries and is regenerated with the ops. The page now points there instead of keeping a second copy by hand.

## Note on the neighbouring PR

`crates/dialect-mir/README.md` carries its own copy of the operation inventory, stale in the same way and by a *different amount* — it says 55, and already had `set_discriminant` the book was missing. Two hand-kept copies drifting apart at different rates is the argument for reading `src/ops/` rather than either. Fixed separately, no file overlap with this PR.

I checked #946 before writing these numbers: it touches all 35 generated `dialect-nvvm` files but adds **zero** `#[pliron_op(` declarations (only the regenerated catalog-SHA headers change), so the counts here are stable against it.

## Testing

Local, no GPU.

- [x] Every count recomputed from the tree by script; all 12 dialect-mir modules, all 7 hand-written and all 34 generated dialect-nvvm modules, and all 10 grouped areas match exactly
- [x] The types table's nine rows match `#[pliron_type(` in `dialect-mir/src/types.rs` exactly
- [x] `just book` (`sphinx-build -W --keep-going`) succeeds
- [x] `check-book-api-names.sh`, `check-toolchain-parity.sh`, `check-cli-doc-coverage.sh` pass
- [ ] `cargo oxide run <example>` — not applicable, documentation only

author: thebhulawat
body:
## What this adds A Retell agent runs on Retell's servers, so it can never export telemetry the way a LiveKit agent does. This PR gives egma the other door the field settled on: watching a Retell agent through the connection egma already holds. - **Watch production** is a per-connection switch, off for every existing connection. Flipping it on starts capture; flipping it off stops it and keeps what was stored. - **Two transports, one write path.** A poller in the API process asks Retell every 30 seconds for conversations that ended since its per-connection cursor — the floor that works behind NAT with no public address. A webhook endpoint receives Retell's `call_ended` deliveries; when the deployment knows a public address, switch-on registers the webhook automatically and switch-off deregisters it. While the webhook is delivering, the poller drops to a safety-net cadence — never off, so a missed delivery costs minutes, not the conversation. - **One normalizer.** Retell's call record becomes span rows directly: turns from the transcript with their tool calls, latency aggregates riding the root span only (no fabricated per-turn timings), the ending reason, the recording link as the audio reference, and the vendor payload kept verbatim so nothing egma did not extract today is lost. - **Exactly once, by construction.** The trace identity is minted deterministically from the call id and the connection. A transport inserts a claim row unique on that identity — first insert wins, the loser walks away, so two transports racing on one conversation is settled by the constraint, not by timing. The protocol is claim (Postgres, payload on the row) → append (ClickHouse) → mark written; a lease sweep replays crashed claims from their own stored payload, so a replayed append is byte-identical and the store's insert dedup absorbs it. - **The cursor never passes work that is not durably written.** Conversations are checkpointed one at a time, oldest first; pages drain by Retell's pagination key; a failure stops the sweep and the next tick resumes from the last durable item; a payload the normalizer cannot fully parse is written degraded — verbatim kept, flagged, counted — so a poison item can never wedge the connection. - **Grading needs nothing new.** The write closes the root span, the existing bookkeeping files the grading job, and production-scoped graders judge Retell conversations from day one. ## Security and tenancy - Webhook deliveries are verified — HMAC over the raw request bytes, constant-time compare — against the sealed keys of switched-on connections matching the event's agent id. No match, switch off, or failed verification is refused, counted in a bounded counter, and never stored. Event kinds other than `call_ended` are acknowledged and dropped. - Every write carries an auth context resolved from the connection's own project. The same agent registered in two projects is two connections filing one copy each, and the minted identities cannot collide. ## Testing Scoped tests only in this branch; the full suite runs in CI. 48 tests across the two new Retell test files, plus the touched db/api module suites, all against the real local Postgres and ClickHouse, driven by Retell-shaped payloads served from a loopback stub — no Retell keys anywhere. Adversarial coverage includes both transports racing on one conversation (both orders, twice by one transport, and concurrently), crash recovery in both protocol windows, a sweep killed between two items of one page, a burst larger than one page, and clock-skewed, timeless, and unparseable payloads. Retell's wire shapes are written from their documentation; the live proof against a real Retell agent is deliberately the next step, not this one. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

Greptile Summary

The PR adds production monitoring for Retell agents through polling and signed webhooks, backed by deterministic trace claims and crash recovery. - Adds Retell API, signature verification, normalization, webhook registration, and ingestion paths. - Adds per-connection watch state, cursors, claim leasing, and database migrations. - Updates polling to paginate through already-claimed webhook calls while advancing the durable cursor. - Adds integration and data-access coverage for normalization, transport races, recovery, and watch behavior.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The PR is not yet safe to merge because an in-flight verified webhook can still store a conversation after production watching has been disabled. The webhook retains a previously resolved watched target, while switch-off and trace claiming occur in independent database operations and the write path does not revalidate or atomically enforce the current watch state. **Files Needing Attention:** apps/api/src/routes/retell-webhook.ts, apps/api/src/retell/write.ts, packages/db/src/access/production-watch.ts

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/api/src/production-sweep.ts | Implements periodic Retell polling, pagination, cursor checkpointing, and stale-claim recovery. | | apps/api/src/routes/retell-webhook.ts | Receives and verifies Retell deliveries, but the previously reported switch-off race remains in the current handler. | | apps/api/src/retell/write.ts | Unifies webhook and pull ingestion through deterministic claims, span append, bookkeeping, and completion. | | packages/db/src/access/production-watch.ts | Provides watch resolution, cursor advancement, claim leasing, replay selection, and webhook delivery state. | | packages/db/migrations/0034_watch_production.sql | Adds the persisted watch configuration and production-ingestion ledger required by the integration. |

Sequence Diagram

 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Retell participant Webhook as Webhook handler participant Poller as Production sweep participant Claims as Postgres claims participant Store as ClickHouse Retell->>Webhook: Signed call_ended payload Webhook->>Claims: Claim deterministic trace ID Retell->>Poller: Paginated ended calls Poller->>Claims: Claim deterministic trace ID alt Claim acquired Claims-->>Webhook: First writer Webhook->>Store: Append normalized spans Webhook->>Claims: Mark written else Already claimed Claims-->>Poller: Already accounted for Poller->>Claims: Advance durable cursor end ```

author: agentydragon
body:
## Why the gate cleared

`transport.py`'s `CLEANUP(added 2026-08-14)` said to delete the `HELLO_SECONDS` wait and its fallback "once no runner image predating `Hello` can still be running". That gate never self-cleared — the tombstone's reasoning ("`session_ttl_seconds` bounds it at two hours") is wrong, because `_renew_lease` slides a sandbox claim's `shutdownTime` on every heartbeat, so a session a replica is tending never ages out and its runner keeps its image indefinitely. `legacy_purge.md` already records that correction.

Both halves happened on 2026-08-16 23:5x:

- Purge phase 1 deleted every `sessions` row (302), so no session predating anything survives.
- The `Sandbox` CR `haku-cp94x` — 7h36m old, pod template rendered at claim time — was **deleted**, which re-renders the template rather than regenerating the same pod. `kubectl get pods -n haku-sandbox` afterwards shows no stale runner.
- A replacement session (`6bcf64ba-1bfa-4f63-a712-c65365dc8da7`) provisioned at 23:56:30 on a freshly rendered sandbox and is recording frames.

Every runner that can now connect is on a current image, which necessarily carries `Hello`.

## What changes

`_negotiate` no longer waits and then assumes `PROTOCOL_VERSION` on silence. A connection that does not open with `Hello` is an error:

- silence → `RuntimeError("runner sent no hello in {n}s")`, raised from the `TimeoutError` the cancel scope produced;
- any other frame first → the existing `runner sent {kind} before saying hello` sequencing error, unchanged.

The constant survives, renamed `HELLO_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` and raised 2s → 30s. It is no longer "how long a legacy connection costs" but a liveness bound on a handshake that is required: `Hello` is the runner's first write after the socket opens, so anything past a round trip is a runner that will never speak. Deleting it outright would hang instead — `WebSocketTransport.connect()` has no outer deadline (`ClaudeCli.connect()`'s `control_timeout` only covers the `initialize` that follows), so a wedged runner would park the session handler forever. It is injectable per transport, the same shape as `ClaudeCli(control_timeout=…)`, so the refusal is testable without a 30s wait.

## Tests

`test_a_runner_that_never_says_hello_is_still_launched` is rewritten as `…_is_refused` rather than deleted — same path, opposite assertion.

The fallback was also silently propping up six other transport tests that called `connect()` and never sent a `Hello`; without it they would hang. They now complete the handshake through a small `connected()` helper (the pair is buffered, so queueing the hello before `connect()` means no task group is needed).

## What this deliberately leaves out

- **No `| None` went away.** I checked: `ClaudeMessage.seq`, `SetupOutput.seq` and `resume_from` are optional because they are additive fields across independently rolling images, not because the fallback could not supply them. `Hello.supported` and `ClaudeLaunch.protocol_version` have real defaults, not `None`.
- **`PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays.** It loses its `transport.py` reader but is still `ClaudeLaunch.protocol_version`'s default.
- **`runner.py` is untouched.** It already sends `Hello` unconditionally on every connection.
- **`bridge/README.md` is untouched** — it does not describe the fallback. (Its "Three kinds" line predates `hello`/`setup_output` and is stale independently of this change; that belongs in its own PR.)
- **`plans/cli_protocol_ownership.md` is untouched.** Its shim paragraph is written in the proposal tense the whole document uses; rewriting one clause of it is a docs pass, not this change.

`legacy_purge.md` loses the inventory row, the "trivially removable now" bullet, and the phase-2 line item; its "three tombstones" correction becomes two, since `transport.py` line 36 no longer exists.

Not run locally: BuildBuddy is unreachable from this container, so CI is the test run.

author: luketmoss
body:
Closes #232

Two defects in #224's elevation-sampling path, both root-causing the reported symptom (every track, every trip, no elevation, no explanation):

1. **`APIProvider` never requested the `elevation` library**, so `google.maps.ElevationService`/`ElevationStatus` didn't exist. Fixed by adding `libraries={['elevation']}` to the provider in `MapCanvas.tsx`.
2. **The status check compared against the now-undefined `maps.ElevationStatus.OK`**, so `status !== maps.ElevationStatus.OK` was `'OK' !== undefined` — true for every response, including successful ones. Fixed by comparing against the literal `'OK'` the callback actually returns.

`ElevationSampler.sampleAlongPath` and `sampleTrackElevation` now return a discriminated result (`{ ok: true, … }` / `{ ok: false, reason }`) instead of `null`/`undefined`, so a failure's cause — the API's own status, or a local reason for the degenerate-series cases — survives up to `useTripImport`, which logs it once per settled batch via `console.warn`. The reader-facing copy (#224's "Couldn't estimate elevation for N tracks") is unchanged.

Verified live in the browser: with the fix, the Maps bootstrap script now requests `libraries=elevation`, `ElevationService` is present, and a direct `getElevationAlongPath` call against the dev key returned `REQUEST_DENIED` — a Google Cloud config issue, not a code one. After enabling the Elevation API and clearing the key's API restriction list (both were needed), the same call returned `status: "OK"` with real elevation data.

author: kanjieater
body:
### Problem

When a user drops a Japanese (or any non-Latin) book into the CWA ingest folder, the resulting path on disk is romanized ASCII gibberish regardless of how the library is configured:

```
# What CWA creates after ingest:
Xiao Ye Bu You Mei/Hei Ci noDao (51042)/Hei Ci noDao - Xiao Ye Bu You Mei.epub

# What the user actually wanted:
小野不由美/黒祠の島 (51042)/黒祠の島 - 小野不由美.epub
```

This breaks file browsing, KOReader sync paths, any external tool that reads the library directory, and produces inconsistent output: a book edited through CWA's web UI gets a correct Unicode path, but the same book added through the ingest folder gets garbled ASCII.

The root cause is that `calibredb add` uses Calibre's internal `ascii_filename()` UDF which always transliterates CJK/Unicode to romanized ASCII, ignoring the `config_unicode_filename` preference. CWA never corrects this after the fact.

### Fix

Add `_fix_unicode_path(book_id)` to `NewBookProcessor`. It runs after each successful `calibredb add` — specifically after `fetch_metadata_if_enabled` (so any metadata-corrected author name is already in the DB) and before `trigger_auto_send_if_enabled` (so the file is at the correct path before being sent to devices).

The method:

- Reads `config_unicode_filename` from `app.db` — if `True` (user explicitly wants ASCII), calibredb already produced it and the method is a no-op
- Computes the canonical path using `get_valid_filename_shared()` from `cps/utils/filename_sanitizer.py` — **the same function the web-UI edit/save path already calls** — so ingest and the web UI are now consistent
- If the computed path differs from what calibredb generated, moves the book directory and renames all book files on disk, then updates `books.path` and `data.name` in `metadata.db`
- Registers `title_sort` via the existing `_register_title_sort_function` helper (required by the `books_update_trg` SQLite trigger)
- All error paths are non-fatal `WARN` prints; no existing behavior is affected if the method fails

### Before / After

| | Path after ingest |
|---|---|
| **Before** | `Xiao Ye Bu You Mei/Hei Ci noDao (51042)/` |
| **After** | `小野不由美/黒祠の島 (51042)/` |

### Testing

1. Set `config_unicode_filename = 0` in CWA settings (the default)
2. Drop a book with a Japanese/CJK author and title into the ingest folder
3. Confirm the library path is `{Japanese author}/{Japanese title} (id)/` instead of the transliterated form
4. Books with ASCII-only titles and authors: no change (method is a no-op)
5. `config_unicode_filename = 1`: no change (method returns early)

### Related

Same fix submitted upstream to crocodilestick/Calibre-Web-Automated: https://github.com/crocodilestick/Calibre-Web-Automated/pull/1493

author: evoludigit
body:
`Dagger — test (stable)` went red on dev `d9b5efbd2` while gating the v2.15.0 cut. This is the fix; the failure is a pre-existing flake, not a regression.

```
thread 'test_development_allows_playground_and_empty_cors' panicked at
crates/fraiseql-server/tests/production_safety_test.rs:148:9:
  in development mode, playground + empty cors_origins must pass validation:
  playground_enabled is true in production mode.
```

## The race

Nothing in that commit range touches Rust — the merge before it was `release.yml`, a Makefile target, a Go line and two new gate files. `test (msrv)` passed in the same run, and the immediately preceding head `e9b86f8d7` passed. Two tests in this **one binary** mutate the process-global `FRAISEQL_ENV` with bare `set_var`/`remove_var`, unsynchronised, on separate threads:

| test | does |
|---|---|
| `test_production_mode_default` | `remove_var("FRAISEQL_ENV")` (:63, :79) |
| `test_development_allows_playground_and_empty_cors` | `set_var(…,"development")` (:138) → `validate()` (:147) |

`validate()` reads `FRAISEQL_ENV`. When the first test's `remove_var` lands between the second's `set_var` and its `validate()`, validation sees an unset variable, defaults to production mode and rejects the playground — exactly the observed panic.

## The fix

Both tests now mutate through `temp_env`, already a dev-dependency here. temp-env 0.3.6 holds a process-wide `static SERIAL_TEST: ReentrantMutex<()>` and locks it for the whole closure, so all `with_var*` callers serialise; reentrancy makes the two sequential calls safe. The read moves **inside** the lock-holding closure — a set-then-read pair outside it is precisely what raced.

The module header claimed `**Parallelism:** safe` while it was true of neither test. It now says why it is safe and warns against reintroducing a bare mutation.

## Verification — RED proven, then GREEN

My first attempt at proof was worthless, and I'm recording it so nobody repeats it: running the **whole binary** 200× passed on *both* versions, because 16 tests dilute the overlap. So did 300× under `taskset -c 0,1 --test-threads=16`. Running only the two racing tests on two threads makes them reliably concurrent:

```
$BIN test_production_mode_default test_development_allows_playground_and_empty_cors \
     --test-threads=2       # ×3000

racing (HEAD~1 content):   213 failures / 3000   (7.1%)
fixed  (this branch):        0 failures / 3000
fixed, full binary:          0 failures /  300
```

Same binary path, same command, only the file's content swapped — the delta is the fix, not the harness.

- ✅ builds clean with the CI `SERVER_FEATURES` set
- ✅ no `std::env::set_var(` / `remove_var(` call remains in the file
- ✅ `pre-commit run` → exit 0, no autofix drift

## Context

`d9b5efbd2` is green on `preflight`, `security`, `feature matrix` and `integration` — the last being its first uninterrupted run since 2026-08-15. This flake was the only red standing between the release content and a fully green head.

author: fmmenchi
body:
`main` is red. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails before anything else runs:

```
[ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_URL_MISMATCH] 3 lockfile entries failed verification:
  @fmmenchi/notify@0.0.12 could not be verified against the registry's published metadata
  @fmmenchi/nx-notify@0.0.15 …
  @fmmenchi/nx-trivy@0.1.1 …
```

**Why.** The lockfile records the download URL pnpm resolved:

```
https://npm.pkg.github.com/download/@fmmenchi/nx-trivy/0.1.1/3888ec3e37…
```

and the supply-chain step re-checks it against the registry's metadata. GitHub Packages serves a content-addressed download URL that does not match what its metadata advertises, so that check cannot pass there. It is a disagreement between two registries' conventions, not a signal about the package — the integrity hash still pins the contents.

**Why it was not caught before merging:** the check passes locally, because the lockfile was written on the same machine that then verified it. Only CI, resolving with a different token, sees the mismatch.

**Scoped on purpose.** `--trust-lockfile` would switch the step off for all 2326 entries; `trustPolicyExclude` removes it for the three that cannot pass it.

body:
Extends reference/config-and-supply-chain.md (introduced in fix/accuracy-and-a02-a03-reference) with the CI/CD platform this team uses, splitting the former single "CI/CD Pipelines" section into GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps.

Azure DevOps has a different injection surface than Actions: `$(variable)` is pasted into the script text before the shell parses it (the injection vector), `${{ }}` resolves at compile time, and `$[ ]` is evaluated by the agent without being pasted into scripts — most reviews miss this distinction and flag the wrong form, or miss the real one.

Covers: fork PR builds with secrets exposed, self-hosted agents building fork PRs, persistCredentials leaving the pipeline token in .git/config, queue-time overridable variables, unpinned resources.repositories templates, unvetted marketplace extensions, service connection scoping and workload identity federation, secret variable handling, and environment approvals/branch policies.

Also updates the Where-to-Look-First table to lead with azure-pipelines*.yml and .azuredevops/**.

body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/dcacleaningfirm/agent-runs/6a824330151f1e5f208cd17a

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** Build an automatic lead intake system that sends all successful website booking submissions from the existing Netlify form named `quick-estimate` into DCA Pro Manager.

Requirements:

1. Do not break or replace the existing `quick-estimate` Netlify f...

✅ **Result:** # Secure login access for the Management Specialist role

DCA Pro Manager gained a Management Specialist role with its own login, its own
permission set, and an account lifecycle that belongs entirely to the owner. The
work also hardened the sign-in path everybody already uses, because a new role is
only as private as the door in front of it.

## The role

`management_specialist` joined the roles an account can hold, alongside owner,
manager, admin and technician. Permissions are now stated explicitly in
`lib/manager-session.ts` rather than inferred: each role maps to a list, and a
Management Specialist gets the office floor — the dashboard, the booking screen,
the lead list, jobs and customers — and nothing else. Crew administration, login
codes, custom charges and the bulk customer import are all outside that list.

Permissions come from the role stored on the employee row and from nowhere else.
The session cookie carries an identity, not an entitlement, and the account row
is re-read on every single request, so what a code unlocks is decided server-side
each time it is used. A code typed at the login screen can therefore only ever
open the account it belongs to: an admin's code cannot produce a Management
Specialist session, and a Management Specialist's code cannot produce an admin
one.

Creating, disabling, renaming the role of, or reissuing the code for a Management
Specialist account is owner-only, in every direction. An admin or a manager
cannot promote somebody into the role and cannot touch an account already in it.
The crew list served to a non-owner drops the code state of those rows from the
payload entirely rather than merely hiding it on screen, so there is nothing for
a browser's developer tools to reveal.

Closing that rule properly meant closing one more door: an admin could previously
create a brand-new owner account with a code of their own choosing, which would
have handed them every Management Specialist power one sign-in later. The owner
role is now owner-only too. The recovery page still creates and promotes owners
for the case where there is no owner left to ask, since it is gated by a site
environment variable only the site's owner can set.

## The temporary code

A Management Specialist code is never typed by the person issuing it. When the
owner adds the account, the app draws a six-digit code from the operating
system's random source, checks it against the same rules a person's code has to
pass, stores only its scrypt hash and a fresh per-code salt, and returns the
digits exactly once — on the response to the owner's own authenticated request,
which is marked `no-store`. The console shows them in a dialog that says plainly
it is the only time they will be readable.

The digits are never written to a log, never persisted in plain text, never put
in the page source or in a build artifact, and never placed in an environment
variable. There is no route that can retrieve them afterwards; a temporary code
that goes missing is replaced by issuing a new one.

Resetting works the same way. The owner confirms, the app draws a new code, the
old one stops working immediately, and the new one is shown once. Because the
owner never chooses the value, they do not end up holding a code that would keep
working after it changed hands.

An account holding a code somebody else issued is marked as such, and the API
refuses every route except the one that changes it. Signing in works, and then
the console puts up a dialog with no way past it but choosing a new code or
signing out. The moment the new code is saved the mark clears, the temporary code
is dead, and the account has full use of its screens.

## Repeated wrong codes

Sign-in had no brake on it at all. It now has two.

Five wrong codes in a row park that account for fifteen minutes, which is what
stops somebody working through the code space on one name. Separately, twenty
sign-in failures from one connection within fifteen minutes are refused whatever
name is being tried, which is what stops the same guesser walking down the crew
list. A parked account is refused before its code is checked, so the wait cannot
be shortened by happening to guess right during it, and a successful sign-in
clears the counter. The route that changes your own code carries the same
per-account brake, since that is the one route a temporary-code holder can reach.

An unknown name, a switched-off account and a wrong code still all come back with
the same message, so the login screen gives away nothing about who exists.

## The security audit log

A new `security_events` table records how access moves: successful sign-ins,
failed attempts, lockouts, connection-level blocks, codes changed, codes reset,
accounts created, roles changed and access turned on or off. Each row keeps the
account and the actor — the same for a sign-in, different for a reset — with
their names copied alongside their ids so the record still reads correctly after
somebody is renamed, plus a short human-readable detail, the connecting address
and the user agent. No code material is recorded anywhere in it, and the recorder
deliberately never receives a code in the first place. Writes never throw: an
audit failure is reported to the function log and must not be able to block a
sign-in.

The owner reads the log from the bottom of the Crew tab. Nobody else can.

## Files changed

- `lib/manager-session.ts` — added the `management_specialist` role, role labels,
  an explicit per-role permission map (`permissionsFor`, `can`), an owner-only
  test, and `canAdministerAccount`, which is the single place the owner-only rule
  for owner and Management Specialist accounts is expressed.
- `lib/manager-pin.ts` — added `generateTempPin`, a six-digit code drawn from
  `crypto.randomInt` and validated against the existing PIN rules. Hashing and
  verification were reused unchanged.

### Summary

Add Triton implementations for all six real-valued ATen `float_power` overloads:

- `float_power.Tensor_Tensor`
- `float_power.Tensor_Scalar`
- `float_power.Scalar`
- `float_power.Tensor_Tensor_out`
- `float_power.Tensor_Scalar_out`
- `float_power.Scalar_out`

The implementation provides ATen-compatible behavior for real inputs:

- Always computes and returns FP64 results, including FP16, BF16, FP32, and integer inputs.
- Supports Tensor-Tensor broadcasting, scalar tensors, zero-sized tensors, and non-contiguous inputs/outputs.
- Preserves caller-provided tensor identity for all `out` overloads, resizes outputs when required, and rejects non-FP64 output buffers.
- Avoids temporary whole-tensor FP64 input conversions by casting values inside the Triton kernel and writing directly to FP64 outputs.
- Registers each overload independently and adds matching metadata, accuracy markers, and benchmark markers.

The initial implementation was generated with KernelGen using `claude-opus-4-8`. KernelGen ran two rounds (initial generation plus one fix-up); the result was then independently reviewed and corrected against native ATen dtype, output, broadcasting, and edge-case behavior.

### Testing

Default-device accuracy tests:

```bash
pytest tests/test_float_power.py -q --disable-warnings
```

Result:

```text
163 passed
```

CPU-reference quick mode required by the CI review workflow:

```bash
pytest tests/test_float_power.py --ref=cpu --quick -q --disable-warnings
```

Result:

```text
83 passed
```

Coverage includes FP16, BF16, FP32, and INT32 inputs; all six overloads; same-shape and broadcast inputs; scalar, empty, and non-contiguous tensors; NaN/Inf/signed-zero cases; output resizing and identity; and invalid output dtype handling.

Core benchmarks:

6 passed

author: arthur-debert
body:
A reusable vocabulary for the invariants the suite could not state, and the render-diagnostics seam behind the strongest one.

`for #313`

> **Body corrected by the coordinator.** The originally-posted body belonged to an unrelated task (a `lookma` version bump, `closes #87`) and described none of this diff. The text below is reconstructed from the implementer's own commit message on `2756fd2`; nothing about the change itself moved. Reviewers who read the first version should re-read from here.

## Context

**The gap.** Existing help assertions are existential over hand-picked strings — `contains("default: auto")`. Every defect that escaped to a downstream app was one of the other two shapes: a **universal** ("every value-taking option shows a metavar") or a **negative** ("no presence flag lists possible values"). Listing strings that should be present cannot express either. That is why #301's bogus `possible values: true, false` row rendered inside the test suite's own output on every run with no oracle to reject it.

**What ships.** `standout_test::invariants` is that missing vocabulary: every tag resolved against the theme, no `[tag?]` marker on the page, no possible-values row for a zero-arity argument, a metavar for every value-taking one, a styled page that strips back to the plain one, and one description column per section — parsed from the whole page rather than from two rows named by hand. Each names the offending tag, argument, or row when it fails. Each has both a `TestResult` form and a page form, and **the page form is what makes the oracle itself testable**: every invariant is proved against a page that violates it as well as one that holds, because an assertion that cannot fail reads as coverage while asserting nothing.

**The seam.** `standout-render` gains a `diagnostics` module. The style-tag pass already recorded every tag the theme could not resolve — the parser collects it *before* it decides what to emit, so it exists identically under `Apply`, `Keep`, and `Remove` — and the render path called `parse` instead of `parse_with_diagnostics` and dropped it. Standout computed "this page is corrupt" on every render and never said it, which is how #303 shipped. The pass is now recorded with the tag transform and unknown-tag policy that produced it, ended at the run boundary the way a framework warning is, and exposed as `TestResult::tag_resolutions()`.

That is the **strong form** of the tag invariant: it holds in `Text` as firmly as in `Term`, needs no ANSI and no TTY, and names the tag — where the `?]` scan is a search for a symptom that only the styling modes emit. Both are kept: one proves the theme is incomplete, the other proves the corruption reached the page a user sees.

**The scope amendment's line is intact** (issue #313's amendment): no rendered byte changes — 2243 tests, every existing snapshot and string assertion green; the framework still does not warn, error, or degrade on an unresolved tag; and the hardcoded `UnknownTagBehavior::Passthrough` becomes *observable*, not configurable.

## Two things reviewers should weigh, not skim

**1. Nothing is `#[ignore]`d, and that is a change in the world rather than a weakened test.** #301, #302 and #303 are now **closed** — fixed on this base — so the fixture page satisfies every invariant. This issue's acceptance criteria were written when they were open and asked for `#[ignore]` markers referencing them; that criterion is no longer satisfiable because there is nothing left to ignore. The assertions are therefore **pins** rather than red tests.

The consequence is the thing to check: an oracle that has only ever been seen to pass proves nothing. What binds these is the per-invariant failing-input self-tests described above. Judge those seriously — they are now the *only* evidence the oracles can fail. WS05 (#314) carries the complementary proof by construction (removing a field from the help data extractor must make its differential fail).

**2. The fixture here is local to the test file**, because WS03's shared fixture (#312, PR #330) was not on this branch when the work started — the two ran in parallel. This is temporary duplication of exactly the kind WS03 exists to delete. Coordinator is tracking the migration onto the shared fixture as a required convergence step once both land; it is not an argument against this PR, and it should not be "fixed" here by cherry-picking WS03's crate.


**3. WS02 is merged in, and its colour latch does not interact with the capture window.** `origin/ROB01/umbrella` at `656cb1b` is merged (both conflicts were the same collision — WS02 removing the TTY seam where this branch added the diagnostics accessor; both sides kept, `is_tty`/`no_tty` not resurrected, per ADR-0022).

The coordinator asked whether WS02's `console` colour latch and this branch's capture window interact, since both hook the run boundary. **They are independent**, on two grounds:

- *Ordering.* The latch is step 0 of `TestHarness::run` — it reads `console`'s four colour globals before fixtures, cwd, env, and detectors. The capture window opens inside `App::run` / `App::run_to_string` (`execution.rs`), i.e. entirely after step 0 and strictly nested within the harness's own call. Neither can observe the other mid-flight, and they share no state: the latch is a process-global in `console`, the window stack is thread-local to `standout-render::diagnostics`.
- *Semantics.* `resolve_tags` records a pass on exactly one condition — `is_capturing()` — and the record is built from `parse_with_diagnostics`' error list, which the parser produces *before* it decides what to emit. Colour cannot change what is recorded; it only changes the `TagTransform` value carried *in* the record. That is the same property that makes the tag invariant hold in `Text` as firmly as in `Term`.

Stated explicitly for WS06's benefit: these two seams do not need to be reasoned about together.

One integration fix the merge required beyond the two conflicts: `tests/invariants.rs`'s fixture called `.no_tty()`, which WS02 deleted — git merged that hunk cleanly because neither side edited the same lines. The call is dropped (the fixture already pins width, colour, and output mode explicitly). Renumbering the guide's new `4.8 Invariant assertions` / `4.9 Running the real binary` sections also stale-linked two `#48-running-the-real-binary` anchors WS02 wrote; both are corrected.

Verified against the merged tree, not the branch alone: `pixi run test` green at **2282 tests**, lint green, no `is_tty`/`no_tty` `TestHarness` method or detector left in `crates/`, and no `ADR-0019` reference anywhere.

author: drudge
body:
Closes two Milestone 1 roadmap items: RFC 9250 DNS-over-QUIC server and client transports, and per-source block-list health with retry backoff.

## DNS-over-QUIC

Set `encrypted_dns.doq_listen` in TOML, or fill the field on Settings → Protocols, and Sable opens a UDP listener alongside DoT and DoH using the same certificate.

- One query per bidirectional stream with the two-octet length prefix DNS already uses over TCP.
- `doq` ALPN only, TLS 1.3 only. QUIC has no lower version to fall back to, so a configured `minimum_tls_version = "1.2"` does not apply to this listener.
- TSIG-signed requests are verified and responses are signed. (Note for a reviewer: `dohResponseWriter.TsigStatus()` returns nil unconditionally, so DoH does not do this. That is pre-existing and untouched here, but worth a separate look.)
- Fatal-for-the-connection cases per the RFC: zero-length message, unparsable message, and `edns-tcp-keepalive` all close with `DOQ_PROTOCOL_ERROR`.
- Shutdown closes established connections. Closing the QUIC listener alone leaves them running until they idle out, which is longer than `shutdown_timeout`.

Client side:
- The console DNS Client transport picker already had a QUIC `<option>` with `disabled` on it. It now works.
- `sable query --transport quic --server dns.example:853 example.com A`
- Forwarders and `FWD` records accept a `quic://` prefix next to `udp`, `tcp`, and `tls`. Defaults to port 853.

DoQ binds UDP, so a `doq_listen` address may reuse a port `dot_listen` already holds on TCP. Config validation rejects one that collides with `server.dns_listen`.

Adds `github.com/quic-go/quic-go v0.61.0`, the first new direct dependency in a while.

## Block-list health and backoff

Refresh was all-or-nothing and nearly silent. One unreachable URL aborted the whole refresh, the only recovery was a flat one-hour retry, and `UpdateStatus` carried a single timestamp for the entire set — so a list could stop updating for weeks while the console kept showing the last time *any* refresh succeeded.

Each source is now tracked independently, keyed by URL so a rename does not reset its history: last attempt, last success, last error, consecutive failures, bytes, next retry.

**Behavior change worth reviewing:** a failing source no longer aborts the refresh. It keeps serving its cached copy, every other list still updates and recompiles, and the failing one backs off exponentially from 5 minutes to a 6 hour ceiling. A source that has *never* downloaded successfully is still fatal, since there is no cache behind it and the compiler would fail on the missing file. The staged-swap-and-rollback path for the sources that did download is unchanged.

The scheduler wakes at whichever comes first, the configured `update_interval` or the earliest pending retry. Pressing **Update Block Lists** clears every pending backoff first.

Surfaced in three places:
- Console: failing lists carry an inline warning with failure count and time to retry; the block-list card turns red with a degraded count.
- Logs: one structured line per unhealthy source with consecutive failures and retry deadline.
- Prometheus: `sable_block_list_source_healthy`, `_consecutive_failures`, `_downloads_total`, `_failures_total`, and `_last_success_timestamp_seconds`, each labelled `list` and `url`, plus `sable_block_list_sources_degraded`.

## Testing

`mage verify` is clean and the full suite passes under `-race`.

New coverage:
- End-to-end DoQ round trip over a real QUIC connection, two queries on one connection to prove per-stream handling.
- `edns-tcp-keepalive` and zero-length message both abort the connection.
- Shutdown closes an established connection.
- Client stream framing against a minimal RFC 9250 server, and the message ID being zeroed per §4.2.1.
- Config: DoQ/plain-DNS UDP conflict rejected, DoQ sharing the DoT port accepted, certificate required for DoQ.
- Backoff doubling and capping; a failing source backing off while its neighbours still update; abort when there is no cached copy; `ClearBackoff` forcing a retry; health pruned when a list is removed.

`staticcheck` segfaults on Go 1.27 on this machine (`honnef.co/go/tools@v0.4.7`). Unrelated to this branch, but it means static analysis beyond `go vet` did not run.

## Copy — verbatim, checked word by word

The Google Docs are now the editorial source. All four bodies were replaced with their canonical text and compared token by token against it:

| Story | Title | Deck | Body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 001 | MATCH | MATCH | **IDENTICAL** — 324 words |
| 002 | MATCH | MATCH | **IDENTICAL** — 507 words |
| 003 | MATCH | MATCH | **IDENTICAL** — 650 words |
| 004 | MATCH | MATCH | **IDENTICAL** — 386 words |

The only transformations were mechanical: normalising the blank-line padding Docs export adds, and extracting lines 1–3 into `title` / `summary` / date+location. **No sentence was reworded, shortened or "improved."**

002 becomes *Aprender Santiago desde el manillar* and its date moves to 1 August per its dateline. **Slugs and URLs are untouched** — no redirects needed.

Every closing line that used to live in `note:` frontmatter is now inside the canonical body, so those fields are removed rather than repeating as pull quotes.

## Anchors repositioned to the new text

Not left where the old paragraphs used to be:

- **002** — the bicycle follows *"comprar una bicicleta de segunda mano"*; the cordillera view follows the paragraph about using the Andes to get one's bearings (a better fit than before).
- **003** — the long table follows the sentence recalling that first Sunday lunch.
- **004** — the dish follows *"apareció un conejo con pistachos"*.

All twelve photographs stay, three per story. None moved between stories; no caption invents anything the source doesn't say.

## Banner

On the front page it **is** the `h1` — the drawn title replaces the set one rather than appearing beside it, and its `alt` keeps the heading readable to screen readers and search. Nothing duplicated, nothing hidden. Story pages keep the small set wordmark, where a banner would overwhelm the article.

At 2.35:1 it's wide and short: **390 × 166 px on mobile**, so no crop is needed, nothing of the drawing is lost, and the reader isn't scrolling past a hero to reach the news. Served via `<picture>` with a half-width source below 760px. Re-encoded from the 2.4 MB PNG to **299 KB / 81 KB** — the alpha channel was fully opaque, so JPEG costs nothing.

## Unchanged

Palette, typography, story accents, front-page hierarchy, photography treatment, motion, archive, About block, asensios.com, WhatsApp, read-state, analytics, build system, slugs.

## QA

Rendered at 1440 / 390 across homepage and all four stories: zero overflow, zero broken images, no console or network errors, no anchor tokens in HTML. Confirmed the superseded copy is gone from every page.

## Problem
The series store defines two actions, `fetchSeries` (GET /series) and `toggleDraft` (POST /series/{id}/toggle-draft), that call backend routes which do not exist.

## Cause
No backend, Flask or FastAPI, has ever served GET /series or POST /series/{id}/toggle-draft. Neither action has a caller: `seriesStore.fetchSeries(` has zero matches in src, and the only similarly-named call, `toggleDraftFantasyMatch` in MatchDetailsView.vue, calls `updateDraftSeries` instead, a different action.

## Fix
Deleted both actions from src/stores/series.store.js. Both had no consumer and no backend route, so deletion is the root-cause fix, not a new route. No state fields were removed: `series`, `draftSeries`, and `isLoading` are all still used by the remaining actions.

## Proof

2. `grep -rn "fetchSeries\|toggleDraft" src/` shows only `fetchSeriesBySeason` and `toggleDraftFantasyMatch`, two different symbols kept unchanged. No leftover reference to the deleted actions.

author: justinelbertpr
body:
## Why

The mobile menu and header were rejected twice, and the desktop nav vanished outright. Both traced to one mechanism: a `<details>` holding the nav, an inline script closing it below 640px, and a media query hiding its `<summary>` above 640px. Load narrow, widen, and the nav was gone with no way back.

This deletes that mechanism rather than guarding it. **Five short links do not need a door** — no disclosure widget at any width, no open/closed state, no JS deciding nav visibility. The failure becomes unrepresentable rather than defended against.

## The design

Two bands in one sticky box:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  txschools.net   Unofficial · not affiliated with the      │  NAMEPLATE
│                  Texas Education Agency · what this is [☾] │  scrolls away
│ ---------------------------------------------------------- │
│  Home  Districts A–Z  Rankings  Download  About  [search Q]│  TOOLS · pins
└════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════┘
```

Sticky with a **negative `top`** equal to the nameplate's measured height, so exactly that slice scrolls off and the rest pins. Pinned height: **135px → 65px** desktop, **157px → 119px** mobile — while everything is now visible at every width instead of behind a tap.

`initHeaderH` becomes `initMasthead`, publishing `--mast-scroll` (leaves) and `--header-h` (stays). Every existing `--header-h` consumer wants the pinned height; none of their rules change.

## Three pre-existing defects found and fixed

- **The disclaimer was `display:none` on every JS-enabled phone load.** On a domain one character from a `.gov`, that's the headline fix.
- **`SEARCH_CSS` was unpinning the masthead.** `header:has(.sitesearch-panel…)` set `position:relative` at a specificity/source-order that beat `header.site`'s `position:sticky`, so opening the header autocomplete snapped the masthead to the top of the document mid-typing. Now sets `z-index` only.
- **`.sitesearch-input`'s border was ~1.2:1 contrast** (needs 3:1) on the site's highest-value control. Now `--ink-3`, fixed at source so the hero search benefits too.

Also fixed while verifying: the search form needed `min-width: 0` — flex's `auto` min-width floor punched it ~20px past the header's content box at 320px, taking the page into horizontal scroll.

## Regression guard

Four new tests forbid the **mechanism**, not a rendering: no `<details>`, no inline script in the header, no stylesheet rule that can hide the nav, no width-based `matchMedia` in `app.js`. A rendering checked at two widths is exactly what missed this — the failure lives in the transition between them.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` — 907/907 (+4 new)
- [x] The narrow→wide resize that caused this: nav present, 5 links, at every step
- [x] 320 / 375 / 768 / 1280, light + dark
- [x] Sticky: `--header-h` (65px) == header's rendered bottom; nameplate scrolls off, tools pin
- [x] Tab order matches visual order; all controls 44px under coarse pointer
- [x] Zero horizontal overflow at 320px
- [x] Autocomplete no longer unpins the masthead
- [x] CSP: exactly 3 distinct inline scripts across all page types, all covered; `NAV_INIT_SCRIPT` hash removed

⚠️ Two things I could not verify in the browser harness (it doesn't dispatch `resize`, deliver IntersectionObserver callbacks, or advance CSS animations): the sticky-bar reveal, and a real drag-resize. Both were verified by construction/geometry instead — and notably the resize test now passes *without any event firing*, since there's no state to repair.

Design synthesized from four independent approaches scored by three judges including an adversarial pass.

author: tetrisgm
body:
## Summary

Two fixes to the debug server's capture path, found while standing up an automated
screenshot-driven test loop for a widescreen enhancement on a game repo.

1. **`screenshot_hires` corrupted every frame it captured** — an `out_pitch` units bug,
   plus a second path where it could emit untouched allocation.
2. **No capture command showed the presented frame**, only the pre-fit display buffer.
   Adds `present_shot` / `present_shot_seq` to close that gap.

Both are framework-level and game-agnostic; nothing here is title-specific.

---

## 1. `screenshot_hires` pitch was in pixels, not bytes

`handle_screenshot_hires` passed the pixel width as `out_pitch`:

```c
int got = gr_render_display_hires(argb, (int)ow, ...);   /* ow = pixels */
```

But both resolves step rows in **bytes**:

```c
/* gpu_sw_renderer.c: sw_render_display, sw_render_display_hires */
uint32_t *dst = (uint32_t *)((uint8_t *)out_pixels + row * out_pitch);
```

The present path is the authority on the intended convention and passes bytes
(`main.cpp`: `gr_render_display_hires(sdl_pixel_buf, (int)(sw * sizeof(uint32_t)), ...)`).

So the capture advanced `508` bytes = `127` px per row instead of `2032` bytes. The frame
came out tiled **4× horizontally** (`508/127 = 4`) into the **top quarter**
(`256 rows × 127 px` spans only 64 of 256 rows), the rest black. Both call sites were
affected — the hires call and the `gr_render_display` fallback beneath it. `wide_shot` was
already correct, which is why this stayed hidden.

**Measured on WipEout 3 (SCES-02845), OpenGL, internal scale 1x:** rows containing any
non-black pixel went **65/256 → 256/256**.

### Partial-cover leak in the same handler

While verifying the above: `gr_scale()` reports the GL backend's internal scale, but
`sw_render_display_hires` falls back to the native resolve when the CPU hi-res mirror does
not exist (`!g_hr || g_scale <= 1`). That fills `w*h` of an `ow*oh` buffer and still returns
non-zero, so testing `!got` alone let a mostly-uninitialized buffer reach `png_write_rgb`.
The buffer is now `calloc`'d, and the resolve must report **full cover** or the capture
redoes itself honestly at native size.

## 2. `present_shot` — capture the composed frame

`screenshot`, `screenshot_file` and `screenshot_hires` all resolve the display buffer
*before* the backend fits it to the window. On a 508×256 display in a 4:3 window they
answer 508×256 while the player sees 640×480 logical / 1280×960 actual — the same pixels
at a different shape.

Correct for faithfulness work, wrong for anything aspect-shaped. A widescreen change moves
the GTE squash and the present fit, which is precisely the stage those captures skip — so a
regression is invisible and the check reports green. `WIDESCREEN.md` already warns about
the neighbouring case ("the VRAM `screenshot_file` shows the pre-stretch frame"), and the
`screenshot_hires` header notes that mis-reporting geometry correction as fixed is how it
went wrong once before.

`present_shot` reads back the composed present surface instead. Request state lives in
`main.cpp`; fulfilment belongs to whichever backend owns the present:

- **OpenGL** — `glReadPixels` immediately before `SDL_GL_SwapWindow`, after the display
  quad and OSD are drawn, with the bottom-up row flip GL requires.
- **SDL software** — `SDL_RenderReadPixels` between `SDL_RenderCopy` + `host_osd_draw_sdl`
  and `SDL_RenderPresent`.

Contract details worth calling out:

- **Threading.** GL fulfilment can run on the frame-interpolation thread
  (`interp_present` → `gl_swap_with_osd`), not only the emu thread where command handlers
  run. The path buffer and pending flag are mutex-guarded and the counters are atomic;
  `present_shot_take()` claims the request under the lock, so two present paths cannot
  fulfil the same shot.
- **No wedge.** A staged shot is *overwritten* by a later request rather than refused —
  the same choice `savestate`'s `request_save_inner` makes. A present that never arrives
  (static frame, backend that stops presenting) therefore cannot brick the command.
- **Vulkan.** It presents through its own swapchain and has no readback hook, so the
  request is refused there rather than accepted and never fulfilled. Silently accepting a
  shot that can never complete is exactly the debt `CLAUDE.md` rule 15 forbids. Happy to
  implement the VK readback in a follow-up — I had no Vulkan SDK to test against here, and
  shipping an untested readback seemed worse than an honest refusal.
- **Honest completion.** `present_shot_seq` advances on success *and* failure, so a
  polling client always terminates; its `wrote` field says whether a PNG actually landed.
- **SDL2 sizing.** That branch sizes its buffer from `SDL_GetRendererOutputSize` rather
  than a `viewport × scale` reconstruction, which can round independently of the region
  `SDL_RenderReadPixels` actually fills.

Readback costs a GPU sync, so it only runs when a shot was explicitly requested — no
per-frame cost when unused.

## 3. Smaller items

- `tools/debug_client.py`: `screenshot_file` and `turbo`/`turbo_state` had no mappings and
  fell through to the raw `key=value` handler, so the documented
  `debug_client.py screenshot_file out.png` failed with `Unrecognized arg`. They now take a
  positional path / value like their siblings, as does `present_shot`.
- `TCP_COMMANDS.md`: `screenshot_hires` had a blank **N** column, which reads as
  Beetle-only despite being registered on the native server. Added curated rows for the two
  new commands and regenerated the index with `tools/gen_tcp_commands.py`.

---

## Testing

Built and run against a real title — WipEout 3 SE (PAL), OpenGL backend, `RelWithDebInfo`
with `PSX_DEBUG_TOOLS=ON`.

- `screenshot_hires`: before/after on an identical in-race scene — the 4× tiling and the
  black three-quarters are gone; content rows 65/256 → 256/256.
- `present_shot`: emits a 1280×960 PNG matching the on-screen window, including the 4:3 fit
  the buffer-level captures do not carry.
- Completion signal: `seq` 0→1 with `wrote: 1` on success; `seq` 1→2 with **`wrote: 0`** for
  an unwritable path (poll still terminates).
- Overwrite semantics: two `present_shot` calls back-to-back are both accepted — no
  "already in flight" refusal.

**Not covered:** only the OpenGL path was exercised at runtime. The SDL software
`SDL_RenderReadPixels` branch, the SDL2 (non-`PSX_SDL3`) branches, and the Vulkan refusal
are compile-verified only — I had no software-renderer, SDL2, or Vulkan configuration to
test against. Worth a look from someone who does.

author: rodneygagnon
body:
## v1.8.5 fixed the wrong layer

Raising the **gateway's** rate limits did not clear the symptoms — still "Too many requests" in the Representatives section, still 0 committees. The logs said why:

```
gateway:            0 throttle rejections
opuspopuli-region:  4 throttle rejections    ← since the v1.8.5 restart
```

Every service registers its own `ThrottlerModule`. The gateway's limits were inline in its module; all four subgraphs share `THROTTLER_CONFIG`, which was still at **10 req/s**.

`BriefingCommittees`, `MyCountySupervisors` and `GetRepresentativesByDistricts` are all region-service queries — exactly the two sections that were failing. The committees section rendered 0 not because nothing matched (85 live committees exist, and the user's `interest_tags` were correct) but because the query was rejected before it ran.

## The subgraph limit was worse than a wrong number

The throttler keys on **IP**, and every subgraph request arrives from the **gateway's single IP**. There is no per-user dimension at all.

So `10/s` was never "10 requests per second per user" — it was a **global cap on total system throughput, shared by every user at once**, against a briefing load that needs ~21 requests. It survived only because there was effectively one person using the platform. Two concurrent users would have throttled each other, and it would have looked like random breakage under launch traffic.

It also buys no security. Subgraphs are not publicly reachable and require a valid `X-HMAC-Auth` signature — anyone able to flood them has already defeated something more important than a rate limit. The meaningful per-caller control is the gateway's, which keys on the real client IP.

Raised to a level that acts as a **runaway backstop** (a looping bug should still be stopped before it saturates the database) rather than a throughput cap.

## Both configs now live together

`GATEWAY_THROTTLER_CONFIG` and `THROTTLER_CONFIG` are both in `shared-app.config.ts`, with comments explaining that one is per-client-IP and the other is effectively global.

The gateway's were inline, which is precisely how the previous fix missed the subgraphs. Same file now, so changing one puts the other in front of you.

## Testing

- All five services build
- Backend suite 138 suites / 2383 tests green
- lint, `lint:sonar`, jscpd clean
- After deploy: the Representatives and committees sections should populate on first sign-in, and `docker logs opuspopuli-region | grep -i throttler` should stay clean

## Note

The underlying defect is still the fan-out — ~21 requests per briefing load, with duplicate `BriefingPrefetch`/`MyProfile` calls and unbatched per-bill queries. Tracked in #1024. These limits buy room; they are not headroom to spend.

## Review status

**Self-reviewed** — needs countersignature for separation of duties.

## Data classification

None — rate limit configuration. No change to what data is returned.
