body:
## O que o dono via

Um contato salvo no celular como **"Anderson Corretor"**, **"Imobiliária Central"**, **"Construtora Boa Vista"** ou **"Plantão Centro"** entrava na carteira como **"Cliente não identificado"** — e a análise daquela conversa saía errada, sem nenhum erro aparecer na tela. É justamente o **corretor parceiro**, que o sistema atende de propósito.

## Como foi encontrado

Auditoria de 16/08/2026 (`AUDITORIA-v1281.md`), reproduzida **rodando as funções de verdade** — mesmo texto de conversa, mudando só o nome do contato:

```
"Anderson Ruviaro"    → cliente "Anderson Ruviaro",         2 tentativas  ✔
"Anderson Corretor"   → cliente "Cliente não identificado", 3 tentativas  ✘
"Imobiliária Central" → cliente "Cliente não identificado", 3 tentativas  ✘
```

A terceira "tentativa" era a fala **do próprio cliente**.

## O estrago, rastreado até o pedido enviado à IA

1. `ehLadoDaEmpresa` elimina autores com `construtora|imobiliária|corretor|atendimento|plantão|incorporadora`. A lista existe para reconhecer o rótulo do **próprio** corretor.
2. `pickClientName` aplicava a lista **antes de olhar a prova** → zero candidatos → `"Cliente não identificado"`.
3. Sem `clientName`, `_ladoDaMensagem` perde a regra "autor que contém o primeiro nome do contato é o cliente" e classifica as falas dele como do corretor.
4. Com isso, as falas do cliente entravam em dois blocos do prompt:
   - **`TENTATIVAS DO CORRETOR AINDA SEM RESPOSTA`** (v1277) — o pedido do cliente virava "oferta que ele já ignorou", com a instrução *"NENHUMA das três pode ser isto de novo"*. A IA ficava **proibida de tratar exatamente o que o cliente pediu**, e a contagem inflada disparava a regra de duas tentativas.
   - **`COMO ESTE CORRETOR ESCREVE`** (v1212) — o estilo do **cliente** virava a régua de voz do corretor.

Passava nos 437 testes da suíte.

## A correção

**Prova vence palpite.** A exportação do WhatsApp nomeia o arquivo com o **contato**, nunca com o dono do aparelho. `pickClientName` passa a procurar esse nome **entre todos os autores, antes do filtro** — a ordem anterior apagava a resposta antes de a pergunta ser feita.

Guarda nova: o atalho não vale se o autor for o próprio corretor, via `ehOProprioCorretor` — extraída de `ehLadoDaEmpresa` **sem alterar o comportamento dela**.

Nada mais foi tocado: a lista de palavras continua valendo, `_ladoDaMensagem` não mudou (se conserta sozinha com o nome certo) e a regra da **v1180** (sem prova e com 2+ candidatos, o app não escolhe) segue de pé.

Depois da correção, os três casos entregam o nome certo e as 2 tentativas certas, sem a fala do cliente na lista. **Leads antigos se corrigem ao reimportar** — o nome é recalculado do arquivo em toda análise.

## Guarda

`tests/v1282-contato-com-corretor-no-nome.test.mjs` — roda as funções de verdade com 5 nomes de contato e testa as duas fronteiras (o rótulo do próprio corretor nunca vira cliente; sem prova com 2+ candidatos segue "Cliente não identificado").

**Suíte: 23 arquivos checados + 438 testes, todos verdes.**

## Também neste PR

`AUDITORIA-v1281.md` — a auditoria completa do sistema, refeita com rastreamento de cada achado no código (e as correções das afirmações que a primeira versão fazia sem rastrear).

# exp41port-v6: Item A + Item B + Item C + Item D (station-hold chain drain overlap, full host CPU/GPU overlap)

## Attribution

Built by the lighterfast prover agent. This is the **first half of the host CPU/GPU overlap
task**: it addresses the **block-tail cold-buffer-stall** component only. It inherits v2's
Item A (decode overlap) + Item B (early pre-proof release) unchanged, and adds **Item C**
(the block-tail LDE column-store prewarm moved earlier so it overlaps the entire tx/chain
pipeline). The station-hold half (the ~13.5 ms/step GPU-station hold on the tail) is
deliberately NOT touched here; the parent is doing that as a separate second item.

## What the tip already brings (inherited, not our work)

The base is the v2 stack = the abd4b3da tip (Item T-WINDOW depth 4 + Item T-DEAD packed-lane
store) plus our Item A and Item B. Description is identical to the v2 note; only `Item C` is
new in this tree.

## What WE add on top (three items)

- **Item A — decode overlap (`bench/src/bin/prove.rs`).** Byte-scanner swaps the top-level
  `txs` array for an empty one so the pre-execution proof parses a tx-free envelope; serde
  stays the authority for the full parse. (Inherited from v2, unchanged.)
- **Item B — early pre-proof release (`bench/src/prover.rs`, `prove_block_after_pre`).**
  `drop(pre_proof)` right after the final-block early witness feed lowers the concurrent peak
  footprint. (Inherited from v2, unchanged.)
- **Item C — block-tail cold-buffer prewarm earlier (host overlap, gradual)**
  (`bench/src/prover.rs`). The final block's LDE wire-column store is ~2 GiB (136 cols x
  2^21 LDE rows x 8 B; `CIRCUIT_CONFIG`-derived), larger than the Metal column-store pool
  cap, so without help `take_or_new_column_buffer` freshly zero-faults it inside the run's
  most serial window — the block-tail cold-buffer stall (~230-330 ms) the multiply-bound GPU
  otherwise idles on. v2 already warmed this store, but only from a detached thread spawned
  when the **heavy** path retired deep inside `prove_path`, so it overlapped just the
  light-phase slack and its completion depended on the heavy/light tail balance. Item C moves
  that detached, utility-QoS page-walk to the **very start of `prove_block_after_pre`**, so it
  overlaps the ENTIRE tx/chain phase and is guaranteed to be published (publish-after-walk
  preserved) well before the final serial tail's LDE fill. Scheduling-only: store contents are
  fully overwritten by the LDE fill before any kernel read, the stash is published only after
  the walk, and a size miss falls through to a fresh allocation — the contract is identical to
  a fresh buffer (prewarm publish-after-walk correctness repair retained). The old deep spawn
  was removed so the ~2 GiB is walked once, not twice.

## Scope note on the rest of the cold-buffer stall (what remains)

exp30's lesson is "Column LDE != sponge state != digest != set.input": the tail's first
submit also cold-binds the streamed-Merkle sponge state (~192 MiB) + digest output (~128 MiB)
and the set.input/staging/digest buffers. Those stashes live inside `vendor/plonky2/.../
poseidon2/metal.rs` (`STREAMED_BUFFERS`, `PREWARMED_STORE` Vec, absorbed input bindings). This
task constrained the worker to `bench/src` only (vendor + circuit fixed), so Item C prewarms
the one tail buffer reachable from `bench/src` — the LDE column store. The sponge/digest/input
prewarm per exp30 requires a vendor/metal.rs stash port and is OUT OF SCOPE of this
bench/src-only fire; it remains for a vendor-eligible fire. The station-hold half is also
untouched (parent's second item).

## Bisection plan (Item C is the degraded-scheduling suspect)

Declared incrementally so a bad ranked draw is easy to bisect:
- **If a draw regresses, suspect Item C first** — it is a scheduling-class change (the prewarm
  walk now runs underneath the heavy/light tx phase instead of just the light-phase slack, so
  it shares the pipeline's early window). It is well-scoped to the tail but is the only Item C
  in this tree that changes *when* work runs rather than *what* bytes are produced. Revert
  Item C (restore the heavy-path-retirement spawn) alone for a controlled A/B.
- Only if Item C is cleared, suspect Item A (byte-deviating, larger behavioral change), then
  Item B.
- Items A/B/C are separate commits on top of the v2 base, so each can be reverted alone.

## Correctness / validation

- Local smoke (`benchmark.sh public-synthetic-smoke`) on this v5 tree: `passed: true`,
  `verified_proofs: 1/1` (candidate SHA 80731aa3), verifier SHA 3418587865..., fixture
  6f1fbd2d. Correctness gate is verifier accept (trusted-verifier parent), NOT byte-identity
  to master: Item A intentionally changes the pre-proof's bytes; Item C changes no computed
  value (scheduling-only).
- Dev box M5 timing is NOT ranked-representative (the smoke proving time ~31 s / ~16 TPS here
  is a local-throughput claim only, subject to the documented dev-box noise). No local
  regression in smoke; Items A+B were already rank-verified 5/5 on prior bases.

## Validation and verification

- Local smoke (benchmark.sh public-synthetic-smoke) on this v5 tree: `passed: true`,
  `verified_proofs: 1/1` across three runs (one ~65 s outlier while the local fire loop

- Bisection guidance (declared): if a ranked draw regresses below the no-Item-C baseline,

  `3265147b` C) so any single item can be reverted alone.


## Item D — station-hold removal in chain drain phase (host overlap second half)

In `bench/src/prover.rs` `prove_path`, the strictly sequential chain drain previously blocked
synchronously in the path thread on `proof_handle.join()` before spawning the next chain step.
Even though the next step's phase-1 witness only requires its own transaction proof (and does not
depend on the predecessor chain step's proof), the main path thread was held waiting on the join,
stalling the spawn and leaving the GPU station idle between serial steps.

body:
Branch = codex `81c54b5` (unchanged) **+ two commits**: `1b7e5bc` (the durability analysis) and `a96ea4b` (closures for the open routes). 28 new tests, all passing; the pre-existing 196 also pass.

Applies the method from the HS branch (`claude/canine-genetics-alphafold-ttyxyf`) — compute the bar, test achievability against real trial data, enumerate escape routes, close what can be closed — to hemangiosarcoma. Plain-language write-up: **[Hemangiosarcoma Escape Routes](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/c8094f3b-e5e8-44c7-92fe-45c87dd81bd1)**.

## Part 1 — `hsa_durable_response_analysis.py` (`1b7e5bc`)

**The drug is nearly irrelevant to durability.** `clone_growth_margins` gives a bar of **0.0515/day** at the module's assumed full exposure and **0.0550/day with no drug at all** — a 7% spread. The inhibitor drives the sensitive clone to −0.0919 and moves the three resistant clones by 1–2%.

Sharper: rapamycin's real canine trough (10.9 nM, Paoloni 2010 PMID 20543980) against VDC-597's real 543 nM IC50 (Pyuen 2018 PMID 30011343) is **50× below IC50**, and at that exposure the sensitive clone isn't suppressed either (+0.0545 vs +0.0550 untreated). Scoping correction, not retraction — the drug never carried durability.

**Achievability from two real trials in the disease.** ERstrePs (PMID 37686485) and eVim (PMID 41009669) each buy ~+30 pp of 1-year survival. The engine reaches +30 pp at `vaccine_max_kill` ≈ 0.03 against a bar of ~0.052 — **short by ~1.7×**, and that's a lower bound since the trials report survival and the engine reports progression-free.

**The antigen-loss route is over-weighted for HSA.** Escape-clone coverage is hard-coded to 0.0, inherited from HS's peptide/MHC-I vaccine. eVim raises antibodies against *extracellular* vimentin (MHC-I uninvolved — `hsa_scenarios` establishes this itself, then models MHC-I loss anyway); ERstrePs raises both humoral and T-cell responses; and MHC-loss variants upregulate NKG2D ligands that primed CD8s kill through (Lerner 2023 PMID 37537301). Simulation agrees: at 0.06 it never fires even at 10× the assumed rate.

**A hypothesis that failed, recorded as such.** Modelling the splenectomy every comparator trial performed *raises* durable response (1-yr 0.665 → 0.750 at `preexisting_prob` 0.30), moving further from the eBAT benchmark — so it cannot explain the 0.30 → 0.70 recentering. Independently useful: surgery moves 1-yr by 8–11 points and 2-yr by 1.5–4. It is a delay mechanism, matching the real 48-day surgery-alone median (Wendelburg 2015 PMID 26225611).

## Part 2 — `hsa_open_route_closure.py` (`a96ea4b`)

### A self-refutation first

Part 1 proposed closing route 4 with "eBAT minus its 28-day cap." **That experiment was run.** SRCBST-2 (Borgatti et al. 2020, Vet Comp Oncol 18(4):664-674, PMID 32187827) gave three cycles instead of one in 25 dogs: greater toxicity (six acute hypotension, two hospitalised), *reduced* efficacy, no significant survival benefit vs contemporary standard of care. More eBAT was worse than less. The modelled requirement (≥0.05/day persistent agnostic kill) stands; the proposed agent does not.

### Route 5 — rupture/haemorrhage → **PARTIALLY CLOSED**

Modelled as an independent competing hazard, so it multiplies:

| annual rupture hazard | 0% | 5% | 10% | 20% | 40% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5-yr joint durability | 0.967 | 0.748 | **0.571** | 0.317 | 0.075 |

- **5a Yunnan Baiyao ± aminocaproic acid — FAILED.** Murphy et al. 2017 (JVECC 27(1):121-126, PMID 27669112): 16 YB, 8 YB+EACA, 43 controls; median survival 18 d vs 16 d, time to recurrence 12 d vs 14.5 d, neither significant. It *does* kill canine HSA lines in vitro (Wirth 2016, PMID 24976212) — a clean in-vitro-doesn't-transfer case.
- **5b IMRT + vinblastine + propranolol — real, positive, small.** Moirano et al. 2023 (Vet Radiol Ultrasound 64(6):1099-1102, PMID 37800663): 7 dogs, right atrial tumours, **effusions resolved in all seven**, median PFS 290 d, OS 326 d.
- **5c Liquid-biopsy screening — strongest lever.** CANDiD (Flory et al. 2022, PLOS ONE 17(4):e0266623, PMID 35471999): 1,100 dogs, 78.4–90.9% sensitivity for the aggressive-cancer group including HSA, 98.5% specificity, four presymptomatic detections. Converts emergency rupture into elective splenectomy — changes the hazard rather than treating it.

### Route 6 — vaccine failure without antigen loss → **CLOSABLE**

Modelled as a take rate; ~6.7 points of durability per 10 points of take (0.967 → 0.833 → 0.699 → 0.565 at take 1.0/0.8/0.6/0.4). Largest lever after potency, and the only one directly measurable.

- **Mechanism, measured in canine HSA itself:** the tumour induces M2 polarisation and PD-L1 on tumour-associated macrophages, and HSA tumours with PD-L1⁺ macrophages contain **fewer T-cells** (Gulay et al. 2022, Sci Rep 12(1):2124, PMID 35136176).
- **6a anti-PD-L1 (c4G12):** 29 dogs, metastatic oral melanoma, 143 d vs 54 d historical control, 1/13 CR, 51.7% any-grade AEs (Maekawa et al. 2021, NPJ Precis Oncol 5(1):10, PMID 33580183). Never given for HSA; the selecting biomarker is the same IHC that produced the mechanism.
- **6b measure the take.** Neither real HSA vaccine trial powered responder-vs-non-responder survival. A trial-design closure, and the cheapest item here.

### Route 7 — disease outside the resected compartment → **ALREADY CLOSED**

Quantified in-disease: **22% of liver lesions found at surgery were missed on preoperative ultrasound** across 99 dogs (Ramirez et al. 2024, JAVMA 262(11):1499-1503, PMID 39111340).

Running HSA's 5-clone scenario through `run_monte_carlo_two_compartment` — built for the HS work, never called by HSA:

| P(occult second site) | 0.0 | 0.3 | 0.6 |
|---|---|---|---|
| durable, vaccine on | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| relapses in that site | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| durable, vaccine off | 0.340 | — | 0.325 |
| relapses in that site | 0 | — | **46 of 135** |

Surgery structurally cannot reach it; a systemic persistent mechanism reaches it as well as the first compartment. **No new agent needed** — this is the sharpest argument for the vaccine in the analysis. Backstop for non-takers: metronomic oral chemotherapy, median OS and DFI both 178 d vs 133/126 d on doxorubicin (Lana et al. 2007, JVIM 21(4):764-9, PMID 17708397).

## Audit findings from the first pass (unchanged, still worth fixing)

- `Wong et al. 2017` (PMID 29190660) is **Wang G et al.**; `Megquier 2019` lacks its PMID (31570656); `HSA_RAPAMYCIN_BENCHMARK` records `p_value: 0.0001` where the paper says `p < 0.0001`; ERstrePs is `Cancers 15(17):4209`, not `4402`.
- README's "immune_escape fraction (1.7–2.7%) **among relapses**" is a per-*trial* fraction (8 and 5 of 300). Those are 100% of relapses.
- `verify_antigen_convergence` passes vacuously on HSA clone names — verifies 1 of 3 routes, reports `all_drug_resistance_routes_covered=True`.
- `dog_hsa_preset`'s IC50 anchor is numerically inert: `css_reference` is defined as 5× it, so results are bit-identical at 300, 100 or 5000 nM.
- `find_exposed_linear_epitopes` has no pLDDT floor; on real dog VIM it returns windows at mean pLDDT 37.6 / 50.0 / 39.0 — the disordered head and tail.

author: jiayan-xu
body:
## 背景

代码自我进化引擎（Phase 7）在 Windows 上无法落盘：`/api/evolve` 的 apply 轮走到 `git_commit()` 时稳定失败，导致进化结果无法提交。

## 根因

`resolve_isolated_target` 对目标路径执行 `canonicalize()`，在 Windows 上返回 **verbatim 路径**（`\\?\` 前缀，如 `\\?\C:\Users\user\evo-sandbox`）。`git_commit` 将 commit 消息写入 `repo.join(".evo_commit_msg")`（verbatim 路径，Rust 侧写入成功），随后执行：

```
git -C <verbatim repo> commit -F <verbatim 绝对路径>
```

Git for Windows 把 `\\?\C:\...` 转成 `//?/C:/...` 后无法打开该文件，报：

```
fatal: could not read log file '//?/C:/Users/user/evo-sandbox/.evo_commit_msg': No such file or directory
```

复现证据（100% 稳定复现）：
- `git commit -F "\\?\C:\Users\user\evo-sandbox\.evo_commit_msg"` → 上述 fatal
- 同路径不带 `\\?\` 前缀 → 正常
- 引擎内部 `git add` / `git diff` / `git checkout`（均用 `-C <repo>` + 相对路径）不受影响，因此 dry-run 模式一切正常，仅 commit 落盘失败

## 修复

`git_commit` 的 `-F` 参数从绝对 verbatim 路径改为**相对路径**（相对 `-C` chdir 后的目录）：

```rust
git -C <verbatim repo> commit -F .evo_commit_msg
```

与 `git add` / `git diff` / `git checkout` 既有的 `-C` + 相对路径用法一致。验证：修复后引擎 apply 轮真实提交成功（`commit 1f224bc 代码进化(gen 3): 优化 fib`，迭代版 fib，bench 2.4ms → 0.0ms）。

## 附带增强

commit 失败诊断：错误信息从仅含 stderr 扩展为 `exit / stdout / stderr` 三件套，便于定位 git 子进程在 Windows 控制台代码页下静默失败（stderr 为空）的场景。

## 测试

- 本机服务（agent-core v0.10.0 本地构建）apply 轮端到端：propose → apply_patch → eval_crate 双门 → improved → git_commit 成功 → commit 短哈希返回
- dry-run 路径不受影响（diff / revert 行为不变）
- 手动复现：verbatim `-F` 失败 / 相对 `-F` 成功，与本修复一致

author: bdf1992
body:
## Work

- **Issue:** closes #73

## Change

Adds the practitioner seam from the exact #71 open-plan attachment to the existing #34 Brink/Closure contract, stopping before #16 Mana commitment.

```text
#71 exact open CrossingPlan
  -> non-authorizing construction receipt
  -> verify Situation + open-plan attachment
  -> independent Environment effect/Mana probes
  -> verify attachment again after probes
  -> observe Brink
  -> close()
  -> ClosedPlan
  X  no Mana movement / Technique execution / CAST
```

New Work module: `cast/practitioner/brink_closure.py`.

Key properties:

- `OpenPlanAttachment` retains the #69 Situation evidence digest plus a domain-separated construction digest over the complete #71 open-plan material. This is local integrity only: it is not Closure, `plan_digest`, provenance, or authority.
- `EnvironmentBrinkProbe` names kind, Environment, observer, provenance, and read mechanism.
- Probe observer may not be the caster or selected Technique, and the probe must belong to a situated Environment.
- Missing/raising probes flow through #34 as `unobservable`, never zero.
- The open plan and Situation attachment are verified **before and after** the probes, so observation code cannot mutate the plan and then have that changed material sealed.
- `close()` remains the existing #34 implementation, but this work exposed and corrected a real nested-alias immutability defect in it: Closure now deep-snapshots the complete plan graph (and Brink finding) before computing `plan_digest`, so later mutation of the caller's open plan cannot rewrite `ClosedPlan` material.

## Metadata impact

- **Domains:** Cast practitioner + Environment observation boundary
- **Lifecycle crossing:** none; all new material remains Work
- **Audit impact:** `REPOSITORY_AUDIT.md` inventories the new module/test and records the Closure snapshot correction as part of the completed #34 Work contract

## Validation

`cast/tests/test_brink_closure_73.py` covers:

- end-to-end #67/#69/#71 path through independently observed Brink to ClosedPlan;
- exact zero effect/Mana deltas and observer/provenance evidence;
- missing and raising effect/Mana probes refuse as unobservable;
- nonzero Cast-attributable effect or committed-Mana delta refuses Closure;
- unrelated Environment activity does not block an attributable-zero Brink;
- caster/Technique self-observation is refused;
- pre-Closure mutation sweep over target, Situation digest, receipt, attenuated handle, Demand, authority material, obligation, evidence contract, residual bound, Technique, and declarative Mana;
- Situation mutation with recomputed digest still breaks the frozen attachment;
- a probe cannot mutate the plan during observation and then close it;
- two Subject Familiar projections close to identical plan identity;
- existing post-Closure `verify()` / `digest_matches()` catch later mutation;
- Closure leaves synthetic Mana and Technique state unchanged;
- static boundary check excludes Magic/Kernel/consequence/execution/CAST-sealing paths.

Evidence history:

- Initial Agent Spells CI run **31981197419** exposed two classes of failure: the expected audit inventory gap and a real #34 Closure immutability defect. `ClosedPlan.plan` aliased the caller's mutable open `CrossingPlan`, so mutating the open plan after Closure also mutated the supposedly frozen closed material. `digest_matches()` noticed the hash mismatch, but `verify()` lost the original value because both sides referenced the changed object.
- `close()` was repaired to deep-snapshot the full plan graph before computing the final digest.
- Agent Spells CI run **31981317045** then ran **386 tests** with every substantive test passing; the only remaining failure was the audit guard naming exactly the two new #73 paths.
- The audit was repaired without weakening its completeness guard and records the discovered Closure snapshot correction.
- **Final Agent Spells CI run 31981431938 passed all 386 tests on Ubuntu, Windows, and the symlink-disabled checkout** at `fdcde5c06cd20b54bf4f6c67c45eb889a3349423`.
- **Work Metadata run 31981431940 passed** on the same branch head.

## Residuals

- This PR does not commit/settle Mana, execute a Technique, classify consequence, evaluate post-execution observations, or create CAST.
- #16 begins immediately after successful Closure: sealed declarative Mana participation may become a real Claimed -> Committed transition exactly once before effectful execution.
- #35 remains post-execution observation; #38 remains full Kernel/milestone integration.
- No lifecycle promotion occurs.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>jonwiggins/xmloxide (aqua:jonwiggins/xmloxide)</summary>

### [`v0.5.0`](https://redirect.github.com/jonwiggins/xmloxide/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#050---2026-08-08)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jonwiggins/xmloxide/compare/v0.4.4...v0.5.0)

##### Changed

- **XPath attribute results are first-class attribute nodes** ([#​47](https://redirect.github.com/jonwiggins/xmloxide/issues/47)).
  Node-sets (`XPathValue::NodeSet`) now hold `XPathNode` entries — either a
  tree node or an attribute identified by owner element and index — instead
  of bare `NodeId`s. This fixes a family of wrong-answer bugs rooted in the
  old one-value-per-element override map: `//a/@​x != //a/@​y` comparisons no
  longer clobber each other's values, `@*` yields one node per attribute
  (previously only the first per element), `count((//a)[1]/@​href)` returns a
  number instead of a type error, `name()`/`local-name()`/`namespace-uri()`
  work on attribute nodes, `@attr/..` navigates to the owner element,
  predicates evaluate with the attribute as context node, and namespace
  declarations (`xmlns`, `xmlns:*`) are no longer visible as attributes per
  the XPath 1.0 data model. Mixed node-sets (`//a | //a/@​x`) sort in
  document order with attributes directly after their owner element.
  **Breaking:** code matching `XPathValue::NodeSet` must handle
  `XPathNode`; use `.anchor()` for the owning tree node or
  `.as_tree_node()` to filter attributes out. The single-match collapse
  (attribute paths returning `XPathValue::String`) is gone — convert with
  `string()` where a string is wanted. `xmllint --xpath` prints attribute
  results as `name="value"` lines, matching libxml2. The C API keeps
  `xmloxide_xpath_nodeset_item()` (returns the owner element id for
  attributes) and adds `xmloxide_xpath_nodeset_item_is_attribute()`,
  `..._attr_name()`, and `..._attr_value()`.
- **XPath step predicates apply per context node** per XPath 1.0 §2.4:
  `//a/b[1]` now selects the first `b` of *every* `a` (previously the first
  of the merged set), and `position()`/`last()` in step predicates are
  relative to each context node's own node-set, matching libxml2. The
  parenthesized form `(//a/b)[1]` keeps global-position semantics.
- **Schematron rules with attribute contexts** (`context="//@​id"`) now fire
  with the attribute itself as the context node — `.` is the attribute
  value and `<value-of select="."/>` reads it, per ISO Schematron.
  Previously such rules either never fired (single match) or misfired
  against the owner element.

##### Security

- **Fix exponential-time entity recursion check** ([#​42](https://redirect.github.com/jonwiggins/xmloxide/issues/42), thanks [@​hey-jj](https://redirect.github.com/hey-jj)). The
  WFC: No Recursion walks in the DTD validator re-visited entities once per
  path, so a 474-byte document with chained entity declarations took 8+
  seconds to parse and a 694-byte one about 22 hours. The walks (including
  parameter entities and ATTLIST-default validation) now memoize entities
  proven acyclic, making the check linear in the size of the DTD. Cycle
  detection is unaffected.
- **Bound element nesting across entity expansions.** Entity replacement text
  is parsed by nested sub-parsers, which now inherit the outer parser's
  nesting depth so total element depth stays bounded by
  `ParseOptions::max_depth` instead of `max_depth` per expansion level.

##### Fixed

- **General entity replacement text is parsed as content** per XML 1.0 §4.4
  ([#​43](https://redirect.github.com/jonwiggins/xmloxide/issues/43), thanks [@​hey-jj](https://redirect.github.com/hey-jj)). `EntityRef` nodes now carry their parsed expansion
  as children: character references in declarations are expanded when
  replacement text is built (§4.5), nested entity references are included,
  and markup-bearing entities produce real element children instead of
  escaped text — while serialization still emits `&name;`, keeping
  round-trips lossless. Replacement text must match the content production
  (§4.3.2); unbalanced or split tags are rejected. Entity expansion is
  subject to the expansion counter, a nesting-depth cap, and the 5x
  amplification guard, matching libxml2. DTD content-model validation sees
  through entity references (§4.4.3), so entity-supplied elements are
  validated too.
- **XPath `!=` uses its own existential semantics for node-sets** per XPath
  1.0 §3.4 ([#​44](https://redirect.github.com/jonwiggins/xmloxide/issues/44), thanks [@​hey-jj](https://redirect.github.com/hey-jj)). `!=` was evaluated as `not(=)`, inverting
  empty-node-set comparisons and breaking multi-node sets (both `=` and `!=`
  can hold at once). Node-set vs boolean keeps boolean-conversion semantics;
  scalar comparisons are unchanged. An absent attribute step now also yields
  an empty node-set (false under both `=` and `!=`) instead of an
  empty-string sentinel.
- **XPath filter-path continuations navigate instead of filtering** ([#​20](https://redirect.github.com/jonwiggins/xmloxide/issues/20),
  thanks [@​ancientcatz](https://redirect.github.com/ancientcatz)). `(//a)[1]/@​href` parsed to the same AST as
  `(//a)[@

💡 **What:** Replaced the sequential `await sendPushNotification(...)` loop with a chunked concurrent implementation using `Promise.all()` and a chunk size of 10.

🎯 **Why:** The previous implementation processed push notifications for overdue invoices entirely sequentially. The execution time scaled linearly with the number of users receiving notifications, creating a potential timeout/bottleneck as the userbase grows.

body:
## Why
Cloudflare's current AI REST API requires a `cf-aig-gateway-id` header for Workers AI requests. The merged adapter only sent the header when `ZUMI_CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY_ID` was explicitly configured, which could make an otherwise valid production connection fail.

## Fix
- default gateway ID to `default` when no explicit gateway is configured
- always send `cf-aig-gateway-id` on Workers AI calls
- preserve explicit custom gateway override
- add tests for both default and explicit gateway behavior

Cloudflare documents that `default` auto-creates the account gateway on first use, minimizing setup while retaining AI Gateway controls.

## Safety
No PHI posture changes. `baaOnFile` remains false and the existing Zumi governance/redaction/kill-switch boundary remains unchanged.

body: HK-020 only. One hole. Draft. Do not mark ready. Do not merge. ## Hole A run is the durable control record for one goal: objective, orchestrator id, status, workers, pending card, next wake, budget. `RunRecord` on main was missing orchestrator id, next wake, and budget. This slice persists those kernel-owned fields on the tenant computer so a restart still shows the same run. ## Exact `RunRecord` fields (for CoS) ``` runId: string tenantId: string goal: string // objective. Existing name stays. Do not rename. status: RunStatus orchestratorId: string // loaded orchestrator. Kernel sets. Field SHALL NOT. workers: string[] // booked worker ids. Empty or one today. nextWake: string // empty until HK-024. Persist only. No fire loop. budget: number // kernel-owned empty/zero (0). Not T0–T3. Field SHALL NOT. workerId?: string // kept as the 0-or-1 case workerType?: WorkerTypeId pendingCardId?: string // existing pending card pendingEffect?: PendingEffect pendingIntent?: "launch_worker" journeyId?: string recordId?: string talkingDidHeavyWork: false createdAt: string updatedAt: string ``` ## What this does - Kernel stamps `orchestratorId` from the loaded orchestrator on every persist. - `workers` is the booked set (0 before launch, 1 after a held coder). Existing `workerId` stays. - `nextWake` is persisted as empty. No fire loop, ticker, or adapter-set path. - `budget` is the kernel empty/zero (`KERNEL_RUN_BUDGET = 0`). Not a trust-ladder number. - Field-supplied `orchestratorId` or `budget` on a wake is `SURFACE_VIOLATION` (fail closed). author: gabrielgraciano
body:
O Nível 1 fechou nas vinte e cinco lições do primeiro par de livros, e o próprio `livros.md` dizia que o que vem depois — futuro, partículas de objeto, conjunções — pediria uma seção nova em vez de mais aulas naquela. É o que este PR faz, com os capítulos 1 a 5 do par seguinte.

## As cinco aulas

| Aula | Ponto | Exercícios |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `-(으)ㄹ 거예요` — o futuro | 25 |
| 2 | `-을 / -를` — a marca do objeto | 23 |
| 3 | `그리고, 그래서` — e, e então, por isso | 23 |
| 4 | `-하고, -(이)랑` — e, e com | 22 |
| 5 | `요일` — os dias da semana | 24 |

São **117 exercícios** em `dados/licoes2.json`, no mesmo esquema de `licoes.json` e corrigidos pela mesma `src/licoes.js` — três tópicos de explicação, três grupos com dono e um grupo solto de ditado por aula, cobrindo as catorze faixas de ditado do caderno. Nenhum tipo de bloco novo, nenhum tipo de exercício novo.

## O custo em código

Menor que o das Histórias, como `protocolo.md` previa: um cartão de atalho, uma tela de listagem, uma linha em `ir()`, mais um `fetch`, e `abrirAula()` sabendo voltar para uma terceira lista.

De quebra, `pintarNivel1()` virou `pintarNivel()` recebendo a coleção e onde pintar — o Nível 1 e o Nível 2 são a mesma tela com outro arquivo por trás, e um Nível 3 já não custa cópia.

## Vocabulário

Das 44 palavras apresentadas, **23 já estavam no banco** e foram reusadas; as **21 novas** entraram com `baralho: false`. O baralho continua com **114 cartões**.

`커피숍` ficou de fora de propósito: `카페` já existia e é a mesma coisa, então a aula reusa a entrada em vez de criar uma segunda para o mesmo lugar.

Como a numeração das aulas recomeça a cada nível, as palavras do Nível 2 levam um campo `nivel` e o dicionário do mapa as marca como `N2 · aula N`.

**A aula 5 é a que mais rende fora dela mesma:** as sete sílabas dos dias entram no índice sino-coreano e a família do 日 salta de três palavras para dez, de modo que 생일 passa a se ler como “dia do nascimento” sem que ninguém precise dizer. A família do 火 passa a juntar 화요일, 화성 e 화나다.

## Uma terceira lacuna do motor de pronúncia

Depois do `-(으)ㄹ` do futuro, o 제27항 tensifica a consoante seguinte — 갈 거예요 é [갈 꺼예요] — e `pronunciar()` não aplica. Não dá para consertar olhando só a cadeia de sílabas: o ㄹ de 갈 é terminação e tensifica, o ㄹ de 달 é radical e não (달과 é [달과]). É a mesma família das duas lacunas que `livros.md` já registra.

Por isso a aula 1 ensina o [꺼] **em prosa**, num bloco `destaque`, e não num bloco `som` — `som` chama o motor na hora de desenhar e mostraria a forma errada. Os blocos `som` do Nível 2 estão todos em palavras que o motor acerta (밥을, 옷을, 목요일, 금요일, 일요일), cada uma conferida contra ele antes de entrar.

## Verificação

Sem suíte commitada (Regra zero). O que rodou:

- **Invariantes de exercício** nas três seções: 2350 ids únicos, enunciado e explicação presentes, todo grupo alcançável, `conferir()` aceitando a certa e recusando as erradas, toda montagem solúvel e `completou()` sem disparar em prefixo. Zero problema. O checador foi rodado contra `licoes.json` e `dias.json` para conferir a si mesmo — os 671 exercícios de montar que já existiam continuam solúveis.
- **Integridade do banco**: ilustração faltando, confundível órfão, par órfão e sem reciprocidade, hanja sem verbete, `sino` com sílaba fora da palavra, dica que vaza a resposta — todos zero.
- **Distratores**: 0,00% de classe errada e zero repetição nos dois baralhos que o app alcança (114 cartões e 541 com os 25 dias promovidos).
- **Invariantes antigos**: `pronunciar('학교')` = 학꾜, `intervalo(21)` = 21.0000, `recuperabilidade(21, 21)` = 0.900.
- **Fluxo no navegador (Playwright)**: as cinco aulas abertas, tópicos e atalhos batendo com o JSON, “Praticar isto” trocando de aba e revelando o grupo certo, os 117 exercícios respondidos **lendo o gabarito do próprio JSON**, contador de cada aba em `n/n`, progresso sobrevivendo ao `reload`, zero erro de console. Um segundo trecho confere que o baralho continua em 114 depois de tudo respondido e que as famílias de morfemas mostram o efeito da aula 5.

Duas coisas que a bateria aponta e que **já eram assim antes desta leva**, registradas em `nivel2.md` para não serem confundidas com regressão: nove `confundiveis` cruzam classe gramatical entre palavras que só existem no dicionário, e o vocabulário das Histórias cita 좋다 e 맛있다, que no banco estão como 좋아요 e 맛있어요. Nenhuma das duas afeta baralho nenhum.

## Documentação

`nivel2.md` é o mapa da seção, no molde de `livros.md`. `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `livros.md` e `protocolo.md` apontam para ele — e o `protocolo.md` ganhou as armadilhas novas desta leva (o `[data-ir="hoje"]` que existe em toda tela, o morfema que não forma família sozinho, e o checador que não pode normalizar peça a peça).

Closes #248. AFK-built (sandcastle, containerized).

**Compound gate GREEN in-container** — ruff + format + `mypy --strict` + pytest, on ONE linux cell.

⛔ **The gate is necessary, NOT sufficient — it is not equivalent to CI.** CI additionally runs the other three test-matrix cells (including both windows cells), structural-bans, drift-check, release-gate, CodeQL and residue-check. Platform-sensitive defects (path separators, symlinks, line endings, file modes) are invisible to the gate by construction — a CRLF bug once passed this gate and merged before CI caught it. **Judge this PR on its CI run, not on the gate.**

⛔ **Before merging, confirm this PR reflects the branch.** A PR object can lag its own ref: at
S249 a fix was pushed, the branch tip moved server-side, and this PR kept showing the OLD head and
the OLD diff, fired no CI on the new commit, and reported `mergeable: null` — the merge then
consumed the stale precomputed head and put a defect on `main`. These two must agree:

```
gh api repos/MrBinnacle/skill-harness/pulls/<N> --jq .head.sha
gh api repos/MrBinnacle/skill-harness/git/ref/heads/agent/issue-248 --jq .object.sha
```

author: ossykelvin
body:
Three listening sessions produced **no results at all**, not even a discard entry. That is different from the previous failures: the recognizer emitted nothing, rather than emitting something the app rejected.

## Measured cause

| Step | Cost |
|---|---|
| PowerShell start, assembly load, Add-Type compile | ~1.2s, **once per process** |
| Acquire microphone | 25ms |
| Release microphone | 9ms |
| Re-acquire microphone | 25ms |

Spawning a process per press put a **~1.4s dead window at the front of every push-to-talk**, which is exactly when someone starts speaking. A short press recognised nothing because the engine was still starting up.

## The fix

One warm recognizer process, driven by stdin commands:

- `LISTEN` acquire the microphone and recognise
- `STOP` release the microphone and wait
- `QUIT` exit

A press is now live in about **25ms instead of 1400ms**.

The microphone is still genuinely released between presses via `SetInputToNull()`, so warm does not mean an open microphone. `main.cjs` disposes the process on `before-quit` so no `powershell.exe` is left behind.

Verified against the real script: READY at ~1s, LISTEN/STOP cycles accepted, recognition works while listening, and QUIT exits cleanly in 80ms.

## Tests changed deliberately

Two tests from #62 guarded a race between a stopping child and a starting one. That race is now structurally impossible, so they assert the stronger properties instead: repeated presses never spawn a second `powershell.exe`, and the microphone is released on every stop.

Writing the second one found a **real bug in this change**: a dead child's `exit` event arriving after a replacement existed cleared the live session's `listening` flag, so the next `stop()` silently did nothing. Shared state is now only mutated by the current child. That is precisely the hazard the original test existed to catch.

`npm run verify`: **315/315**.

author: kwpledger
body:
Docs only — `docs/BACKLOG.md` alone. Files the two things you called *"items 98 and 99."*

## Why a separate section rather than items 6 and 7

This file's premise is that the top numbered item is the next thing to do, so list length isn't a neutral cost — a longer list is the failure mode the file exists to prevent. Both entries below are real and worth keeping, and neither is load-bearing. A bin outside the numbering keeps the ordered list short while still writing them down.

The header now states the three-section structure (live work → Polish → Shipped) and says explicitly **never to offer a Polish entry as the next thing to do** — if the numbered items are all blocked, say so rather than reaching down into it. Without that, a session hunting for work will find these and surface them.

## The two entries

**Display tags and ingredients are not linked**, and never have been. You authored the tags by hand while editing the JSON, which is why `"Boneless, Skinless Chicken Breast"` carries a comma the ingredient name doesn't. The drift: an ingredient added through the editor gets no tag, a renamed one leaves its old tag standing.

Filed with the reasoning that *"link them"* isn't obviously the fix. `"Salmon"` reads better on a card than `"salmon fillet, raw"` — the hand-written tags being better copy is the whole reason two fields exist, so auto-deriving trades good copy for consistency. If it's ever picked up, **warn on drift** is probably the more interesting design than **derive**: you keep authoring the copy and only get told when a tag has gone stale.

**`searchName` has no production usage.** Zero ingredients carry one, including the two it was specifically built for — the quinoa and zucchini corrections went into the ingredient name, which turned out to be the right place because the seed's naming convention already puts USDA-friendly text there.

Recorded with the condition under which it should be **retired rather than defended**: the field is genuinely the right tool for one case — USDA wording that would be unacceptable in the grocery list, the meal detail modal, or the Cronometer export, the three places `name`/`raw` actually surface. If that case never arrives, the conclusion is that the seed's naming convention had already solved the problem.

## Checks

`npm run build` and `npm run lint` green — three pre-existing unused-eslint-disable warnings in `App.jsx` and `ingredientLibrary.js`, untouched. No source files changed.

author: msoliman1975
body:
## The report

> backfill still showing this error for greenFarm_Test, while I can see the
> imagery, thermal and weather in the farm level configs —
> *"4 blocks · 0 subscriptions · about 0 scenes … This farm has no active
> imagery subscriptions"*

**The backfill console was right.** Measured on prod for greenFarm_Test:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| active farm imagery subscriptions | **2** (`s2_l2a`, `landsat_c2_l2_st`) |
| `fetch_farm_aoi` | **false** on both |
| active **block** subscriptions | **0** |
| block ingestion jobs | **0** |
| farm ingestion jobs | **0** |
| `last_attempted_at` | **NULL** — never even tried |
| weather observations | 52 ✅ |

Weather is farm-shaped and farm rows are authoritative, so it works. Imagery
is not: `fetch_farm_aoi` false means *"this farm is fetched one block at a
time"*, and the block sweep is driven by `imagery_aoi_subscriptions` and by
nothing else. With no block rows, both paths decline — the farm sweep because
the flag is off, the block sweep because there is nothing to sweep.

So the subscription was active, listed, and reported as **per block** on the
Farm tab, while fetching nothing since the day it was created. Every surface
agreed it was fine except the one the user was looking at.

## The fix

Resolve the path at the write, where the farm's shape is known:

- **blocks already subscribed** → nothing moves. This is the case that must
  not become a silent cutover: flipping a farm with a running block sweep onto
  the farm path puts a ~0.7% step in every block's series.
- **no blocks, no per-block history, boundary fits in one request** → take the
  whole-farm path. Nothing is reading a series that a stitched surface would
  step, and it is the direction the platform is moving. *This is
  greenFarm_Test, and it is what any new farm looks like.*
- **otherwise** → subscribe the blocks, which is what the row said all along.
  Covers a farm too large to fetch whole (>2500 px/side) and one whose
  subscriptions were revoked but whose history is still on screen.

Either way the invariant holds: **a farm imagery subscription always has a path
that fetches.** No migration — this is a decision at write time, not stored
state.

## Verification

Four integration tests, one per branch above, driving the real `POST
/farms/{id}/imagery/subscriptions` exactly as the Farm tab does (no flag in the
body):

- new farm → `fetch_farm_aoi: true`, blocks untouched
- blocks already subscribed → `false`, no duplicates, no removals
- history but revoked subscriptions → `false` + blocks resubscribed
- 48 km farm → `false` + blocks resubscribed, and the read reports
  `farm_aoi_fetchable: false` so the UI can say why

`backend/tests/{integration/imagery,integration/backfill,unit/imagery}` —
**195 passed, 4 skipped**. ruff, black and mypy clean.

## Note on existing data

This fixes the write path. greenFarm_Test's two rows were written before it and
stay inert until they are re-saved — re-subscribing the product from the Farm
tab now resolves them correctly.

author: deruelle
body:
The failure that kills the inngest bootstrap also kills the channel that would explain it. Vector — the host's journald → Better Stack shipper — is installed **by** the bootstrap, so a non-zero exit leaves the failing unit's stderr in journald and nowhere else, readable only over SSH, which `hr-no-ssh-fallback-in-runbooks` forbids.

## Measured, not hypothetical

The 2026-08-16 `inngest-host-replace` that delivered #7516 is the worked example. The zot arm did its job — `zot-login-ok` → `pre-zot-pull` → `inngest_zot` (*"bootstrap image served by zot ep=10.0.1.30:5000"*) → `oci-pull-rc-0`, with `ghcr-login-FAILED` confirming zot was the **only** path that could have supplied the image. Then:

```
[inngest-bootstrap] durable Redis ready
[inngest-bootstrap] inngest-server ExecStart: durable backend (env-delivered URIs; …)
Job for inngest-server.service failed because the control process exited with error code.
See "systemctl status inngest-server.service" and "journalctl -xeu inngest-server.service" for details.
```

That is the entire diagnostic: a pointer, not the content. Better Stack held **zero** journald rows for `soleur-inngest` — only phone-home rows, which are direct-curl and independent of Vector.

The leading hypothesis was *prod Postgres unreachable* — the very reason the diagnostic-boot branch exists. It is **false**, and could only be falsified by probing Supabase from elsewhere: `aws-0-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432` resolves, accepts TCP, and authenticates (`PostgreSQL 17.6`, session-mode pooler, `sslmode=require`). So a whole replace cycle bought no answer, and the real cause is still unknown.

## What changes

On non-zero `boot_rc`, before `exit`, the failure path phones home a `bootstrap-failure-journal` marker carrying:

- `systemctl --failed` — **captured separately and first**, because it names *which* unit broke. A future `inngest-redis.service` regression would otherwise land in a block that only ever quotes `inngest-server` and read as "no journal": the same silence in a new place.
- 30 lines of `journalctl -xu inngest-server.service`, scrubbed through `inngest-redact.sh` and bounded.

Both are capped (300 + 1200 chars). The journal carries env-delivered Postgres/Redis URIs and signing keys on a failed `ExecStart`, and this lands in a source the whole team reads, so it goes through the same scrubber the existing `boot_tail` already trusts.

## Guard Row 7 — and why ordering is the load-bearing half

Seven assertions with an exact anti-vacuity floor. Three check presence; **two check ordering**, and those are the ones that matter: a capture emitted after `exit "$boot_rc"` is dead code that every presence-only assertion would still certify green. That is precisely the vacuity class #7516 shipped (a 39-assertion guard green with its property inverted by one character).

Mutation-proven rather than asserted — each mutant **KILLED**, with attribution scoped to `^  FAIL` lines so a description echoed on PASS cannot fake a kill:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| emit moved after `exit "$boot_rc"` | KILLED |
| redaction pipe removed | KILLED |
| output bounds removed | KILLED |

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `cloud-init-inngest-bootstrap.test.sh` | **129/129** (was 121, +8 for Row 7) |
| Zot mutation battery / boot emitter | PASS / PASS |
| `bash -n` + `dash -n` on the runcmd block | clean (`shellify()` concatenates into one `/bin/sh`) |
| Template render + `cloud-init schema` | **8/8** |
| `terraform fmt -check -recursive` | clean |

## User-Brand Impact

- **If this lands broken, the user experiences:** nothing at merge — this arm is inert until an `inngest-host-replace` dispatch. The realistic failure is a *noisier* failure marker, not a changed boot outcome: the capture runs only on a path that was already fatal, and is wrapped in `set +e` so it cannot itself convert a diagnosable failure into a hang.
- **If this leaks, the user's data is exposed via:** the shipped journal excerpt. That is the actual risk this diff adds, which is why the capture is scrubbed through `inngest-redact.sh` and bounded, and why the guard pins both properties.
- **Brand-survival threshold:** `none` — an observability capture on an already-fatal boot path, on a host that serves no user traffic.

*Scope-out override:* `threshold: none, reason: the diff touches only the failure branch of a host bootstrap that is already exiting non-zero, never an app-serving surface.*

## Delivery

**Inert at merge.** `hcloud_server.inngest` is in no `-target` on the per-merge apply path. It reaches the host on the next `apply_target=inngest-host-replace` — which is also when it earns its keep, by making that boot's failure self-describing.

Ref #7228 · Ref #7462 — both stay OPEN, both enrolled in the follow-through sweeper via `inngest-zot-boot-7462.sh`, which currently reports `bootstrap_incomplete`.

## Changelog

### Fixed
- A failed inngest bootstrap now ships the failing unit's journal and the set of failed units off-box, so the cause is diagnosable without SSH on a host whose log shipper the failure itself prevents installing.

author: theagenticguy
body:
## What

`embedMissing` was all-or-nothing: one embed failure discarded every vector the pass had already paid Bedrock for. Under a sustained token throttle a large corpus could never complete — measured on a 4,219-chunk import (2026-08-16) where five consecutive `rebuild --embed` passes each wrote zero rows.

## How

The pass now embeds and persists in slices of `EMBED_PERSIST_SLICE` (960 texts, ten of `@memhtml/llm`'s 96-text wire batches). A slice that lands is progress the next invocation never re-pays: vectors key on chunk_id (content hash), so the re-run's pending scan finds only the remainder. A slice that fails still stops the pass — the throttle that killed it would kill the next slice too — and the log line now reports how many chunks were written and that a re-run continues from there.

`embedPersistEvery` is injectable on `IndexerDeps` so the test can force multiple slices over the 20-chunk fixture corpus; production callers leave it alone.

## Verification

- New test: an embedder that succeeds once then throttles must leave the first slice persisted (8 rows), and a healthy re-run must finish exactly the remainder (12) with no re-embedding.
- Mutation-verified: with the sliced loop reverted, the new test fails.
- `mise run check` green, 58/58.

author: sellybros711
body:
## The problem, measured

A first-time visitor is shown a button before they are shown a reason. On a 390×844 screen:

| position | what's there |
|---|---|
| 414px | **"Draft a setlist"** |
| 694px | Leaderboard and Your shows |
| 780px | the HOW IT WORKS heading |
| 809px | step 1 — and all five steps end below the fold |

The primary button lands 400 pixels above the first word of explanation, and the two buttons under it are never explained at all. Somebody presses Draft not knowing what a draft is, what they're scored on, or that "Your shows" is where their own concert history lives.

Moving the rules above the button fixes the first visit and taxes every visit after it. So the rules come to the player instead.

## What this adds

A walkthrough that runs itself once and points a large arrow at each thing in turn. Four steps, in the order somebody actually needs them:

1. **The goal** — what the game is, and the one thing about the scoring that isn't guessable: you're measured against the best show available from the exact nights you were dealt.
2. **Start here** — an arrow at the Draft button, plus how a turn works and the three clock budgets.
3. **The leaderboard** — both ranking axes and why the percentage one is the fairer fight.
4. **Your shows** — the attendance tracker, and that it stays on the device.

"Picking at random gets you about three quarters of it" is measured, not asserted: six full games played by choosing a random legal song every round scored **71, 71, 76, 78, 88 and 93 percent** of that ceiling.

It reopens from a button under the rules, which is the difference between a manual and a popup, and the last step deals a show rather than just closing.

## Three things the measurements decided

- **Centring the target and then asking which side fitted could never have worked.** A 350px panel plus the arrow and its gaps needs 442px; a centred target on an 844px screen leaves 393 above and 392 below. The panel got clamped to the top with the arrow drawn across its bottom 33 pixels. Room is now made *before* a side is chosen.
- **Everything measures from the ring, not the target.** The ring is the target plus its 6px halo, and leaving the halo out put the arrow's tip on the ring's own border.
- **At 320px the nav row wants 315px of a 260px content width**, so it wraps and the primary button drops to its own line.

## The spotlit element is pressable

The overlay covers the page, so a press on the very button the arrow points at reaches the overlay and nothing else — "press this one first" would have stepped the walkthrough forward instead of dealing a show. A dim can't pass clicks through selectively, so the target's rect is hit tested and the press forwarded.

## Verification

- `check_data.mjs` — all passed, including a new `the walkthrough` section; all 8 new guards mutation-tested
- `verify-scoring.mjs` — 286 passed, 0 failed
- `sync_counts.mjs --check` — counts current
- 11 behaviours tested end to end: opens once, stays closed, reopens, Escape closes, last step drafts, a new visitor still gets it
- layout measured at 320 / 360 / 390 / 430 / 768 — nothing off screen, nothing overflowing
- full 16-pick playthrough still reaches the scorecard with no repeats

author: ramitha-silva
body:
## The bug

Tapping **Get Started** on the passenger app's language screen (SCR-PA-002) does nothing — it never reaches Enter Mobile Number (SCR-PA-003). The driver app's **Continue** on SCR-DA-002 has the same defect.

## Why

Both screens called `Activity.recreate()` *instead of* navigating, on the premise — written into the comment on each — that the rebuild re-enters the graph at the splash, which would then route onward:

```kotlin
if (model.finish()) {
    context.findActivity()?.recreate() ?: onContinue()   // onContinue never runs
} else {
    onContinue()
}
```

It does not re-enter at the splash. Both shells take the default `rememberNavController()`, which is a `rememberSaveable` over `NavControllerSaver` — the back stack is **saved and restored** across the rebuild, so the app comes back to whatever was on top rather than to `startDestination`. That was the language screen itself.

On a first run there is no stored language, so `finish()` / `confirm()` always reports a change and the `recreate()` branch is always the one taken. The tap rebuilt the screen and went nowhere.

The passenger's case does not recover on a second tap either: `recreate()` retains view models the way a configuration change does, so the same `OnboardingViewModel` returns still holding `renderingLanguage = null` and still answering "rebuild".

## The fix

Navigate first, rebuild second. Login is then what sits in the saved state that gets restored, and it is still drawn in the chosen language because `attachBaseContext` re-inflates resources on the way back.

```kotlin
val rebuild = model.finish()
onContinue()
if (rebuild) context.findActivity()?.recreate()
```

| App | File | Screen |
|---|---|---|
| Passenger | `onboarding/OnboardingScreen.kt` | SCR-PA-002 → SCR-PA-003 |
| Driver | `onboarding/LanguageCityScreen.kt` | SCR-DA-002 → Login |

**Deliberately untouched:** `SettingsScreen` and `DriverProfileScreen` also call `recreate()`, but they *stay* on their own screen — back-stack restoration is exactly what they want.

## Verification

- `:apps:passenger-android:testDebugUnitTest` — green
- `:apps:driver-android:testDebugUnitTest` — green
- `:apps:passenger-android:assembleDebug :apps:driver-android:assembleDebug` — green

## What this PR does not include

- **No regression test.** The defect is in the composable's click lambda, out of reach of the JVM view-model tests (`OnboardingViewModelTest` asserts only what `finish()` *returns*, which was always correct). Catching it needs a Compose UI test driving the tap and asserting the route, and neither module has an `androidTest` source set for these screens.
- **Not verified on a device.** Confirmed by reading the navigation-compose save/restore path, not by running either app.

author: debugmcpdev
body:
## Summary

Implements #343 — the residual gap from #337: when the server is SIGKILLed or hard-crashes while a proxy worker is also wedged (so the worker's own safety nets — IPC-disconnect self-shutdown, heartbeat failure, the ppid check — never ran), nothing reaped the orphaned proxy chain. Mirrors the JVM orphan reaper (`src/utils/jvm-orphan-reaper.ts`) structurally and in its test seams.

### How it works

- **Tag at spawn** — `ProxyProcessLauncherImpl.launchProxy` appends `--mcp-owner-pid=<server pid>` and `--mcp-session-id=<uuid>` after the script path, so node passes them through as inert script argv (`proxy-bootstrap.js` reads no argv; verified live that debugging is unaffected).
- **Scan at startup** — new `src/utils/proxy-orphan-reaper.ts` lists processes (Linux `/proc` cmdline scan, darwin `ps`, win32 `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`), identifying workers **two-factor**: a `proxy-bootstrap` cmdline token AND a valid owner marker. Unmarked node processes, pre-upgrade workers, and malformed tags are never touched; workers whose owner is alive (concurrent server) or matches selfPid (PID-recycle defense) are skipped.
- **Kill with the #339 cascade in mind** — POSIX: SIGTERM first so the worker's own shutdown runs the graceful DAP disconnect + adapter group/tree kill, then a bounded 3s poll before SIGKILL escalation (the cascade takes ~2s worst case; escalating earlier would re-orphan the adapter chain). win32: `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` sweeps the tree directly — Node's cross-process `SIGTERM` on Windows is TerminateProcess and can never run the worker's JS handler.
- **Wiring** — runs in `main()` concurrently with the JVM reaper via `Promise.allSettled` so the two worst-case 5s listing timeouts don't stack; single entry point covers stdio/http/sse.

In Kubernetes shared-PID-namespace sidecars (#332), a fresh debug sidecar now automatically reaps the chain a hard-killed predecessor left behind — the manual `kill` step from the #337 incident, automated.

### Known limitation (in issue scope)

A worker that was itself already SIGKILLed leaves untagged adapter descendants the reaper cannot find (adapters are arbitrary runtimes); Java debuggees are covered separately by the JVM orphan reaper.

## Testing

- `tests/unit/utils/proxy-orphan-reaper.test.ts` — behavior via injected `lister`/`isAlive`/`killer` seams (8 cases incl. concurrent-kill input-order partitioning)
- `tests/unit/utils/proxy-orphan-reaper-internals.test.ts` — platform listers via module mocks, `parseProxyArgs` null-cases, SIGTERM→poll→SIGKILL escalation matrix, exact `taskkill` args + exit-code handling
- `launchProxy` argv assertions added to `tests/unit/implementations/process-launcher-impl.test.ts` (env-var owner + `process.pid` fallback)
- New module ~95% line coverage (uncovered lines are the platform-dispatch switches, same as the JVM reaper)
- Full gates: lint clean, unit 3477 passed, integration 23 passed

## Manual verification (Windows)

1. Live session through the dev proxy: worker cmdline shows `--trace-uncaught --trace-exit ...proxy-bootstrap.js --mcp-owner-pid=17516 --mcp-session-id=<real session uuid>` with owner = server PID; stopOnEntry pause/close work normally.
2. Fabricated orphan (real `proxy-bootstrap.js` process tagged with a dead owner PID, confirmed alive 5s pre-start): killed within 10s of `node dist/index.js http` startup, with `[proxy-reaper] Killed orphan proxy worker pid=... owner_pid=... session=smoke-343b` and `[startup] Reaped 1 orphan proxy worker(s) from prior runs` in the server log.

Closes #343

author: antoinetoussaint-byte
body:
Closes #297.

## Summary

- Issue #297 is a **cross-repo tracker**: every one of its four tasks needs a caller that does not exist in `core` — the CLI solution command group (in the `codefly` binary repo) and the host executor. I confirmed nothing in `core` drives the lifecycle through `solution.Client` or any ceiling; only the definitions and the interceptor install in `agents/manager/loader.go` exist. So there is **no substantive code deliverable in `core`** for these tasks, and none is fabricated here.
- The load-bearing assumptions the tracker worries about are already regression-guarded by tests (`TestSolutionRPCMethodPolicyIsMachineEnforceable` pins `Render` = `REGISTRY_READ`/`LOCAL_WRITE`; `TestOperationCeilingsAdmitExactlyTheirRPCs` pins the `Inspect < Scaffold < Render < Publish` cut). What was *not* recorded anywhere durable is the reasoning that these are provisional — it lived only in the transient #295 → #296 → #297 trackers, which is exactly what the tracker feared losing.
- This gives that reasoning a durable home next to the enforcement code, and sharpens one doc comment that over-stated the guarantee: the `Ceiling` doc claimed the constructors give the ceiling "a provenance," but that is only **intent** provenance (which operation a caller named). The gate enforces caller-asserted intent, not an authority-derived grant — a real trust-boundary caveat a reader of `EnforcingClientInterceptor` should not miss.

## What is *not* done here (remains open, cross-repo)

Per the issue's own premise, all four tasks "only become answerable once a real caller exists," and that caller is not in `core`:

- **Wire the first host caller** — the CLI solution command group lives in the `codefly` binary repo.
- **Validate the ceiling vocabulary** / **Confirm the Render network assumption** — both need the real host operations and the host executor implementation.
- **Give the ceiling a real provenance** — needs the consumer to shape it at a trusted chokepoint.

Closing #297 discharges its role as a *core-side* placeholder (the deferred design context now lives in the code); the actual work moves to the repos where it can be done. If the team would rather keep #297 open until the cross-repo caller lands, drop the `Closes #297.` line on merge.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./solution/...`
- [x] `go vet ./solution/...`
- [x] `go test ./solution/...` (documentation-only change; behavior and existing guard tests unchanged)

author: dave356w
body:
Follow-up to #8. Checks the outline against the DWM3001C **module** datasheet (Rev F, Oct 2025) — the document identified in #8 as the one needed to close the open accelerometer question.

Documentation only. No source changes.

## Open question resolved

**The accelerometer is present**: an ST LIS2DH12TR on the nRF52833's I²C bus (module pins 14/15, documented as serving both). No added hardware is needed for the Phase 1 gate, and the board selection stands unchanged.

Qorvo's stated rationale is worth noting — accelerometer-gated ranging to extend battery life is the vendor's intended usage pattern, and it is exactly the architecture Section 6 treats as mandatory.

**But it is not a BMA456.** The LIS2DH12 is a lower-specification part than the sensor currently in `falcon_srcs`, and the existing algorithm discriminates at `MOVING_ACC_THRESHOLD` of 0.05 m/s² (~5 mg). Phase 1 compares ranging against the accelerometer approach *on the same runs*; if the accelerometer arm runs on a noisier sensor than the product would use, the comparison is biased toward ranging and the gate could pass for the wrong reason. Documented with two options: keep a BMA456 on the exposed I²C bus, or characterise and account for the difference.

## Landmine found

The kit part number is **DWM3001CDKE1.0** — an *Engineering* Development Kit — and the datasheet warns for that exact part number:

> *"do not use the Channel 5 Antenna Delay in OTP — use default value 16390."*

This is on the critical path, because Section 8 selects Channel 5 for hoistway propagation. The failure mode is the dangerous kind: a wrong antenna delay is a **constant bias**, so by Section 4's own reasoning it is invisible in the rate data — Δrange and closing-rate results look healthy — while every absolute range and every time-to-contact figure is silently offset.

## Vendor corroborates the top Phase 1 risk

The datasheet has a section titled *"Note on Ranging Performance in Harsh Multipath Environments"*. The antenna is cross-polarised, which genuinely helps hold link budget under arbitrary mounting orientation — but Qorvo warns the same diversity *"can lead to variation in ranging accuracy as tags move in harsh multipath environments, such as where there are many reflections in confined indoor spaces, e.g. narrow corridors."*

A hoistway is a narrower, more reflective, fully metal-lined version of that example. The multipath entry in the risk register is now marked vendor-corroborated, and the stated mitigation (keep the module ≥1 cm from the carrier PCB edge) is recorded for Phase 4.

## Correction

The SS-TWR error figure was pessimistic by roughly an order of magnitude. The module crystal is **factory trimmed to under 2 ppm**, so a realistic module-to-module offset gives ~0.6 m uncorrected, not the 3 m implied by a 20 ppm worst case. The conclusion — use CFO correction, prefer single-sided — is unchanged.

## New constraints captured

- **Antenna keep-out**: 10 mm clear of metal either side, no copper pour, and explicitly no battery beneath the antenna. In direct tension with magnet-mounting to a steel counterweight; flagged as a named Phase 4 enclosure constraint. It also pulls against the ≥1 cm PCB-edge guidance above, so the two must be resolved together.
- **VDD max is 3.6 V**, while a fresh Li-SOCl₂ cell sits near 3.67 V open-circuit — over the limit before any load. Cannot be connected directly.
- **Channel 5 now wins on power too**: 18 mA idle against Channel 9's 32 mA.
- Measured per-state currents (SLEEP 850 nA through TX/RX 40 mA) added for the Phase 2 budget, which should be recomputed against them.

body:
### Purpose
This pull request introduces a new GitHub Actions workflow to automate the forward-porting of merged pull requests from the `1.0.x` patch branch to the `main` branch. The workflow cherry-picks the commits from the original PR onto a new branch off `main`, preserves commit history, creates a new PR, and assigns relevant users. If conflicts occur during cherry-picking, the workflow opens the PR as a draft for manual resolution.

### Approach

**Forward-port automation:**
* Adds `.github/workflows/forward-port-pr.yml`, a workflow that triggers on merged PRs to the `1.0.x` branch and cherry-picks their commits onto `main`, creating a new PR with preserved commit history. If conflicts arise, the PR is opened as a draft with conflict markers committed.

**User assignment and notifications:**
* Collects the original PR author and all approvers, assigns them to the new forward-port PR, and @mentions them in a comment. If there are merge conflicts, the comment includes a warning and instructions for resolution.

**Workflow configuration and automation details:**
* Configures Git user, fetches necessary refs, and uses the GitHub CLI and API to automate cherry-picking, PR creation, and user assignment, ensuring a smooth and auditable forward-porting process.

author: jlroper
body:
## Summary

Continues [plan/2026-08-16-phase-3-parallel-dev-plan.md](plan/2026-08-16-phase-3-parallel-dev-plan.md)'s Track 3.A Week 3+ port order (follow-up to #86/#87). Ports seven more actions onto the `POST /games/:name/commands` bus:

- **TradeResources**, **ResolveBattle** — had dedicated routes (`/trade`, `/resolve-battle`); those routes are now deleted.
- **RecruitHero**, **UpgradeTownHall**, **SetAutoTrade**, **ReorderStack**, **CaptureSettlement** — had **no server round-trip at all** before this. Each ran exclusively client-side via `src/state/turnController.ts`, with only a fire-and-forget audit-log call reaching the server.

**Deferred** (explicitly out of scope, per the plan doc's own status note now added):
- `UpgradeSettlement` — needs `GameMap`+RNG wiring into `CommandDeps` that no shipped command needed yet.
- `StartCharter`/`AdvanceCharter` — blocked on the pre-existing `activeCharters` schema gap (no DB column; Phase 3 explicitly rules out schema changes).
- `BuildStructure` — blocked on a missing `@heroes/engine` validate+apply function (Stage 6 prerequisite, not Phase 3 work).
- Lobby claim/start — low priority, session/social layer, not game-rules.

## Validation gaps closed (per command)

| Command | Gap closed |
|---|---|
| `TradeResources` | `tradeResources()` only checks `from.ownerId === to.ownerId`, never against the acting player — closed with an explicit ownership check |
| `ResolveBattle` | No server-side adjacency check existed anywhere (client's `detectAdjacentEnemy()` chose the pairing and was trusted); now re-derived and verified server-side. Also fixes the long-standing `obstacleSeed` replay gap — persisted in the `BattleResolved` event now, sourced from `ctx.rng()` instead of `Date.now()` |
| `RecruitHero` | No separate hole — `recruitHero()` already checks settlement ownership itself |
| `UpgradeTownHall` / `SetAutoTrade` | Neither engine function checks settlement ownership |
| `ReorderStack` | **No existing code anywhere** (client or engine) checked hero ownership |
| `CaptureSettlement` | **Largest gap found**: `captureSettlement()` never compares hero position to settlement position at all — that guarantee only ever existed because the client's caller pre-filtered to the hero's own tile |

## Other changes

- `createLiveCommandDeps()` is now async — it queries `unit_types` to populate `ctx.catalog.unitTypes` (previously always an empty placeholder; `ResolveBattle` is the first real consumer). `server/http/routes/commands.ts` lazily awaits and memoizes it on first request.
- Six new fire-and-forget client hooks (`TurnControllerHooks`), wired the same way `onAiMove` already informs the server of AI moves — local reducer runs first (no UX change), hook call afterward persists it server-side. Closes a real gap: these six actions previously had zero server round-trip, so doing one and then ending your turn would have the next `mergeFromEndTurn` silently revert it.
- Docs updated: `docs/module-documentation-and-relationships.md`, `TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATIONS.MD`, the plan doc's status note, plus stale `/resolve-battle` route references corrected in `docs/army.md`, `docs/heroes.md`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/battle-view-architecture.md`, `docs/CombatResolutionEngine-TechnicalDesign.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm run lint:deps`
- [x] `npm run test:all` — smoke/multiplayer/cityview green; `test:unit` 23/23 (14 new tests: happy path + the specific gap closed, per command)
- [x] **Live verification beyond the mocked suite** (the two things no existing test touches against a real DB): ran `createLiveCommandDeps()` directly against the dev Postgres container (12 seeded unit types load correctly), and round-tripped `TradeResources`, `SetAutoTrade`, `RecruitHero`, `UpgradeTownHall`, `ReorderStack`, and `CaptureSettlement` through a live server + real game, confirming each persisted correctly via a follow-up `GET`.

## Note for reviewer

While auditing the client call sites for this port, found (but did **not** fix, out of scope) a pre-existing gap: human-initiated `MoveHero`/`TransferGold` — unlike AI moves and `EndTurn` — still have **no server round-trip at all** today. `io/api.ts`'s `transferGold()`/`spendMovement()` exist and work, but nothing in `turnController.ts`'s `requestMove()`/`transferGold()` methods calls them for human-initiated actions (only the AI-move path does). Flagging for a follow-up.

author: augusto-romero-arango
body:
## Resumen

Pipeline mefisto-tooling completado:
- Writer: implementacion de la tarea
- Reviewer: revision de calidad

## Decisiones del pipeline

<details>
<summary>Writer -- 5m 7s</summary>

# Stage 1 (writer) — Issue #664

## Que se hizo

Se extendio `.claude/scripts/mefisto-metrics-report.sh` (reporte interno de
metricas del pipeline `mefisto-tooling`) para segmentar por `harness_version`,
portando el mismo shape que el reporte publicado (`scripts/metrics-report.sh`,
issue #669, ya mergeado):

- **`by_version`** (CA-1): nuevo `def version_summary`/`def version_sort_key`
  en el jq de `compute_metrics_report_json`, mas la agrupacion de `$entries`
  por `_version` (con `(sin version)` para el historial previo a #668/lineas
  sin el campo). Agrega los mismos agregados que el resto del reporte
  (n_total/n_instrumented, wall medio de las instrumentadas, turnos medios,
  %API, costo medio), ordenados por semver numerico (no lexicografico).
- **`harness_sha` per-run** (CA-2): se agrego `def run_cost_usd` (faltaba en
  el interno, necesario para `version_summary`) y el campo `harness_sha` en
  cada entrada de `$per_run` (null si la linea no lo trae) — nunca es eje de
  agrupacion.
- **Render** (CA-3): nueva funcion `render_by_version` (seccion "POR VERSION
  DE HARNESS") llamada en `main()` despues de `render_comparison` y antes de
  `render_legacy`; la tabla "Por corrida" de `render_wallclock` suma una
  columna "SHA" al final, sin tocar las columnas existentes.

## Tests (CA-4)

Se agrego el bloque `[L]` en `.claude/scripts/tests/test-metrics-report.sh`:
fixture con 4 corridas — con ambos campos, solo `harness_version`, solo
`harness_sha`, y sin ninguno — verificado contra `compute_metrics_report_json`
(agrupacion por version, columna `harness_sha` en `per_run`) y end-to-end
(seccion renderizada y columna SHA en "Por corrida", incluyendo el caso "sin
sha" para descartar corrimiento de columnas). Total: 64 pass / 0 fail en la
suite completa del archivo. Se corrieron ademas todas las demas suites de
`.claude/scripts/tests/` y `scripts/tests/` — sin fallos.

## Changelog

`changelog.d/664.added.md` (categoria `added`).

## Notas

- No hubo bloqueos de scope: ambos archivos modificados (`.claude/scripts/mefisto-metrics-report.sh`,
  `.claude/scripts/tests/test-metrics-report.sh`) y el nuevo `changelog.d/664.added.md`
  ya estaban en el listado de escritura permitido.
- No se toco el lado publicado (`scripts/metrics-report.sh`): ya tenia
  `by_version` desde el issue #669, sin `harness_sha` por-corrida (el issue
  #664 es exclusivamente interno, MEF-ADR-0019).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reviewer -- 5m 5s</summary>

# Stage 2 — Reviewer — issue #664

Segmentar `mefisto-metrics-report.sh` por `harness_version` con `harness_sha`
como detalle per-run.

## Veredicto

**Aprobado con una correccion aplicada.** La implementacion del writer cumple
los 4 criterios de aceptacion y porta fielmente el shape de la version
publicada; el unico defecto encontrado fue de trazabilidad (numeros de PR
citados como si fueran numeros de issue), corregido en este stage.

## Verificacion de los criterios de aceptacion

- **CA-1 (dimension `by_version`)**: cumplido. `$entries | group_by(._version)`
  con `version_summary` produce `n_total`/`n_instrumented`/`wall_mean_instr_s`/
  `pct_api`/`turns_mean`/`cost_usd_mean` por version, y `_version` cae a
  `"(sin version)"` cuando `harness_version` no es string (ausente o `null`
  JSON — que es exactamente lo que el pipeline escribe cuando el helper
  degrada, verificado contra `HARNESS_VERSION_JSON` en
  `mefisto-tooling-pipeline.sh:25-27`, asi que el guard `type == "string"`
  cubre el caso real). El shape coincide campo por campo con
  `scripts/metrics-report.sh` (issue #663), incluido `version_sort_key` con
  orden semver numerico.
- **CA-2 (`harness_sha` no es eje de agrupacion)**: cumplido. Aparece solo como
  campo de `wallclock.per_run[]`, con `null` cuando la linea no lo trae. No hay
  ningun `group_by` sobre el.
- **CA-3 (render)**: cumplido. `render_by_version` se invoca entre
  `render_comparison` y `render_legacy`, **el mismo orden que el reporte
  publicado** (`scripts/metrics-report.sh:867-869`). La columna SHA se suma al
  final de "Por corrida" via `JQ_ROW` (no `@tsv` crudo), asi que respeta la
  invariante anti-corrimiento de columnas del archivo. Ninguna otra seccion
  cambia: lo confirman las 64 aserciones de la suite, incluidos los bloques
  [I]/[K] que verifican alineacion de filas.
- **CA-4 (fixture con mezcla)**: cumplido y exhaustivo — 900 (ambos campos),
  910 (solo version), 920 (solo sha), 930 (ninguno). Cubre las cuatro
  combinaciones, no solo las tres que pedia el CA.

## Correccion aplicada

**Referencias a PRs citadas como issues.** El writer atribuia el estampado de
los campos a "#668" y el porte publicado a "#669". Verificado con `gh`: ambos
son **numeros de PR**; los issues correspondientes son **#662** (estampado
interno) y **#663** (porte publicado). El fragmento de changelog incluso los
etiquetaba literalmente `(issue #668)` / `(issue #669)`, lo cual es falso.

Importa porque toda la vecindad cita issues, no PRs (`#426`, `#427`, `#660`,
`issue #662`, `issue #664`), y porque el fragmento de changelog termina en
`CHANGELOG.md` publicado: dejaria una referencia incorrecta permanente.

Corregido `#668 -> #662` y `#669 -> #663` en:

- `.claude/scripts/mefisto-metrics-report.sh` (5 + 3 ocurrencias: cabecera del
  archivo, comentario de `version_summary`, de `_version`, de `harness_sha` y
  de `render_by_version`)
- `.claude/scripts/tests/test-metrics-report.sh` (comentario del fixture [L] y
  el `title` de la linea 930 del fixture)
- `changelog.d/664.added.md` (las dos etiquetas `issue #66x`)

## Revisado y dejado como estaba

- **Densidad de comentarios**: MEF-ADR-0044 seccion 5 deja **explicitamente
  fuera de alcance** el "Markdown/bash del propio plugin", que se rige por las
  convenciones del repo. La densidad del writer es la del archivo que edita y
  la del homologo publicado — no se poda.
- **`(sin version)` vs cadena vacia**: una linea con `harness_version: ""`
  agruparia bajo `""` y se renderizaria `-` en vez de `(sin version)`. No es
  alcanzable desde el pipeline (escribe `null`, nunca `""`) y el reporte
  publicado tiene el guard identico: divergir romperia la paridad que el issue
  pide mantener.
- **`per_run` excluye las corridas legado**, asi que una corrida sin
  instrumentar no muestra su SHA. Es comportamiento preexistente de `per_run`
  (`$instr`), no algo que este issue introduzca, y CA-2 acota el SHA a las
  filas de `per_run`.
- **MEF-ADR-0019 (scope)**: los dos archivos ya estaban registrados en la
  allowlist interna; `test-guards.sh` pasa con 125 aserciones.

## Tests

Las **35 suites** de `scripts/tests/` + `.claude/scripts/tests/` corren en
verde tras la correccion. Sin regresiones: en particular
`.claude/scripts/tests/test-harness-version.sh` bloque [K] — que agrega un
historial mixto con `mefisto-metrics-report.sh` — sigue pasando pese a la
seccion nueva.

</details>

## Commits

4511a75 mefisto-tooling(#664): revision -- corregir referencias a PR citadas como issues
335a295 mefisto-tooling(#664): implementacion

Closes #664

Stacked on #6691 (Block 122). Opens campaign 3 (the stress-tensor
