Block 122 closed the local U(1) chapter and named the stress/momentum
route. This block executes its first half and breaks the campaign's
most stubborn wall:

- **The shift identity.** `[U_x, Q] = 0` exactly; the routed current of
  the spatial-translation symmetry obeys the off-shell
  divergence-commutator identity at all 32 sites, both routings, seam
  included — Block 121's telescoping argument is matrix-generic, and
  per momentum sector the commutator reduces exactly to the invertible
  phase `i^k` times the U(1) commutator.
- **The definiteness theorem (the wall, reframed).** Closed-carrier
  Gauss population is obstructed exactly when the charge operator is
  *definite* on the certified package. The U(1) charge is the identity
  — its total is the norm, strictly positive on every nonzero state:
  that was Block 121's wall, now with its true mechanism named. The
  quotient momentum charge `P_x = diag(0,1,2,-1)` (units `pi/2`, from

- **The population break.** The nonzero certified-positive state
  occupying the paired momenta `k=1` and `k=3` has vanishing expected
  total momentum under either sign convention (`1+(-1)=0`;

  unoccupied). The momentum-constraint source therefore admits

- **The pin transfer.** The local-observable wall is momentum-blind:
  the shift residual is `i^k` times the U(1) residual with `i^k`
  invertible, so every Block 122 descent and adjointness failure
  transfers verbatim (0/32).
- **The energy scope, honestly.** No per-slice time-translation
  symmetry exists (the Floquet structure); the per-period conservation

author: jin1c-3
body:
## Why

A polygon reaching this plugin was handled everywhere except where a reader
could see it. `trackFeatures()` pushed it into the drawn collection without
looking at its geometry type, `projectGeometry()` shifted its rings into the
tile datum with the nesting intact, and `extendBounds()` counted every one of
its vertices toward automatic framing. Nothing drew it: the line layer admitted
`LineString`/`MultiLineString` and the point layer admitted `Point`/`MultiPoint`.

So a GeoJSON file holding a boundary, a park or a search area made the camera
fly to that area and show blank map — no error, and no way to tell an
unsupported geometry from an empty file. KML fared accidentally better: a
`<LinearRing>` was read as a `LineString`, so a KML area drew as an outline.

## What this does

- Draws `Polygon`/`MultiPolygon` in a fill layer at the bottom of the owned
  group, in the owning note's colour, with holes left unfilled.
- Strokes boundaries with the existing line layer — a `line` layer renders a
  polygon's rings as closed lines, so a boundary picks up the track's colour,
  width and opacity with no second paint path.
- Keeps direction arrows `LineString`-only and mints no start/end markers for a
  ring: an area has no travel direction.
- Reads KML `<Polygon>` as an area — `<outerBoundaryIs>` as the region, each
  `<innerBoundaryIs>` as a hole — closing a ring the writer left open and
  dropping one with too few corners to enclose anything. A `<LinearRing>` no
  polygon claimed stays a line.
- Derives fill opacity from the existing **Track opacity** setting rather than
  adding a knob, so a large area never hides the roads underneath.
- Makes an area the lowest-priority pointer target.

**Behaviour change:** KML areas that draw as outlines today will draw filled.
Noted in the changelog.

## Live check

Driven against a real Bases map in a test vault — a plain GeoJSON polygon, one
with a hole, a KML polygon with a hole, a KML ring left open, a bare
`<LinearRing>`, and a file mixing an area with a route and a waypoint:

![Areas read from GeoJSON and KML on a Bases map: filled regions in their note's colour, two with unfilled holes, a route with a green start, red ring end and direction arrows crossing one, a triangle closed from an open KML ring, and a LinearRing no polygon claimed still drawn as a line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jin1c-3/obsidian-advanced-maps/a2d2db565794d7f14efe3269c038875af8fab255/docs/area-fill.png)

Measured on that map: seven owned layers in order beneath `marker-pins`; holes
report zero rendered features inside and non-zero on the ring band, for both
GeoJSON and KML; arrows deliver only on `LineString`; the line layer holds both
`LineString` and `Polygon`; the opacity knob at 40% put the fill at 0.1 and the
boundary at 0.4 and restored both; a switch to GCJ-02 moved every ring once and
came back bit-identical; a style reload rebuilt all seven layers and reapplied
the paint; an area-only inline embed drew its area with no statistics bar and no
elevation profile; the map context menu opened over an area with every item
intact; `dev:errors` stayed empty throughout.

## What the live check caught

Registering the area last was not enough. The native view binds its own
`marker-pins` handlers **after** this plugin's layers — the delegated-listener
table reads `…, advanced-maps-track-areas, marker-pins` — so MapLibre handed an
overlapping click to the area first. Clicking a pin standing inside a region
opened two notes: the region's, then the pin's.

Registration order can rank this plugin's own layers against each other; it
cannot rank one of them against a layer bound later. The area now asks what is
rendered under the pointer and stands down when a native marker holds it. Only
the area asks — every other owned feature is small enough that landing on one is
a deliberate choice, and a photo over a pin is already the more specific answer.

## Spec

OpenSpec change `2026-08-17-draw-polygon-areas`, archived here: one added
requirement for area rendering, the KML-format and route-features requirements
amended in `track-map-rendering`, and the inline statistics requirement amended
in `inline-track-maps`.

## Checks

`npm run check` green — 574 tests, format, lint, types, build, smoke.

author: ryo-wtnb11
body:
Closes #138

Summary: from_terms now assembles a finite-state machine over labelled bond states before touching any wide tensor — states are IdL, IdR, and one per distinct open left-partial-string; each state carries its own GradedSpace (running fused charge for rank-3 ops, or the Leg _split's SVD derived for rank-2k ops); the bond at each cut is the direct sum of its live states' spaces (dead states pruned by reachable ∩ co-reachable); edges placed via 0/1 embedding isometries built with from_dense at default atol (inconsistencies raise, never projected). direct_sum has left network/mps.py. cutoff=None skips both compressing sweeps — the MPO is the exact FSM with no floating-point tolerance in assembly; default 1e-13 keeps the two sweeps. Mixed rank-3 + invariant terms in one MPO now build (previously raised).

Performance table (measured on this machine, before → after): R=4 1/r² N=96 (M=374): 10.42 s → 0.18 s; all-pairs 1/r² N=32 (M=496): 5.78 s → 0.20 s; nn Heisenberg N=12: 0.15 s → 0.06 s. All budgets met with wide margin.

Bond verifications (CI-asserted): cutoff=None Heisenberg N=12 bulk bond == example MPO_BOND {0:3,+2:1,−2:1} dim 5, end bond dim 4 by pruning; agrees with default at 8.9e-16; R=4 N=32 widest bond cutoff=None == default == 6; all-pairs N=32 pre-compression widest 32 (bound ≤ 40, prediction 33); SU(2) bulk {0:2,2:1} 3 blocks both settings; SU(3) degeneracy(EIGHT)==2 under cutoff=None; mixed-form kron oracle ~9e-16; inconsistent embedding raises inside from_dense.

Gates: 3465 passed, 2 skipped (+8 tests, all pre-existing unmodified); examples/dmrg.py byte-identical; test_mpo.py 46 tests in 4.9 s (budget 12 s, none over 3 s); ruff check / format --check / mkdocs build --strict clean.

Deviations: one sentence of _split's docstring reworded (cited direct_sum, which the hygiene test now forbids in mps.py; behavior unchanged); constant-shift terms (coeff, []) preserved via identity closing edge at the last site.

author: jayjmuir-hub
body:
Jay: *"check the adhjrt.com repo for age bands … we need the ability for players to play up one age group with a notification"*.

## The answer was in the tournament repo

`…\GitHub\adhjrt`, `Quins JRT.dc.html` has held the whole model since July: the cut-off, the band per group, the ladder, and the wider allowance for the girls'"' squads. This is a **port** of it, read from that repo rather than reasoned out again — and the club'"'"'s 15 squads map onto its 15 age groups exactly.

**The cut-off is 31 August.** "Under X" means exactly X−1 on that date — so a U13 squad is mostly **twelve-year-olds** for most of the season, and the governing cut-off is *last* August for eight months in twelve.

## ⚠️ The model is hybrid, and neither half works alone

I ported it as a pure ladder walk first and two tests caught it:

- **Boys and mixed — walk one rung of the LADDER.** Subtracting years is wrong at the double bands: a 14-year-old in U18B is **one** group below, because U16B is for 14s *and* 15s, but 16 − 14 says two and would refuse a real play-up.
- **Girls — subtract YEARS, allow one or two.** The ladder is wrong here because it has **holes**: U12G is for 11s and U14G for 13s, so there is no group at 12 at all and one hop steps over a real twelve-year-old. That refused a live U14G registration on the tournament site in July, which is why Jay widened it there.

So each branch is the fix for a bug the other branch has. Do not simplify it into one rule.

## What the form does

- **Play-up** → says which way and that the squad'"'"'s coaches will be told, then asks for the parent'"'"'s tick. **Refuses to save without it** — a consent nobody gave is not a consent.
- **Mismatch** → warns and still saves. Blocking typos would block genuine dispensations too, and this is the club'"'"'s own roster, not a tournament entry form.
- **Neither** → silent.

## ❌ This supersedes a model written the same morning

`dobBandMismatch` guessed a plausible band from "age today" with a year of grace, because nothing in this repo recorded the cut-off. Honest while the fact was unknown; wrong to keep now it is known. Deleted rather than left beside the real one.

⚠️ **Two test files silently depended on the real clock.** Eligibility moves every 31 August, so a fixed birthday changes squad on that date. Both now pin it — with `toFake: ['"'"'Date'"'"']` only, because faking the timers as well hangs userEvent and reads as a test that never finishes.

## 🟡 The notification is NOT in this PR, and the obvious route is a trap

The registration already emails the squad'"'"'s coaches through `notify-approval` — exactly the right audience. But that function is Deno and cannot import `src/lib/ageGrade.js`, so teaching it to work out a play-up means a **third copy** of the UAERF model. Two copies already have to be kept in step by hand across two repos.

Store the answer at the moment of consent instead and let the email read a column. That also fixes an ordering problem: the membership insert fires the email **before** the date of birth is written, so anything derived at trigger time reads a row that does not exist yet. Written up in the plan.

## Also

`allowsOwnContact` is **no longer blocked** — the cut-off is known, so it is ordinary work now, with the safeguarding rule still attached (a DOB may only ever make that gate *stricter*, because a parent may write their own child'"'"'s birthday).

Full suite green (2,662) except `tests/pwa-build.test.js`, which spawns its own `vite build` from a `node_modules/` an agent worktree does not have.

## Description

The VMDK disk type compatibility table in `docs/guide/target/vm.md` still lists `monolithicSparse` as unsupported, but support for it landed in v0.71.0.

#10575 upgraded `go-vmdk-parser` to a revision that contains [a12df68](https://github.com/masahiro331/go-vmdk-parser/commit/a12df6824e31e824cbbefd7647fa8178d2dae953) (Add MonolithicSparse support), so `vmdk.Open()` now dispatches `createType` to both `streamOptimized` and `monolithicSparse`. That PR also flipped the `testdata/monolithicSparse.vmdk` case in `pkg/fanal/artifact/vm/vm_test.go` from an expected `unsupported type error` to a happy path. Only the documentation was left behind, so the docs currently tell users the format cannot be scanned.

Verified against the revision pinned on `main` today (`go-vmdk-parser v0.0.0-20260423020818-08305fa668d2`):

```
=== RUN   TestNewArtifact/happy_path_for_monolithic_sparse_vmdk_format
--- PASS: TestNewArtifact (0.00s)
ok      github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/pkg/fanal/artifact/vm
```

| VMDK disk type   | Support |
|------------------|:-------:|

After:

| VMDK disk type   | Support |
|------------------|:-------:|

| monolithicSparse |    ✔    |

No associated issue. Following the [contributing guidelines](https://trivy.dev/docs/latest/community/contribute/pr/), this is a one-line documentation correction for already-shipped behaviour, so the justification is written above instead.

author: timothy-le7
body: ## Summary - Audited all 246 commits on `main` for recurring operational friction, and mapped the full `npa` CLI surface against `skills/index.yaml`. Both passes pointed at the same gaps: the deployment path (readiness, failure triage, teardown, cold start, GPU driver strategy) had no skills at all, and six advertised workbench command groups had none either. - Adds **11 skills**, taking the manifest from 61 to 72. Every command, flag, default value, file path, and toolRef is verified against the installed CLI and the source — not written from memory. A fact-check pass found three wrong claims, which are fixed in the second commit. - Each skill is registered in `skills/index.yaml` with smoke checks that `test_skills_index.py` actually executes, so a future CLI rename breaks the test rather than silently rotting the guidance. ### Deployment path (previously uncovered) | Skill | Why it exists | |---|---| | `workflows/first-run-setup` | Zero to a first verified result, with a **gate** at each step, so a missing token surfaces before a cluster exists rather than at stage three | | `atomic/health-preflight` | There is no `npa doctor`; `npa workbench health preflight`/`access` are the readiness gates, and gated HF licenses can only be cleared interactively | | `atomic/debug-failed-run` | Triage from run id through status (pod-level reason for `PENDING`), stage logs, S3 evidence, image pullability, scheduling, to resume-vs-cancel | | `atomic/teardown-and-cost` | Cancel-before-destroy ordering, which commands touch cloud vs local state, the orphan audit, and choosing the cheapest tier that proves the point | | `tools/gpu-cluster-provisioning` | The managed-image vs GPU-Operator driver decision. Operator mode is unsafe on NVSwitch (Fabric Manager can start before MOFED exposes the IB management devices); this was not covered by `nebius-infra`, `fleet`, or `gpu-selection` | ### Workbench tools that had no skill `tools/token-factory` (zero-GPU hosted inference — the cheapest tier producing a real artifact), `tools/vlm-eval` (scoring rollouts into a gate), `tools/golden-eval` (proving a container image works), `tools/burst` (one gang-scheduled multi-node job), `tools/detection-training` (LanceDB view → Faster R-CNN), `tools/artifact-viz-share` (dataset conversion, `.rrd`/MP4, time-boxed share links). ### Evidence behind the selection Recurring failure classes in the history that these skills encode: 12+ commits on image publish/pull credentials, 8–10 on Blackwell/`sm120`/CUDA routing and mk8s driver defaults (`#298` made managed drivers the GPU-pool default), a repeated preflight-accretion loop (`FTUE-AUDIT.md` → `#197` → `#217` → `#302`), and live-forensics fix bundles (`#236`, `#258`) whose diagnosis steps existed nowhere in writing. Deliberately not duplicated: the Blackwell two-target matrix stays in `gpu-selection`, teardown ownership-gating detail stays in `nebius-infra`, and Token Factory's full reference stays in `docs/workbench/token-factory.md`. The new skills cross-link to those instead of restating them. ## Verification - [x] Ran the relevant unit, smoke, or workflow checks. - [x] For workflow/tool changes: ran or updated the matching skill smoke in `npa/tests/guardrails/test_skills_index.py`. - [x] Checked public-repo hygiene: no customer names, VM IPs, private endpoints, project IDs, tenant IDs, registry IDs, bucket names, or secrets. ``` npa/.venv/bin/python -m pytest npa/tests/guardrails/ npa/tests/smoke/test_golden_eval_manifest.py -q # 2067 passed, 1 skipped npa/.venv/bin/python -m npa.guardrails.confidentiality --built-in-nebius-infra \ --diff-range origin/main..HEAD # confidentiality scan passed; hits=0 ``` `test_skills_index.py` enforces set-equality between `skills/*/*/SKILL.md` and the manifest, frontmatter/name agreement, and execution of every smoke, so all 11 entries are proven wired. Smokes use `cli_help` against the real Typer app, `npa_workflow_yaml` validation of referenced specs, and `file_exists` for docs and manifests. No Python or CLI behavior changed, so `docs/cli/` has no drift. ## Exercised against live credentials Ran the documented commands on the shared dev/operator VM, inside an isolated worktree + venv + tmux session so no other agent's checkout was disturbed: - `npa workbench health preflight` returned 4 pass / 0 fail against real Hugging Face, NGC, S3, and Token Factory credentials, and `--checks s3` scoped correctly — the flag names and valid values in `health-preflight` are right. - Token Factory authenticated and reported a live model list, confirming the premise of `token-factory` that this is a real zero-GPU tier rather than a documented aspiration. - `npa workbench workflow gpus` and `validate-spec` behave as `debug-failed-run` describes. That run also surfaced a gap in `health-preflight` worth fixing, now in the third commit: **a green `s3` row does not mean the submit can write.** The health check lists the configured project bucket, while `submit` puts a unique object into the bucket the *workflow* resolves — a different bucket whenever `NPA_S3_BUCKET` or `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` is set. On this VM the two disagree, so preflight passed and the submit then refused with `writable S3 for this workflow (S3 write permission was denied.)`. An agent trusting the green row would have read that as a regression instead of an environment mismatch. ## Skill Maintenance - [x] I updated the relevant root `skills/` entry and `skills/index.yaml`, or this PR does not change behavior that needs skill guidance. `skills/index.yaml` gains 11 entries; `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` gain matching index lines. Skills were added only under the root `skills/` tree — the `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills` symlinks pick them up automatically, and the single-tree rule is unchanged.

body:
## What this is

The UI half of the versions slice (feedback-wave refill item #1; CEE half: olumi-assistants-service #1001). #739 gave version history ONE home — but browser-local, and its own panel says so. This adds the durable half to the SAME home: versions of the shared model (`scenarios.graph`), persisted by CEE in `model_versions`, visible and restorable from any browser with access to the scenario.

- **`src/adapters/cee/modelVersions.ts`** — list/save/restore client on scenarioGraph.ts's transport rules, inherited in full: literal same-origin `/bff/cee` base (never the PLoT-baked `VITE_CEE_BFF_BASE` — trap 18's live form), POST with identity in the body, guest sentinel never sent, typed outcomes for every server refusal (`VERSION_STALE`, `SIGN_IN_REQUIRED`, `VERSIONS_DISABLED`, `RESTORE_INCOMPLETE`, `NOTHING_TO_SAVE`, `VERSION_NOT_FOUND`), and **writes never auto-retried** — retrying a partial restore is safe (no data loss) but is the user's decision, and the mechanism is: a same-hash retry answers 409 (the server's pre-restore machinery already moved the head — reviewer-measured); a retry after re-reading the list completes it, appending two more version rows. The section refreshes the list on `RESTORE_INCOMPLETE`/`VERSION_STALE` so the user's next attempt carries the fresh head hash.
- **`ServerVersionsSection`** in the versions panel (one import + one mount line in WhatChangedPanel; the #739 local sections are untouched). Rows show v-number, label, time, provenance in user terms (`auto — saved on change`, `auto — before a restore`, `restored`), and mark the current head.
- **Restore, guarded twice**: an explicit CONFIRM must be clicked before any network call (a mutant wiring the first click straight through REDs 6 tests), and the server's pre-restore snapshot comes back as a real **Undo** button. The CAS expectation carries the head hash the user was shown. The apply is `reconcileAppliedGraph` — the receipt-class reconcile with authoritative deletion semantics and layout preservation — never a second bespoke merge. If the reconcile changes nothing after a non-deduped restore, the panel says so honestly (reload guidance) instead of claiming silently.
- **Guests**: the honest sign-in invitation, no network call spent; local history keeps working. **Failed reads never render as 'no versions'** — an unreadable history is an unknown, not an absence.

## User journey (who sees what, from which browser)

Signed-in user saves "Before pricing pivot" on browser A → the same user (or any collaborator with access, once sign-in-shared scenarios exist) opens the scenario on browser B → the panel lists it (plus CEE's auto commit-versions) → Restore (confirm) → the server's working model AND the canvas now show that version; the next turn/analysis is computed from it → Undo restores the pre-restore snapshot. Guests: local-only history + honest sign-in copy.

## Evidence

- RED-first at pristine for both new specs (collection failure before the modules exist); adapter 13/13 + section 13/13 + whole versions module 161/161 + impacted suites (adapters/cee, TopBar.versionHistory, vitestExcludeRegister) 293/293 GREEN.
- **Mutant kit, throwaway worktree outside the repo root, write-test isolation proven, applied-check per mutation (control = exactly 0):** M6 confirm-gate-removed → 6 RED · M7 restore-unbound-from-chosen-row (identity binding, trap 19) → exactly the identity pin RED · M8 reconcile-fed-empty-graph → 1 RED · leading + trailing controls 13/13 GREEN.
- `pnpm typecheck` gate PASSED (ratchet: 2325 → 2308, none added). Scoped eslint clean.

## Fences honoured

No changes to `OutputsDock.tsx` (cockpit #741 owns the panel-header trigger per R4 — this PR mounts nothing new; the existing #739 TopBar trigger + panel host are unchanged), Model Editor files (#742), `useConversation.ts` (#743), or the #737 selector files. `serverGraphHydration.ts` (#727) and `adapters/cee/client.ts` (#682) are not touched — the new adapter is its own file.

## Depends on

CEE #1001 deployed to staging. Until then the section answers its honest failed/disabled states — nothing lies.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Fix round (head `20e44ff8`) — the edge seam

The first cut was **dead on the wire**: `cee-proxy.ts`'s `ALLOWED_TARGETS` (the service-key blast-radius allowlist) did not carry the three versions paths, so every browser call 404'd at the edge before reaching CEE — while all 26 unit tests stayed green, because every instrument sat above the seam (adapter mocks fetch, section mocks the adapter; trap 3b's shape). Caught by review executing the real regexes.

Fixed RED-first with the instrument that sees it: three ON-LIST cases added to `tests/ci-guards/bffProxyPathAllowlist.spec.ts` (drives the REAL handler) — **RED at the pristine edge (3 failed), GREEN with the three regexes added** (`…/versions$`, `…/versions/save$`, `…/versions/restore$`). Guard spec 52/52; versions+adapter+guard 213/213; typecheck gate PASSED; scoped lint clean. Also corrected the retry-convergence mechanism above per the reviewer's measurement (same-hash retry 409s; refreshed retry converges at +2 rows; no data loss).

author: daus95
body:
Moves the `[Unreleased]` section into a dated `[0.6.11]` and bumps `VERSION` to match the tag (`tempa version` reads that file).

0.6.11 closes the loop on what a user actually does when the QA convergence guard halts an epic (#158):

- **The halt no longer tells you to "fix the underlying conflict".** That named one cause as though it were the only one — the guard trips on a *pattern*, and that pattern is sometimes a spec contradiction, sometimes an ordinary regression, sometimes just nitpick churn, each wanting a different response. Notably, the EPIC-13 halt that started this line of work was the third, so the old wording actively misdirected. The message now describes how to tell them apart.
- **Each epic's card has a Spec button** opening that epic's own specification. It was unreachable from the dashboard before — `sources.epics` is a sibling of the PRD folder the Specification tree is rooted at — which meant the file QA grades an epic against, and the one to correct when rounds genuinely contradict each other, was the one file you had to leave the dashboard to read.

author: the-x1x1
body:
**PLAN.md §2 R1, the declaration half.** The colony's contracts and its runtime disagreed in both
directions at once, and the disagreement was invisible because each side was checked only against
itself.

### The defect: five roles declared model calls they cannot make

`soldier`, `medic`, `archivist`, `ui_cartographer` and `scribe` declared `AllowsModelCalls: true`
with `ModelRequirement`s. None of their ants takes a `ModelRouter`. They have never been able to
make a model call.

Nothing failed, because **a requirement is only falsified where the thing it constrains happens**.
`AntModelFitness` graded these five against the routed model, reported them UNFIT, and sent
operators to change models for roles that ask a model nothing. That is the origin of the "seven
roles need a capable model" warning on a colony with five such roles — and the archivist's 32k
context requirement, the largest number in the table, was describing a read of mission state that
happens in process, over objects, with no window at all.

The arguments in those contracts were good, which is why they survived three releases of review. The
`ui_cartographer` entry called itself "the clearest case for the whole mechanism" — a role that walks
a repository with tools, and a model that cannot call them maps the UI from priors. Every word true,
and none of it about `UiCartographerAnt`, which holds a `ToolRegistry` and asks nothing.

### The mirror image: three routes that call models and had no declaration at all

`planner`, `strategist` and the answer-synthesis `scribe` call a model on every mission and every
autonomy cycle. They are not mission roles, so they have no contract, so the fitness report — which
enumerated contracts — **never graded them**.

The planner is the one that cost something. Its shortfall is silent by construction: a model that
cannot emit JSON does not error, `TasksFromJson` rejects, `Plan` returns `FallbackTasks`, and the
mission runs a generic static plan. An operator sees a colony that ignored their goal, with a green
run behind it, and the one report that could have named the cause was enumerating a different set.

### What changed

- **`ModelRouteRequirements`** — a new table declaring what each of the eight routes that actually
  reach the router needs, who calls it, and **what silently happens when the requirement is unmet**.
  `AntModelFitness.CheckAll` and the reasoning-aware reroute both read it. `ContractDeclarationTests`
  pins it in both directions: every route string in `src/` is declared, every declaration is reached.
- **The five contracts state what their ants can do** — `AllowsModelCalls: false`,
  `ModelRequirement.None`, and `Capability.ModelInvoke` dropped where it was granting a call that
  cannot happen.
- **A contract now agrees with itself.** `soldier` and `ui_cartographer` declared model calls without
  requiring `model.invoke`; `medic`, `archivist` and `scribe` required `model.invoke` for calls they
  could not make. Two fields of one record, disagreeing, with nothing comparing them.
- **The `verifier`'s structured-output requirement is removed**, which R1 asked to be *checked before
  changing*. It was checked: the verdict is deterministic, the model's reading is recorded beside it
  as `model_verdict_overridden` and never promotes, and `VerificationVerdict.Parse` reads prose by
  design. The requirement described a use of the model that v3.8.22 ended.
- **One existing invariant changed, and it was made stronger rather than weaker.**
  `EverySpecialist_HasVersionedContract_WithTaskTypesAndHandoffs` asserted every specialist requires
  at least one capability, and it held only because the archivist declared `model.invoke` for a call
  it cannot make. With the lie gone the archivist requires nothing — the honest description of an ant
  that reads in-process mission state — but "empty because nothing is needed" and "empty because
  nobody filled it in" look identical. The rule is now: a role may require no capabilities **only if
  it declares no tools, no model calls, no side effects and no patch proposals**. Empty has to be
  consistent across four fields before it counts as a claim.

### `ResponseSchemaJson` was declared, plumbed, gated — and set by nobody

`ModelRequest` has carried it since v3.4.0. `ProviderWireFormat` turns it into an OpenAI
`response_format: json_schema`. `ModelCapabilityCatalog.Negotiate` strips it for a model that cannot
honour one. Three correct, tested layers, and **no producer ever set the field** — there was no
parameter on `GenerateTyped` to set it with.

So the colony asked in English instead, in the same user turn as the operator's untrusted goal. That
makes the output format a request the model may decline, which is why the coder has a retry loop and
why "malformed patch output" is a named failure class. It is also the last seam where prose was used
as a control channel.

`GenerateTyped` now takes a `schema`, and `coder`, `planner` and `strategist` send one.

**Each schema was written against the PARSER, not the prompt, and the two disagreed three times —
each of which would have turned this fix into an outage:**

- `depends_on` is not an array of integers. The planner's resolver exists because models emit indices
  *or* task titles, and both are normalised. Typing it as `integer` would have made the provider
  reject the exact output the parser was written to tolerate.
- `skill_id` is optional in the prompt, absent from its example, and read by `TasksFromJson`. With
  `additionalProperties: false` it would have been forbidden on the wire — silently ending skill
  attribution rather than breaking anything visible.
- `new_content` is not required. A `delete` has none, and demanding it would have made deletions
  unrepresentable at the provider.

### Two guards for defects that had no detector

- **`ChecklistIntegrityTests`** — a ticked box must agree with the prose under it. §5's repair line
  for S7 sat unticked for ten releases while its own section recorded the suites as landed in
  v0.3.8.65. `DocumentCurrencyTests` sees only version claims and this line names no version, so
  finished work stayed on the forward plan and got scheduled again.
- **`SourceHygieneTests`** — no source file may contain a raw control byte. Two did:
  `AntModelFitness.cs` held a NUL and `FailureContext.cs` a 0x1F, both as separators inside string
  literals, written as bytes rather than escapes. The compiler is happy and the runtime is correct;
  what breaks is everything else. **`grep`, `ripgrep` and `git grep` classify such a file as binary
  and skip it in silence** — so the model-fitness report and the typed failure signature at the
  centre of bounded repair answered "no match" to every search ever run over this repository. Both
  now use the escape, which produces the identical string and identical signatures.

That second one was found by accident, and the guard is what replaces the luck.

### Not in this release

The **provider-adapter conformance suite** — the other half of R1's exit gate. Four adapters against
eight capabilities is its own body of work, and crowding an unverified 32-cell matrix into a release
this size would be the opposite of thorough. It is next.

author: mxschmitt
body:
Third and last finding from the audit for siblings of #627. Same family — an `any` parameter resolved at runtime — this time an unchecked type assertion.

## Problem

The `GetBy*` text parameters are `any` because Go has no `string | RegExp` union. Both selector escape helpers assumed anything that was not a regexp had to be a string (`locator_helpers.go:35`):

```go
func escapeForTextSelector(text any, exact bool) string {
	switch text := text.(type) {
	case *regexp.Regexp:
		return escapeRegexForSelector(text)
	default:
		if exact {
			return fmt.Sprintf(`%ss`, escapeText(text.(string)))   // ← unchecked
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf(`%si`, escapeText(text.(string)))
	}
}
```

## Minimal reproducible

```go
page.GetByText(42)
// panic: interface conversion: interface {} is int, not string
```

The blast radius is wider than it first looks — everything funnels through these two helpers:

- `GetByText`, `GetByLabel`, `GetByPlaceholder`, `GetByAltText`, `GetByTitle`, `GetByTestId` — on **Page, Frame, Locator and FrameLocator** (24 methods)
- `GetByRole`'s `Name` and `Description` options
- the `HasText` / `HasNotText` locator options, via `newLocator` (`locator.go:31`)

## How upstream does it

Upstream doesn't check, because it doesn't have to. Every one of these parameters is typed `string | RegExp`, so the compiler rejects `42` at the call site, and the helper can treat "not a string" as "must be a regexp" (`packages/isomorphic/stringUtils.ts:110`):

```ts
export function escapeForTextSelector(text: string | RegExp, exact: boolean): string {
  if (typeof text !== 'string')
    return escapeRegexForSelector(text);
  return `${JSON.stringify(text)}${exact ? 's' : 'i'}`;
}
```

playwright-go ported that inverted shape faithfully — but without the union type that makes it safe. This is the one finding of the three where upstream has no runtime behavior to copy: the fix has to come from Go's own conventions instead.

## Fix

Both escape helpers and the `getBy*Selector` helpers above them now return an error, and each `GetBy*` returns a `Locator` carrying it:

```go
selector, err := getByTextSelector(text, exact)
if err != nil {
    return newErrorLocator(f, err)
}
return f.Locator(selector)
```

This is the package's existing convention in two respects:

1. **`Locator.Err()` is already how deferred locator errors surface.** `Locator(selectorOrLocator)` already returns `l.withError(fmt.Errorf("invalid locator parameter: %v", ...))` for a bad parameter — same situation, same reporting. `locatorImpl` uses `l.withError`; the other three receivers use a new `newErrorLocator(frame, err)`.
2. **Naming the offending type in the error** is what `Fetch`, `NewCDPSession`, `Clock.parseTime`/`parseTicks`, `convertInputFiles` and `ToContainClass` already do. `newURLMatcher`'s bare panic is the outlier, not the norm.

```
expected string or *regexp.Regexp, but got int
HasText: expected string or *regexp.Regexp, but got int
```

`newLocator` folds `HasText`/`HasNotText` failures into the locator's existing `err` field, right next to the `ErrLocatorNotSameFrame` handling that was already there.

## Tests

`TestGetByRejectsInvalidArgumentType` covers all four receivers across the GetBy* family, `GetByRole`'s `Name`/`Description`, and `HasText`/`HasNotText`. It asserts the error is reachable **both** from `Err()` and from an action on the locator (`Count()`), then confirms valid string and regexp arguments still work.

Verified against `main`:

```
--- FAIL: TestGetByRejectsInvalidArgumentType
panic: interface conversion: interface {} is int, not string
```

Full `go test ./...` is green with the fix (unit suite + the whole `tests` package).

author: jarred-sumner
body:
Folds the open `bun install` / `bun pm` / pack+publish PRs from Aug 12–17 into one branch so they can be reviewed and landed together. Each original PR is one squashed commit here (`<title> (#N)`), in dependency order, so `git log`/`git blame` attribute every hunk to its PR; conflict resolutions between overlapping PRs live in the later PR's commit. Cross-PR API reconciliation is in the `mega-merge fixup:` commits at the end, so the per-PR commits after #38804 (`e2cf8c4305`) do not build on their own until `0adcafaf8b` — bisect across the fold with `--first-parent` on the fixups, not inside it.

**171 PRs folded**, 3 excluded (see below); #38557 was re-ported by hand onto the newer `audit_command.rs`. A simplification pass then roughly halved the net `src/` addition (see below). `cargo check --workspace` and `cargo clippy --workspace` are clean, the debug build links, and all 94 `test/cli/install/**` files pass locally on Linux (debug+ASAN); see Verification.

## Not folded

| PR | Why |
|---|---|
| #37925 | semantic conflict with #39002 (which needs optional peers bound at load); #39002 is newer and explicitly calls this out |
| #38777 | security screen: make_executable() follows an absolute bin-target symlink out of a file:/link: package and chmods the real file (CVE-2019-16775 class) when the folder dep resolves to an ancestor dir; needs rework before merging |
| #38810 | dropped on request: installing a git dependency's devDependencies before `prepare` is rarely needed and runs a nested install (fetching and, via prepare, executing third-party devDependencies chosen by the git repo) outside the project's bunfig protections — too much attack surface for the benefit |

## Security screen

Every folded diff was reviewed for regressions (path traversal, credential leakage, TLS/integrity weakening, lifecycle-script trust widening, terminal injection, new `unsafe` on untrusted input). One PR was dropped for it (#38777 above) and one more on review (#38810). Items a reviewer may still want to eyeball — none were judged exploitable regressions:

- #37851 (concern, low): bunx serialises concurrent installs into the shared <tmp>/bunx-<uid>-<pkg> dir with an flock on <dir>/.bunx-lock; the lock file is opened by path with O_CREAT|O_RDWR and without O_NOFOLLOW, adding a small symlink-following primitive inside the pre-existing TOCTOU window of the cache-dir trust check.
- #38741 (concern, low): New bun.lock files are stamped lockfileVersion 1 instead of 2, so the two v2-only parse-time fail-closed checks (off-registry npm tarball URL without a supported integrity hash; unsafe git `.bun-tag`) no longer apply to any lockfile created after this lands. The reduction is defence-in-depth only: the checks are keyed on a digit the lockfile tamperer also controls, main already stamps v1 whenever bun's own output would trip them, a tamperer can supply a matching integrity for their own tarball anyway, and the git tag is re-validated at checkout/extract time (repository.rs:923, extract_tarball.rs:484; github tags stay checked at every version).
- #38795 (concern, low): Default-trusted check now ignores the URL fragment; the claim that this is exactly as strict as before is slightly off because bun_url lets a `?` after `#` leak the fragment into the request path, though no attacker-chosen tarball results.
- #38800 (concern, low): .npmrc //host/path/ credentials are now resolved by request URL (npm nerf-dart semantics): scopes without credentials pick them up by registry URL, and tarballs on a host other than the registry get that host's own .npmrc credentials. Scope credentials still never leave the scope origin, but the by-URL match is scheme-agnostic and path-unnormalized, which slightly widens where a registry-controlled dist.tarball can make bun present a token.
- #38990 (concern, low): package-lock `file:` targets inside a registry/tarball/git package are now migrated as package-relative folder rows without normalising the sub-path, so a hand-edited key with `..` is no longer skipped at migration time and containment relies on the installer (hoisted linker checks it, with an overrides-name exemption; isolated linker does not).
- #39084 (concern, low): Skips openat2/fchmodat2 on Android (kernel release contains 'android' OR both ANDROID_ROOT and ANDROID_DATA env vars set); symlink-safety semantics are preserved by the fallbacks, but the env-var trigger lets any environment downgrade RESOLVE_BENEATH/RESOLVE_IN_ROOT hardening on ordinary Linux.

Product-behaviour changes that need a maintainer decision before this lands: #38741 (new `bun.lock` files are stamped `lockfileVersion: 1` again — its own PR defers this to a maintainer, and it obsoletes the open #36464; the sibling snapshots are already re-stamped inside the fold, so pulling it back out is one revert + `fixlv`), #38797 (`libc` filtering needs the full registry document for every optional dependency on every OS, since npm's abbreviated document omits `libc`; measured: `@esbuild/linux-x64` 43 KB → 54 KB gzipped, `@rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu` 40 KB → 58 KB, one-time per package per manifest cache, in exchange for not downloading the other libc's multi-MB tarballs on Linux and a host-independent lockfile), #38804 (a migrated lockfile and its package.json edits are only written when the command saves a lockfile), #38923 (`bun pm ls` lists what is installed and exits 1 without node_modules), #38813 (pack/publish resolve `workspace:`/`catalog:` from package.json files, not bun.lock).

## Simplification pass (after folding)

The PRs were written independently, so the folded diff carried duplicate helpers and a lot of narrative comments. A follow-up pass (the `simplify(...)` commits) cut the `src/` diff against main from **+12,081 / −6,723 (net +5,358)** to **+10,284 / −7,559 (net +2,725)** with no behaviour change intended and the full `test/cli/install/**` suite green before and after. Main items:

- One `Lockfile::packages_named` / `package_satisfying` / `patched_package_satisfying` replaces nine "package_index → first candidate whose resolution satisfies a range and a predicate" helpers spread over lockfile.rs, bun.lock.rs, PackageManagerEnqueue.rs, update_transitive.rs and prune.rs.
- `update_transitive.rs` (#38919/#38770) no longer re-implements the resolver's rules: it calls `keep_locked_if_ahead`, `is_named_update_row` (split out of `should_update`) and `dedupe::applied_override` directly, and its `Plan`/`Planned`/`InstanceEdges`/`KeepLocked` scaffolding is gone; reachability uses `lockfile::reachable`.
- One checked NUL-terminated join (`resolve_path::join_abs_string_buf_z_checked`) and one spill helper replace `bin.rs::join_z_checked`, `PackageManager::join_path_z`, and pack's `normalize_buf_spill`; the bunx install lock (#37851) is a single `InstallLock` RAII type.
- Isolated linker: one `append_store_path_at(buf, entry, Which)` family; `PackageInstall::destination_dir_subpath_buf` and the `DestinationSubpath` guard removed in favour of `join_z_spill`; staging installs re-target a `PackageInstall` instead of threading `dest_subpath` through every backend; `remove_link` shared.
- yarn.rs: one dependency-section table instead of four loops, git URL parsing folded into `Entry::set_git_source`, root/workspace package.json parsing shared; pnpm.rs: one merge-based `copy_into_root`, one `workspaces` object path; `finish_migration` builds the one error shape.
- Options/registry: `RegistryPath`, `set_scope_registry` and the second credential lookup removed in favour of `scope_for_package_name` + `UrlAuth::find`; `fmt::for_terminal(x)` = `EscapeControlChars(Redacted(x))` at every call site; `MinimumReleaseAgeExcludes` is one list.
- Multi-line justification comments added by the PRs trimmed to one line or removed throughout (SAFETY lines kept).

Two small behaviour fixes fell out of the review agents' cross-checks and are their own commits: `bun audit fix` now rewrites a matching rule in `resolutions` as well as `o

author: victor-siu
body:
**In short:** calls to Telegram had no time limit and could crash on network errors. This adds timeouts and handles those errors.

### What was wrong
The HTTP call to Telegram had no timeout:
```ruby
http = Net::HTTP.new("api.telegram.org", 443)
...
response = http.request(req)
```
The message and button paths call this **while handling the webhook request**. If Telegram is slow or down, the web worker waits for a very long time. Any network or parsing error also crashes the caller (a 500 error, or a failed job).

### The fix
- Set `open_timeout = 5` and `read_timeout = 10` seconds.
- Wrap the request in a rescue for the errors an HTTPS call can raise: timeouts, `OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError` (TLS problems), `EOFError` (dropped connection), `SocketError`, `SystemCallError` (for example, connection refused or reset), and `JSON::ParserError`. On error, log it and return `false` — the value the callers already treat as "failed".

I listed the errors on purpose instead of catching everything, so real programming mistakes still show up.

### How to verify manually
Point the bot token at an unreachable host, or block `api.telegram.org`. Before: the request hangs or 500s. After: it fails within ~10s, logs one line, and returns `false` (callers already handle this).

### Note for reviewers
This PR and #44 both edit `telegram-notifier.rb`, but different regions (`doRequest` here, a new `deleteWebhook` method in #44), so they should merge without conflict.

author: tjsasakifln
body:
## Why

Skeptic on EXTRA-002: fixture ASCII dump, key only on restore-root (lost with the VPS), systemd had no assembler, and keys leaked into scratch evidence.

## What

- `assemble` copies the newest **real** `pg_dump` (PGDMP / gzip) plus CAS blobs; refuses `PGDUMP-…` ASCII fixtures.
- Encrypt key lives in the existing vault (`~/.config/extra-consultoria/joint-offsite.key` / `EXTRA_JOINT_KEY_FILE`) and an off-site sidecar `backups/extra-002/sidecar/joint.key`. Never `restore-root/joint.key`.
- systemd: `assemble` then `joint --require-real-dump --persist-sidecar --key-file`.
- Staging pushes are labeled `staging_isolated` / `live_nfs=false` so they cannot be mistaken for NFS.

Refs #271 #277 #421

## Honesty

Isolated restore of the campaign `extra_test` custom dump (3.6 MiB, magic `PGDMP`) + CAS-stored `sample_edital.pdf` is hash-identical using **sidecar/vault only**. Live NFS push is **not** in this PR run: VPS SSH `:2222` Connection refused at 2026-08-17T03:47Z (`offsite-launch-unavailable`). Timer stays disabled. No `VPS_OPERATIONAL`.

author: mushfiquehk
body:
Feature 16 T1 from PLAN.md — the till stops dropping to cash-only on every reload.

**The defect:** `hasPaymentIntegration` was computed from `integrations`, which is `useState([])` in `store.tsx`. Every reload put the store back to cash-only, and the gate protected nothing — "connecting" Stripe Terminal charged no card, it only unlocked the ability to *label* a sale as Card.

**The change**
- `shared/schema.ts`: `TENDER_METHODS_KEY` (`payments.methods`), `DEFAULT_TENDER_METHODS` (`["Cash", "Card"]`), `tenderMethods()` for reads, and `validateSetting()` — per-key validation at the settings `PUT`.
- `pos.tsx`: reads the setting on load and renders one button per accepted method. `hasPaymentIntegration`, the `(Setup Integration)` label and the `integrations` read are gone. A method the store has since stopped accepting cannot stay selected.
- `settings.tsx`: a **Payment Methods** block in General Settings — a switch per method, saved immediately, rolled back on a rejected save.
- Saving an empty list is rejected by the API (400), not just disabled in the UI. An unset or unusable value reads as the default rather than as "accepts nothing".

**Tests:** `npm test` → 68 pass, 0 fail. The new one covers the empty list, a list with a blank entry, a non-array, and non-strings; asserts a rejected write leaves the working value in place; and pins the read fallback.

`npm run check`: the same 6 pre-existing client tsc errors as `main` (two are `pos.tsx` line-shifted); none introduced here.

Not in this task: `store.tsx`'s `integrations` state and its "Successfully linked" toast — that is T3, which deletes them once nothing reads them. Nothing reads them from the till any more.

author: lsegal
body:
## Summary

#214 added a cooperative comment-based handoff protocol (signed `/glorp:UUID` comments) alongside the existing `agent-started` label, but kept the label because dispatch logic (`shouldDispatchIssue`, `workStateMatchesRemote`, `resetFailedWork`) and much of the test suite were built around it as the authoritative "is this issue being worked" signal. This PR finishes the migration: the `agent-started` label is gone, and the comment protocol is the sole authority for whether a repository issue is claimed.

## Root cause / change

- Removed the `agent-started` label entirely: dropped `IssueLabeler`, `GHCLI.SetIssueLabel`, its entry in `managedLabels`, and every call site that set/cleared it.
- `pendingIssue` gained a `contested` field, computed once at dispatch time from local history (`hadLocalRecord := restored[key] || seen[key]`, excluding known local failures/active resumes). `negotiateContestedIssues` now gates the "does anyone have this?" comment handshake on that field instead of `hasLabel(issue, agentStartedLabel)`.
- `shouldDispatchIssue` no longer reads a label for repository issues; a never-seen issue is always a candidate, and a previously-seen one is a candidate again unless this instance already recorded it as completed (`wasCompleted`), so completed repository work doesn't loop forever with no label left to suppress it.
- `workStateMatchesRemote`'s repository "active" case now trusts a locally persisted active session only when it carries enough identity to actually resume it (`SessionID` and `Agent` both set); an incomplete record is treated as stale and reset so a fresh pickup renegotiates ownership through comments.
- `resetFailedWork` dropped its `labeler` parameter along with the label-clearing call.

## User impact

No more `agent-started` label maintenance or noise on repository issues; ownership is tracked entirely through handoff comments, which was the eventual goal of #214/#215.

## Changelog

Added an `Unreleased` entry in `CHANGELOG.md`; updated `README.md`'s description of managed labels and the handoff protocol section accordingly.

## Tests

- Updated `glorp_test.go`/`handoff_test.go` fixtures and assertions that relied on the `agent-started` label to use `pendingIssue.contested` and completeness of persisted session state instead.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean.
- `go test ./...` passes; also verified with `go test -race -count=2 ./...`.

No UI-affecting files changed, so no screenshots are included.

Closes #216

author: peezydoesit
body:
## Frozen dice
`DiceFace.vue` animated from `watch(() => props.face)`, so a die that re-rolled the number it was already showing never moved — a 1-in-6 chance per die, per roll. It now watches an optional `roll` counter alongside the face. Yahtzee keeps one counter per die and bumps only the dice that actually rolled, so held dice stay still.

Farkle, Pig, SCC and LRC still have the original bug; they don't pass the new prop yet.

## Tap-to-stop
Optional. The roll button becomes ROLL → STOP: the first press spins the dice freely, the second rolls the values and lands them, so the tap is the throw rather than a reveal. Off by default; toggle lives in the dice settings panel. Bots skip the spin entirely, and a spin is cancelled on turn change.

## Yahtzee setup on desktop
Two columns at 1100px and up — players and play order left, computer players and dice mode right — so the screen fits a laptop without scrolling. Sections are placed explicitly rather than by auto-flow, because Play Order only exists once a player is picked.

author: mikepantz
body:
## What changed

The Stage-0B image stages NetworkManager wifi profiles correctly (right SSID, `autoconnect=true`, priority 100) but has never shipped a wifi backend for NetworkManager to drive — `wpasupplicant` was missing entirely, so `nmcli d` reported `wlan0` as `unavailable` and the profiles were inert. Found on hardware 2026-08-16 (#286); this is what makes #285 (rootfs never expands) unrecoverable — a headless card with a full disk and no working network has no way in.

Two changes:
1. **`scripts/pi/image/layer/overboard-base.yaml`** — added `wpasupplicant` and `python3-spidev` to the `packages:` list, next to the existing `iw`/`rfkill` wifi-tooling block. This is what actually gets them installed on the image; `pins.env` alone doesn't drive package selection (verified by reading `build_image.sh` — the mmdebstrap `packages:` list is the only thing that does).
2. **`scripts/pi/pins.env`** — pinned both to explicit trixie/arm64 versions (`wpasupplicant=2:2.10-24`, `python3-spidev=3.6-1+b6`) in `PINNED_PACKAGES`, per AC-1 and per the issue's own ask. CI's `verify-pins` job resolves these against the live archive on every PR — that's the authority on whether the pin is right, not this PR. `python3-spidev`'s version matches what the issue reporter measured directly on hardware; `wpasupplicant`'s version I corroborated independently via web search against the Debian trixie archive (direct fetch of packages.debian.org is blocked from this sandbox, so I could not run `verify_pins.sh` myself before opening this — flagging that rather than claiming a verification I didn't do).

## Why not fixed differently

`cpufrequtils` (the issue's third finding) needed no change — `git grep` confirms zero references anywhere in the tree already, so that acceptance criterion is already satisfied.

## Acceptance criteria from #286

- [x] `pins.env` carries `wpasupplicant` and `python3-spidev` at explicit versions.
- [x] No reference to `cpufrequtils` survives anywhere in the tree (already true, confirmed).
- [ ] **"A freshly flashed card associates with a staged wifi profile on first boot, with no console intervention."** Cannot verify this from a sandbox with no Pi and no docker daemon — this needs the next hardware flash. Flagging rather than claiming it, per this project's rule against unverified facts.

## What I deliberately left out

- Did **not** attempt to bring the rest of the image's package list (`iw`, `rfkill`, `network-manager`, `openssh-server`, `avahi-daemon`, `apt`, `iproute2`, `stress-ng`) into `PINNED_PACKAGES`. `pins.env`'s header comment calls itself "the single source of truth for what goes on the card," which reads as broader than what it actually is: `PINNED_PACKAGES` only pins a subset (now: `rt-tests`, `can-utils`, `wpasupplicant`, `python3-spidev`), and the rest of the image's packages are unpinned, floating-version installs that `verify_pins.sh` never touches. That's a real, pre-existing gap against AC-1's literal wording ("every directly-installed package is pinned"), not something introduced or fixed here — flagging it rather than silently expanding this PR's scope to cover it.
- Did not attempt to run the actual image build or a QEMU boot (#261/PR #263, not yet merged, and QEMU can't emulate the wifi radio in any case) — this fix is functionally unverifiable outside a real flash.

## Checks run locally
- `python3 .github/policy_check.py` — clean (pre-existing advisories only, none new).
- `python3 scripts/pi/check_layer_headers.py` — clean.
- `python3 scripts/pi/check_image_pin.py` — clean.
- `scripts/pi/verify_pins.sh` — **not** run; needs the live Raspberry Pi archive + a `debian:trixie` container, neither reachable from this sandbox. CI's `verify-pins` job is the real check on the two new pins.

Relates to #182. Companion to #284/#285 (both already have open PRs, #287 and #288).

author: genewgeorge76
body:
Found by calling the live endpoint instead of assuming #74 and #75 were sufficient:

```
POST https://jworden-api.fly.dev/api/v1/auth/register  ->  Internal Server Error
```

## Cause

```
NotNullViolation: null value in column "subscription_status"
of relation "tenants" violates not-null constraint
```

`tenants.subscription_status` exists in production as `NOT NULL` with **no default**, and was **missing from the `Tenant` model**. Every INSERT built from the model omitted the column, so Postgres refused the row.

So `/auth/register` answered 500 for every signup attempt. That — not a missing account — is why `users` was empty and nobody could log in. The sign-in page in #75 was necessary but would have had nothing to sign in *with*.

## This is drift in the opposite direction

#74 fixed columns the **model** had that the **database** lacked. This is the reverse: a column the **database demands** that the **model doesn't know about**. The earlier check couldn't see it by construction — it only walked `Base.metadata` outward.

I added the reverse check and ran it across the whole schema. Exactly one column qualifies, so this is the complete set, not the first of a queue.

## The fix

- `Tenant.subscription_status` declared with a `"pending"` default.
- Migration adds the matching **server default**, so an INSERT bypassing the ORM is safe too, and creates the column outright on any database lacking it (it was never in the migration chain).

**`"pending"`, not `"active"`** — `register_tenant` commits the tenant *before* Stripe checkout runs, so a brand-new tenant has not paid and must not be recorded as though it had. Nothing reads the column today; Stripe drives real billing state. The single existing production row holds `'mock'` and is left alone.

`downgrade()` drops only the default, never the column — it predates this migration in production, so dropping it would destroy data this didn't create.

## Verification

Against PostgreSQL 16 reproducing the exact production state (column `NOT NULL`, default explicitly dropped):

```
reproduced production state: subscription_status NOT NULL, no default
upgrade x3d1r2i3f4t5 -> y4s1t2a3t4u5                        applied

register -> {'status': 'success', 'tenant_id': '61NpJ0DJn-InUUWt'}
login    -> JWT issued, len 224
tenant subscription_status = 'pending' | tier = pro
```

Plus: `app.main` imports, **forward drift 0**, **reverse drift 0**, single alembic head (`y4s1t2a3t4u5`).

author: guillermo-rebolledo
body:
Two unrelated blockers, both of which stopped `pnpm verify` and therefore any release.

## 1. Migration 0018 was unrunnable

`drizzle/0018_perfect_arachne.sql` was the only one of **19** migrations missing the `-- migration-phase: expand` header. `assertExpandOnlyMigrations` requires it of *every* file, so `pnpm db:migrate` refused to run **any** migration rather than just that one. That is why 0018 never reached production — not the Sensitive env vars and not the Git auto-deploy, which merely hid it.

Labelling it expand is correct: it drops `user.timezone`'s default and its `NOT NULL` (both widening) and backfills the rows that only read `'UTC'` because of that default. The migration's own comment explains why that backfill is self-correcting in both directions.

`pnpm release:rehearsal` goes from `BLOCKED · 4 pass · 1 fail` back to `PENDING · 5 pass · 0 fail · 3 manual`.

## 2. The tests were never asserting anything wrong

Both failures are the heaviest jsdom cases in the suite — a full 100-item bounded window driven through fake-indexeddb — and both pass in isolation:

| Test | Isolated | Under full-suite load | Budget |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| retains only a bounded number of loaded pages | 1429ms | **6446ms** | 5000ms `testTimeout` |
| pages through a deterministic bounded offline window | 584ms | fails at 2185ms | 1000ms `vi.waitFor` default |

The first simply exceeds the test timeout under contention. The second is subtler: `vi.waitFor` has its **own** 1s default independent of `testTimeout`, so it gave up mid-render and asserted the pre-click state (`expected 20, got 100`). Raising `testTimeout` alone would never have fixed it — which is why it was still failing at 2185ms with a 60s test timeout during diagnosis.

Neither budget was ever measured against a machine doing anything else. This suite runs ~1000 tests with one worker per core.

**Not masking a hang.** The work provably completes in 1.4s; only contention pushes it past the limit. Both new limits stay far below what a real hang would consume.

- `testTimeout: 20000` in `vitest.config.ts`
- `asyncUtilTimeout: 5000` configured once in `src/test/setup.ts`, where it governs every `findBy*`/`waitFor` in the suite instead of hundreds of call sites
- The two component tests move from `vi.waitFor` to Testing Library's `waitFor` so that single knob reaches them
- The remaining `vi.waitFor` calls are Vitest's own helper, so they take an explicit budget instead

I also tried `userEvent.setup({ delay: null })` first and **reverted it** — 1429ms → 1397ms, so the cost is React rendering 100+ items in jsdom, not event delays. Not worth a no-op edit.

## Verification

Five consecutive full-suite runs: **995 passed, 0 failed** (was 993 passed / 2 failed).

`format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck` all pass.

author: mlpditto
body:
## Why

`firebase-admin` must stay on `^13.x` while `firebase-functions` is on 7.x — admin 14 falls outside the peer range and `npm ci` fails with `ERESOLVE`.

[#717](https://github.com/mlpditto/INTERN-PORT/pull/717) (13.10.0 → 14.2.0) was the second such PR closed by hand. Dependabot's own close reply confirms it will re-open one on every new major:

> OK, I won't notify you again about this release, but will get in touch when a new version is available.

## What

Adds an `ignore` block to the `/functions` npm ecosystem in `.github/dependabot.yml`:

```yaml
ignore:
  - dependency-name: "firebase-admin"
    update-types: ["version-update:semver-major"]
```

- **Still proposed:** patch + minor bumps (13.10 → 13.11, security patches included)
- **Suppressed:** majors only (14.x, 15.x)
- **Unaffected:** every other dependency, and the pip + github-actions ecosystems

## Reverting

Delete the block once `firebase-functions` ships a version whose peer range accepts `firebase-admin` 14. The comment in the file says so inline.

## Risk

Config-only. No runtime code touched, no functions deploy needed, no version bump (this PR touches neither `public/index.html` nor `public/admin.html`).

## Summary

As part of the recurring Woxi Studio compatibility check, this PR verifies support against a randomly sampled Wolfram Demonstration (a Wolfram Cloud "Regelation" notebook — not included in this repo, and no code from it is copied here per the project's copyright guidance).

The sampled demonstration is a `Manipulate` wrapping a `Graphics3D` scene built from `Cuboid`, `Tube`, and `Cylinder` primitives, styled with `EdgeForm`, `CapForm`, and `Opacity` directives, and driven by a single `Labeled` continuous slider.

Woxi Studio already renders and re-renders this construct combination correctly with no code changes needed. This PR adds a regression test with an original, non-copied scene (a block of "ice" with a loaded wire through it) exercising the same set of primitives/options, so the coverage is locked in going forward.

- Added `wire_through_ice_manipulate_animates_its_depth_slider` to `woxi-studio/src/main.rs`, following the existing `instantiate_stored_manipulate` regression-test pattern used for other sampled Demonstrations in this suite.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p woxi-studio` — all 134 tests pass, including the new one
- [x] `cargo test` (full workspace default members) — all ~27,000 tests pass
- [x] `make format`

## Summary

CLAUDE.md keeps a running set of incident precedents that motivate its class-search rule. This change adds two entries found by the reflect pass on the a71f331 fleet repair.

The first entry records the electron.cjs unzip direction reversing after landing: six independent commits re-added a preferred system `unzip` path on top of merged work within about two hours.

The second entry records that the vendored reflect skill and its canonical catstack copy have silently diverged in both directions, which the vendoring rule exists to prevent.

## Review Claim

The two new CLAUDE.md entries accurately describe what the reflect pass found in this repair's own history, and nothing else in the repo changes.

## Review Lane

docs

## Review Unit

docs

## Safety Invariant

This slice edits only guidance text in CLAUDE.md. Every edit lands through this PR's normal human review; no product or tooling code is touched, and nothing is applied on the workflow's own authority.

## Slice Rationale

Kept downstream of the repair slice so "did this fleet repair teach us something durable" is its own reviewable claim, separate from the fix itself.

## Non-goals

- No edits to any file other than CLAUDE.md.
- No changes to skills in this repo or in catstack.
- No product, tooling, or CI behavior changes.

## Summary
- Live `/gspc-arena` 308s to `/sov-space/`, and `/sov-space` 308s back. Eight hops, zero bytes.
- Cause: the 200 rewrite to `/sov-space/index.html` is canonicalized by Pages into a 308. Combined with the new outbound 308s, it loops.
- Fix: drop that rewrite. SPA catch-all serves `/gspc-arena`. App mounts Council Space there. Old `/sov-space` paths stay 308 away.
- Title refreshed to the locked line.

## Test plan
- [ ] `curl -sI https://councilof.ai/gspc-arena` is 200 (not 308)
- [ ] `/sov-space` 308s once to `/gspc-arena`
- [ ] `/gspc-scoreboard` and `/gspc-verify` still 200
- [ ] No `sov-*` in the public chrome

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Routing and CDN redirect behavior change affects all inbound links to Council Space and old `/sov-space` URLs; incorrect deployment could break deep links or reintroduce loops, but scope is limited to static redirects and client routes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a **live redirect loop** where `/gspc-arena` and `/sov-space` bounced off each other (a 200 rewrite to `/sov-space/index.html` was canonicalized by Cloudflare Pages into a 308, conflicting with outbound 308s to `/gspc-arena`).
> 
> **Council Space** is now canonical at **`/gspc-arena`**: the edge rule that rewrote arena to `/sov-space/index.html` is removed so the SPA catch-all serves `/index.html` and the app mounts `SovSpace` on that path. **`/sov-space`**, **`/sovereign-space`**, and **`/simulate`** client- and edge-redirect to `/gspc-arena`. Layer deep links (`towns`, `globe`, `world`, etc.) now target **`/gspc-arena?view=…`** instead of `/sov-space?view=…`.
> 
> Home and document titles (HTML, OG, Twitter, `ROUTE_TITLES` for `/`) are updated to the locked line **“Council of AI — we measure, we sign, we re-attest.”** `generate-redirects.mjs` comments document why the old `/gspc-arena` 200 rewrite must not return.
>

author: danieljoffe
body:
Trivy went red on #809 — a PR that changes **no dependencies and no image files**, only Python and TypeScript source.

9 HIGH findings, all in the Debian layer: the util-linux family (`bsdutils`, `libblkid1`, `libmount1`, `libsmartcols1`, `libuuid1`, `util-linux`) carrying **CVE-2026-53615**.

## Not #809's fault, and not new

Debian published the fix in `2.41.5-0+deb13u1`. The Trivy DB simply caught up — which means **the image has been serving production with the vulnerable packages** since before this sweep started. #808 passed Trivy hours earlier against the same packages.

## Why a pinned digest didn't protect us

Pinning the base by digest makes the base *reproducible*, but it also **freezes its OS packages** at whatever shipped that day. A CVE fixed in Debian after the digest was cut waits for a new base image to be published *and* for Dependabot to bump it.

`apt-get upgrade` in the runtime stage closes that gap at build time.

The trade is a floating layer — same Dockerfile, different packages as Debian publishes fixes. That's the correct direction for a runtime: the **base stays pinned and reproducible**, while security patches don't wait on a digest bump. The reasoning is written into the Dockerfile so the next person doesn't "restore determinism" and silently reopen the hole.

## Verified locally, against CI's exact command

Same pinned Trivy digest, same `--severity` / `--vuln-type` / `--ignore-unfixed` / `--ignorefile` flags:

| build | result |
|---|---|
| without `apt-get upgrade` | **Total: 9 (HIGH: 9)** — reproduces the CI failure, same CVE |
| with `apt-get upgrade` | **Clean, exit 0** |

And the packages in the built image now read `2.41.5-0+deb13u1` — the exact version Trivy asked for, across all six.

## One thing worth knowing for next time

An **unfiltered** local scan reports 14 findings (`perl-base` ×8, `gzip`, `ncurses*`, `libacl1`) that CI never shows. Every one is `fix_deferred` or `affected` — Debian ships no fix — and CI runs `--ignore-unfixed`.

Those are real but not actionable: `apt-get upgrade` can't clear them and neither can a base bump. Recording it so a future unfiltered scan doesn't read as a regression.

## Residual risk

- Build output is no longer byte-identical across time. Deliberate, and scoped to the runtime layer only.
- `apt-get upgrade` is broad. A targeted `--only-upgrade util-linux …` would be narrower but needs editing every time a CVE lands in a different package — which is the failure mode that produced this PR.

— Claude (Claude Code)

author: hndrewaall
body:
## The bug

An obligation registered with a `satisfied_by` block never cleared, even
though the action it demanded was genuinely performed. The operator had to
clear it by hand.

`satisfied_by.command_pattern` is one regex asked to do two unrelated jobs:

- **identify which command counts** — otherwise the rule clears on any
  unrelated invocation, so it necessarily names the program and its
  addressing arguments;
- **assert what that command carried** — otherwise the rule clears on a
  send that never mentioned the thing the obligation is about.

Written as one pattern the two halves fight each other. The natural shape is
`prog\b(?=.*A)(?=.*B)`. Both lookaheads are evaluated at the offset just
past the program token, and `.` does not cross newlines, so they can only
see the rest of *that line*.

Now consider a CLI that refuses stdin, and where an inline `"a\nb"` argument
writes a literal backslash-n. Any multi-line payload *must* be staged:

```bash
f=$(mkstage); cat > "$f" <<'EOF'
...body...
EOF
mysender --to alice -F "$f"
```

The payload is sitting **in the command string**, on earlier lines, and the
pattern cannot reach it. The rule can never self-satisfy.

## Why `file_arg_flags` did not already cover this

`satisfied_by.file_arg_flags` was added for exactly the file-payload shape,
and it is live. It still does not fix this, for a deeper reason:

**A payload file contains the message and nothing else** — no program token,
no addressing arguments. So a pattern anchored on command shape (which is
every pattern that is safe to write) can never match a file body. Turning
the flag on hands a command-shaped regex a second haystack it cannot use.

Reproduced, with the path resolved and the file present on disk:

| case | file consulted? | match |
|---|---|---|
| combined pattern, heredoc form, payload in command string | n/a | no |
| combined pattern, `-F <literal path>`, file present | yes | **no** |
| combined pattern, `-F "$f"` (variable), file present | no — declined | no |
| combined pattern, `-F <literal path>`, file deleted | no — gone | no |

Row 2 is the one that matters: everything worked and it still did not match.
A secondary finding is row 3 — a `-F "$f"` argument is an unexpanded shell
variable, which the AST path extractor declines by design, so no file is
consulted at all regardless.

## The fix

Add `satisfied_by.body_pattern` (CLI: `--satisfied-by-body-regex`): a second,
independent regex for the payload, searched **on its own** over the same
haystacks — command string first, then any `file_arg_flags` file bodies.

```
--satisfied-by-cmd-regex  'mysender\b(?=.*--to\s+alice\b)'   # which command
--satisfied-by-body-regex 'Order\s*#\s*42\b'                 # carrying what
```

**Both must match.** This is strictly *narrowing* — an obligation that gains
a `body_pattern` becomes harder to satisfy, never easier. Nothing is
relaxed; the only change is that each half is looked for where it actually
lives. Existing rows without a `body_pattern` behave exactly as before.

Also in here:

- `--satisfied-by-file-flag` now accepts either regex as its anchor rather
  than requiring the command one specifically.
- `add` refuses an uncompilable satisfy regex (exit 2). It was silently
  skipped at match time, which registers a rule that can never fire — the
  exact failure this area exists to prevent.
- The regex decision moves into `_satisfied_by_regexes_match`, called by
  `_satisfy_by_completion` and exercised directly by the tests.

## Why this class of bug is worth the surface

An obligation that **cannot** self-satisfy is worse than one that never
existed. The operator does the real work, the gate stays standing and blocks
every later call it matches, and the only way out is an override. Train that
reflex often enough and the override stops being an exception — which
inverts the point of having a gate at all. A gate that can only be escaped
teaches escape.

## Tests

19 new tests in `tools/obligations/tests/test_satisfied_by_body_pattern.py`,
covering the heredoc form, the `-F <file>` form, the file-already-deleted
case, the variable-path residual, the narrowing guarantees, backward
compatibility of command-line-only matching, and end-to-end `add` +
`post-satisfy` through the real CLI against a temp HOME. Two of them pin the
*bug* — if the combined-pattern shape ever starts matching, the split stops
being justified and those go red.

Suite: **153 → 172, all green.** Rust suite unchanged at 1770 passed.

Sabotage-verified (break the fix, confirm red, restore green):

| sabotage | tests failed |
|---|---|
| `body_pattern` ignored at match time | 5 |
| patterns ORed instead of ANDed | 5 |
| uncompilable stored pattern fails **open** | 1 |
| CLI drops the uncompilable-regex refusal | 2 |
| file-flag guard reverted to cmd-regex only | 1 |
| `body_pattern` never persisted by `add` | 1 |

The first sabotage pass earned its keep: it showed that five of the unit
tests were checking a re-implementation of the matching logic rather than
the shipped code path. Extracting `_satisfied_by_regexes_match` and pointing
the tests at it is what makes the table above meaningful.

## Known residual

When the payload exists **only** in a file and the `-F` argument is a shell
variable, there is nothing readable at match time and the rule still will
not clear. That is tested and documented rather than papered over. The
heredoc form — payload also present in the command string — does clear, and
that is the shape that motivated this change.

author: sebawag
body:
## ✨ Closes #9 — script to import the Wikidata dump

Adds `scripts/wikidata-import.sh`, which streams a Wikidata dump straight into a MillenniumDB database.

Wikidata publishes its data as **N-Triples dumps compressed with bzip2** (18 GB for Truthy, ~110 GB for the full dump). This script streams the dump through `mdb import --format nt`, so **no extra disk space** is needed beyond the final database.

### Usage

```
./scripts/wikidata-import.sh <db_folder> [--file dump.nt.bz2 | --download] [options]
```

| Mode | Description |
|---|---|
| `--file <dump>` | Import a local dump (`.nt`, `.ttl`, or `.bz2`) |
| `--download` | Download the latest **Wikidata Truthy** dump and stream it directly (no temp file) |
| `--buffer-strings/--buffer-tensors/--btree-permutations` | Optional knobs passed through to `mdb import` |

### Pipeline

```
curl -L URL | lbunzip2 -c | mdb import <db_folder> --format nt
```

- Uses `lbunzip2` when available (parallel decompression), falls back to `bunzip2`/`bzcat`
- Uses `curl` when available, falls back to `wget`
- Memory/disk usage stays bounded regardless of dump size

### Verification

Tested both modes against a small dump:

```
$ ./scripts/wikidata-import.sh /tmp/mdb_wd --file test_wikidata.nt.bz2
[wikidata] Importing Wikidata into /tmp/mdb_wd ...
Catalog:
  triples:                4
  distinct predicates:    3
...
Total Import duration: 26 milliseconds
[wikidata] Wikidata import finished.

$ ./scripts/wikidata-import.sh /tmp/mdb_wd --download   # against a local HTTP mirror
...same success...
```

`bash -n` passes; `--help`, missing-file and conflicting-options cases give clear errors.

### Notes

The maintainers noted in the issue that the benchmark used the *Wikidata Truthy* N-Triples dump (not the JSON dumps), which is exactly what this script consumes. `mdb import` already handles IRIs natively, so no pre-transformation is needed.

body:
The Runs on picker still did not look like the design. Its rows carried a **second line of prose under every name**; the design's `.fopt` is one 34px line — icon, name, and the check at the **end** rather than the start.

## What changed

- **No detail line.** The sentence each row was spending a line on becomes a `title` tooltip. What stays on the row is the compact fact worth scanning: `2 daemons` for a group, `offline` / `needs update` for a machine that cannot take the agent.
- **Check on the right**, `.fopt.on` for the selected row — the design's own convention, already in `globals.css`.
- **Plain 16px marks**, not tiles with coloured backgrounds.
- **No Cloud badge.** The name already says Cloud, and a group carries its own name; the `layers` mark is what says "a set, not a machine".
- **The menu is no longer pinned to the trigger's width.** `.fmenu` is `min-width: 210px` and free to exceed it — pinning it is why names truncated to `1111…` in a third-width field.

## Reviewing

`DaemonSelectOption.detail: string` becomes `meta?: string` (the compact right-aligned fact) and `title?: string` (the full reason). Splitting them is what stops the row from growing a second line again: `meta` has nowhere to put a sentence.

Nothing else changes — same options, same ordering, same disabled rules, same keyboard behaviour.

Verified against a live control plane: the Add-agent picker renders `lab · 0 daemons` and `11111111 · offline ✓` on single lines, names no longer truncated.
