author: hossain-khan
body:
### Summary
Implements smart sleep mode and duplicate screen detection when loading next display images in full-screen device preview.

### Details & Motivation
1. **Dynamic Signed Storage URLs**: TRMNL display responses from S3/DigitalOcean Spaces include query parameters (`X-Amz-Date`, `X-Amz-Signature`) that change on every API call. Direct URL string comparison previously caused identical images to be treated as new ones, duplicating cache entries.
2. **Normalized URL Helper (`normalizeImageUrl`)**: Added with comprehensive KDoc explaining how query parameters are stripped for underlying asset comparison.
3. **Smart Sleep & Duplicate Detection**:
   - When `display.filename == "sleep"` or `special_function == "sleep"`, the device is in sleep mode: notifies user (*"Device is in sleep mode. No new screen available."*) without advancing or duplicating cache history.
   - When the normalized base URL matches the current screen (`normalizeImageUrl(new) == normalizeImageUrl(current)`), the rotation did not advance: notifies user (*"No new screen to display. Device may have only one screen in rotation."*) without duplicating cache history.
4. **UX Refinement**: Removed redundant *"Next display image loaded"* snackbar on successful next image fetch for a smoother reading flow.

### Verification
- [x] Unit tests added in `DevicePreviewScreenTest` for `normalizeImageUrl`, sleep mode detection, and duplicate detection
- [x] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` passes (100%)
- [x] Tested live on emulator and verified via Logcat


### Sample

```json
    {
      "status": 0,
      "image_url": "https://trmnl-screens.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/...",
      "filename": "sleep",
      "refresh_rate": 16023,
      "reset_firmware": false,
      "update_firmware": false,
      "special_function": "identify"
    }
```

author: mbasa-geolonia
body:
# Fix town/koaza matching priority and address post-processing edge cases

## 概要

住所として妥当な入力であるにもかかわらず、本来到達すべき正規化レベル8（街区符号・住居番号まで特定）に届かず、レベル2〜3で処理が止まってしまっていた11件の不具合を修正した。原因は大きく2つに分類される。

- **町字・小字名のパターン生成**（`src/lib/cacheRegexes.ts`）：町字・丁目・小字名をマッチさせるための正規表現が、広すぎたために実データを持たない候補や方角違いの誤った候補が正しい候補より先に採用されてしまうケース、あるいは狭すぎたために本来マッチすべき数字・助数詞の表記揺れに対応できていなかったケース。
- **町字マッチ後の番地部分の後処理**（`src/normalize.ts`）：「番」「号」形式の番地表記を街区符号・住居番号の形へ変換する正規表現が、実際に存在するいくつかの表記パターンを想定できていなかったケース。

各コミットは、個別の住所で発見した1件の不具合に対する最小限の修正であり、それぞれ独立して検証済み。コミット順は以下の通り。

| # | 対象アドレス例 | 修正内容 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `名古屋市守山区小幡太田１６－２２` | 町字候補のソート時、先頭の「大字」だけでなく出現する全ての「大字」「字」を減点対象にした |
| 2 | `稲沢市小沢２－４－２５－１０１` | 最長の街区符号・住居番号候補が一致しない場合、より短い数字グループへフォールバックするようにした |
| 3 | `名古屋市南区三条二丁目16番42号` | 助数詞（丁目・条・番町など）のマッチを、入力と同じ種類の助数詞のみに制限した |
| 4 | `名古屋市瑞穂区神穂町2丁目2番地` | 丁目を持たない町字に対して、先頭の「N丁目」を街区符号の区切りとして扱うようにした |
| 5 | `名古屋市千種区若水3丁目5-23` | 「町」省略エイリアス生成時に、数字表記（漢数字／全角／半角）の揺れを考慮して重複判定するようにした |
| 6 | `那覇市字古波蔵１－３０－１` | 入力先頭の「大字」だけでなく単独の「字」も除去するようにした |
| 7 | `名古屋市熱田区１番３丁目８番２５号` | 「番町」「番丁」だけでなく単独の「番」も、算用数字表記に変換可能な助数詞として扱うようにした |
| 8 | `名古屋市中村区大日町１－７` | 「丁目」省略の緩いマッチが、実データ（住居表示・地番）を持たない町丁目にまで適用されないようにした |
| 9 | `沖縄市海邦1丁目-14番-15号` | 「番」「番地」と番地本体の間にハイフンが入る表記を許容するようにした |
| 10 | `札幌市白石区本郷通8丁目南2-24` | 「丁目」省略の緩いマッチが、方角（北・南）違いの同名小字同士を区別できずに誤ってマッチしないようにした |
| 11 | `札幌市白石区本通14北5-15` | 丁目数字の直後に区切り文字（「丁目」の記載やハイフン）を挟まず方角が続く表記にも対応した |

不具合10・11は、`test:addresses` のフルスイート実行時に「並行実行（`concurrency: 4`）に起因する非決定的な失敗（フレーキーテスト）」だと当初考えていた失敗の大部分の真の原因であったことが調査で判明した。実際にはアドレス群全体にわたる決定的な不具合であり、非決定的だったわけではなかった。

## 今回のPRに含まれないもの

以下の失敗は、対応方針について別途相談が必要なため、本PRの対象外としている。

- 番地部分に含まれる3つ目の数字グループが、たまたま実際に登録されている支号（住居表示の枝番）と一致してしまうケース。多くの場合、実際の利用シーンでは街区符号・住居番号レベルの表記が期待される（例：`那覇市松尾2丁目2-25-4`）。
- テストデータ自体に文字化けと思われる不正な文字（`?`）が含まれているケースが1件。

## テスト内容

- [x] `npm run test:main` — 各コミット後に39件全て成功することを確認
- [x] `npm run test:addresses` — 実データ（10,616件）を用いた回帰テストを各コミット後に実行し、直前の失敗一覧と差分を取って新規の失敗（リグレッション）が発生していないことを確認
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` / `npm run lint` — クリーンであることを確認（`src/normalize.ts:312` の `tsc`警告はこのブランチ以前から存在する既知の無関係な警告）

body:
판독 서버화 2단계(마지막). 1단계(#293·#294)에서 사진첩·급여데이터함을 옮겼고,
여기서 **명함첩·경력관리**를 옮긴다. 이걸로 판독 열쇠가 브라우저를 완전히 떠난다.

## 왜

그 둘은 공용 층을 안 쓰고 **각자 따로** 구글을 불렀다. 남아 있는 한
실시간DB 의 열쇠를 지울 수 없고, 지우기 전까지는 로그인한 모든 직원이 읽는다.
그 열쇠는 `AQ.` 로 시작하는 AI 스튜디오 열쇠라 웹사이트 제한 같은 자물쇠를
채울 방법도 없다(2026-08-17 확인).

## 무엇을

- `js/pu-ai-call.js` (새 파일) — 「서버를 부르는 일」만 떼어 낸 작은 호출기.
  큰 층(`js/pu-doc-read.js`)을 안 쓴 까닭: 명함첩·경력관리는 제 프롬프트와
  제 결과 다루기를 갖고 있어, 통째로 실으면 프롬프트가 두 벌이 된다.
- 서버가 답 길이 지정을 받아 넘기되 **위를 막는다**(8192). 경력관리가 1500 을 쓴다.
  안 받으면 긴 증명서에서 답이 잘리고, 통째로 받으면 부르는 쪽이 요금을 정한다.
- 남은 열쇠를 **지운다** — 이 기기(둘 다)와 클라우드(`kcareer/{uid}/_secrets`).
  안 지우면 기기를 바꿀 때 되살아난다. 열쇠 입력칸·공유 스위치도 없앴다.
- 판정 기준을 「열쇠가 있나」 → **「로그인했나」**. 열쇠 판정을 남기면 다시 읽어 온다.

## 안 바꾼 것

프롬프트는 한 글자도 안 바꿨다 — 바꾸면 이미 읽힌 명함·서류와 답이 갈린다.

## 배포 뒤에 할 일 (이 PR 밖)

1. `firebase functions:secrets:set GEMINI_KEY`
2. `readDoc` 에 `secrets: ["GEMINI_KEY"]` 다시 달기
3. 실시간DB 의 `pucards/config/geminiKey` · `data/app_config/geminiKey` 지우기
4. `js/pu-doc-read.js` 의 옛 길(`getKey`) 걷어내기

**배포 전에 3번을 하면 판독이 멈춘다.**

## 검사

검사 4123개 통과(새 검사 18개). 뮤테이션 18건 모두 잡힘.
함수를 뽑아 **실제로 돌려** 확인한다 — 글자 찾기는 주석·죽은 문자열에 속는다.

⚠ 낡은 검사 둘을 고쳤다. 부르는 자리의 **개수를 못 박아** 두어 부름이 공용
호출기로 옮겨 가자 깨졌다(시간 제한은 그대로 붙어 있었는데도). 개수 대신
「시간 제한 없는 부름이 남았나」를 보게 했다.

author: pablof7z-agent
body:
Fixes #1819.

## What

`LocalOrigin` was encoded twice — standalone under `LOCAL_MAGIC` for
canonical rows, and embedded in `PROVENANCE_MAGIC` for displaced rows —
and the two decoders disagreed on what counts as corrupt:

- `decode_local` required strictly ascending owner ids (`DuplicateOwner`,
  `InvalidOwnerOrder`).
- `decode_provenance` accepted owners in any order, rejecting only
  duplicates.

Both encoders emit from a `BTreeSet`, so round-trips agreed and nothing
failed today. The divergence: bytes rejected as a canonical local row were
**accepted** as displaced provenance.

Fix: both decoders now call one shared `decode_owners` helper. There is a
single place that owns the strictly-ascending invariant; `decode_local`
and `decode_provenance` are both callers of it, not independent copies.

Two smaller items in the same "parallel durable representation" family,
flagged in the same issue:

- `DeadKeys::decode` (`postings.rs`) re-implemented `new`'s non-empty and
  strict-ordering checks inline and built `Self { keys }` directly,
  bypassing `new`. It now ends in `Self::new(keys)`.
- `encode_run` (`postings.rs`) checked id↔key consistency both ways but
  never that one key carries one `created_at`. Not reachable today —
  `memberships_for_pending` builds every membership of one event from a
  single shared `Arc<RunEvent>` — but it was a hole in an otherwise
  exhaustive validator, not a live bug. Closed it.

No backwards compatibility kept: the looser `decode_provenance` check is
deleted, not aliased.

## Falsifiers

Each fix is proven by a test that fails against the pre-fix code and
passes after. I verified this by temporarily reverting each fix in turn
and re-running the corresponding test:

**`provenance_local_owners_reject_the_same_orderings_as_standalone_local`**
— reverting `decode_provenance`'s owner loop to duplicate-only checking:
```
thread '...provenance_local_owners_reject_the_same_orderings_as_standalone_local' panicked at crates/nmp-store/src/binary_event.rs:1564:44:
called `Result::unwrap_err()` on an `Ok` value: Provenance { seen: {}, local: Some(LocalOrigin { owners: {IntentId(3), IntentId(8)}, sig_state: Signed }) }
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed
```

**`dead_keys_decode_rejects_through_new_not_a_parallel_check`** —
reverting `decode` to its own inline empty-block message:
```
thread '...dead_keys_decode_rejects_through_new_not_a_parallel_check' panicked at crates/nmp-store/src/redb_store/postings.rs:1540:9:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: "empty dead-key block"
 right: "dead-key block is empty"
test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 1 failed
```

**`encode_run_rejects_one_key_carrying_two_created_at_values`** —
reverting the new `created_at` check:
```
thread '...encode_run_rejects_one_key_carrying_two_created_at_values' panicked at crates/nmp-store/src/redb_store/postings.rs:1338:37:
called `Result::unwrap_err()` on an `Ok` value: EncodedRun { dictionary_entries: 1, postings: 1, ... }
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed
```
(silently drops one of the two conflicting memberships into a single dictionary entry instead of erroring)

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p nmp-store` — master's lib suite is 203 tests; this PR
      adds 3 (`provenance_local_owners_reject_the_same_orderings_as_standalone_local`,
      `dead_keys_decode_rejects_through_new_not_a_parallel_check`,
      `encode_run_rejects_one_key_carrying_two_created_at_values`), so
      203 + 3 = **206 passed**, confirmed.
- [x] `cargo check -p nmp-store --features bench-instrumentation` — clean.

author: xieyubo
body:
## The defect

```cpp
int* p = &x;
[&p]() { [[scpp::unsafe]] { *p; } }
// cannot dereference ('*') 'this.p': only a raw pointer (inside
// '[[scpp::unsafe]] { }'), a function pointer being called, a class
// with operator*, or '*this' is supported here
```

An over-rejection inside the one construct that exists to permit a raw-pointer dereference, reported with a message that denies a pointer was involved.

## What is actually implicated

Neither the lambda nor the `this.p` spelling.

- The same failure reproduces with **no closure at all**: `int* p = &x; int*& q = p; [[scpp::unsafe]] { *q; }` and an `int*&` parameter both fail identically.
- A real class pointer field derefed as `*this.p` inside an unsafe block **already worked**.

The common factor is the *type*: `[&p]` gives the closure a reference-typed field (`by_reference_capture_type`), so the capture is merely one of three ways to produce a `T*&`.

The `[[scpp::unsafe]]` block was **never consulted** — the type test failed and returned before `state.unsafe_depth` was read. This was not an unsafe-tracking bug.

## Root cause — an asymmetry, in two layers

`validate_deref_expr` (`movecheck/dataflow.cppm`) computed a reference-stripped `underlying` and used it for the class-`operator*` test, but asked `is_raw_ptr`/`is_fn_ptr` of the *declared* type. `int*&` is `TypeKind::Reference`, so it failed "is this a pointer?" and hit the first diagnostic, never reaching the unsafe check below it.

Spec §5.1(5.1) and ch03 §7.1(4) gate indirection through "a value of pointer type" — a question about the pointer, not about how the program reached it. So the fix looks through the reference exactly as the class test already did, making the **spelling irrelevant** rather than adding a case for `this.p`.

`codegen_lvalue`'s Unary case carried the identical asymmetry, with a comment asserting a reference operand could not reach it — true only because movecheck rejected these shapes first. Fixing movecheck alone would have relocated the failure to codegen instead of removing it.

## Grid

INSIDE `[[scpp::unsafe]]`:

| | shape | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | `[&p]` `*p` | **rejected** | ok |
| A2 | `[p]` `*p` | ok | ok |
| A5 | `[&p]` `p->v` | **rejected** | ok |
| A7 | `[&p]` `const int*` | **rejected** | ok |
| A9 | `[&p]` `*p = 9` | **rejected** | ok |
| C1 | plain `int*` | ok | ok |
| C2 | `int*& q = p;` `*q` | **rejected** | ok |
| C3 | `int*& q` `q->v` | **rejected** | ok |
| C6 | `int*` parameter | ok | ok |
| C7 | `int*&` parameter | **rejected** | ok |
| D1 | field `*this.p` | ok | ok |

OUTSIDE any unsafe block — the critical controls, all still rejected:

| | shape | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | `[&p]` `*p` | rejected, **wrong message** | rejected, correct message |
| B2 | `[p]` `*p` | rejected | rejected |
| B3 | `[&p]` `p->v` | rejected, wrong message | rejected, correct message |
| B6 | `[&p]` `*p = 9` | rejected, wrong message | rejected, correct message |
| C5 | `int*& q` `*q` | rejected, wrong message | rejected, correct message |
| C8 | `int*&` param | rejected, wrong message | rejected, correct message |
| D2 | field `*this.p` | rejected | rejected |

## Tests

- 4 movetest positives, verified to **fail against a freshly built `origin/main`**: captured-pointer deref, captured `->`, and the two no-lambda shapes (which is what proves the fix is about the type, not the capture).
- 5 movetest negatives (safe-context controls). These **passed pre-fix**, because pre-fix they were rejected by the *wrong* check — they never reached the unsafe gate. Proof-by-deletion: disabling the `state.unsafe_depth` check makes all 5 flip to accepted, so they do guard the gate on the newly widened shapes.
- 2 driver tests pinning runtime semantics (a write through a by-reference-captured pointer reaches the original referent). Both fail pre-fix.

## Validation

- clean `-Werror` build: 23 warnings, all `-Wunknown-attributes` (baseline)
- `ctest` 6/6
- blackbox 626/626 on this branch, 626/626 on a freshly built `origin/main`
- self-hosting intact (`ast`/`lexer`/`parser`, plus `--workspace`)
- probe unchanged: `constexpression.cppm:1313`, `check_moves`
- `git diff origin/main -- docs/ blackbox_test/` empty; no `throw`/`try`/`catch` added

## Separate defect found, not fixed here

Raw-pointer **subscript is not gated by `[[scpp::unsafe]]` at all**: `p[0]`, `q[0]` (`int*&`) and `this.p[0]` are all accepted outside any unsafe block, including on a plain local pointer with no reference and no lambda. §5.1(5.1) gates "indirection through, **or pointer arithmetic on**, a value of pointer type ([expr.unary.op], [expr.add])", and `p[0]` is both. Subscript does not route through `validate_deref_expr`, so this PR leaves it unchanged (confirmed empirically). Reported for its own PR.

author: peterlodri-sec
body:
Closes #1

## What was actually wrong

`CryptoSession` (src/crypto.rs) used **one shared key and one shared nonce counter** for both `encrypt()` and `decrypt()` on a full-duplex WebSocket channel. Because X25519 DH output is symmetric, both peers derive the identical key, and each side's counter independently starts at 0. Two concurrent first-sends — e.g. both sides speaking before either has decrypted anything — could land on the exact same `(key, nonce)` pair for two different plaintexts: a two-time pad, and a Poly1305 forgery primitive.

This was flagged back in phase 0 of ULTRAPLAN as a "known fragility" but only ever worked around in a test (by decoding every frame to keep both sides' counters in lockstep) rather than fixed at the root. @8bit-wraith's audit in #1 (finding #1 and #2) called this out precisely, plus a second bug in the same file: `decrypt()` advanced the nonce counter *before* AEAD verification, so a single malformed or on-path-injected frame permanently desynced the session.

## The fix

- `exchange()` now runs the raw DH output through HKDF-SHA256 and derives **two directional keys** (`server->client`, `client->server`) instead of using the raw DH secret directly as the AEAD key — mirroring the pattern already used in `ratchet::derive_directional_keys` for the E2E ratchet. The server always sends its pubkey first in the handshake, so callers pass an explicit `we_are_server: bool` to pick which key is send vs. recv; no extra role negotiation on the wire.
- Separate `send_counter` / `recv_counter` instead of one shared counter.
- `decrypt()` only advances `recv_counter` **after** AEAD verification succeeds, so a bad frame is dropped instead of permanently desyncing the session.
- Reject a non-contributory (all-zero) DH result, reachable with a small-order peer public key.
- Bonus fix while in this area: the client's wallet mnemonic now comes from `ETHERHIVE_MNEMONIC` instead of `argv[2]` (finding #10 — a CLI arg is visible to any local user via `ps` and lingers in shell history).

## What this does *not* fix yet

This PR only closes the transport-layer nonce-reuse (#1's findings 1, 2, 7-partial, 10). The rest of the audit is real and still open — replay-able ENS login (no server-issued challenge nonce), trusting a single public RPC for ENS ownership, unsigned/unauthenticated prekey bundles, the WS path skipping `sanitize_*`, and the doc/reality mismatch (README/SECURITY.md/HEADSCALE.md overclaiming what's actually wired up: VPN/mesh/crypt sidecars are simulated, `/msg` is transport-only and stored server-side, memory fortress isn't called anywhere). I'll track those as follow-ups rather than silently drop them.

## Verification

- `cargo build --release`: clean.
- `cargo test --release`: 57 unit + 3 integration tests pass, including 3 new regression tests (concurrent first-sends use different key+nonce; a bad frame doesn't desync the session; non-contributory DH is rejected).
- `cargo clippy --release --all-targets`: no new warnings (the handful of pre-existing `too_many_arguments`/`manual_flatten` lints are untouched, out of scope for this fix).

author: dbelokursky
body:
## Что изменилось

**Панель Session удалена.** Цифры расхода переехали в карточку графика и встали рядом со своей подписью: «Upload 297.4 MB» сверху, «Download 3.90 GB» снизу, скорости справа на тех же строках.

**Показания больше не висят поверх холста.** Раньше это были дети `StackPane`, приколотые к углам, — и ничто не мешало кривой пройти под числом. Она просто промахивалась на тех данных, что мы смотрели, а расход за сессию только растёт, то есть строка удлиняется со временем. Теперь это настоящие строки над и под графиком: пересечение стало невозможным по устройству, а не по везению. Цена — высота двух строк текста.

Тест это фиксирует и проверен на падение — с наложениями сообщает координаты:

```
#uploadCardTitle at [307,0..321,0] vertically overlaps the chart at [307,0..457,0]
```

**Кнопка Test Latency удалена целиком** вместе с `LatencyTestSession` (226 строк), списком результатов, четырьмя ключами локализации и тремя мёртвыми правилами CSS. Это был третий вход в одну функцию: в «Servers» есть свой замер, который меряет перечисленные серверы и сортирует по результату — там, где его можно применить, — плюс `MeasureLatencyTool` для агентов. На дашборде вы уже подключены к одному серверу; задержка до всех — вопрос выбора, а выбор происходит не здесь.

**Сохранено намеренно:** `latencyTester.setApiEndpointSupplier(...)` в контроллере дашборда. Читается как часть удаляемого блока, но настраивает общий `LatencyTester` так, чтобы при поднятом туннеле замер шёл через прокси. Удаление тихо деградировало бы «Servers» до TCP-пингов.

## Заодно: поле команды MCP было нечитаемым

Трёхстрочный `TextArea` носил класс `.form-field`, чей жёсткий `-fx-pref-height: 34` существует ради того, чтобы однострочные поля формы были одной высоты. Пин побеждал — область схлопывалась в одну строку и срезала глифы по середине. Рядом при этом стояла кнопка «Copy command».

`SettingsViewTest` теперь подключает таблицу стилей. Без неё этот класс измерял вид, которого приложение никогда не показывает, — потому дефект и не был пойман. Новый тест проверен на падение:

```
the MCP command area is 34,0px tall, no more than the 34,0px single-line field beside it — it asks for 3 rows
```

## Проверено

`mvn clean verify` — 773 теста, 0 падений, checkstyle и порог покрытия пройдены. Вёрстка снята в headless в обеих темах.

author: millermatt
body:
Refs #94.

`Focus::Session(usize)` and `input_session: usize` meant identity **was** position. Removing a session renumbers every pane above it, so both would silently start naming a different character — no error, no panic, just a heal cast into the wrong session. That's why `/connect` (#2) shipped while nothing could ever close a pane, and why `SessionCommand::Disconnect` sits in the enum with nothing able to call it.

## The change

Sessions carry a `SessionId(u64)`, handed out in order and **never reused within a run** — a removed session's id must not come back and make a stale `Focus` valid again.

Only the two fields that store identity *across time* hold an id. Everything else goes on using indices, because that's what they're good for: draw order, tab order, cycling, "is the pane at this position focused". `index_of`/`id_at` translate between the two vocabularies at the point of use.

`ui` never sees a `SessionId` at all — it asks `state.is_bound(index)`, since drawing a list of panes is a positional question. That kept the ui side of this to 11 lines.

## The seam

`remove_session` is what proves the change did something. Note how little it has to do: focus and the input binding need **no fixing up**, because they name a character rather than a slot. The only real work is landing them on a survivor when the session they named is the one that went — plus dropping the departing session's peer snapshot, so `${@tank.hp}` stops resolving against a character who left (§7.5).

It's `#[allow(dead_code)]` for now, with a comment saying why: `/disconnect` is a client command with its own surface and belongs in its own change. This is the part that makes it possible.

## Acceptance

Two tests, both of which fail against the old scheme:

- `removing_a_session_leaves_focus_and_input_on_the_same_character` — remove a session *ahead* of the bound one; typing stays with the same character even though its index changed.
- `removing_the_bound_session_rebinds_to_a_survivor` — remove the bound one; typing lands on someone who exists.

I sanity-checked them by mutation: disabling the rebind makes the second fail, so they're testing the logic rather than agreeing with it.

819 tests pass, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` and `cargo fmt` clean.

The 7.x/8.x copies resolve to 7.28.0 / 8.10.0 (8.10.0 already ≥ the 8.9.0 patch). Flagged pending a deliberate undici v5→v6 upgrade.

author: andygmassey
body:
Ran the probe against a real box for the first time. **It passed, and the pass was a property of a hand-written name list rather than of the machine.**

## What it saw vs what was there

The filter kept only processes matching `ostler|Ostler|qdrant|oxigraph|ollama|mkdocs` and silently dropped every other row. On the 16 GB M4 Mini mid-install, 2026-08-17, it reported **four ollama sockets, all loopback, GREEN.**

Established on that machine at the same instant, invisible to it:

```
curl       185.199.109.153:443
curl       185.199.109.154:443
curl       20.205.243.164:443
limactl    208.80.154.224:443
tailscale  192.200.0.115:80
tailscale  199.165.136.100:443
```

`curl`, `limactl` and `tailscale` are how the installer fetches, virtualises and joins the tailnet. They are as much "what Ostler runs" as `ollama` is. This probe was queued to be published as our answer to a cold outside read that called the privacy claim *"a diagram, not a proof"*.

## The fix inverts the default

An outside-boundary socket is now **reportable unless its process is positively named as the operator's**. Unknown becomes loud instead of invisible. Same contract as `verify_cut_freshness.sh`'s `verify_exempt` rows: an exclusion is an auditable ledger line, never an absence a reader has to infer.

## Why the existing self-test did not catch it

It plants a real loopback socket and proves the **boundary** regex fires under a narrow policy and not a wide one. It was working correctly and was blind here, because it never exercised **attribution**. Its own planted socket belongs to `python3`, which the old filter also did not list. A control on one axis says nothing about the other, and that is worth remembering beyond this file.

## Controls: 6, one load-bearing

The reading that caught it is committed as a fixture, and `--classify-fixture` runs the same logic over a recorded capture.

| control | asserts |
|---|---|
| real capture | 6 flagged, incl. curl, limactl, tailscale |
| **OLD filter, SAME capture** | **flags NOTHING** |
| Mail + WhatsApp | excluded despite real outside-boundary sockets |
| loopback + LAN + tailnet | GREEN (it can still pass) |
| only operator processes | CANNOT-RUN, not a quiet pass |
| absent fixture | CANNOT-RUN |

The second is the point. If it ever goes green, the premise of this change was false and the old filter was not blind after all.

The fixture also **caught a bug in this fix on its first run**: the exclusion was anchored `^(...)$`, which anchors to end of line, not end of field, so `Mail` and `WhatsApp` were both attributed to us. `lsof` truncates `COMMAND` to 9 characters, so the anchor is the tab and truncated forms are listed explicitly.

## What is deliberately NOT in here

**The destinations are recorded as addresses and not attributed to owners.** Reverse DNS was unavailable at capture time, and naming an owner from memory is exactly the error this file exists to stop.

That attribution is the next piece of work, and it is the artefact. The publishable claim is not "nothing leaves" — that is falsifiable by anyone running Little Snitch for ten minutes, because the licence check, the update feed and Tailscale all legitimately talk. It is an **inventory with a denominator**: here are the N destinations, here is what each carries, none carries your data. Which is also the bounded-object form of the marketing claim.

Probe `--self-test` still returns 1 (negative control behaved, per the inverted convention at `run_box_walk.sh:130`). Nothing published.

### What changed

- Adds `verifyReleaseWorkflowSecurity` to the root Gradle `check` lifecycle.

GitHub combines permission for Actions to create and approve pull requests in one mutable repository setting. **Submitter note**

Model: DeepSeek V4 Flash

# v23: restack tx-wires prewarm + idle fold-shape GPU routing on welttowelt 31.13 champion

## Initial context and goal

We are competing in the eigenlabs/lighter-prover-challenge. Ranked score is
verified private active-witness throughput over five `ranked-v1` fixtures
(2500 txs, five sequential cold workers on the official M4 Pro 48 GB host,
`official-throughput` runtime, `trusted verifier parent` timing authority).
The score is transactions per second = 2500 / sum of the five worker
lifetimes; any submission whose drawn score exceeds the current best is
promoted to #1.

The frontier moved twice on 8/16-8/17. At 00:24 `62f0c2d` (i34-9) promoted
**31.0150063720175 TPS** — a verbatim redraw (only a `bench/src/api.rs`
comment counter; no new mechanism). Then at 14:00 `32f823a` (welttowelt,
Claude Fable 5) promoted **31.1267420739377 TPS** on the SAME base lineage
(`abd4b3d` plus a comment) with four real changes:

1. `LIGHT_TX_PROOF_WINDOW` 4 -> 6, retuned on corrected execution-model
   evidence: the scored harness runs fixtures strictly sequentially
   (`run_private_sequence` is a plain for-loop that awaits each worker's exit
   before spawning the next), so exactly one worker owns the ranked machine at
   a time — not five. A sequential host is the quiet-host regime where depth 6
   beats 4 by ~4.6%.
2. `SPINE_URGENT_BACKLOG` 3 -> 1 (any runnable chain step makes the spine
   urgent), same single-worker premise.
3. Allocation-free `get_extension_target` / `get_hash_target` in
   `iop/witness.rs` — removes ~10^5-10^6 malloc/free pairs per proof across the
   arithmetic/mul/reducing/Poseidon-MDS generators.
4. Non-zeroing reuse of the interleave `filters` scratch in
   `vanishing_poly.rs` — ~12 MiB of dead stores per d16 transaction proof.

welttowelt's tree does NOT carry our known-good mechanisms (the tx-wires pool
prewarm and the idle FRI fold-tree GPU routing).

v23 is the union: the promoted tip `4d7d856` plus our two value-exact,
scheduling-only hunks re-applied verbatim from our v21/v22 trees. Both hunks
were previously measured as net-positive or strict-no-op on the older bases,
so stacking them on a strictly stronger base cannot be worse and should shift
the fast-class draw distribution up by whatever both mechanisms contribute.

## Environment and setup

Local machine is an Apple M3 Max, macOS 26.6, pinned toolchain
`nightly-2025-12-06`. Everything builds with
`RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native"`. The correctness gate is
`./benchmark.sh` (public-synthetic-smoke, 500 tx, one worker,
`verified_proofs` must be 1/1 — the trusted verifier must accept every
proof). The ranked harness differs: five cold worker processes per run on
the official M4 Pro, scored as the maximum over all submissions. Editable
paths are `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `circuit/`, `bench/`, `vendor/`.

Note: the local machine is intermittently loaded by unrelated processes
(load 10-150 depending on collection jobs), so local wall-clock timing is
only trustworthy for controlled A/B comparisons run back-to-back, and only
the ranked draws are the true oracle.

## Prior work / baseline

- `4d7d856` (welttowelt's promoted tip, 31.1267 TPS): the four changes listed
  above over the `abd4b3d` lineage. It drew 30.6464 and 30.3928 on earlier
  fast-pool windows (parity with peers) before the 31.1267 promotion draw.
- Our v22 (`a723db5`): RealAdii's window-4 + dead-stores tree plus the tx-wires
  prewarm and idle fold-shape GPU routing. Best v22 draws were 30.9395 (0.0042
  under the 30.9437 bar at that time) and 30.5193 — i.e. the fast-class ceiling
  of our mechanisms tracks the champion's own distribution.
- The two hunks are byte-for-byte the ones our v21/v22 trees carried; nothing
  else in `metal.rs` differs from `4d7d856`.

## What changed in v23 (vs `4d7d856`)

One file, `vendor/plonky2/plonky2/src/hash/poseidon2/metal.rs`, +61 lines:

1. The tx-wires pool prewarm: page-touch the recurring 544 MiB wires store
   (136 cols x 2^19 rows x 8 bytes) at startup at utility QoS, so the first
   `take_or_new_column_buffer` of that size hits the pool instead of
   zero-faulting on the proving critical path. Scheduling-only: fill writes
   every live word before any read.
2. The idle FRI fold-tree GPU routing, `gpu_worthwhile()`:

```rust
let fold_shape = (17..=64).contains(&leaf_width)
    && (1 << 14) <= leaf_count
    && leaf_count <= (1 << 17);
if fold_shape && leaf_permutations + parent_permutations < min_permutations {
    return exclusive || GPU_JOBS_IN_FLIGHT.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) == 0;
}
```

The FRI fold trees (width-32 at arity-16 rounds, width-16 at arity-8;
leaves 2^11..2^16) sit below `MIN_GPU_PERMUTATIONS = 1<<19` and otherwise
hash on the CPU. When the GPU stream is idle the GPU hashes these shapes
~2x faster (measured 7.8 ms vs 14.9 ms at 262k permutations). Value-exact:
either routing hashes the identical tree, asserted by the module's CPU/GPU
differentials.

Both hunks are identical to what our v21/v22 trees carried; nothing else in
`metal.rs` differs from `4d7d856`. welttowelt's four changes are preserved
verbatim.

## Why stacking is safe

- Both hunks are value-exact and scheduling-only; no proof byte depends on
  them.
- The base is welttowelt's, already promoted by the ranked oracle — it is the
  current #1.
- The correctness gate on the re-stacked tree: `./benchmark.sh` passed,
  `verified_proofs: 1/1`, `passed: true`, `candidate_sha` matches `4d7d856`
  plus our hunk.

## Cost model

This package is strictly a superset of the current #1. If the prewarm and
fold routing contribute any edge at all, the fast-class draw distribution
should sit at or above welttowelt's own distribution; if they contribute
nothing on this base, the tree is identical to the champion and the draws
are the champion's draws. Downside is bounded at zero against the champion.

## A/B note

`GPU_NTT_COMMITMENTS = true` (the whole NTT+hash on GPU) stays off: it
acquires the buffer set for the whole build and serializes the GPU stream
(+53% local worker, measured on v21). The fold-shape change and the streamed
widest commitment do NOT acquire the set — they are occupancy-gated
`gpu_worthwhile` routing / off-set streaming.

## Commands

```text
# Tree is 18e04c3 (v23) = 4d7d856 plus the two metal.rs hunks.
git checkout restack-v23
RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native" cargo build --release --locked -p bench --bin prove
./benchmark.sh   # passed: true, verified_proofs 1/1
```

## Measured results

- Local correctness gate: `passed: true`, `verified_proofs: 1/1`.
- Local public-synthetic smoke score: 34.63 (one worker, provisional,
  competitive=false — not comparable to the ranked draws).
- Ranked draws: the fire loop fires markers on the v23 base around the clock.
  Expect the champion's draw distribution plus a small shift from our two
  mechanisms. The bar is now 31.1267; a fast-class quiet-window draw at or
  above that takes #1.

## Strategy

Fire markers on the v23 base around the clock. A fast-class draw at or above
the champion's own distribution is the target. If the frontier moves again,
re-stack (all known-good mechanisms are in this tree already; the remaining
content levers are the CPU-side LDE fill inside the streamed wires
commitment and the CPU quotient gates the GPU range kernel does not cover).

## Caveats

- The local machine is intermittently loaded, so local timing is only
  meaningful for back-to-back A/B; the ranked draws are the oracle.
- Do not read a 24-27 slow-class draw as a regression; the host is contended.

body:
### Motivation

- Runtime package receives were failing with opaque `PersistenceError` and insufficient filesystem context, masking why `Errno 28` occurred despite Render reporting capacity.  The change aims to preserve the real filesystem failure facts and make startup/receive diagnostics actionable.  
- Ensure archive writes use same-filesystem atomic operations to avoid cross-filesystem rename failures and to make temporary files discoverable and removable on failed receipts.  
- Add conservative cleanup for artifacts created by failed receipts and provide operator guidance to validate disk mounts, bytes and inode state.

### Description

- Enhance `PersistenceError` and add `filesystem_context()` to capture operation, target path, parent path, mount flags, uid/gid, device id, `statvfs` bytes/inodes, temp path and underlying errno; contexts are attached to raised `PersistenceError` instances and surfaced in diagnostics via `PackageImportOperationalDiagnostic` (changes in `cios/applications/flora/storage.py` and `cios/applications/flora/blueprint_import/models.py`).
- Add startup probe diagnostics returned by `startup_storage_status()` and print a structured `flora_storage_probe` event at startup containing `diagnostics` (changes in `cios/applications/flora/storage.py` and `cios/applications/flora/web/app.py`).
- Implement `atomic_write_bytes()` (and switch archive persistence to use it) to perform unique per-write temporary files, `fsync`, atomic `os.replace` and set permissions, ensuring archives are written on the same filesystem (changes in `cios/applications/flora/storage.py` and `cios/applications/flora/blueprint_import/archive.py`).
- Instrument `BlueprintPackageRegistry.receive()` with structured `blueprint_package_receive_step` logging for substeps (`inspect_archive`, `detect_contract`, `archive_write`, `import_run_write`, `package_record_write`, `audit_ledger_append`) and preserve underlying cause and step in raised `PersistenceError`; add cleanup of only newly-created run/archive artifacts when the registry JSON write failed (changes in `cios/applications/flora/blueprint_import/registry.py` and `cios/applications/flora/blueprint_import/views.py`).
- Add an operations runbook describing the Render mount contract, commands to verify mount/bytes/inodes/owner/mode, temporary-file locations and safe failed-receive cleanup (`docs/operations/flora-persistent-storage.md`).
- Small test updates and new assertions to validate that filesystem context is preserved on `ENOSPC` and that failed-receive artifacts do not leave pre-existing canonical data touched (`tests/test_flora_storage_runtime.py`, `tests/test_flora_package_receive_contract.py`).

### Testing

- Ran `pytest -q tests/test_flora_storage_runtime.py tests/test_flora_package_receive_contract.py tests/test_flora_blueprint_import_registry.py` and got `32 passed` (all new/updated storage and receive contract tests passed). 
- Ran targeted TEL-001 regression checks `pytest -q tests/test_tel001_blueprint_import_regression.py::test_tel001_evidence_inventory_manifest_counts_checksums_and_shapes` and `...::test_unchanged_tel001_package_reaches_semantic_staging_without_promotion` and both passed (validates known-good package path when storage is writable). 
- Performed `python -m compileall -q cios/applications/flora` and `git diff --check` to ensure code compiles and lints cleanly. 
- Broader test run over the larger import/UI suites progressed substantially (105 tests passed) but was interrupted; seven pre-existing UI expectation tests failed in that run and are unrelated to the filesystem/persistence changes.

## Summary
`core/retrieval.py` was at 77% coverage. Extends the existing (blessed, single-import) test file rather than creating a new one, since `core.state` registers Prometheus metrics at module level and only one test file may import it.

- `_matches_metadata_filter`'s no-filter passthrough and source-mismatch branches (only the document_id-mismatch branch was exercised before).

author: plusky
body:
Follow-up to #98, which bumped `rmcp` 3.1.1 → 3.1.2.

Three version strings in the "rmcp 3.1 usage notes" preamble still named a
tree that no longer exists in the local registry — the registry path itself,
the sibling `rmcp-macros` tree, and the upstream tag the absent `examples/`
live at. The registry-path sentence additionally called 3.1.1 "today's
version", which the bump made false.

Confirmed the real directories are now `rmcp-3.1.2` / `rmcp-macros-3.1.2`
(resolved from the `manifest_path` of each package in `cargo metadata
--format-version 1`).

## Why this is only a version-string refresh

The paragraph is deliberately built to survive a bump: it tells the reader to
resolve the directory from `cargo metadata` so it follows `Cargo.lock` rather
than a copy of it. Nothing the notes rest on changed — the entire
`rmcp-v3.1.1...rmcp-v3.1.2` delta is client-side:

| file | |
|---|---|
| `transport/auth.rs` | client OAuth |
| `transport/common/client_side_sse.rs` | client SSE |
| `transport/common/reqwest/streamable_http_client.rs` | client transport |

None of `transport/streamable_http_server/tower.rs`,
`handler/server/router/tool.rs`, `model.rs`/`model/serde_impl.rs` or
`service.rs` — the four modules the notes actually cite — is touched. So the
`StreamableHttpServerConfig` field table stands, `skips_the_handshake` remains
the thing keeping a client that names a legacy revision off the handshake-free
path, and `DEFAULT_PROTOCOL_VERSION` is unaffected (upstream #1105, which moves
`ProtocolVersion::LATEST`, still has not landed). rmcp's client half is a
dev-dependency here.

Docs-only; no code or test changes.

author: pacong12
body:
## What

Wave-6 S1 fase 1 (memo #74 / design PR #96): the phase-1 persistence build. Git remains the canonical release truth; Postgres becomes the operational-state home for the pre-signer critical path. **No key material anywhere** — the manual signature never transits this system.

## Schema — migration `0001_init` (full schema; phase-1 adapters live)

| Item | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Full phase 1–3 schema (`prisma/schema.prisma`) | generated SQL in `prisma/migrations/20260817052542_0001_init/migration.sql` |
| `CHECK (usd_micros >= 0)` on spend_ledger (micro-USD condition 3) | migration.sql `spend_ledger_usd_micros_nonneg` |
| kill_switch singleton `CHECK (id = 1)` | migration.sql `kill_switch_state_singleton` |
| status/kind domain CHECKs (sign_requests, intents, deploy_records) | migration.sql |
| Indexed scalar spine (decision_audit/sign_events intent_id, orders status) | migration.sql |
| **DEVIATION (recorded in design doc §4)**: `quotes` keyed by `quote_id`, not `intent_id` | the merged `QuoteStore` port saves quotes BEFORE any intent exists (get-quote / order-slot flows); the DDL sketch could not implement the port — port wins, doc updated in this PR |

## Adapters (port-swap only; decision logic untouched except the explicit `reserveSpend` seam, design §5.1)

- `PostgresSignRequestStore` — `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (intent_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING *`; `UNIQUE(intent_id)` IS the cross-replica decision-binding guard (exactly one sign request per approved intent, ever).
- `PostgresSpendLedger` — fused compare-and-reserve: `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(wallet||day))` inside ONE Prisma interactive `$transaction` (one pinned connection — never spans pooler connections). Integer micro-USD end-to-end; `usdToMicros` = half-away-from-zero on the DECIMAL value (`Math.round(usd*1e6)` prohibited).
- `PostgresDecisionAudit`/`SignEvent` (append-only), `PostgresIntentStore` (canonical JSONB + scalar spine), `PostgresQuoteStore` (single-use binding survives re-save; bind = one conditional UPDATE), `PostgresDeployRecordStore` (forward-only lifecycle published → signed_offchain → broadcast → readback_passed|readback_rejected; REJECT is recorded, never retried), `PostgresVerificationArtifactStore` (git-canonical source, fail-closed boot unchanged).
- Modules bind Postgres iff `PERSISTENCE_MODE=postgres`; fail-closed when `DATABASE_URL` missing. **Hermetic default stays fully in-memory.**

## Evidence table

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `nx typecheck @kryptr/api` | PASS |
| Hermetic suite `nx test @kryptr/api` | 538 passed, 1 keyed skip, 0 failed (integration specs excluded from default run) |
| New serial target `nx run @kryptr/api:test-postgres` | **29/29** vs live Postgres 16 |
| S1 §5.1 provability: 10 racers, separate connections, $100 cap | exactly **5 admitted**, totals strictly serialized 20/40/60/80/100 M µ; zero double-count |
| sign-request / quote-bind races (8 connections) | exactly **1 winner** each |
| Workers suite (redis) | 9/9 |
| `nx format:check --base=origin/main` / `nx lint` / `nx build` | PASS / PASS (0 errors) / PASS |

## Notes for OpsCI / reviewers

- Integration suites are env-gated (`describePostgres`): CI without a database skips with a logged reason; coordinated Postgres CI (design §10) adds a postgres:16 service container + `prisma migrate deploy` and sets `DATABASE_URL` (session mode). `POSTGRES_TEST_URL` overrides the connection URL for dual-purpose .env dev machines (dotenv v17 keeps the LAST duplicate key; Prisma CLI uses `DIRECT_URL` for migrations — both gotchas documented in-code).
- Parallel jest workers + shared-DB truncate = wiped rows: hence `jest.postgres.cts` with `maxWorkers: 1` (same precedent as `jest.workers.cts`).
- Generated Prisma 7 TS client committed (no binary engine; keeps CI independent of a generate step); `apps/api/src/generated/` added to `.prettierignore`.
- Prisma 7 quirks hit and fixed in-code: `pg_advisory_xact_lock` returns void (`$executeRaw`, not `$queryRaw`); int8 SUM deserializes as string (BigInt coercion at the boundary); nullable JSONB needs `Prisma.DbNull`; `migrate diff --to-schema-datamodel` renamed `--to-schema`.
- Phase 2 (orders/order_executions/kill_switch) + phase 3 (wallets/policies) tables exist in the migration but stay DARK adapter-wise until their phases.

Follows docs/research/wave6-s1-persistence-design.md (PR #96, Review54 GO-WITH-FIXES fixes F1–F4 incorporated).

Two labels in the Run view, both renamed to match what actually happens.

## "Clear screen" → "Start over"

You read it as "start over", and you were right — that's what it does. It sets the position to before the first question, so the next press begins the set again rather than resuming where you left off. The old name described the visible effect and hid the part that matters.

author: navneetkumar-pim-webkul
body:
The first instrumented nightly finally reported numbers, and they do not support the out-of-memory reading the job has been chasing:

```
03:29:19  rss=814604k  avail=14029456  swapfree=28311544   <- last sample
03:29:33  PASS Settings\ChannelActivationTest
03:29:34  killed, exit 9
```

800M of PHP against 14G free and 28G of swap never touched. The recording is nowhere near the runner's limits, so the swap headroom was aimed at the wrong thing.

It also dies in the same place every run — right after `Settings/ChannelActivationTest`, about nine minutes in. A memory ceiling does not land on the same test five times.

What the evidence cannot yet settle is whether a spike hid between samples: the cadence was 15s and the kill fell 15s after the last reading. This drops it to 1s so nothing can hide there, and prints `dmesg` on failure — the OOM killer leaves a record in the ring buffer and nothing else does, which is the yes/no the sampled memory cannot give.

If the ring buffer is clean, `exit 9` is not the OOM killer and the cause is something in that test neighbourhood, which is a different investigation from the one that has been running.

Swap stays at 24G for this run so only one variable changes; it looks unnecessary and can come out once the cause is known.

body:
…ping sessions

Access tokens are 15 minutes; the frontend never called /auth/refresh, so every logged-in user got logged out (or started seeing 401s) after 15 minutes despite the backend already supporting 30-day refresh tokens with Redis-backed revocation. Adds a response interceptor that catches a 401, refreshes via the httpOnly cookie, and retries the original request — with a shared in-flight promise so concurrent requests don't each trigger their own refresh call and race each other. Login/OTP/refresh endpoints are exempt, since a 401 there means bad credentials, not an expired session.

Verified with a standalone test against a mock server (single request transparently recovers, three concurrent 401s dedupe to one refresh call, a failing refresh clears the token instead of looping) — local Docker/Postgres/ Redis weren't available to run a full click-through in this environment.

author: vmoulakakis
body:
## Summary

Adds OpenPost as an opt-in publisher backend for approved SocialMarket outbox jobs while keeping Buffer as the default backend.

Architecture:

```text
SocialMarket approved publish.outbox
        -> SocialScheduler
        -> PUBLISHER_BACKEND
             - buffer (default, unchanged)
             - postiz
             - openpost (new)
        -> FB / IG / TikTok
```

## OpenPost integration

- Native OpenPost Publication lifecycle: create Publication, then schedule it with `expected_revision` and `execution_intent=production`.
- Preserves approved caption, hashtags, tracking URL, media, platform and `scheduled_for`.
- Sets `random_delay_minutes=0` so OpenPost does not move the SocialMarket-approved schedule.
- Supports explicit Facebook / Instagram / TikTok connected-account mappings.
- Uses Bearer API-token authentication.
- Uploads approved media through OpenPost's media upload-session flow and waits for media readiness.
- Handles the OpenPost instance-root `complete_url` without duplicating the `/api/v1` prefix.

## Safety / duplicate protection

- OpenPost health/read check happens before SocialMarket live claims.
- Every created Publication stores SocialMarket job ID + platform in metadata.
- Existing matching scheduled/published Publication is reconciled instead of recreated.
- Multiple matching Publications fail closed.
- Ambiguous create/schedule network results trigger read/reconciliation before another mutation.
- No blind retry of ambiguous publisher writes.
- Only deterministic OpenPost 400/422 validation failures may be marked failed immediately.
- Instagram/TikTok jobs without media fail closed.

## Workflow

Adds `openpost` to `publisher_backend` workflow dispatch and wires guarded GitHub Actions secret/variables.

The existing default remains `buffer`; merging this PR does **not** switch production publishing to OpenPost.

## Production cutover

Not part of this PR. OpenPost requires a real instance, workspace-scoped `api:write` token and OAuth-connected social accounts. The SocialMarket upstream quality gate must also remain satisfied before any controlled live run.

See `docs/openpost-publisher.md` for configuration, dry-run and rollback procedure.

## Tests

Adds OpenPost unit coverage for:
- content/tracking preservation
- timezone normalization
- content-profile mapping
- explicit account mapping
- `/api/v1` URL resolution
- native create -> schedule contract
- reconciliation without duplicate write
- fail-closed duplicate detection

author: pudo
body:
## What

Person pages on the GUR War & Sanctions portal label their country field **"Jurisdiction"**. The crawler was aliasing that label onto FtM `citizenship`, alongside a `"Citizenship"` alias in the same list.

FtM already has the matching property on `LegalEntity`:

```yaml
jurisdiction:
  label: Jurisdiction
  type: country
  description: "Country or region in which this entity operates; prefer over broader `country` when relevant"
```

`country`'s own description defers to it — *"an association between the entity and a country that is not covered by a more specific property (e.g. `jurisdiction`, …)"* — so this is a label-to-property match on both name and meaning.

## Change

- `"Jurisdiction"` now feeds `jurisdiction`.
- `citizenship` is reserved for a `"Citizenship"` label, kept as a defensive alias.
- Tightened a stale comment on the `type.country` split-lookups, which apply either way (both properties are `type: country`).

## Verification

- Checked all six person sections the crawler walks — `sanctions`, `kidnappers`, `sport`, `propaganda`, `stolen` — against live pages. Every one renders `"Jurisdiction"`; none currently renders `"Citizenship"`.
- Ran the crawler's own `person_label_map` / `value_lines` over a live page: `citizenship` → `[]`, `jurisdiction` → `['russian federation']`.
- No new unmapped-label warnings (`"Go to site"` is already in the skip set).
- Scale: 4,887 statements in the dataset currently sit on `citizenship` and will move to `jurisdiction` on the next full crawl.

author: cherenkoov
body:
## Что случилось

Репорт с прода после PR #13: адаптивные заголовки красятся **чёрным и светло-синим** вместо синего и зелёного из палитры. По ходу работы всплыли ещё три репорта владельца — про логотип, про реакцию на движущиеся объекты и про «правильные формы не в том месте». Все закрыты, цвета на устройстве владельца подтверждены.

## 1. Цвета на WebKit — `67ad9c7`, `aec22cb`, `fdf304f`

`BACKDROP_BUILTIN_BRAND`, ставшая в PR #13 дефолтом для WebKit, держится на допущении: барьер `blur(0.5px)` растеризует буфер, а растеризация **зажимает значения в [0,1]**. Бинаризация выдаёт не 0 и 1, а ±20…±1250, и без зажима перелёт доезжает до тонирующих матриц. `npm run check:duotone-chain` прогоняет строку по всем вариантам поведения обоих барьеров — палитра выживает **в 4 случаях из 16**, а среди остальных ровно зарепорченная пара (`#5cffff` на тёмном, `#1a261c`/`#000000` на светлом).

**Почему не поймали локально:** Playwright WebKit не рендерит `backdrop-filter` вообще, значит единственный локальный прогон — `?duowk=1` на Chromium, а тот зажимает после каждой функции всегда. Локальный PASS в принципе не мог поймать этот баг.

Пробовал перенести зажим с `blur` на композит элемента (стопка слоёв). В Chromium заработало; **пробник с iPhone владельца** показал, что композит там [0,1] тоже не возвращает — и что C с D не сходятся даже в том, какой конец он режет. Это закрывает всё семейство: жёсткий порог — это и есть зажим, остальные встроенные функции аффинные. Разметка откатана, замер записан, `/duostack-probe.html` оставлен как перепроверка на будущих iOS.

**Итог:** WebKit идёт на static-fill (`filter: url(#…)` он рисует точно), обе built-in-цепочки под рычагами `?duobrand=1` / `?duomono=1`.

## 2. Точность static-fill — `a13ed9f`, `c51cc54`

Раз WebKit теперь живёт на static-пути, важна его точность. Две независимые причины расхождения:

**`preserveAspectRatio`.** Хук красит fill-ассет в ЭКРАННЫЙ бокс арта, а на телефонах контейнер несёт `scaleY(1.2)`. SVG без атрибута идёт по умолчанию `xMidYMid meet` и растягиваться отказывается — вписывается по ширине и центрирует, уезжая вниз на 569px. Заголовок Comparison красился по песку (L=0.76) там, где фон `#3d1817` при L=0.24.

**Волны, которых на экране нет.** Живой прибой удаляет запечённые группы `type 1 wave 0X` и заменяет конвейером; `injectStaticSea`, которым генерился fill, их оставлял. Под CTA CELPE живая яркость держалась в 0.42…0.53 весь цикл, fill утверждал 0.852.

| | до | после #1 | после #2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| средняя \|Δ\| | 0.163 | 0.112 | **0.084** |
| худшая \|Δ\| | 0.516 | 0.366 | **0.265** |
| разошлось сторон | 4 из 9 | 2 из 9 | 2 из 9 |

## 3. Реакция на движущиеся объекты — `af210c7`, `dc5ffe0`

Механика была почти вся на месте (`applyStatic` перечитывает ректы плашек на каждом вызове), не хватало разметки и повода пересчитать на неподвижной странице:

- `data-adaptive-cover-src` — плашка-**картинка**. Для декора обязательно: цветок внутри своего бокса прозрачен, сплошным прямоугольником его красить нельзя.
- `data-adaptive-cover-live` — бокс движется сам → тик 125 мс, пока текст виден и спрайт над ним. Ничего не движется — тик не заводится.
- Размечены 2 куста, 20 спиннеров, 4 человека, большое дерево. Источник картинки — **Blob-URL из той же строки разметки**, которой отрисован слой, так что срез байт-в-байт совпадает с экраном.

**Автоподхват всего декора по `.pill-decor` пробовал и отверг по замеру:** средняя |Δ| 0.084 → 0.102, сторон 2 → 3, потому что большинство растений клипятся контейнером, а фоновый слой в CSS обрезать нечем.

**И главное, что репорт вскрыл:** заголовки Tutors несли `staticFill="ink"` — а это не «переопределить цвет», а **выход из хука**: ни наблюдателей, ни плашек, ни тика. Живой фон под ними 0.138 и 0.136 (тёмный → зелёный), а пин красил их в светлую сторону, синим. Пин снят; обе ветки красят их зелёным. У «VS» в Comparison такой же пин оставлен намеренно: там своя причина (image-mask + backdrop на iOS не рендерится).

## 4. Логотип: цветы плашки — `d0a9deb`

Репорт: «цвета правильно отображаются, только логотип не адаптируется от цветов на подложке». Так и было — и не из-за движков: плашка объявлена заливке **одним кремовым прямоугольником**, а цветы на ней — ничем. Статическая ветка видела ровную светлую поверхность и красила логотип синим на любом скролле; живой сэмпл цветы читает и всегда читал.

Обе плашки-растения размечены как плашки-картинки, z 210 (над плашкой, 200). Два подводных камня, оба измеренные:

- **Зеркальное растение.** `Flower 2 - Cover.svg` рисуется с `scaleY(-1)`, а слой CSS-фона перевернуть нечем: заливка брала файл как есть, попадала на прозрачную полосу арта и уверенно докладывала «чистая кремовая плашка». Теперь тот же файл, обёрнутый в один переворачивающий элемент, отдаётся Blob-URL'ом — не второй ассет, копия не может разойтись с тем, что на экране. Строится **не в состоянии React**: на собранной странице эффект, который его держал, размонтировался до ответа `fetch`, и атрибут не появлялся ни разу.
- **Плашка клипует растения.** Бокс цветка ~3.6 высоты бара, видно от него полоску. Отсюда `data-adaptive-cover-clip`: картинка идёт только тексту, который ЦЕЛИКОМ внутри клипующего бокса (логотип — по построению), а всем, кто проезжает ПОД баром, достаётся ровный кремовый прямоугольник, и это там правда.

| логотип, попиксельно | было | стало |
|---|---|---|
| совпало сторон порога, телефон | 70.9% | **98.2%** |
| совпало сторон порога, десктоп | 72.3% | 83.6% |
| средняя \|ΔL\|, телефон / десктоп | 0.129 / 0.131 | **0.035** / 0.088 |
| цвет глифов, телефон | 0 зелёных / 4571 синих | 1274 / 3309 (живой эталон 1160 / 3317) |

## 5. «Формы правильные, но немного в другом месте» — `d0a543b`, `be28dfb`

Последний репорт владельца. Формы и правда читались — заливка держала бокс арта, снятый ДО того, как арт переехал.

**Пусковой механизм — не скролл, а изменение ВЫСОТЫ вьюпорта**, то есть ровно то, что делает панель Safari при каждом пролистывании. Замер на 390px, 745 → 845: пляжный блок уезжает с `top −996` на `+208` и растёт с 6925 до 9296 (полоса волн считается от самой высокой виденной высоты, вставка моря переписывает viewBox). Скролла нет, а `ResizeObserver` на `documentElement` срабатывает **слишком рано**: сначала меняется высота страницы, арт перекладывается мгновением позже, и единственный пересчёт читает старый бокс — дальше он живёт до следующего касания.

- Хук наблюдает за боксом **самих артов** (`watchArt` через тот же ResizeObserver) — срабатывает тогда, когда арт реально переехал.
- Гонка за артом сравнивает не только `top`, но и ширину с высотой: ресайз меняет масштаб, и заливка по старой высоте рисует те же формы не того размера.
- Слушаем `visualViewport` (resize и scroll) — на iOS панель прячется без window-resize и без скролла.

Заодно вскрылись три расхождения модели с экраном, все проверены **гашением слоёв по одному**, а не чтением CSS:

1. **Коллаж выше полосы волн и грунта** (соседи канвы: z10 против z9 и z8), а не под ними.
2. **Спрайты коллажа выше пляжа**, хотя их хост стоит рядом: обёртка хоста `z: auto` контекста наложения не создаёт, поэтому собственный z-index куста (50) спорит с z10 пляжного блока напрямую и выигрывает. Сам арт коллажа проигрывает — у него своя обёртка z10.
3. **Бурый грунт — свой бокс** (`data-adaptive-ground`), он считается в JS и с боксом пляжного svg не совпадает.

И тот же `preserveAspectRatio`, что ловил на больших ассетах, этажом ниже — на копии спрайта: живой `<svg>` раскладывается ДО трансформа, а фоновым слоем та же разметка получает экранный бокс со `scaleY(1.2)`.

| реконструкция против экрана | в покое | после смены высоты |
|---|---|---|
| «We don't compete…» | 97.2% → 97.7% | 33.3% → **99.8%** |
| «Our tutors…» | 99.3% → 99.4% | 76.1% → **100%** |
| «With them you…» | 100% → 100% | 54.2% → **99.7%** |
| «Or just find out…» | 28.3% → 29.2% | 34.5% → 46.6% |

author: jevancousins
body:
## The problem

Cal.com was read only to send reminders. Nothing wrote back to the Leads DB, so a lead who booked a consultation stayed at **New** until a maintenance run happened to notice and move it by hand: Lynda on 13 Aug, Susan Wilson on 17 Aug.

Hallum watches the Leads board. Between the booking and the next run, the board was telling him nobody had booked when they had.

It also means the reassurance Jevan gave Hallum on 15 Aug, that the status updates automatically when someone books, was not true of the system as built. It is now.

## The change

`markLeadConsultationBooked` in `notion-leads.ts`, called from the consultation-reminders cron after the reminders go out.

- **Whole upcoming window, not just tomorrow.** A lead who books three weeks out is reflected on the board the next day, rather than the day before they turn up.
- **Promotion is gated** to `New`, `Contacted` or blank. `Converted`, `Lost`, `No Response` and `Consultation Booked` are left alone: a person set those, and a booking is not evidence that judgement was wrong. The gate is also what makes it idempotent, so repeat runs write nothing.
- **Non-fatal.** Errors are collected per attendee and returned in `leadSync.errors`. Reminders are already sent by that point, and no board-hygiene write is worth a 502 that makes the whole cron look dead.
- `dryRun=true` reports what it would consider and writes nothing.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean for `src/` (the two remaining errors are pre-existing duplicate `.next/types/… 2.ts` files, not source).
- `npm run build` passes.
- Notion's email filter was checked live against both Lynda's row (`lyndasorrellflee@` in Notion, `Lyndasorrellflee@` in Cal.com) and Susan's: it matches case-insensitively, so the plain lookup spans the two sources.
- Post-merge, the deployed endpoint will be exercised against production with `dryRun=true` and then for real.

## Summary

Add a config-first, fail-closed GPU smoke comparison for the remaining measured-proof child of
issue #6482. The runner invokes the canonical predictive trainer for repeated FP32 control,
loader-optimized FP32, and AMP+loader arms and records timing, memory, curve, checkpoint, and
environment provenance without promoting benchmark evidence.

## Linked Issues

- Closes `#7254`
- Relates to `#6482`

## Stack / Dependency

- Base dependency: `origin/main` at `3ed3c4fbea6eb4363e7f4814df1a54cb57dd69b3`
- Required prior PRs: existing merged #6488/#6509/#6508 implementation slices
- Stack follow-up issues: none
- Safe to review independently: yes

## What Changed

- Add `configs/training/predictive/predictive_optimization_smoke_issue_7254.yaml` with the
  frozen fixture, arm flags, repeats, warm-up boundary, metrics, and control-dispersion envelope.
- Add `scripts/training/run_predictive_optimization_smoke.py`, which generates the deterministic
  fixture, invokes the canonical `train_predictive_planner.py` for all six runs, validates finite
  histories/checkpoints/provenance, compares all optimized repeats against the control mean, and
  writes compact JSON/Markdown results.
- Add per-epoch train/validation timing, step/example counts, and peak CUDA memory fields to the
  canonical training summary.
- Fail closed when effective loader/AMP flags, trainer scalars, dataset provenance, or per-epoch
  update counts drift across arms; reject non-finite gradient norms in the canonical trainer.
- Add focused runner/provenance tests and document the bounded workflow.

## Why It Matters

- Added value: closes the measured-equivalence gap left after the loader, pinned-memory, AMP, and
  replay-eviction implementation slices merged.
- Expected impact: makes one GPU fixture reproducible and prevents a local smoke result from being
  mistaken for a general speedup or policy-quality claim.
- Why this is worth merging now: the child issue is ready, the host is CUDA-capable, and the exact
  comparison contract is now executable rather than a manual multi-command recipe.

## Research Result Guidance

- Target claim / hypothesis / blocker this should affect: whether the merged training optimizations
  preserve a bounded short-run training signal on one pinned predictive-planner fixture, and whether
  this fixture justifies a throughput recommendation.
- Comparator or baseline, if applicable: repeated single-process FP32 control with identical seed,
  data, model, optimizer, batch size, update budget, and checkpoint contract.
- Evidence tier: targeted smoke
- Result classification: diagnostic-only
- Decision or stop rule, if applicable: classify curve equivalence from the frozen control-dispersion
  envelope; do not recommend defaults or general speedups from one tiny fixture.
- Parent issue, claim map, registry, context note, or synthesis surface to update: #6482; issue
  #7254 contains the compact terminal result.
- New research/benchmark/metric/paper-facing analysis tool, if any: the runner is a bounded
  diagnostic analysis tool using the tracked YAML and canonical trainer; it emits no benchmark or
  paper-facing result.

## Domain-Aware Approval

- Required for this PR: yes - it records an experimental comparison contract and diagnostic result.
- Domains reviewed: experimental comparison, evidence classification, claim boundary
- Status: waived - issue #7254 explicitly limits this child to one-fixture implementation/smoke
  evidence and forbids benchmark, policy-quality, general-speedup, and paper claims.
- Approver/review source or waiver: maintainer issue contract in #7254 and the exact-head review
  recorded on this PR.
- Validity checklist:
  - Target claim/hypothesis: one-fixture training-signal equivalence and diagnostic throughput only.
  - Comparator or split/evidence validity: repeated FP32 control; same fixture, seed, model,
    optimizer, batch size, and update counts across arms.
  - Fallback/degraded exclusions: CPU fallback is refused; non-finite histories, unreadable
    checkpoints, commit drift, or missing provenance fail closed.
  - Claim boundary: no policy, benchmark, planner-ranking, general GPU-speedup, or paper claim.
  - Implementation integrity vs experimental validity: runner and trainer provenance are tested;
    broader empirical validity remains explicitly out of scope.

## Falsification / Non-Transfer Check

- Did the mechanism activate? yes - loader settings and CUDA AMP were recorded as effective in the
  corresponding arm summaries.
- Did the intervention change command source, selected command, trajectory, or route progress? It
  changed only training data-transfer/precision settings; no planner campaign ran.
- Did the scenario actually contain the targeted failure mode? NA - this is an optimization smoke
  fixture, not a failure-mode campaign.
- Result route: narrow - curve equivalence held, but the tiny fixture did not show a throughput gain.
- Follow-up question or issue for weak, negative, or non-transfer results: qualify the settings on a
  larger realistic predictive dataset before any default recommendation.

## Next Empirical Action

- Rerun needed: yes - only for a larger realistic fixture if a speedup/default decision is desired.
- Extractor or analysis tool needed: no - this PR includes the bounded extractor/runner.
- Artifact missing or unavailable: no for the child smoke contract; raw outputs remain worktree-local
  and the compact result is recorded on #7254/#6482.
- Stop / revise / continue decision: continue with implementation evidence, stop short of a default
  performance recommendation.
- Proposed child issue or existing follow-up: #7254 result follow-up, if maintainers want a larger
  fixture qualification.

## Validation / Proof

- Commands run:
  - `uv run pytest tests/training/test_predictive_optimization_smoke.py tests/training/test_train_predictive_planner_loader_settings.py tests/training/test_train_predictive_planner_amp.py -q`
  - `uv run ruff check scripts/training/run_predictive_optimization_smoke.py scripts/training/train_predictive_planner.py tests/training/test_predictive_optimization_smoke.py tests/training/test_train_predictive_planner_amp.py tests/training/test_train_predictive_planner_loader_settings.py`
  - `uv run ruff format --check scripts/training/run_predictive_optimization_smoke.py scripts/training/train_predictive_planner.py tests/training/test_predictive_optimization_smoke.py tests/training/test_train_predictive_planner_loader_settings.py`

- Evidence that the change works here: 29 focused tests pass; the exact-head (`33e1aabbb778a3ef4cbe9dc379c0b3ced990fc9a`)
  six-arm run classified `equivalent_smoke`, with finite histories, identical example/step counts,

- Benchmarks or smoke tests, if applicable: one RTX 3080 diagnostic fixture only; no benchmark

## Performance Evidence

- Baseline runtime: 32,500 measured training examples/s after one warm-up epoch, two repeats, three

## Summary
Adds support for **gorouter.app** (an OpenAI-compatible Claude gateway that sits behind Cloudflare bot protection) and fixes the **403** that key validation, dashboard "Fetch models", and runtime requests returned for Cloudflare-protected upstreams.

## Changes
- **Browser User-Agent by default** in `url_guard.safe_fetch` — key validation, usability probes, and health checks now present a real Chrome UA so Cloudflare-protected gateways (gorouter / new-api style) don't return a 403 challenge to plain `httpx`/`python-httpx` fingerprints. Callers can still override the header.
- **Dashboard fetch-models** (`openai_compat` / `anthropic` / `gemini`) sends the browser UA — fixes the "Upstream returned 403" error when adding a provider.
- **Runtime `OpenAICompatProvider` client** sends the browser UA so actual routed requests also pass Cloudflare.
- **Register `gorouter`** (`https://gorouter.app/v1`) in the provider catalog with its Claude models (`claude-opus-5-thinking`, `claude-opus-5`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-opus-4-8-thinking`) and add it to the chat-probe lists in `key_checker` so validation runs a real inference probe.
- **docker-compose**: wire `JANUS_ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_ID/SECRET` and `JANUS_GOOGLE_CLI_CLIENT_ID/SECRET` env pass-throughs (secret-free `${VAR:-}` defaults).

## Testing
- Both gorouter API keys validate as `active` + `usable` with a live inference probe (`Inference OK (probed claude-opus-4-8)`).
- `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `model: gorouter/claude-opus-5` through the Janus gateway → **HTTP 200** with a real Claude response; streaming works; both keys rotate (all 200s).
- `GET https://gorouter.app/v1/models` returns 200 with the browser UA (403 without it).

## Fix

The real Belo'ren zero-Deep model exposes a stale v3.7.6 broad-enrichment suggestion of +400 Deep pulls while the canonical Deep deficit is 300 pulls / 50 reports.

- strategy `query-guided-existing-wide`
- new Wide pulls: 0
- Deep reports: 50
- Deep pulls: 300
- exact fight IDs from the existing trusted Wide cache

This PR adds a guide for extending Oppia's translation infrastructure to a new
entity type. It comes out of the work in oppia/oppia#24933, which generalised
translations from explorations only to skills and exploration metadata.

It covers:
- The four parts of the translation system that a new entity type has to be
  registered with.
- Making a domain object translatable, and giving every field a stable content ID.
- The opportunity lifecycle, including the difference between an entity that stops
  being reachable and one that is deleted.
- Suggestions, serving translations to learners with an English fallback, and the
  contributor dashboard endpoints.
- Backfilling existing entities, making translated content searchable, and rolling
  out behind a feature flag.
- A checklist, and the gotchas that cost the most time while building this.

## What changed

- Added `Adding-a-new-translatable-entity-type.md`.
- Updated `_Sidebar.md` to link it under the I18n/Translations Guide entry.

author: at-wr
body:
Adversarial white-box coverage for three count-0 nil-receiver safety guards in the production dependency implementations. Each method begins with a `ctx == nil` guard, a `ctx.Err()` guard, and then a nil-RECEIVER guard that returns a "missing" error before any field of the receiver (or any method argument) is dereferenced.

- `production_dependencies.go:39` `(*BlindRSAAdmissionVerifier).VerifyAdmission` — `v == nil` -> "handshake: Blind RSA admission verifier is missing" (fires after the `ctx == nil` guard at `:33` and the `ctx.Err()` guard at `:36`, before `admission.VerifyBlindRSA2048` dereferences `v.verificationKeyDER` at `:42`).
- `production_dependencies.go:84` `(*StaticAccessHintResolver).ResolveAccessHint` — `r == nil` -> "handshake: static access hint resolver is missing" (fires after the `ctx == nil` guard at `:78` and the `ctx.Err()` guard at `:81`, before `r.credentials` is indexed at `:87`).
- `production_dependencies.go:131` `(*FixedProxyPolicySelector).SelectPolicy` — `s == nil` -> "handshake: fixed proxy policy selector is missing" (fires after the `ctx == nil` guard at `:125` and the `ctx.Err()` guard at `:128`, before `offer.ValidateStructural` at `:134` / `s.accept()` at `:140`).

The existing handshake tests only ever drive these methods on a constructed (non-nil) receiver, so the nil-receiver branch stayed count-0 even though each is plainly reachable by invoking the method through a nil pointer receiver.

**Proof technique**
Invoke each method through a typed nil pointer receiver (e.g. `var v *BlindRSAAdmissionVerifier; v.VerifyAdmission(...)`). A nil pointer receiver is a well-defined Go call — the method body runs with the receiver == nil — and the guard's condition is then satisfied, so the branch executes and returns the "missing" error. The "is missing" message uniquely identifies the nil-receiver guard: the fall-through paths return different errors (an admission-verification failure, "credential is unavailable", or an offer-validation failure).

**Properties**
- nil-RECEIVER guards (the branch taken when the receiver is nil); each exercised guard is the nil-receiver guard, NOT the `ctx == nil` guard (each method's own `ctx == nil` guard is earlier and already covered), so the test passes `context.Background()` (`ctx.Err() == nil`) and there is no SA1012 surface
- No network, no goroutine, no real proof / credential / offer — each guard returns before any argument is dereferenced, so the test is pure
- In-package (`package handshake`) because the package owns the method set

**Verification**
- `gofmt` clean, `go vet ./handshake/` clean
- `TestBlindRSAAdmissionVerifierNilReceiverGuard`, `TestStaticAccessHintResolverNilReceiverGuard`, `TestFixedProxyPolicySelectorNilReceiverGuard` PASS
- Per-line coverage: all three guards flipped count-0 -> count>=1 (true before/after comparison with the test file excluded then included)
- `handshake` statement coverage 84.7% -> 84.9% (same-method `go tool cover -func` comparison)
- U1000: test file adds only `TestXxx` entry points and references existing exported in-package symbols -> no new unused-symbol surface (CI staticcheck@v0.7.0 will confirm)

Coverage-driven maturation cadence; one open PR at a time.
