author: matthieunoirbusson
body:
> **Merge after #798.** The single-binary layout, the hardening and the docker
> cgroup fallback are described here and implemented there. Merging this first
> would ship notes for behaviour that is not in `dev` yet.

## Two reconciliations, which matter more than the additions

Both were statements the release itself had made false.

**The Kubernetes `_ratio` section** said `senhub_kubernetes_up_ratio` was
deliberately left alone, "because every probe's `up` declares unit `1`, and
breaking that alignment for one probe would trade a naming defect for a naming
inconsistency across forty others."

That reasoning was right — and it pointed at the real fix rather than at leaving
it. The whole set moved together instead. The section now says so and links
onward, rather than describing a decision that was reversed three days later.

**The #723 entry** described `update` reconciling the two binaries a hardened
install carried. This release *removes* the second binary, so as written the
notes announced a repair for a mechanism the same version deletes. Reframed as
what it actually is: it matters for the upgrade itself, and then stops
mattering.

## Added

| Entry | Section |
|---|---|
| The agent is on disk once, and the daemon cannot write it (#794) | Breaking changes |
| Boolean and enum metrics lose their `_ratio` suffix — 118 series (#791) | Breaking changes |
| `ntp` measures the clock against a reference (#788) | New |
| Container metrics without granting host root (#797) | New |
| `chrony` produced no measurement at all, on any host (#787) | Fixed |
| The systemd unit is hardened, and you can check it yourself (#794) | Security |

The 118 renames ship with the **full before/after table**, in a `<details>` so
it does not swamp the page. The entry leads with what does *not* change —
percentages, genuine ratios, and every non-Prometheus sink — because that is
what most readers need, and then names the consumer that mattered: the shipped
vmalert rules, where a rule matching a name that no longer exists stops firing
in silence.

The hardening entry carries the measured **5.9 MEDIUM → 2.0 OK** and, more
usefully, the command to check it (`systemd-analyze security senhub-agent`) plus
a pointer to where the *remaining* exposure is documented. A page claiming an
agent is hardened is worth less than the command that proves it.

## Known follow-ups

Three added with issue numbers: `smart` reporting a clean cycle while reading
nothing (#795), `process.open_file_descriptors` absent-but-unexplained (#796),
and the cgroup fallback covering v2 only (#797).

author: m0lte
body:
## What

Port-concept **PC2** ([#723](https://github.com/packet-net/packet.net/issues/723), umbrella [#726](https://github.com/packet-net/packet.net/issues/726)), after PC1 (#722, a port owner + state model) and PC3 (#724, per-port link policy). All five numbered items in the issue.

1. **The outbound-dial claim is keyed by `(portId, remote)`.** `ClaimOutbound` / `ReleaseOutbound` / `IsOutbound` and the console-suppression test in `OnSessionAccepted` all carry the port; the NET/ROM interlink dial claims its own port. The arrival port is captured at bring-up (`listener.SessionAccepted += (_, e) => OnSessionAccepted(port.Id, …)`) rather than reverse-looked-up from the listener, so `PortIdFor` is gone.
2. **The app-callsign registry is keyed by `(callsign, port scope)`.** The rule, stated on `RegisterAppCallsign` and enforced by `ConflictingScope`: a **wildcard** bind (`portId` null, the RHP wire's `bind` with no port label) claims every port and conflicts with any other registration of that callsign in either order; two per-port binds conflict only when they name the same port. `OnAppSessionAccepted` resolves `(Local, arrival port)` first, wildcard as fallback. A config apply whose new `identity.callsign` collides with a live registration is refused (see below). A port **rename** re-scopes the registrations bound to it.
3. **One canonical port ordering: configuration order.** `CanonicalServingPortIds()` is the single derivation, behind `RunningPortIds` (and so `/ports`' running set, `/sessions`, the metrics, the hail service) and `ResolveDefaultConnector()` - which is now the first **enabled and serving** port in that order. `PORTS` numbering and `C <n> <call>` were already config order and are unchanged; `PORTS` already reads live state from PC1's projector (verified, not changed).
4. **The NET/ROM interlink egress port is deterministic and logged:** the neighbour's last-heard port, else the first attached port in canonical order, at Information **with the reason**. The NODES broadcast walk takes the same ordering. Wired via a new `NetRomService.PortOrder` seam.
5. **The API session identity carries the engine's full key.** New `Packet.Node.Core.Api.SessionIds` mints and parses one convention: `{port}:{remote}` when the local half is the node's own callsign (**unchanged**, so every existing id keeps working), `{port}:{remote}>{local}` otherwise. `SessionInfo` gains `local`; `DELETE` / `send` / `stream` resolve on the full key; the over-RF sysop `SESSIONS`/`KICK` pair drops its private copy of the split and goes through the same helper.

Docs: new operator chapter [`operating/10-your-ports-in-order.md`](operating/10-your-ports-in-order.md), a `docs/node-api.md` note on the ordering + the id convention, and a `docs/plan.md` §17 entry.

## Why

The assessment's finding (evidence: `portmap-evidence.md`, identity-routing + tests) was structural: **a port was in scope for everything and in the key for nothing.**

- While port A dialled G8XYZ, an inbound SABM from G8XYZ on port B was accepted by the engine (UA sent, link up) and then returned from before the console started. The caller got a connected link and **dead air** until T3/DISC, with **no log line at all**. A dial holds its claim for up to (N2+1)xT1V.
- Two apps could not answer for one callsign on two ports (a local BBS on VHF, a gateway BBS on HF is ordinary multi-port practice), and `OnAppSessionAccepted` resolved by `Local` alone, never comparing the arrival port it computed on the very next line.
- Renaming the node onto an SSID a BBS had already bound rerouted every connect for that app to the node prompt, silently: the node-wide reset rebuilt each listener under the new `MyCall`, and `OnSessionAccepted`'s split is `Local != listener.MyCall`.
- Three different answers to "which port": on a node configured `[vhf, hf]`, a bare `C G8XYZ` left on `hf` (ordinal-first) and `C 1 G8XYZ` on `vhf` (config-first). Operator-visible port numbering was not trustworthy.
- `attachments.Values.FirstOrDefault()` over a `ConcurrentDictionary` decided which band a NET/ROM SABM left on for a neighbour we had not heard, and seeded the per-(port, peer) capability cache for a port the link would not use.
- One station on the node console **and** on a bound app callsign produced two `/sessions` rows with the **same id**, and `DELETE` / `send` resolved with a `FirstOrDefault` on the remote: you could drop the BBS link when you meant the console.

## How tested

Every new .NET case is multi-port and asserts **on the air** over separate in-memory RF channels, with port ids chosen so **config order and id order disagree** (`vhf` before `hf`). Every earlier multi-port test used `a`/`b` or `alpha`/`bravo`, where the two coincide, which is exactly why three orderings could coexist unnoticed.

`tests/Packet.Node.Tests/Integration/PortConceptCrossPortTests.cs` (8):
- dial out to X on port A while X connects in on port B, and B's session gets a node console;
- the same app callsign bound on two ports routes each caller to its own port's app;
- the negative: an app bound to A does not answer on B and does not fall through to the console;
- the wildcard conflict, in both directions, plus the legal same-callsign-different-port bind;
- an identity change onto a bound app callsign is refused, `MyCall` is untouched, and the app still answers over the air afterwards;
- a rename carries the binding with it (the handler sees the NEW port id);
- config order is the one ordering (`RunningPortIds`, `Snapshot`, the default connector, `C 1` / `C 2`);
- the default connector skips a port that is not serving.

`NetRomInterlinkEgressTests.cs` (2): three ports, `EchoStation`s for the neighbour on each channel - an unheard neighbour is dialled on the config-first port (`vhf`, not the alphabet's `hf`); a neighbour heard via NODES on `hf` is dialled there.

`SessionIdentityApiTests.cs` (2 + 14 convention cases): the same station on the node's own callsign **and** on a bound app callsign, over the real booted node - two rows, two distinct ids, `DELETE` on the long id leaves the console circuit up, and a `send` to the short id is a 404 rather than a fallback to "any session with that remote".

Verification run:

- `dotnet build -nodeReuse:false` clean (no warnings).
- `dotnet test tests/Packet.Node.Tests --filter "Category!=HardwareLoop&Category!=Interop"` - **2331 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed**.
- `dotnet test tests/Packet.NetRom.Tests` - **309 passed**.
- `web/packetnet-ui`: `npm run lint` clean, `npm run build` clean, `npx vitest run` - **438 passed (33 files)**. `SessionInfo.json` regenerated by the contract fixture test (the DTO gained `local`), and the fixture now carries the two-circuits-one-station pair.

## Design decisions

- **The short id form is preserved verbatim.** `{port}:{remote}` still means "the circuit to this port's own callsign", so nothing that stored or scripted an id breaks; only a circuit to a *different* local callsign takes the long form. On resolution the short form matches the listener's `MyCall`, **not** "any local" - that is what makes the two independently addressable.
- **The identity collision is refused in two places, deliberately.** The config-write API asks `PortSupervisor.LiveApplyConflicts` **before** persisting and answers `422` against `identity.callsign` (the panel already renders that against a field). The supervisor re-checks and refuses the apply **whole** - not "apply the ports, skip the colliding alias", which would leave the node half-way between two identities - for a config that arrived round the back (a hand-edited conffile never passes the API). `ApplyAsync` now returns a `PortApplyOutcome`; on a refusal `NodeHostedService` leaves its applied-config baseline where it was, so the next edit re-plans from what is actually running rather than from a config that never took effect.

body:
Three things on screen existed for a developer, not for the person using this. All three are gone.

**The route-by-route log.** `helper 1 · normal route`, `helper 3: needs a pass — skipped` — and it was being flung open *automatically on every failure*, so the worst moment in the app was also its most technical. `log()` is now a no-op: the engine still narrates internally, nobody has to read it. Status text loses the helper numbers and route names too — it says "Finding your video…" and "Still looking…".

**The Get button.** A link in the box is the instruction, so a pasted address now starts on its own after a short pause for typing to settle. Enter and the Paste button still work. **The chain icon** beside the field goes with it — decoration that told nobody anything.

**Long failure messages.** Now one line and one sentence: *"Can't download this one."* plus what to do, instead of a three-bullet explanation of YouTube's blocking behaviour. The status pill hides itself when an error appears, rather than stacking two failure messages on top of each other.

Also fixes a **double focus ring** — the field drew its own ring inside the bar's ring whenever focused.

body:
## What

Adds an Enablement App migration status banner to this repo's first documentation page.

Status for this repo: **not-migrated**.

## Why

The Dynatrace Hub lists 26 repos, but nothing on the Hub, in the GitHub Pages docs
or in the Enablement App tells a learner which trainings are already immersive,
interactive and self-service in the app, which are mid-conversion, and which are not
migrated yet. This banner makes that visible on the page itself.

## Why inline text and not a `docs/snippets/` include

The app's importer strips `--8<-- "snippets/..."` lines
(`stripSnippetIncludes`, `api/import-lab.helpers.ts`). A snippet-based banner would
look right on GitHub Pages and be silently dropped in the Enablement App — the surface
it exists to serve. So the banner is literal Markdown in the page.

## Verification

Rendered through both real parsers, not a reimplementation:

| Surface | Parser | Result |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub Pages | Python-Markdown `admonition` | `<div class="admonition ...">` with working contact links |
| Enablement App | `stripSnippetIncludes()` + `preprocessMarkdown()` | `<div data-admonition="...">`, banner is the first block |

## Please leave this PR open

This is one of 23 repos in a fleet-wide wave. Framework **1.10.0** will add a
minimalistic Orbital-specific container greeting, and the `FRAMEWORK_VERSION` bump
will be pushed onto this same branch so the banner and the greeting ship together.

💡 **What**: Added clear search ("X") buttons inside the search input fields in both the Location Search and Mosque Finder components.

🎯 **Why**: When typing long city names or making a typo on a mobile device, users need a fast, one-tap way to clear the input rather than relying on backspace. This is a standard mobile-friendly UX pattern that reduces friction.

Before: Users had to manually backspace to clear the input field, which is tedious on mobile keyboards.
After: A small, accessible "X" button appears inside the input as soon as the user starts typing, letting them clear the field with a single tap.

- Added `aria-label="Hapus pencarian"` to ensure screen readers can announce the icon-only button's purpose.

author: emmanuel-a-otchere
body:
## feat: CR-007 — Decision, Intent, Policy, Governance & Agentic Semantics (v0.12.0)

Implements CR-7 (§1–§66). Depends on CR-001..006, all merged.

### The central principle (§1)

**An Agent is not the center of the metamodel. Decision, intent, authority, policy, evidence, action and accountability are. Agents are participants in that semantic system.**

```
INTENT → OBJECTIVE → POLICY → DECISION → ACTION → CHANGE
                                            ↓
   ┌── Human / Agent / both ────────────────┤
   ↓                                        ↓
EVIDENCE ← ASSESSMENT ← OUTCOME ← ARCHITECTURE STATE
   └──────────────→ new Decision (the closed loop, §2/§68)
```

### What lands

| CR-7 block | Deliverable | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| A–B Intent & Objective (§3–§6) | Intent, Objective; Objective ≠ Outcome | motivates/seeks wiring |
| C–D Policy & Constraints (§7–§10) | Policy, PolicyRule; Constraint + strength (hard/soft/preference/guideline) | test_constraint_strength |
| E–G Decision structure (§11–§17) | DecisionOption, DecisionCriterion, DecisionRecord; Decision core + rationale/confidence/uncertainty/assumptions/authority_ref | G001/G002 |
| H Authority & Delegation (§18–§19) | Authority, Delegation (scope/limits/validity/revocation); capability ≠ authority | G005/G006/G010 |
| I–S Agent & profile (§20–§33) | Agent (specializes Actor), AgentProfile, AgentSkill, Tool/ToolPermission, Memory | §21/§30/§31 distinctions tested |
| T–U Governance (§34–§37) | GovernanceBody/Rule; governs/approves/establishes; RACI-via-relationships (consults) | G016 |
| V Policy enforcement (§38–§39) | PolicyEvaluation → PolicyDecision (permit/deny/escalate); ≠ enterprise Decision | G-rule file |
| W Decision lifecycle & risk (§40–§43) | Decision lifecycle (via CR-6); Action reversibility + materiality; mitigates → Risk | G012 |
| Z–AB Orchestration (§46–§50) | Orchestrator/Controller/Orchestration/Workflow/Task — never collapsed into Agent | profile structure |
| AD–AG Agent accountability (§52–§56) | owner_ref, authority, policy, lifecycle, AgentOpportunity (derived) | G007/G013 |
| AH–AK Agentic systems (§57–§59) | AgenticSystem composition boundary; anti-AI-washing rules | test_agent_reuses_core_semantics |

### Key rulings

- **§65 enforced in CI**: no `AgentDecision`/`AgentAction`/`AgentOutcome` types can exist — Decision + `made-by` Agent, Action + `performed-by` Agent, Outcome + `results-in` AgenticSystem (test fails if duplicates appear).
- **Decision ≠ Change ≠ Action** (§12/§13; G003): decision authorizes; action executes; change modifies architecture.
- **Capability ≠ Authority** (§18): structural via Authority/Delegation with scope, limits, validity — G005/G006/G010.
- **Autonomy is not a boolean** (§23): AutonomyPolicy + configurable AutonomyLevel + HumanOversight patterns (approve-before / review-after / intervene / supervise).
- **Tool ≠ Service, Workflow ≠ Agent, LLM ≠ Agent** (§21/§31/§57): recorded as profile rules — the anti-AI-washing guard.
- **Evidence reuse** (§16): decisions are `informed-by` CR-5 Evidence — no DecisionEvidence duplicate.

### Verification

- 112/112 conformance tests (24 new in test_013); G003 and G006 negative-tested (injection → fail, restore → pass)
- All CI validators green locally: 122 JSON schemas, TTL parse, entity-graph schema, SQLite apply (99 tables), 119 pydantic modules compile

### Deferred (explicit)

- 32 governance/agentic entities await upstream OpenDEAM allocation before entering `entity-graph.json`
- RACI profile (§37), AI Agent Maturity assessment profile (§54), agent readiness scoring (§55) → follow-up profiles on CR-5 machinery
- LLM/prompt/RAG/vendor-framework specifics → technology profiles, deliberately out of scope (§66)

Next per CR-7's own recommendation: **CR-8 — OpenDEA Semantic Architecture & Conformance Specification** (consolidation of CR-1..7 into an implementable standard).

author: jdx
body:
## Summary

- add `usage-rs`, the single dependency for compiled usage CLIs
- re-export the four derives, the argv runtime, and `ValueHint` from the facade
- forward cold-path `spec`, `help`, `completions`, and `diagnostics` features
- make generated derive paths resolve either `usage-rs` or a direct/renamed `usage-argv` dependency
- retain direct `usage-argv` compatibility for low-level adopters

Applications can choose the short public crate name in Cargo:

```toml
[dependencies]
usage = { package = "usage-rs", version = "5.1" }
```

and then keep the declaration on one API:

```rust
use usage::Cli;

#[derive(Cli)]
struct Cli {
    #[usage(long, value_hint = usage::ValueHint::FilePath)]
    file: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
}
```

## Why

Depending on `usage-derive` and `usage-argv` separately exposes an implementation split and allows their versions or features to drift. The facade gives adopters one versioned package while leaving the zero-allocation runtime independently usable.

The facade crate target remains `usage_rs` to avoid colliding with the existing `usage-lib` target inside this workspace. The documented Cargo alias provides the intended `usage::…` source spelling.

## Stack

Base layer for #965, which migrates `usage-cli` to this facade.

## Checks

- `cargo test --all --all-features`
- `cargo clippy --all --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo +1.91.0 check -p usage-argv -p usage-derive -p usage-rs --all-features`
- `cargo test -p usage-rs --no-default-features`
- external path-dependency check using the documented `usage = { package = "usage-rs", … }` alias

_This PR was generated by Codex._

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Macro-generated path resolution affects every derived CLI; behavior is covered by new fixtures, but a wrong `crate_name` resolution could break adopters at compile time across the ecosystem.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces **`usage-rs`**, a workspace crate meant to be depended on as `usage = { package = "usage-rs", … }`. It re-exports **`usage-argv`**, optional **`usage-derive`** macros behind the `spec` feature, and forwards feature flags for help, completions, and diagnostics so adopters get one versioned package instead of splitting derive and runtime.
> 
> **`usage-derive`** now uses **`proc-macro-crate`** to pick emitted paths at compile time: a direct **`usage-argv`** dependency wins over the facade (for mixed/low-level setups); otherwise generated code goes through **`usage-rs::argv`** and the facade’s derive re-exports. Emitted tables import the chosen runtime as `usage_argv` locally, and unit subcommands use the resolved derive path instead of hard-coded `::usage_derive`.
> 
> Docs and model hints shift public examples from `usage_argv::ValueHint` to **`usage::ValueHint`**. CI MSRV matrix includes **`usage-rs`** at Rust 1.91; integration tests cover the Cargo alias fixture and mixed direct + facade dependencies.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 8fe3c3cf9b8acccaf1c994e107a10b1b7d71c5a7. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

Replaces #953 after flipping the stack so the CLI can consume the facade.

body:
Hello!

Recently I built the project with ASan & UBSan and ran ctests.

```bash
mkdir -p build && cd build

cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
	-DPHOENIXDKIM_ENABLE_ASAN=ON \
	-DPHOENIXDKIM_ENABLE_UBSAN=ON \
	..

make -j$(nproc)
ctest
```

I get some errors LSan:

```bash
4: Test command: /home/petr/u/PhoenixDKIM/build/libphoenixdkim/tests/t-conformance
4: Working Directory: /home/petr/u/PhoenixDKIM/build/libphoenixdkim/tests
4: Test timeout computed to be: 10000000
4: 
4: =================================================================
4: ==1727628==ERROR: LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks
4: 
4: Direct leak of 235 byte(s) in 1 object(s) allocated from:
4:     #0 0x7ffff78e6f4b in malloc (/lib64/libasan.so.8+0xe6f4b) (BuildId: d7d37a712ed67f505b486de13595e3f6cc124ee8)
4:     #1 0x7ffff7427c51 in dkim_malloc libphoenixdkim/dkim-util.c:51
4:     #2 0x7ffff742800b in dkim_strdup libphoenixdkim/dkim-util.c:103
4:     #3 0x7ffff7423a3f in dkim_test_dns_put libphoenixdkim/dkim-test.c:167
4:     #4 0x000000418925 in test_rfc8463_ed25519_wrong_keytype libphoenixdkim/tests/t-conformance.c:2497
4:     #5 0x000000418df3 in main libphoenixdkim/tests/t-conformance.c:2628
4:     #6 0x7ffff64105b4 in __libc_start_call_main (/lib64/libc.so.6+0x35b4) (BuildId: 88c03969b4319fc0140734fe863825ec4a1cdb0d)
4:     #7 0x7ffff6410667 in __libc_start_main@@GLIBC_2.34 (/lib64/libc.so.6+0x3667) (BuildId: 88c03969b4319fc0140734fe863825ec4a1cdb0d)
4:     #8 0x000000400d54 in _start (/home/petr/u/PhoenixDKIM/build/libphoenixdkim/tests/t-conformance+0x400d54) (BuildId: c61287463aa80b87ce7630bcc33d0b5753f111dc)
```

... and fixed it.

dkim_sig_process() assigned sig->sig_keytype only after the key had been decoded, but three early-exit paths in the Ed25519 branch return between the DKIM_MALLOC() of struct dkim_ed25519 and that assignment.  Since DKIM_KEYTYPE_RSA is 0 and DKIM_SIGINFO is zero-initialised, dkim_free() then reclaims the 40-byte Ed25519 struct as a 56-byte struct dkim_rsa: it reads (and NULLs) rsa_rsaout 8 bytes past the end of the allocation, free()s whatever heap word lives there, EVP_PKEY_free()s the raw key buffer and BIO_free()s a size_t.  Reachable from unauthenticated input: any a=ed25519-sha256 message whose DNS p= tag is not a valid 32-byte raw key takes the first of those paths.

  - assign sig_keytype immediately after the struct is allocated, in both the Ed25519 and the RSA branch;
  - complete dd57c64d: the success path of dkim_test_dns_get() still used a bare DKIM_FREE(), leaking the strdup()'d dns_query and dns_reply of every dequeued reply;
  - drop the workaround in test_rfc8463_ed25519_wrong_keytype() and call dkim_free() again — that test now covers both fixes.

t-conformance: 339/339 clean under ASAN+LeakSanitizer (was: 24402 bytes leaked, or heap-buffer-overflow once the handle is actually freed).

Running tests with sanitizers is now successful.

author: cristinalakasz
body:
Phase 4: an operator window, and the Phase 2 design error it exposed.

```
python tools/make_demo_recording.py demo
python -m biocam.ui --replay demo.raw --meta demo_meta.json     # no instrument
python -m biocam.ui --live                                      # lab machine
```

## It runs without a BioCAM, and that is the point

`biocam/ui/factories.py` confines the difference between a replayed file and
the instrument to two classes, so the same window, controller, writer, clock,
gap tracking and stimulation path run either way. Only the packets and the
stimulator are stand-ins.

That is not a convenience mode. It is the only way this could be written from
600 km away, and it is how the colleague can learn the controls before spending
bench time on them. It also means the UI is genuinely *tested*: 42 of the new
tests drive the real window.

Tkinter because it ships with Python. The lab machine already depends on a
pythonnet/.NET/DLL arrangement delicate enough to be worth not adding to.

## What building it exposed

**`Stimulator` had the lifecycle wrong, since Phase 2.** 3Brain's sample does
not nest the four calls — it brackets them against different things:

```
Initialize / Close   <->  device control    MainForm.cs:111 / :122
Start / Stop         <->  data streaming    MainForm.cs:186,192 / :210,213
```

Fusing all four into one context manager made that ordering **structurally
impossible to express**: the stimulator was necessarily started before any
acquisition existed, on every session — and the latency it reports is measured
"relative to the beginning of the acquisition". Now split, with
`stimulating()` as the streaming bracket.

A worse consequence hid behind it: **a stimulator that would not initialize
blocked all live recording**, because the window had no way to open a session
without one. It now degrades to recording-only.

## Guardrails

The person using this did not write it and cannot ask questions
mid-experiment, so every refusal is written next to the button, live, as you
type: stimulating with nothing recording, out-of-range amplitudes,
out-of-array or 0-indexed electrodes, shared columns. A charge-unbalanced
pulse is not expressible — the second phase is built as the mirror of the
first. A red banner means LIVE; blue means simulation, and a simulated
stimulus log now says so in every record.

## Three review rounds, and what they caught

Findings the tests or the reviewers caught that a manual look did not:

- **`ttk.Button["state"]` returns a `Tcl_Obj`**, and `Tcl_Obj == "disabled"`
  is `False`. The guard in `_render` never ran, so after the first recording
  the Start button would have stayed greyed out **permanently**.
- **The device and stimulator were entered and never exited.** A leaked
  `BioCamDevice` stays claimed until the process dies.
- **Tkinter was being touched from two other threads.** On the stimulator path
  a Tk failure would propagate out of `send_now` *after the pulse was
  delivered* and be counted as a failure — **a stimulus that fired would have
  been displayed as not delivered**.
- **The teardown ordering was still inverted after the "fix"**: `stop_source`
  is what `record_session` calls, not `stop_source_safely`.
- **The fix for that introduced a new leak**: `start_source` now makes two
  driver calls and sat outside the try/finally that stops the stream.
- **`ReplayFactory`'s docstring claimed simulated records were marked.**
  Nothing marked anything.
- **The stimulus log was never written by the window at all.**

## Untested

**Nothing on the live path has ever run.** The lab list, in order: whether

body:
## 取り込み時の解析を並列化

変換はプールで並列化済みでしたが、投入直後の解析（長さ・Peak・LUFS の計測）は1ファイルずつ直列でした。同じプールに載せています。

- プレースホルダを1件ずつ追加していたのを**まとめて登録**に変更。221ファイル投入時、リストに全件が即座に出ます（配列の作り直しが221回 → 1回）
- 解析をプールのスロットに分散。**変換バッチが走っている間は並列度1に落として**、解析と変換でメモリ予算を取り合わないようにしています（従来と同じ挙動）
- メモリ入場制御は変換と同じ `MemoryGate`。解析は中間ファイルを作らないので見積りは1コピー分

### 実測（3秒ステレオ × 221ファイル）

| | 変更前 | 変更後 |
|---|---|---|
| 解析 | 81秒 | **19秒**（4.3倍） |
| 投入直後のリスト表示 | 1件ずつ増える | 全221件が即座に表示 |

変換も221件36秒で完走し、Peak 正規化の結果は全件 -1.0 dB、エラー0件。処理中に投入した場合は並列度1に落ちることもログで確認済みです。

## CI にテストを追加

これまで CI は `npm run build` のみで、**テスト141件と svelte-check を走らせていませんでした**。

- `push` / `pull_request` の両方で `npm test` と `npm run check` を実行
- アーティファクトのアップロードとデプロイは `push` のときだけ
- Node 20 が deprecated 警告を出していたので 22 に更新

## 今回やらなかったこと

- **`static/coi-serviceworker.js` の削除**: v0.3.1 で自壊スタブを配ったばかりで、既存ユーザーがまだ受け取っていません。今削除すると旧 SW が永久に残るため、1〜2リリース後に消すべきです。
- **ChannelSettings / MetadataSettings のスキーマ移行**: 構造的にスキーマ形（`enabled` + フラットなパラメータ + `param-row`）に合いません。ChannelSettings は `enabled` を持たず「変換なし/モノラル/ステレオ」のラジオ＋条件付きの balance、MetadataSettings は per-field で unchanged/bulk/individual を切り替える別物の UI で、`param-row` は0個です。無理に載せると見た目が変わり、削減にもなりません。

author: nakyahara
body:
## 概要

発注管理のロジザード在庫は従来、会社PCの run-zaiko.bat → Gドライブ → 手動取込ボタンの経路だった (毎時取込の開始 8/16 で run-zaiko.bat は手動バックアップに降格済み = Drive上のCSVは更新されない状態)。

本PRで、**発注画面を開くだけで mirror_logizard_stock (miniPC毎時取込の複製・同一warehouse-mirror.db内) から在庫オーバーレイが自動更新される** ようにする。手動アップロード経路は miniPC 停止時のバックアップとして残す。

## 仕組み

- computeAll の頭で `maybeRefreshFromLogizardMirror()` — mirror の captured_at が進んでいたら在庫オーバーレイ (po_ne_overlay_rows) を再生成。60秒throttle・fail-soft・**cron/定期ジョブ無し** (台帳登録不要)
- 集計はSQL一発 (良品のみ・商品IDごとロケ横断SUM・実測34ms/8,349行)。手動CSV経路と同じルール (在庫0埋め含む)
- **発注サイクル (✅発注確定済み・×非表示) は進めない** — サイクルは人がデータ更新した時だけ

## 共存ルール (新しい方が勝つ)

| 状況 | 動作 |
|---|---|
| 通常 (毎時mirror更新) | 自動反映。操作不要 |
| 手動取込 (logizard/NE CSV) | captured_at=取込時刻で後勝ち。次のmirror更新まで手動が保持 |
| NEマスタCSVが有効適用中 | 自動反映スキップ (原価・取扱区分の上書きを消さない)。翌朝PML同期で失効したら再開 |
| 「CSV取込を解除」 | 同一mirror世代では復活しない。次の毎時更新で自動再開 |
| miniPC停止 | captured_atが進まない→自動は動かず手動経路がそのまま生きる |

## 鮮度表示 (中原さん決定 2026-08-17)

- 「在庫: 🟢ロジザード YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM 時点 (毎時自動反映・反映 N/M件)」— **何時時点かを必ず表示**
- **3時間超は⚠️を出すが数字は使う**
- 朝のPML同期より古いmirrorは適用しない (朝のNE在庫が正)

## 安全弁

- mirror商品数が下限 (既定500・実データ約2,900) 未満なら反映しない (大量在庫0上書き防止)
- 負数在庫の行があれば全体スキップ (行単位検査・ロケ間相殺でも検出)
- 世代チェック〜置換は単一即時トランザクション (毎時push/手動取込の割り込みと競合しない)

## レビュー・テスト

- Codex 4巡: R1 High1/Med2/Low1 → R2 High1/Med1 → R3 Med1/Low1 → **R4 クリーン** (全指摘対応 or 設計意図回答+挙動固定テスト)
- smoke 21件追加 (自動反映/後勝ち/NE共存/解除サプレッション/夜間→翌朝/負数/下限ガード/鮮度表示)・**全1,018件 pass**

author: sawtaytoes
body: Two things, and the second is a copy bug I shipped. ## The per-show override `on_complete_by_show` — a map keyed by ratingKey (`section-` for a whole item bucket), the **same shape and keying** `starts` and `weights` already use. A rule-derived show has no stored entry to hang a field on, so a map on the set is the only place it can live. **Three states per show, not a boolean:** | stored | means | | --- | --- | | absent | follow the pool's own `on_complete` | | `restart` | start this show over when it finishes | | `drop` | let this show finish, **even on a pool that restarts** | That third one is the whole ask — *"it would be good for each show to override this set-level config"* — and the case described was a pool set to restart with one show carved out. A boolean could only ever have expressed the other direction. An unrecognised value **follows the pool** rather than inverting it. `sets.yaml` is hand-edited over SMB, and a typo that silently flips a show to the opposite of what its pool says is the failure that looks exactly like the feature working. It lives on the pool grid, beside the weight picker already on that tile: | default | overridden | | --- | --- | | | | ## The copy was lying The set-level option said **"Drop it — it leaves this pool"**. It does not, and the owner caught it: > "I hope you mean 'drop it' as in 'mark as completed' and don't play it again, but it doesn't 'drop it' in terms of removing it unless we configured the settings that way for the queue." He's right, and `select.ts` is unambiguous: a finished show yields an empty `unwatched`, the `if (eps.length)` guard never pushes a bucket, and **nothing is written and nothing is deleted**. A filtered pool is recomputed from libraries and ratings on every scan, so the show comes back **on its own** the moment a new episode lands. Removal is a different mechanism on a different kind of set — the curated queue's `done` flag and its `remove_completed_after` TTL, which really do delete entries from `queues.yaml`. Exactly the distinction he drew. It now reads **"Let it finish — nothing plays from it"**, and the hint says outright that nothing is removed. A control that claims to delete something is a control nobody dares press. ## Gates `e2e/on-complete-test.ts` gains: both directions (restarting pool + one show told to finish; dropping pool + one told to restart), that an override names **one** show and leaves its neighbour alone, that junk follows the pool on **both** kinds of pool, and that the spelling is case-insensitive. Re-ran green: `engine-parity`, `set-passthrough-parity`, `curated-parity`, `binding-parity`, `playback-length`, `lineup-knobs`, `topup`, `rotation-length`, both typechecks, biome, 82 web tests, both builds. **Driven against a live pool**, not just unit-tested: picking "Let it finish" on Alphablocks wrote `on_complete_by_show: {"190990": drop}` to disk and read back after a full reload. Decision: [`2026-08-17-a-show-can-override-its-pools-on-complete.md`](docs/decisions/2026-08-17-a-show-can-override-its-pools-on-complete.md) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: xsahil03x
body:
# Submit a pull request
Linear: [FLU-700](https://linear.app/stream/issue/flu-700/stream-core-flutter-migrate-to-material-ui-and-cupertino-ui)

## CLA

- [x] I have signed the [Stream CLA](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScFKsKkAJI7mhCr7K9rEIOpqIDThrWxuvxnwUq2XkHyG154vQ/viewform) (required).
- [x] The code changes follow best practices
- [x] Code changes are tested (add some information if not applicable)

## Description of the pull request

Flutter split Material and Cupertino out of the framework into the flutter.dev-published [`material_ui`](https://pub.dev/packages/material_ui) / [`cupertino_ui`](https://pub.dev/packages/cupertino_ui) packages — both **v1.0.0, published 2026-08-12**, the same day as Flutter 3.47 stable. Both require `flutter: >=3.44.0`.

**Stacked on #150**, which raises the floor to exactly that version — that is what unblocks this, so review #150 first and merge it first.

### What changed

- **195 import directives across 194 files** rewritten from `package:flutter/material.dart` to `package:material_ui/material_ui.dart`. Every occurrence was verified to be a plain import directive first — no export directives, no `show`/`hide` clauses. Reordering moved the directive relative to its neighbours, so `directives_ordering` was reapplied via `dart fix`.
- **`material_ui` registered in `melos.yaml`** (the workspace's single version registry) and added to the three pubspecs that import it: `stream_core_flutter`, the gallery, and the `stream_thumbnail` example.
- **`migrate_design_widgets` enabled** in `all_lint_rules.yaml` to hold the line.
- **`STYLE_GUIDE.md` and the gallery's `AGENTS.md`** — the import-convention code samples showed the old URI, which is what the next contributor would copy.

### `cupertino_ui` gets no direct dependency — deliberately

Nothing in this repo imports `package:flutter/cupertino.dart`; the only `Cupertino` hits are a doc-comment link and a private `_CupertinoSwitchDefaults` class name in `StreamSwitch`. So `cupertino_ui` arrives transitively through `material_ui`, and adding it directly would be an unused dependency. If a widget starts importing it, add it then.

### Why this is breaking

`material_ui` ships its own implementations and Flutter 3.47's `material.dart` does **not** re-export them, so `flutter/material`'s `ThemeData` / `ThemeExtension` / `ColorScheme` are *unrelated types* to `material_ui`'s. Concretely, an app that does

```dart
MaterialApp(theme: ThemeData(extensions: [StreamTheme(...)]))   // Flutter's Material
```

no longer compiles against this package. It must import `material_ui` and use its `MaterialApp` — which is also what supplies the `MaterialLocalizations` several components read.

### Two prefixed bridges remain

Each is for a dependency that has not migrated, and each carries an `// ignore: migrate_design_widgets`. Neither changes rendering:

| Site | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `StreamMessageText` | `flutter_markdown_plus` (latest, 1.0.12) still takes Flutter's `ThemeData` in `MarkdownStyleSheet.fromTheme`. The bridge maps exactly the fields that factory reads — the five `textTheme` slots, `cardTheme.color`, `cardColor`, `primaryColor`, `dividerColor`, and the `colorScheme` — so the sheet it produces is unchanged. |
| `ThemeConfiguration.buildWidgetbookTheme` (gallery) | Widgetbook still takes Flutter's `ThemeData` for its own chrome. The Stream branding is restated over the same colors, so the gallery looks the same. |

None of the other Material-adjacent dependencies needed one — `alchemist`, `shimmer`, `flutter_svg`, `cached_network_image_ce`, `svg_icon_widget`, `device_frame_plus` and `flutter_colorpicker` either take shared types (`Color`, `TextStyle`, `Widget`) or none at all.

### The lint is safe at the floor

`migrate_design_widgets` is recognised by the 3.47 analyzer and not by 3.44's. That does not break `legacy_version_analyze`: `undefined_lint` is reported against the *options file itself*, and nothing in CI analyses the repo root where `all_lint_rules.yaml` lives — `melos run analyze` runs per package, and the legacy job runs from `packages/stream_core/lib`. Enabled, the rule reports **exactly the two bridges above and nothing else**, which is the proof the migration is complete.

### Test-only adjustments

Both are consequences of the split, not of anything this repo does unusually:

- **`find.byTooltip` is bound to Flutter's `Tooltip`.** The bottom-nav tooltip test now matches `material_ui`'s by predicate.
- **Alchemist scaffolds golden tests with Flutter's `MaterialApp`,** whose `MaterialLocalizations` the migrated `StreamBottomNavBar` cannot read — it threw `No MaterialLocalizations found` and rendered an error box. Its two golden wrappers now provide `material_ui`'s delegates. Worth knowing for any future component that reads localizations: widget tests are fine (they wrap in `material_ui`'s `MaterialApp`), golden tests are not.

## Testing

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `dart analyze --fatal-infos`, 4 packages @ 3.47.0 | clean |
| `melos run check:barrels` | pass |
| `melos run format:verify` (441 files) | pass |
| `melos run generate:all` | no diff — the generators see the same types |
| `stream_core_flutter` tests (`GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`) | 362 passed, 42 failed — **identical set to before the migration** |
| `stream_core` / `stream_thumbnail` tests | unaffected — neither imports Material |

**On the 42 golden failures:** the pre-existing macOS-vs-Linux baseline (committed goldens are Linux-rendered), carried over unchanged from #150 — `comm` returns empty in both directions against that branch's run. **Zero introduced.** Every golden that *can* be compared on macOS is unchanged; the 42 are the ones whose committed baselines are Linux-rendered, so they are equally unverifiable here before and after. This PR's own CI run on Linux is the check for those. No golden was regenerated, `update_goldens.yml` was not dispatched, and no `.png` is touched by this diff.

## Screenshots / Videos

Not applicable — the migration is pixel-neutral, which is what the golden comparison above establishes.

body:
Documentation seule. La règle que trois audits consécutifs auraient dû me faire écrire dès le premier.

## La même faute, trois fois

| | |
|---|---|
| **A-018** | Le contrôle d'origine, écrit dans une fonction serveur, n'avait pas suivi les trois ajoutées ensuite — qui dépensaient toutes une clé payante. |
| **A-023** | La semaine suivante, le filtre d'hôte : partagé pour l'origine, laissé sur place pour le SSRF. Deux fonctions faisant la même chose, une seule protégée. |
| **A-024** | Entre les deux, j'ai annoncé qu'un calcul d'argent était écrit « trois fois ». Il l'était **quatre**, et le quatrième — l'écran le plus lu — affichait un montant que les trois autres contredisaient. |

À chaque fois j'ai corrigé le cas, et pas le réflexe.

## La règle

Quand on pose un garde-fou, une validation, un calcul partagé : **avant de refermer, chercher dans tout le dépôt qui fait déjà la même chose.** Pas « relire les endroits auxquels je pense » — un motif, exécuté. Ce qu'on n'écrit qu'à un endroit ne suit pas les frères ajoutés ensuite, et personne ne s'en aperçoit avant l'incident.

**Le signe qu'on est en train de commettre la faute, et il est net : annoncer un nombre d'occurrences sans l'avoir compté.** C'est exactement ce que j'ai fait dans #70.

Corollaire : quand la même règle doit vivre à deux endroits, elle vit dans **un** fichier importé par les deux — jamais recopiée. Une copie ne se corrige jamais deux fois.

author: watari-dev
body:
## Type

New app

## App

App ID: `momentbackup-hub`
Upstream project: MomentBackup Hub by Watari Labs Pty Ltd — <https://momentbackup.com/hub/>
Version: 1.0.6

## Summary

MomentBackup Hub is a free, self-hosted overview of MomentBackup backups. It shows whether each computer is protected, when it last backed up and verified, and which computers need attention. It is a companion to MomentBackup, the paid personal backup and recovery app for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

There is no account with the vendor, no telemetry, no licence check, and no update check. The Hub stores no backup data, and it never holds a backup encryption key, passphrase, or destination credential. Notifications by ntfy, webhook, or SMTP are the only outbound connections it can make, and it makes none until one is configured.

It runs in heartbeat mode: each MomentBackup app posts its own Ed25519-signed status report, so the Hub needs no access to the backup destinations. It opens to a first-run page that creates the owner account, then to the dashboard — no SSH, no CLI, no file edits.

| | |
|---|---|
| Image | `ghcr.io/momentbackup/momentbackup-hub:1.0.6@sha256:105fdd243ef9df29cfda71f8a9b0ab0a7eef35512646a609452b634ebf49b234` |
| Platforms | `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64` (multi-arch index digest, both built natively) |
| Manifest port | 8677 (`APP_PORT` 8675 internally) |
| Category | files |
| Repo field | public package page — the Hub's source tree is private |

## Transport: the upstream normally serves HTTPS, and this package turns that off

This is the one decision worth reviewing.

The Hub refuses every credential-carrying request over plaintext by default — creating the owner account, signing in, enrolling a computer, posting a heartbeat, and every command poll — and normally serves HTTPS on 8675 with a certificate it generates itself, which enrolled computers pin.

That does not compose with `app_proxy`. `app_proxy` does expose `APP_PROTOCOL`, but the target would be an upstream with a self-signed certificate that `http-proxy-middleware` rejects by default, the browser leg would still be plain HTTP, and `MBHUB_PUBLIC_URL` would have to name an `https://` origin that umbrelOS never serves.

So this package sets `MBHUB_INSECURE: "1"`. The Hub then serves plain HTTP on 8675 behind `app_proxy`, `MBHUB_PUBLIC_URL` is `http://${DEVICE_DOMAIN_NAME}:${APP_PROXY_PORT}`, and the boot log states plainly what that exposes. Practically: sign-in passwords, session cookies, and each enrolled computer's long-lived command token cross the local network unencrypted — the same posture as every other umbrelOS app, but worth naming here because this app's own docs treat it as the weakest of its three transport options. It is stated in the app description rather than buried.

`MBHUB_TRUST_PROXY=1` would also make the Hub serve HTTP, but it means "something in front of me terminated TLS", which is not true on umbrelOS. `MBHUB_INSECURE` is the accurate one.

## `PROXY_AUTH_WHITELIST`

```
/api/heartbeat,/api/poll,/api/poll/result,/api/enroll/claim
```

Those are the only four paths enrolled MomentBackup computers post to, and they cannot carry an Umbrel session cookie. Each request carries its own bearer token or Ed25519-signed body, which the Hub verifies; the list is exact paths, not a `/api/*` glob, so the dashboard's own `GET /api/status` and `/api/v1/*` stay behind Umbrel auth along with `/setup`, `/login`, and every page.

Umbrel auth in front of `/setup` is a real improvement here: on a bare deployment whoever reaches `/setup` first claims the Hub, and behind Umbrel auth that race is closed.

## Verification

Umbrel testing performed: none — I have no umbrelOS device or test environment. Please treat this as untested through Umbrel.

Environment tested:
- [ ] Umbrel device
- [ ] Local umbrelOS test environment
- [x] Not runtime tested

Architecture tested:
- [ ] amd64
- [ ] arm64

What I did verify:

- `npm run lint:apps -- momentbackup-hub --check-images` → **0 errors, 1 warning** (below)
- `git diff --check` → clean
- Image tag, index digest, and both platforms confirmed against the GHCR manifest list; the image is public and pulls with no credentials
- Port 8677 is free across every `umbrel-app.yml` `port:` and every host-published compose port in this repo (8675 and 8676 are taken)

Known lint warnings or caveats:

```
WARNING access.security_opt momentbackup-hub/docker-compose.yml:24
  Service `server` sets security options; justify this in the PR.
```

That is `no-new-privileges:true`, alongside `read_only: true` with `tmpfs: [/tmp]` and `cap_drop: [ALL]`. It is a restriction, not an escalation: the Hub writes only to `/data`, binds an unprivileged port, and never executes anything else, so it needs none of what those remove. Happy to drop them if you would rather packages not set `security_opt` at all.

## Notes

- **Persistence.** `${APP_DATA_DIR}/data/hub:/data` holds the Hub's command-signing identity, sign-in hashes, sealed two-factor secrets, which key each computer is trusted under, and the audit chain. Losing it means enrolling every computer again, so it should not be in `backupIgnore`. `data/hub/.gitkeep` is committed.
- **User.** The image defaults to uid/gid 10001 but supports any uid; this package runs `1000:1000` to match Umbrel's app-data ownership.
- **No host access.** No Docker socket, no privileged mode, no host networking, no device or host mounts, no permissions, no dependencies. One container plus `app_proxy`.
- **Client requirement.** Joining a Hub needs MomentBackup 1.0.13 or later on each computer. The Hub is free; the desktop app it reports on is paid. Restores never involve the Hub and are never licence-gated.
- **Source is private.** `repo:` points at the public GHCR package page, <https://github.com/MomentBackup/momentbackup-hub/pkgs/container/momentbackup-hub>. `website:` is <https://momentbackup.com>, and the reference compose plus the full configuration prose is at <https://momentbackup.com/hub/>. Every published tag keeps its own digest and keyless cosign signature; the verification command is on that page.
- **`submission:`** is set to this PR's URL.

### Assets

`gallery: []` and no `icon`, per the packaging guide.

- Logo source (SVG): <https://momentbackup.com/favicon.svg>
- Screenshot: not linked yet. The dashboard screenshot currently published on the vendor site carries stale UI wording that is being corrected upstream, and I would rather not hand you an asset that is about to be wrong. I will post a current screenshot in this thread as soon as the replacement is published — please tell me if you need it before review can start.

This release adds a configurable default lockfile format, lets `store prune` reclaim stale global-virtual-store entries, tightens `devEngines` version enforcement, and lets embedders drop the comment-preserving workspace-YAML dependency chain.

#### Added

- **Configurable default lockfile format** ([#​1271](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/pull/1271) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)) — New `defaultLockfileFormat` setting (`"aube"` or `"pnpm"`, default `"aube"`) chooses which lockfile to create when no supported lockfile is present on disk. Existing lockfiles remain authoritative, so the setting never converts a lockfile or writes a duplicate alongside one that already exists. This makes the `aube clean --lockfile` → reinstall workflow reliably regenerate `pnpm-lock.yaml` for projects that need pnpm compatibility. Configurable via workspace config, `settings.toml`, `.npmrc`, and env, and applied consistently across install and the add/remove/update/dedupe/audit write paths. Addresses [#​1264](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/discussions/1264).

  ```
  # settings.toml
  defaultLockfileFormat = "pnpm"
  ```

- **Optional workspace YAML preservation for embedders** ([#​1278](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/pull/1278) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)) — Comment- and format-preserving `pnpm-workspace.yaml` edits are now gated behind a default-on `workspace-yaml-preserve` feature. The standalone Aube CLI is unchanged, but embedders (e.g. mise) can disable the feature to drop the `yamlpatch`/`yamlpath`/`tree-sitter` dependency chain — which required Rust 1.97+ — falling back to a canonical full-document rewrite.

#### Fixed

- **Prune unused global virtual store entries** ([#​1273](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/pull/1273) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)) — `aube store prune` previously only walked the content-addressable store, leaving hashed graph directories under `<cacheDir>/virtual-store` behind even after their projects were deleted. Installs that use the global virtual store now register the project (including warm/fast-path installs after upgrading), and prune uses that registry to keep entries still linked from live projects while removing unreachable ones before continuing with normal content-store cleanup. Installs and pruning coordinate via shared/exclusive locks, registry-managed entries live under a versioned `virtual-store/v1/` namespace so older releases' entries are untouched, and registry failures fail closed with `ERR_AUBE_GVS_PRUNE_FAILED`. `--dry-run` covers the new phase. Addresses [#​1268](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/discussions/1268).

- **Enforce `devEngines` aube version errors** ([#​1269](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/pull/1269) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)) — An explicit `devEngines.packageManager.onFail: "error"` now correctly rejects the invoking aube when its version does not satisfy the declared aube version, instead of silently re-execing to an already-installed match. The same self-version policy is now enforced for `aube --version` (which previously returned before self-version handling), and `aube --version --workspace-root` works outside a workspace. `devEngines.packageManager` entries naming pnpm or other package managers keep their existing compatibility behavior. Fixes [#​1263](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/discussions/1263).

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/jdx/aube/compare/v1.38.1...v1.39.0>

If aube is saving your team install time or CI minutes, please consider [sponsoring at jdx.dev](https://jdx.dev/sponsors.html). Individual and company sponsorships are what keep the project fast, free, and independent.

### [`v1.38.1`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/releases/tag/v1.38.1): : Sharper updates, shims, and filtered installs

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/compare/v1.38.0...v1.38.1)

A small patch release with three targeted fixes to `aube update --no-save`, POSIX shim resolution, and cold-store filtered installs.

#### Fixed

- **Keep `--no-save` resolutions inside the existing range** ([#​1247](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/pull/1247) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)) — `aube update --latest --no-save` no longer treats `--latest` as permission to bump the manifest or catalog specifier. It now refreshes the lockfile to the newest version allowed by the retained range (for both direct and shared catalog entries) instead of recording a `latest` that the specifier itself excludes — which could otherwise make a subsequent frozen install reject the lockfile.
- **Resolve symlinks in POSIX shims** ([#​1249](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/pull/1249) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)) — Generated POSIX `.bin` shims now follow their invocation path through absolute and relative symlink chains (up to 40 hops, guarding against cycles) before computing `basedir`. author: fritzviljoen
body:
Untyped values could travel from an HTTP parameter into an operation and out the
other side: `Date.parse(params[:on])` turning a typo into a 500, a time read in
the server's zone rather than the requester's, a service keyword nobody asserted.

`TypedParams` parses request input once.
`TypedArguments` asserts every service keyword — never coerces — and refuses
zoneless `Time`/`DateTime` as a declared type and as a smuggled value; a
wall-clock reading like "18:30" travels as a String. `Service.call` must answer
with a `Result`.

author: cixzhang
body:
Nightly component audit of `core/Blockquote` against [Component Audit Rubric](https://github.com/facebook/astryx/wiki/Component-Audit-Rubric) **v1.4**, at `b3dd679619`.

| | Score | Grade | Open BLOCKs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 79.7 | C | 1 |
| After | 89.4 | B | 0 |

Pre-fix score is already in the ledger: [`ed9b5538e2`](https://github.com/facebook/astryx/wiki/_compare/ed9b5538e273a33c0247a76e2d1b852b77f3343a). **The post-fix score is not recorded yet**; it is held until this PR is on `main`, and will be written then.

Blockquote is 95 source lines with two props. Most of the rubric does not apply to it, so four sections fall under the one-third non-vacuous threshold and are marked `limited` with their weight redistributed: a11y (3 of 19 items produce a verdict), code health (4 of 21), i18n and RTL (5 of 18), responsive (2 of 11). Sections were not padded to fill the night, and inapplicable items are N/A rather than scored as passes.

## What moved

| Section | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| §1 Accessibility (`limited`) | 3.0 | 4.5 | The `contentinfo` landmark is gone |
| §4 Behavior | 3.5 | 4.5 | Overflow fixed, adversarial finding fixed |
| §6 Testing | 3.5 | 4.5 | Server render asserted, 8 tests to 12 |
| §7 Code health (`limited`) | 3.5 | 5.0 | `isRenderable` replaces the bare nullish guard |
| §8 Docs | 3.0 | 4.5 | Six doc gaps closed, prose corrected |
| §9 i18n and RTL (`limited`) | 4.5 | 4.5 | Long-string story now exists |
| §10 Responsive (`limited`) | 4.0 | 4.5 | No overflow at 320px, narrow story added |

§2 Theming 4.5, §3 API 4.5, §5a 4.5 and §5b 4.0 are unchanged.

## Fixed

### The attribution rendered a `contentinfo` document landmark (BLOCK, §1 A2)

`Blockquote.tsx:87` wrapped the `cite` attribution in a bare `<footer>`. `<blockquote>` is a sectioning root, not sectioning content, so HTML-AAM does not scope that `<footer>` away: it maps to a `contentinfo` landmark, the "footer of the document" landmark.

Measured in Chromium through CDP `Accessibility.getFullAXTree`: three quotes carrying `cite` produced three non-ignored `role=contentinfo` nodes. On a page that also has a real footer, axe reports two violations and the node it prints is Blockquote's own `<footer>`:

```
landmark-no-duplicate-contentinfo (moderate)
  <footer><cite class="astryx1lliihq ...
landmark-unique (moderate)
  <footer><cite class="astryx1lliihq ...
```

The victim is not hypothetical. `packages/cli/assets/templates/blocks/components/Blockquote/BlockquoteTestimonials.tsx` ships three quotes with `cite` in one block, and that is the code consumers copy.

`pnpm a11y:audit --components Blockquote` was green before this PR and is green after it. It missed this because every Blockquote story rendered a single isolated quote, so no second landmark existed for the duplicate rule to fire against. That is the §6 3/5 anchor exactly: axe green partly because the stories are too thin to reach the interesting states.

Fix: render the `<cite>` directly. After, `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` reports **0** `contentinfo` nodes, and the two axe landmark violations are gone. The rendered geometry is byte-identical: root rect `x40 y40 w820 h52` and cite rect `x58 y72 w802 h20` before and after, with `margin-block-start: 8px` on the cite unchanged, because the `<footer>` carried no border or padding and the cite's margin was collapsing through it.

### A falsy `cite` emitted an empty `<cite>` (FIX, §7 C12)

`cite != null` passes for `false`, `true` and `''`, so the ordinary consumer shape `cite={condition && author}` rendered `<footer><cite></cite></footer>`. `@astryx/no-nullish-jsx-guard` already flagged `Blockquote.tsx:86` and named the remedy; the rule is `warn` in both lint tiers, so nothing failed on it.

Now guarded with `isRenderable`. Measured after: `cite={false}` and `cite=""` both render `innerHTML` of just the quote, with no `<cite>` element. Rendered height was 0 either way, so this was DOM and accessibility-tree noise rather than a visible gap. `lint:strict` warnings go from 56 to 55 and Blockquote no longer appears.

### A long unbroken word overflowed its own box (FIX, §4 B10, §10 R1)

At a 320px viewport a 107-character word gave the blockquote `scrollWidth 813` against `clientWidth 238`; a long URL gave `373` against `238`. No document-level horizontal scroll, so this was cosmetic overflow rather than an unreachable control. `overflow-wrap` resolved to `normal`, while `Markdown`, `Code`, `ChatMessageBubble` and `Tooltip` all set `break-word` on their long-form text.

Now `overflowWrap: 'break-word'` on the root. Measured after, both cases: `scrollWidth 238` equals `clientWidth 238`, no overflow.

### No server render test after #4407 (FIX, §6 V12)

[#4407](https://github.com/facebook/astryx/pull/4407) dropped `'use client'` from this file and nothing asserted the result. Verified with a real `renderToString` that it does render on the server, and added that as a test rather than leaving the claim to `check-use-client.mjs`.

### Docs (FIX, §8 X3, X4, X10, X11, X12, X16)

- The overview said "accent-colored left border". The rule is `--color-border-emphasized`, a neutral border token measuring `rgb(212,212,212)` in light and `rgb(82,82,82)` in dark, and it is a logical inline-start border that moves to the right edge in RTL. Corrected in the English, Chinese and dense docs and in the component JSDoc.
- `usage.anatomy` was absent (X4). Added, with the three parts.
- One "don't" where the convention is two or more (X3). Added a second, and a third "do" carrying accessibility guidance (X16), including not to re-wrap the attribution in a `<footer>`.
- `xstyle` was documented but no story touched it, so prop-to-story coverage was 2 of 3 (X10). A pull-quote story now exercises it.
- No long-text, narrow-container or overflow story (X11, X12, §10 R11). Added `LongContent` and `NarrowContainer`. The a11y and RTL sweeps only see what a story renders.
- `playground.defaults` was absent on a component whose `children` are required, so the playground opened blank (X19). Added.

## Needs review

Everything below is a decision rather than a correction, so this pass did not touch it.

**The attribution still sits inside the `<blockquote>`.** The HTML spec says attribution "must be placed outside the blockquote element", with `<figure>` plus `<figcaption>` as the worked example. The accessibility tree confirms the consequence: the blockquote subtree exposes both the quotation StaticText and "Steve Jobs". Moving to a figure changes the rendered structure and the component's theming surface, which is an API decision.

**`cite` reuses a native attribute name with a different meaning (§3 P33, NIT).** `<blockquote cite>` is natively a URL pointing at the source. Here `cite` is a `ReactNode` rendered as visible text. `BaseProps` extends `React.HTMLAttributes`, which never carried `cite`, so there is nothing to `Omit` and no type collision, but there is also no way for a consumer to set the standards-correct source URL. P33's remedy is to keep the semantic name, and `cite` is not a semantic name distinct from the attribute, it is the attribute name. Renaming a public prop or adding one is not a fix-pass call.

**The attribution is a raw `<cite>` rather than `Text as="cite"` (§2 T29).** Composing `Text` would give the attribution the system's supporting-text treatment and a second theme target. It would also add `astryx-text` to the rendered classes, which changes the theming surface.

**The rule's width comes from `spacingVars['--spacing-0-5']` (§2 T3, NIT).** It is a token, but a spacing token used as a border width. `borderVars['--border-width']` exists and is 1px, and the design here wants 2px, so closing this properly means adding a border-width token, which is a system decision. `Section.tsx:95` uses a raw `1` for the same job, so the house is not consistent today either.

**Measure runs past 75ch.** At the story's 820px width and 16px body the line is roughly 102

author: yssion
body:
In `levelsetlattice`, the previous default Fourier truncation of `ntuple(i->2, D)` is insufficient for 14 cubic space groups. For those groups, every modulation, however generic, yields a structure with strictly higher symmetry than requested:
- **Extra point-group operations:** 196, 197, 201, 202, 203, 204, 207, 209, 210, 211
- **Extra translations:** 219, 222, 226, 228

`idxmax` now defaults to `:auto`, resolving to `default_idxmax(sgnum, Dᵛ)`: the smallest symmetry-safe isotropic truncation, floored at the previous default of 2. The 14 affected groups get `(3,3,3)` (197, 201, 204, 207, 211), `(4,4,4)` (196, 202, 210, 222), or `(5,5,5)` (203, 209, 219, 226, 228). The behaviour for the 216 other space groups remains unchanged at `(2, 2, 2)`. The double gyroid (SG 230) example in the docs is thus unaffected. 1D and 2D groups are also unchanged since all their minima are ≤ 2.

An explicitly provided `idxmax` is still permitted; a warning is generated if it is not symmetry-safe. This check is done for both isotropic and anisotropic truncations. I also thought it would be nice if the user can query `is_symmetry_safe(sgnum, idxmax)` and `minimal_idxmax(sgnum, Dᵛ)`. Maybe you have better ideas for function naming or otherwise.

The tabulated data is in `src/tables/fourier_truncations.jl` and is generated from `build/compute_minimal_fourier_truncations.jl`: a truncation is symmetry-safe if the retained `G`-vectors span the centred reciprocal lattice, and no holohedry operation outside the group maps every orbit to itself *or to its negative partner*. The last criterion comes from the fact that `f` is real so an operation mapping some orbit `O` to `-O` has no modulus obstruction, only phase conditions carrying a modulation-dependent unknown. Concretely, a generic lattice in, for example, SG 27 at `(1,1,1)` is exactly centrosymmetric about a centre that *shifts with the modulation* — invisible to any criterion that demands a fixed translation part. This moves the isotropic (anisotropic) minima of 22 (29) groups, but they all fall below the previous `(2, 2, 2)` default so are completely unrelated to the 14 affected groups above.

## Summary

- add lexical `ScopedExpression` compilation and evaluation for separately bound source bodies
- delegate nested type environments so scoped bodies share the same structural declaration model
- preserve deprecated `SymbolSource` compatibility, including namespaced member chains, while normalizing dependency identity to `ReferencePath`

## Why

Some Axiom hosts need to compile a source body once and evaluate it repeatedly against a separately bound local record. `ScopedExpression` provides that lexical boundary without inventing another path representation or weakening the outer program's dependency analysis.

This capability is independent of Product Catalogue's Axiom #93 migration. It is stacked on #93 only because it extends the structural declaration and reference model introduced there.

## Validation

- Pint

Depends on #93.

## What

Adds an Enablement App migration status banner to this repo's first documentation page.

Status for this repo: **not-migrated**.

## Why

The Dynatrace Hub lists 26 repos, but nothing on the Hub, in the GitHub Pages docs
or in the Enablement App tells a learner which trainings are already immersive,
interactive and self-service in the app, which are mid-conversion, and which are not
migrated yet. This banner makes that visible on the page itself.

## Why inline text and not a `docs/snippets/` include

The app's importer strips `--8<-- "snippets/..."` lines
(`stripSnippetIncludes`, `api/import-lab.helpers.ts`). A snippet-based banner would
look right on GitHub Pages and be silently dropped in the Enablement App — the surface
it exists to serve. So the banner is literal Markdown in the page.

## Verification

Rendered through both real parsers, not a reimplementation:

| Surface | Parser | Result |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub Pages | Python-Markdown `admonition` | `<div class="admonition ...">` with working contact links |
| Enablement App | `stripSnippetIncludes()` + `preprocessMarkdown()` | `<div data-admonition="...">`, banner is the first block |

## Please leave this PR open

This is one of 23 repos in a fleet-wide wave. Framework **1.10.0** will add a
minimalistic Orbital-specific container greeting, and the `FRAMEWORK_VERSION` bump
will be pushed onto this same branch so the banner and the greeting ship together.

body:
## Summary
This PR will make the API reference code samples show a meaningful placeholder for each authentication header instead of the same `<api-key>` for all four.

- Replaced `x-example` with `x-default` on the four `apiKey` security schemes in `openapi/openapi.json` and `openapi/v2-subscriptions.json`.
- `x-example` is not an OpenAPI field and is not read by Mintlify, so it never took effect — `x-default` is the extension Mintlify reads.
- Values: `X-Client-ID` → `your-client-id`, `X-Client-Secret` → `your-client-secret`, `X-Merchant-ID` → `sub-merchant-id` (it is the sub-merchant's id supplied by a PSP caller, not the caller's own), `X-API-Version` → `3.0.0` (`2.0.0` in the v2 subscriptions spec, since it is a literal version string and not a credential).
- `openapi/v3/openapi.json` is not referenced by `docs.json` and renders nothing, so it is left untouched.

## ClickUp
- https://app.clickup.com/t/86d423f73

## Test plan
- [x] Verified locally in a browser against `mintlify dev`
- [x] `/api-reference/v3/order/create` renders `X-API-Version: 3.0.0`, `X-Client-ID: your-client-id`, `X-Client-Secret: your-client-secret`, `X-Merchant-ID: sub-merchant-id` — no `<api-key>`

Note: the values are substituted on client hydration, so the initial server-rendered HTML still contains `<api-key>` for a moment before the sample settles. That is Mintlify's rendering behaviour, unchanged by this PR.

author: kwd421
itoh-shun
body:
First of the v3 Trust Foundation issues from the #443 roadmap.

Everything a reviewer needs was already recorded — `task.json`, `acceptance.json`, `provenance.json`, `steps.json`, `approvals.json` — across files that each answer a different question, and none of which answers **"why is this change acceptable?"**. `workbench.py receipt` is the projection that does.

```
$ workbench.py receipt <task-id> --markdown

**acceptable** — task status `accepted` with gate `passed_with_warnings`

- producer harness: not recorded — tasks created before #428 carry no `caller` block…
- verifier identity: not recorded — rig does not record a reviewer identity per task…
- independence: **unrecorded** — independence can be neither confirmed nor denied
- isolation: git-worktree — write isolation from the main tree, not an OS sandbox
- no_gate_tampering: **overridden** — …
```

## It is only a projection

The gate status is copied, never recomputed. The existing accept-time HMAC is referenced and checked rather than duplicated under a second key — two signed records of one fact can disagree, and the disagreement would be rig's to explain. `waiting-approval` is derived from recorded decisions without re-evaluating the quorum; that judgment belongs to `govern`.

## Three things it refuses to do

**Render absence as success.** The producing runtime and model, the verifier's identity, and whether the verifier was independent are absent from task state today. Each is `{"observed": false, "reason": …}` — never a blank, a zero, or a default that reads as fine to someone skimming. The independence verdict is `unrecorded`, not `independent`: no record is not evidence of separation.

**Call a worktree a sandbox.** `eval/cases.py` ranks `none < agent-policy < os-enforced` for evaluation providers. A workbench task's worktree keeps a change off the main tree and holds no OS boundary, so isolation says `git-worktree` / `main-tree` and states what that does and does not buy.

**Let a stale receipt pass as current.** Every projected source is recorded with its digest, **absent ones included** — without that, a receipt taken mid-run stays fresh through `accept` writing `provenance.json`, the most material change a task can undergo, invisible because the receipt never named the file it was waiting for. `--verify` compares content, not mtime.

## Acceptance criteria

All 9 met. Mission Control's `task_detail` carries the receipt, built on request rather than served off disk, with the stored file reported alongside under its own freshness verdict. HTML rendering of it belongs to #426, which is the issue about how the execution graph is shown.

## Evidence

- `pytest tests/` — **2681 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed** (23m14s), re-run after the Mission Control addition rather than reused from before it
- `scripts/validate.py` — 44 PASS / 3 WARN / 0 FAIL; ruff clean
- `eval affected --base master --head <commit> --ratchet` — `status: debt`, `affected_cases: []`, no coverage regression
- **25 mutations, all detected** — including: rendering unmeasured as empty, claiming `independent`, naming `os-enforced`, comparing mtime instead of content, ignoring a source that appeared later, rounding an unmapped status to `acceptable`, and dropping the declared-vs-inferred distinction on `caller`
- **41 tests, no existing test file modified**

Adversarial review: codex (`gpt-5.3-codex-spark`, `--sandbox read-only`, `--ignore-user-config`), two rounds, REJECT both times, **all four findings adopted**:

1. *(HIGH)* The receipt read `final_commit`/`commit`; `record-commit` writes `commit_sha`. Every task with a linked commit reported as having none — the exact false negative this module exists to avoid producing.
2. *(HIGH)* `_FINAL_STATUS` was missing `skipped` and `pending`, and named a task status (`active`) that does not exist. An accepted task read as `in-progress`. Every pair from the real vocabularies is now spelled out.
3. *(MEDIUM)* Absent sources were omitted rather than recorded, leaving the freshness hole described above.
4. *(MEDIUM)* The `waiting-approval` overlay ran before the mapping, so a discarded task or a failed gate could be masked as "waiting on a person". It now applies only where the mapping already said `awaiting-acceptance`.

Closes #428

author: winking324
body:
## Summary

- use the standard `.floating` level for the recommended global PiP mode while preserving all-Spaces and full-screen collection behavior
- retain the previous `.screenSaver` behavior as an explicit “Force topmost” compatibility mode with a clear system-menu warning
- keep the current-Space mode and update settings/context-menu labels to describe behavior rather than only the raw window level
- place the software-update progress panel at `.normal` so it remains below every PiP mode
- update the window-level and tooltip implementation notes

## Root cause

The global PiP mode used `.screenSaver`, whose WindowServer level is above status-bar pop-up menus. A PiP positioned below the menu bar could therefore cover menus opened from menu-bar utilities.

Window level and Space behavior are independent AppKit concepts. The recommended mode can remain visible across Spaces and alongside full-screen apps through `.canJoinAllSpaces` and `.fullScreenAuxiliary` without using the screen-saver level.

## Compatibility and impact

Existing `global` and `normal` preference raw values remain valid. Existing `global` users automatically receive the system-friendly behavior, while users who require the legacy strongest level can explicitly select “Force topmost.”

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- `swift build`
- `swift build -c release`
- `bash scripts/build-app.sh --fast --debug`
- verified the AppKit level ordering at runtime: `normal(0) < floating(3) < modal(8) < mainMenu(24) < status(25) < popUpMenu(101) < screenSaver(1000)`
- verified at runtime that `isFloatingPanel` raises a panel to `.floating`, and an explicit `.normal` assignment restores level 0

The app bundle build completed successfully. The local release signing identity was unavailable, so the validation bundle used the build script’s documented ad-hoc fallback.

author: posthog[bot]
body:
## Problem

- People who open an older password reset email get "The provided link is invalid or has expired", even though the link worked when it was sent. They did nothing wrong and are locked out.
- Every reset request overwrites `requested_password_reset_at`.
- The reset token hash folds that field in, so a second request invalidates every earlier link.
- This rejects account recovery at a measurable rate every month. The linked report has the figures.

## Changes

- Drop `requested_password_reset_at` from the reset token hash, so a new request no longer invalidates earlier links.
- The token still depends on the password hash, so it stops working once the password changes.
- Each token keeps its own timestamp, so every link expires on its own `PASSWORD_RESET_TIMEOUT` window (1 day).
- The reset email now states the link lifetime, so a person with several emails knows each one works until it expires.

> [!NOTE]
> Two items from the report are intentionally out of scope. The request endpoint still returns 204 for an unknown address, because revealing which addresses have an account enables user enumeration. The invalid-link page copy is unchanged, because "requesting a new email voids the previous one" is no longer true after this fix.

## How did you test this code?

- Added `test_reissuing_a_reset_keeps_the_earlier_link_valid`. It requests two resets, then asserts both links validate. No existing test covered two live links at once.
- Ran the four reset tests locally (the new one plus `test_password_change_invalidates_reset_token`, `test_invalid_token_returns_error`, `test_anonymous_user_can_request_password_reset`). All pass.
- Not run: the wider backend suite.

No app UI changed. Only the email template copy changed.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

- Authored by Claude (Claude Code) acting on an inbox report.
- Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`.
- The token hash was the root cause: it mixed in a per-request timestamp field. Django's default already invalidates a token on password change via the password hash, so removing the field is enough to keep older links valid while still expiring them and killing them after a reset.
