author: kingye
body:
## Summary

Aligns jyc's HTTP `User-Agent` behavior across all outbound HTTP paths so jyc doesn't leak its identity by default, while making the existing `ai_providers.<name>.user_agent` config work on every provider.

### Changes

- **Anthropic native provider** (`type = "anthropic"`): `AnthropicProvider::new` now accepts and applies `user_agent: Option<&str>` (model→provider precedence, same as OpenAI-compat). Previously the field was silently dropped on this path.
- **Default UA for all providers:** when `user_agent` is unset, both Anthropic and OpenAI-compat providers fall back to reqwest's default `reqwest/<version>`. No jyc fingerprint leaks unless operators opt in.
- **webfetch tool:** swapped hardcoded `jyc-agent/0.1` UA for a modern Chrome UA (`Mozilla/5.0 ... Chrome/131.0.0.0 ...`) so it actually works on common public sites (reqwest default is widely blocked; Chrome UA is widely accepted). Bump the version by hand every few releases.

### Why

Motivating scenario: disguising jyc as a first-party client (`opencode`, `pi`, etc.) by setting `user_agent` on the provider config — previously impossible on the Anthropic native path. With this change, that works on every provider.

### Tests

- New `complete_sends_custom_user_agent` in `provider/anthropic.rs` (wiremock-based, mirrors the OpenAI-compat equivalent).
- Updated 2 existing in-tree tests (`complete_error_includes_response_body_on_4xx`, `complete_raw_sends_cache_breakpoints_on_the_wire`) to the new 6-arg `AnthropicProvider::new` signature.

### Risk

Behavior change is **one-way**: only takes effect when operators explicitly set `user_agent`. Default path (`user_agent = None`) keeps the previous behavior on OpenAI-compat (already had reqwest default) and now also returns reqwest default on Anthropic native (was: nothing set on the wire, which reqwest filled with its own default anyway — net behavior identical from the wire's POV).

webfetch UA change is observable to upstream servers but matches the existing `invoice-processing` skill's pattern and matches what most user-agents look like.

### Out of scope

- No UA validation (RFC 7231 free-form string; trust-boundary responsibility is on operator).
- No webfetch UA configurability (could be a future `tools.webfetch.user_agent` if needed; YAGNI until then).
- No automatic version bump for the Chrome UA string (explicit choice; not worth the maintenance cost).

author: oberbichler
body:
Follow-up to #6, fixing the cause rather than the symptom.

Both `Cargo.lock` and `uv.lock` record this package's own version, and the release job bumped neither. So after every release the committed lockfiles disagree with `Cargo.toml`/`pyproject.toml`, and the next local `cargo build` or `uv run` silently rewrites them in whoever's working tree ran first. v0.2.0 hit this twice — `Cargo.lock` by hand in #6, then `uv.lock` showed up immediately after, which is this PR's second change.

The bump step now patches both lockfiles by regex on the package's own name-then-version block, and asserts it matched exactly once, so a lockfile format change fails the release loudly instead of shipping a stale version. Deliberately not `cargo update`/`uv lock`: that job sets up only Python, and adding a Rust toolchain plus uv to rewrite two lines would cost more than it saves.

Verified by running the substitution against the real `Cargo.lock` and `uv.lock` (one entry patched in each) and by parsing the workflow YAML. Nothing about the published v0.2.0 artifacts was affected — maturin resolves without `--locked`, and `pip install javapyn==0.2.0` reports 0.2.0.

author: paulossjunior
body:
## O vão, encontrado no dado real

O report "why not everyone?" mostrava **13 pessoas below_floor com "0 tarefas com texto, piso de 15"** — e a investigação pessoa a pessoa mostrou que **nenhuma tem perfil e TODAS têm issues designadas** (leticiacomerio tem 19). O recorte: a primeira geração só contava issues **CLOSED**, e essas pessoas só têm abertas.

## A regra (#399, pedida em 2026-08-16)

Sem perfil e com tarefa designada — mesmo pouca — **gera**. Aberta é intenção, não evidência: o perfil não inventa competência de promessa. Mas "alocada em X, nada concluído observado ainda" responde *quem trabalha em quê*, e pessoa invisível não responde nada. A limitação vai no próprio material (`concluídas: 0, abertas: N`). Da segunda geração em diante, os pisos voltam inteiros.

## Critério de aceite do #399, atendido

Quem não tem perfil só pode aparecer pulado por `no_assignment` ou `observation_ended` — nunca por piso. O motivo fino do report, recalculado na leitura, passa a mostrar essas 13 como "geraria hoje".

## Evidência

- Material da leticiacomerio (19 designadas, 0 concluídas) **monta** na base real.
- Testes: `Material.build` com só-abertas monta em `:primeira` e volta a `below_floor` em `:normal`; `Regeneration.due?` gera para designação só de abertas.
- `mix gates` 13/13 verdes.
- Censo esperado: 47 → **60 elegíveis** de 88.

**Empilhado no #406** (o conserto do crash) — a base reaponta para main quando ele mergear.

Closes #399

author: nao1215
body:
Five loader errors were emitted without a diagnostic code. `internal/loader/matrix.go` built its messages with `fmt.Sprintf` into a plain `[]string` and never touched `internal/diag`, while the rest of the loader reports through `add(diag.Code, ...)`. The changelog states the contract as "every error atago raises while loading a spec now carries a stable, searchable code", and one error list could show coded and uncoded entries side by side — with `atago explain ATG…` and the published error reference having nothing to say about any matrix mistake, including the check added specifically to catch the row that does not bind a `${var}` the scenario name references.

The codes reuse the meanings that already exist rather than minting five new ones: an empty `matrix:` is `ATG2202` (a list that must hold something), an empty row is `ATG2204` (a key written with nothing in it), a key shadowing a built-in is `ATG2404`, a name referencing a variable no row binds is `ATG2403` (a reference naming something the spec does not declare — a matrix name is rendered from the row alone, so an unbound reference survives as literal text), and rows collapsing to one name is `ATG2501`, whose fix text already points at `matrix:` as the way to generate distinct names. The two registry entries that now cover a matrix case say so, which is what the reference renders.

The matrix validator keeps its own phase and its own signature, since it runs on the raw decoded spec before `expandMatrix`, and the order in which the two phases report is unchanged. What changed is that both build their messages through one accumulator, `errorList`, whose only writer takes a `diag.Code` — a phase can no longer hand a raw string back to the caller.

The existing gate runs one way: `TestE2E_EveryCodeIsProvoked` proves every published code is provoked by a scenario, and nothing proved that every error the loader can emit carries a code. That direction is closed by the corpus the loader tests already are: every rejection case now asserts that each message of the returned error names its diagnostic — the single-message form on its first line, since a parse error carries a source excerpt below it, and each entry of the multi-error list form. Reverting the fix makes it fail on five cases by name. Two self-hosted E2E assertions pin the codes users actually see.

Closes #561

author: akiojin
body:
Closes #3457

> **マージ後追記**: develop へ着地済み（マージコミット `088aa06c1`）。#3457 は受け入れ条件の照合を経てクローズ済み（Issue コメント 5324193645）。
>
> **User Verification Result: n/a（実機確認は未実施）** — 本 PR は frontend 無変更（`crates/gwt/web/` の差分ゼロ）で視覚確認の対象がない。ただし Launch の挙動は変わるため、停止中 Issue での実機再投入確認を 4 回依頼したが回答が得られず、自動テスト・CI 全 17 checks・`verify.run`（`vrr-9cf0a8890d934b7da9242003c36cff86`、6 コマンド全 exit 0）のみで判定した。実機で再投入が通らない場合は #3457 を reopen すること。

## 症状

Host がクラッシュすると、その Session の durable な `.toml` だけが残り runtime sidecar はどの PID namespace からも消える。この保持者が Active な execution generation を握ったままだと、誰も settle できないため以後の launch が恒久的に拒否される。

```
an execution generation already exists for spec #N (active generation held by Session <id> (Running));
use Continue work to create a successor, or run the execution.status JSON operation for the exact recovery route
```

案内される Continue work は Work item が無ければ UI に存在せず、`execution.status` の `available_recoveries` も空になるため復帰経路が閉じる。

## 根本原因

`classify_exact_session_runtime` が「sidecar がどこにも無い」を `Unknown`（＝証拠が存在するが信用できない）に潰していた。launch された Session は必ず自 Host の namespace に sidecar を publish し、Host は自分の namespace しか消さない。したがって「どの namespace にも無い」は**どの Host もその Session を実行していない決定的証拠**であり、矛盾証拠とは区別できる。

## 変更

1. `ExactSessionRuntimeDisposition::Absent` を追加し、証拠の不在と証拠の不信を分離した。
2. runtime 証拠を `ManualLaunchRuntimeEvidence`（`Proof` / `Absent`）で型表現。`Absent` は generation owner lease と session lease の下で不在を再検証してから successor を準備する。
3. genesis launch 経路（Issue Monitor 再試行 / Start Work）で、世代が Blocked でないときに保持者を分類し、`Absent` のときだけ exact-terminal successor トランザクションで世代を引き継ぐ。

## 安全側の担保

- 生きた保持者（sidecar あり）・読めない durable 記録・保持者が現行 binding を持たない場合・曖昧な `Unknown` は**従来どおり拒否**する。
- 保持者が sidecar を publish した時点で `Absent` ではなくなるため、生存中の Session から世代を奪わない。
- 既存の拒否テスト `fresh_launch_conflict_names_the_generation_holder_and_recovery_route` は**無変更のまま**通る。

## テスト

新規 4 件（いずれも RED を確認してから GREEN 化）:

- `exact_session_runtime_without_any_sidecar_is_absent_not_unknown`
- `absent_runtime_prepares_a_successor_for_a_still_running_durable_holder`（クラッシュで `Running` のまま残った durable 記録でも回復できる）
- `absent_runtime_evidence_is_refused_once_the_holder_publishes_a_sidecar`（逆方向の安全性）
- `fresh_launch_supersedes_a_generation_whose_holder_is_unreachable`（genesis 経路の end-to-end）

既存 `manual_launch_unknown_terminal_proof_refuses_before_pane_and_authority_mutation` は、sidecar 削除ではなく**信用できない sidecar の publish** を対象に付け替えた（`..._ambiguous_...` へ改名）。sidecar 削除は本 Issue が回復可能にした状態そのものであり、そこでの拒否を固定し続けることはできない。「拒否は pane と authority の変更前に行う」という安全性の主張は保持している。

## 検証

`verify.run` record `vrr-9cf0a8890d934b7da9242003c36cff86`（6 コマンド、全 exit 0）

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p gwt --lib`
- `cargo test -p gwt --bin gwt`
- `cargo test -p gwt-agent`
- `cargo test -p gwt-core`

自動導出された plan には `--bin gwt` が含まれていないため明示的に追加した（#3457 の中核テストはこのターゲットにある。#3640 参照）。

## このブランチに同梱されている他の変更

このブランチは develop から 359 commits 遅れており、取り込みを伴った。以下は #3457 の修正そのものではない。

- **前任セッションの launch_wizard lineage 対応**（Quick Start の Resume/Continue が predecessor と owner を引き継ぐ）
- **テスト安定化**（`board_remote` / `improvement*` / `index_*` / `workspace_cli_test` 等）

### 取り込み時に戻した前任実装

- `prepare_exact_relaunch_execution_authority` — develop の `prepare_resume_producing_authority` / `ReboundCurrent` が上位互換のため develop 側を採用。
- `RuntimeInstanceId` — develop の window runtime incarnation 機構が上位互換。
- `run_origin_operation` の origin skip guard — `production_server_shutdown_waits_for_authority_revocation_and_reaps_child` を決定的に破壊するため撤去。**前任が「credential helper がテストプロセスより長生きして verification runner の出力パイプを掴む」問題に対して入れたものなので、当該 flake が CI で再発したら別途対処が必要。**

### 自動マージが落としていた develop コード（復旧済み）

自動マージがブランチ側の削除を勝たせ、コンフリクトマーカー無しで develop の production コードが消えていた箇所を 1 件復旧した。

- `wizard.rs` の `resume_workspace_agent_events` から linked Resume を authority-producing continuation として扱う経路が消失していた（`linked_workspace_resume_routes_through_authority_producing_continuation` が失敗して発覚）。

### 関連する副産物

- **#3662** — issue-monitor の durable delivery ACK テスト 2 件が Linux CI で flake する件（#3609 の検出契約を通過する残存）。本 PR の CI で 2 回観測し、同一バイトのコードで緑→赤→緑を確認した。
- `.codex/hooks.json` の managed hook 絶対パス汚染を canonical へ復旧（#3567 に実測データをコメント済み）。

author: tobib1505
body:
Hardens the existing Supabase SSR auth rather than replacing it. Email + password sign-in is untouched in substance; the session, guard and redirect layers around it are what changed.

## Session persistence

- **Apply the cache headers `@supabase/ssr` passes to `setAll()`.** They were being dropped. A token refresh writes `Set-Cookie`, Vibe runs behind Vercel's edge cache, and a cached response carrying `Set-Cookie` hands one user another user's session. Now applied on every response the proxy emits, redirects included. This is the most likely cause of the "randomly signed out" reports.
- **Carry refreshed cookies through guard redirects.** A redirect that drops them rotates a refresh token into the void and ends the session permanently.
- **`getUser()` → `getClaims()`**, the currently documented approach for `@supabase/ssr` 0.12.4. Same guarantee, without an Auth-server round trip per call.
- Fail closed rather than throwing when verification is unavailable.

Cookie lifetime was *not* the problem — `@supabase/ssr` already defaults to a 400-day `maxAge`.

## Guards and redirects

- Guard `/app/**` in the proxy so a signed-out visitor never renders a frame of the workspace, and send authenticated visitors away from `/login` and `/signup`. `requireSession()` remains the authorization boundary; the proxy is UX.
- One allowlist-based `sanitizeNextPath()` that every post-auth destination passes through. Route Handlers emit relative `Location` headers, which structurally cannot leave this origin.

## Google sign-in

`signInWithOAuth` via a Server Action, PKCE, exchanged in `/auth/callback`. Vibe's callback and Supabase's provider callback are documented as the two distinct redirect legs they are. Account linking is Supabase's native automatic linking — no merge logic here.

## Password recovery and email confirmation

`/forgot-password`, `/reset-password`, and `/auth/confirm` using `token_hash` + `verifyOtp`, which works when a link is opened in a different browser than the one that requested it — the failure mode this repo already shipped once with PKCE. The reset request answers identically whether or not the address has an account.

## Two bugs found while testing against a running production build

1. `?error=constructor` on the OAuth callback matched `Object.prototype` through an object-literal lookup and stringified `function Object() { [native code] }` into a user-visible redirect. Both lookup tables are now `Map`s.
2. Next's proxy layer rejects a relative `Location`, which 500'd every guarded request. The proxy builds absolute redirects from `request.nextUrl`.

## Test truth

| Kind | Scope | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Unit / integration (automated) | 3542 tests | green |
| Browser E2E (automated, Chromium) | 176 tests, 25 new for auth | green |
| Live verification against a production build | all routes, guard + `next`, open-redirect attempts, spoofed forwarded hosts, rendered HTML | done manually |
| **Real Supabase dogfood** | — | **not performed** |
| **Real Google OAuth dogfood** | — | **not performed** |
| **Session persistence across browser restart** | — | **not tested** |
| **Account linking** | — | **not tested** |

The E2E suite points at a Supabase project that does not exist, which makes the entire signed-out half deterministic. A mocked OAuth test is not a Google test: the PKCE test only proves Vibe builds the correct authorize URL.

## Not included

No database migration. No new environment variables. Google's client secret lives in Supabase's provider configuration, never in Vibe's environment.

## Still required before Google sign-in works

Dashboard and Google Cloud configuration, documented in `docs/setup/supabase-auth.md` — including a **required email-template change** without which password reset does not work, and an open question about `Confirm email` and automatic identity linking that can cost an existing user their password login.

Status: `implementation complete — provider configuration pending`.

author: sumansharmabharadwaj-ship-it
body:
## What changed
- add a static `motion-reduce:hidden` class to the server-rendered veil
- verify the user-visible contract (`not visible`) at the early 260ms checkpoint
- retain the synchronous media-query effect, which detaches the veil after hydration

## Why
On a busy CI runner, the server-rendered node can still exist before React hydrates even though reduced motion is active. Client code cannot remove that node before hydration, but CSS can guarantee it never appears. # Why we need this PR?
Long Markdown messages can grow beyond their initial 400px virtual-row estimate after mount. author: ryan-kipawa
body:
Closes #283. Supersedes #675.

Custom blocks are named arrays of metadata in the dfs header. MIKE 21 keeps the **land value** in `M21_Misc[3]`; without it MIKE Zero greys the land value out and an `.m21fm` setup rejects the bathymetry. MIKE IO could not read them at all, and `mikeio.read(f).to_dfs(g)` destroyed what `mikeio.generic.scale(f, g)` has always preserved.

## `Dataset.custom_blocks`

```python
ds = mikeio.read("waves.dfs2")
ds.custom_blocks
# {'M21_Misc': array([-1.77e-05, 0., 4.51, 10., 0., 0., 0.], dtype=float32)}

ds.custom_blocks["M21_Misc"][3] = -10.0        # MIKE 21 land value
ds.to_dfs("waves_with_land_value.dfs2")
```

A plain `dict[str, np.ndarray]`, editable in place or replaced wholesale. A list is read as `float32`; pass an array for any other dtype:

```python
ds.custom_blocks = {"M21_Misc": [0, 0, -900, -10, 0, 0, 0]}
ds.custom_blocks["Counts"] = np.array([1, 2, 3], dtype=np.int32)
```

Blocks are copied on assignment, carried through Dataset operations (`isel`, `sel`, `interp`, `interp_like`, aggregations, arithmetic, item selection), and written for dfs0, dfs1, dfs2 and dfs3.

## `Dfs0.custom_blocks`, `Dfs1`, `Dfs2`, `Dfs3`

Read-only, and read from the header alone — so the land value of a large bathymetry can be inspected without reading its data:

```python
mikeio.Dfs2("bathy.dfs2").custom_blocks["M21_Misc"][3]
```

## Behaviour worth knowing

- A Dataset stores whatever is assigned; the dfs rules (1-D, C-contiguous, one of the seven dfs dtypes, non-empty ASCII name) are applied on write, before the file is created.
- Propagation is blind: `isel(y=0)` writes a dfs2 `M21_Misc` verbatim into the resulting dfs1. Whether a block still means anything after the geometry changes is the caller's call.
- dfsu ignores them — its sole block, `MIKE_FM`, is regenerated from the geometry on every write. `DataArray.to_dfs` writes none either, having no file-level metadata.
- Reading is lenient: a block MIKE IO would refuse to write is skipped with a warning, so no file becomes unreadable.
- An `int16` block reads back as `uint16` (mikecore reads `Short` as `c_uint16`); prefer `int32`. Writing is correct.

## Docs

`user-guide/dfs2.qmd` gains a **Custom blocks** section with the `M21_Misc` layout; `examples/dfs2/bathy.qmd` gains a land-value step on the GEBCO→dfs2 walkthrough.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## World Composer / Generative World Grammar

### Summary
- Adds a versioned, JSON-safe WorldRecipe grammar for deterministic 2D teaching worlds.
- Materializes recipes into ordinary VOLK-ML observations without a second World state machine.
- Preserves legacy generator Worlds through an explicit legacy adapter path.
- Exposes bounded Agent world-design proposals that still flow through ScenarioSpec validation, preflight, and canonical World operations.

### Canonical semantics
- Recipe v1 supports classification/regression groups with stable IDs, shapes, transforms, split-specific transforms/sampling, position/label noise, local region noise, and semantic outliers.
- Primitives include blob, line, arc, ring, moon, spiral, rectangle, ellipse, polygon, and polyline; presets compile into the same grammar.
- Transform order is scale → rotate → translate.
- Generation is deterministic from the existing World seed plus scoped substreams for world/group/split/purpose/sample, so unrelated groups can retain their realization.
- Generated observations keep bounded recipe/group/shape/sampling/noise provenance.

### Runtime and Agent integration
- New registered operations: SET_WORLD_RECIPE and PATCH_WORLD_RECIPE.
- Recipe Worlds use the existing generated/dirty/frozen/realization lifecycle, Undo/Redo, Experiment synchronization, Repeat, comparison, fidelity, and atomic failure behavior.
- Recipe-level comparison reports changed paths, unchanged paths, affected groups, and split scope while preserving the existing top-level World factor.
- Agent interpretation is bounded to world-design proposals; the deterministic planner produces canonical ScenarioSpecs and never accepts raw generated points or executable model output.
- Existing provider-safe Agent context remains bounded; detailed host inspection remains internal.
- WorldBuilder keeps its legacy workflow and shows a localized recipe summary/regenerate/freeze compatibility view for recipe Worlds.

author: jmylchreest
body:
> R22: *"A provider billed per second of video reports a non-zero cost. Zero is the current answer and it is wrong."*

**It was worse than zero.** Generation reported *nothing* — not an approximation, not a zero with a note, but no cost record at all. A turn that rendered a minute of video spent, as far as the budget was concerned, nothing: the spend cap could not fire on it and the trace could not show it.

## The model

`Usage` carries an optional unit and quantity; `ProviderPricing` carries a `unit_usd` map.

**A map rather than a field per concept**, because the set is open — video seconds, images, audio characters, opaque credits, and R22 then writes an ellipsis. A field per vendor idea means a code change and a release every time somebody meters something new.

**Tokens deliberately stay as their own fields.** They are the common case, they need the cached/uncached distinction a flat map cannot express, and moving them would make every chat turn pay a lookup to price the thing it always prices.

**Added to the token cost, not substituted for it** — a reply that generates a picture costs its tokens *and* its image.

**An unpriced unit costs nothing and is not an error.** A plan-billed provider has no marginal rate, and refusing to account for the turn because nobody wrote down a price would stop the turn rather than the billing. The *quantity* is recorded either way, so consumption stays visible where the marginal cost is genuinely nil.

## Getting it to the budget

A collector on the context, following `ArtifactCollector`. **A builtin has no reference to the `TurnBudget` and should not** — it would then be able to refuse a turn on the budget's behalf, halfway through, from inside a tool. Announcing what was spent and letting the loop decide keeps the decision in one place.

**Drained rather than read**, because a turn generating two videos across two round-trips must not bill the first twice. Recorded *before* the exceeded check acts on the total, because a video generated on the round-trip that tips a turn over its cap is part of why it tipped.

## What reports

Image, per image. Speech, per character of **input** — what every TTS vendor meters, not per second of output, which is not known until the audio exists. A **failed** generation bills nothing: the provider did not deliver, and charging for it would make an outage look like usage.

**Video does not report yet.** The job completes asynchronously and its cost lands on the poll handler; that is the next piece.

## A gap the mutations found — for the second time this session

Removing the loop's drain **failed nothing**. Every test exercised the collector directly and none exercised the wiring — the same shape as the chain-step pipeline not being called. Two turn-level tests now cover it: one asserting a tool's spend reaches the budget, one asserting the cap can actually fire on it, because **a spend the budget records but never acts on is a number, not a limit.**

## Verification

`go test ./... -count=1` green; `-race` green on compute and drivers; `golangci-lint` 0 issues.

| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | unit cost not added | 6 tests fail ✓ |
| B2 | unit cost *replaces* token cost | ✓ |
| B3 | the image builtin reports no cost | ✓ |
| B4 | a failed synthesis still bills | ✓ |
| B5 | the loop drains but does not record | **initially missed** — added turn-level tests; now 2 fail ✓ |

author: 0thernet
body:
On macOS, a custom `chromeProfile` path may not contain `Google/Chrome`, `BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser`, `Arc/User Data`, or `Chromium`. `resolveKeychainForDb()` then falls back to Chrome Safe Storage even when the caller explicitly selected another browser with `chromiumBrowser`, so the cookie database is decrypted with the wrong secret.

This makes `chromiumBrowser` authoritative for both profile-root selection and Keychain selection. Path-based inference remains unchanged when no explicit browser is supplied.

Coverage includes:
- a deterministic mapping law over all four supported browser IDs and generic custom paths
- a macOS provider regression where an explicitly selected browser is paired with a browser-neutral custom path
- a full macOS provider integration that creates a real SQLite cookie store, encrypts a v11 cookie, invokes the provider through its process boundary, validates the exact Chromium Keychain service/account arguments, and verifies the decrypted value
- the existing path-inference and timeout behavior

The integration uses generated data and a validating `security` shim, so it exercises the real filesystem, SQLite, provider, and crypto path without reading a developer's browser profile or Keychain.

This is independent of #42 and can merge in either order.

author: moekify
body:
Bumps Node and every dependency to fix the outstanding security advisories. **43 vulnerabilities (3 critical, 27 high) → 0.** Package count drops 491 → 223. Two commits: the first is pure Prettier reformatting, the second is everything else. Reviewing them separately is much easier than the combined diff. ## Node `.nvmrc` 20.11.0 → **24.19.0** (Active LTS), with `Dockerfile`, `.drone.yml` and the GitHub workflows following. The workflows also move off retired action versions — `codeql-action@v1` and `checkout@v2` no longer run at all — and now read the version from `.nvmrc` instead of pinning `lts/*`. ## Dependencies Everything on latest published at least 48h ago. Majors: Svelte 4→5, Vite 5→8, vite-plugin-svelte 3→7, Kit 2.5→2.70, ESLint 8→10, svelte-check 3→4, svelte-select 5→6, fuse.js 6→7, `@directus/sdk` 16→24, TypeScript 5.4→6. Three deliberate deviations from "latest": - **TypeScript 6.0.3, not 7.0.2.** TS 7 is outside every consumer's peer range — `typescript-eslint` caps at `<6.1.0`, Kit at `^5.3.3 || ^6`. 6.0.3 is the real ceiling. - **Bulma stays at 0.9.4.** It has no advisories, and 1.x is a full Sass/CSS-variable rewrite that would restyle the site — pure visual risk for zero security gain. That migration deserves its own PR and a visual QA pass. - **`cypress`, `dotenv` and `postcss-load-config` removed** as unused: no cypress directory or config (tests are Playwright), `dotenv` referenced only in a comment, no postcss config anywhere. Cypress alone carried the critical `form-data` advisories. `npm-run-all` (unmaintained since 2018, pulling a vulnerable `cross-spawn`) → `npm-run-all2`. The final 4 advisories were `cookie <0.7.0`, which SvelteKit still hard-pins at `^0.6.0`. An `overrides` entry lifts it to `^0.7.2` — worth dropping once Kit widens that range. ## Real bugs this surfaced Three pages ran `beforeUpdate(() => { … goto(…) })`. Svelte 5's legacy shim runs that hook aggressively enough to make it an infinite navigation loop — `/lovecasts` locked the browser main thread outright, so the page rendered but never responded to input. All three are now guarded reactive syncs that skip the navigation when the URL already matches. Two pages keyed an `{#each}` on `Math.random()`. Svelte 5 rejects that with `each_key_volatile`, which was killing hydration for the entire page. They now key on the group's first id. `+error.svelte` was SvelteKit 0.x-era code that rendered `

undefined

` on every error — rewritten against `$page`. ## Things that were already broken - **`npm run lint` crashed before this.** `.eslintrc.cjs` had an invalid property, and the script passed Prettier's removed `--plugin-search-dir` flag, so it errored before ESLint ever ran. Now on flat config and passing, with rules that don't fit this codebase disabled or downgraded and each choice commented. That's also why 23 files had drifted from the configured style — hence the separate formatting commit. - **`npm test` could not complete a run.** The homepage, `/about` and `/lovecasts` loaders hit Directus even under `USE_FIXTURES`, so Playwright's readiness probe on `/` never got a 200. The existing but never-wired `hubs`, `about` and `lovecasts` fixtures are now used (they were recorded in the raw `{ data: [...] }` envelope, unwrapped at the import site). The filter specs were also racing hydration — clicking server-rendered controls before Svelte attached handlers — so `tests/helpers.ts` waits on SvelteKit's `#svelte-announcer`, which is absent from the SSR markup. ## Not addressed `svelte-check` reported **54 errors before this change and 48 after**, verified by message against a baseline worktree — no new ones. The remainder is pre-existing (implicit `any`s, a missing `src/global` module) and left untouched; it's a separate cleanup. `eslint` surfaces 10 warnings, mostly `{#each}` blocks without keys. Adding keys changes list reconciliation, so they're reported rather than enforced until those lists get retested. ## Verification After a clean `npm ci` on Node 24.19.0: | | | |---|---| | `npm audit` | 0 vulnerabilities | | `npm run lint` | passes (10 warnings) | | `npm run build:staging` | passes | | `npm test` | **23/23**, stable across repeated cold-cache runs | `npm run build` (adapter-static) still needs live Directus credentials to prerender, exactly as before — CI supplies them. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: wkosenkow

## Summary

author: prakashuxtech
body:
Two reviewers reported after #1957 merged. Both found defects **in the fixes
themselves**, and one is worse than the bug it replaced. This is the repair.

## Consent could transfer to a different person

Making `opted_in` sticky-True while `whatsapp_number` stayed an unconditional
overwrite meant a sheet carrying a new SDR's mobile and no opt-in column
**inherited the founder's consent**, cleared the dispatch guard, and would have
put a business-initiated WhatsApp template in front of someone who never
agreed. The Tray card shows channel and copy, never opt-in provenance, so no
human review catches it.

The blanket overwrite it replaced did **not** have that hole — it reset
`opted_in` on the same import. A fix must not be more dangerous than the bug.
The number and the consent now move together: a changed number drops the flag.

## The resurrection guard only blocked the literal default

`if body.status != "new"` protected a sheet with *no* status column. An
operator's working sheet is exactly the one carrying a stale `in_sequence`,
which lifted rows back out of the terminal set and let the sweep re-enter the
sequence on people it had retired — including anyone marked dead for asking not
to be contacted. Lifecycle is now never written by an import at all.

## "Last wins" was a mirror of the bug it fixed

Taking the *first* object with a `companies` key let a restated template beat
the answer. Taking the *last* let a trailing recap beat it — and let a nested
`companies` key inside a company entry beat its own parent. Both reproduced.

Position was never the signal. Selection is content-based now, weighted by how
much each row actually says, and the docstring states the honest limit instead
of overclaiming a second time: two candidates of identical shape cannot be told
apart by content. The real guard is that the prompt no longer contains
parseable JSON to echo.

## Also

Zero-width and BOM characters passed the address check, because `str.isspace()`
is False for category Cf. The arq timeout was worker-wide, so the 6× bump also
applied to approved sends and could hold every slot for half an hour behind a
hung socket — scoped to the sweep now, dispatch keeps 300s.
`GROWTH_JOB_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=0` meant 60s rather than "disabled", inverting this
package's own convention. And `_scrub` truncated before scrubbing, so a key
straddling 300 characters leaked its prefix into a durable row.

## The procedural finding, which was the sharpest

**None of the four semantic changes in #1957 had a test or a mutation.** Under
this repo's own rule they shipped ungated, which is how three of them survived.

Now: 14 mutations, all caught, plus `test_upsert_lifecycle.py` covering consent
transfer and resurrection directly. 422 tests, import-linter clean.

One process note worth recording: I pushed the first commit of this branch with
a red test, because the verify chain used `;` between pytest and `git commit`
so the commit was never gated on the suite. Fixed, and every gate here ran
under `set -e`.

author: copilot
body:
This PR standardizes repository directory naming by zero-padding leading numeric serials to 4 digits (e.g., `1-*` → `0001-*`, `121-*` → `0121-*`, `1185-*` unchanged). The rename is applied across all directory depths while preserving non-numeric suffixes exactly.

- **Scope**
  - Renamed all directories whose basename starts with a numeric prefix shorter than 4 digits.
  - Total renamed directories: **42**.
  - Rename conflicts: **0** (no target-path collisions encountered).

- **What changed**
  - Per-directory rename logic:
    - Match leading numeric prefix.
    - Left-pad only that prefix to width 4.
    - Preserve the remainder of the name byte-for-byte.
  - Example renames:
    - `1-two-sum` → `0001-two-sum`
    - `11-container-with-most-water` → `0011-container-with-most-water`
    - `121-best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock` → `0121-best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock`
    - `745-find-smallest-letter-greater-than-target` → `0745-find-smallest-letter-greater-than-target`
    - `882-peak-index-in-a-mountain-array` → `0882-peak-index-in-a-mountain-array`

- **Reference updates**
  - Scanned markdown/plain-text path references for old directory paths and updated where applicable.
  - No markdown link rewrites were required from current content.

- **Review checklist**
  - [x] Directories renamed with 4-digit serial prefixes
  - [x] Markdown/path references updated where needed
  - [x] No content changes beyond path renames

```text
Pattern: ^(\d+)([\s._-]?.*)$
Transform: new_name = zfill(prefix, 4) + suffix   (only when len(prefix) < 4)
```

author: romanovcopy
davemac93
body:
Phase 6 of the v2 plan (decisions 17–19). Turns "I should learn X" into a tracked curriculum whose completion feeds the profile.

## The store

`learn/<topic>/` is everything about one thing being learned:

| Store | Holds | Writer |
|---|---|---|
| `learn/<topic>/plan.md` | `title`, `why`, optional `goal`/`job`, `started`, `curriculum[]` + prose | `/teach` |
| `learn/<topic>/sessions/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` | one study session: covered, solid, shaky | `/teach` |
| `learn/status.yaml` | topic → item id → `{ done }` | **dashboard** |

Same split as `goals.yaml` vs `goal-status.yaml`, so no file has two writers.

## A curriculum item *is* a goal step

Not a lookalike: `lib/dashboard/learn-content.ts` maps every item onto `Goal` and hands it to the shipped `validateGoalTree`, `orderGoalTree` and `computeGoalProgress` (#77). So `after` prerequisites block a tick, prerequisites are ordered first, cycles and dangling ids are rejected on write, and topic progress is the same *unweighted* share of items ticked. One implementation, so a curriculum can never drift into a second notion of "done" — and there is no percentage anywhere anyone could type.

`why` is required: the write path refuses a plan with no goal step, missing job requirement, or user reason behind it. A curriculum with no reason is exactly what this module replaces.

## Evidence

Ticking a `skill:`-tagged item appends to `profile/evidence.yaml` (#76) with the source `learn:<topic>:<itemId>` — idempotent on `(source, skill)`, never retracted on an untick, exactly like `setStepDoneAction`. Verified through the real UI: tick → 1 record; untick → still 1; re-tick → still 1.

## `/teach` rewritten

It writes topics now, not notes: session summaries land in `learn/<topic>/sessions/<date>.md` through `scripts/write-learn.ts` (the vault I/O path — atomic write + one labeled commit), and it no longer creates loose `learning` notes. Its pre-approval moved with the write path (`Bash(node scripts/write-learn.ts *)`); `tests/skill-hardening.test.ts` now asserts the exact script each skill gets. The skill cannot reach `learn/status.yaml` — ticking an item is the user's claim, made in the Learn tab. `/note` keeps owning `notes/`.

## Dashboard

- **Learn tab** — topics with derived progress, why they exist, session counts; least finished first.
- **Topic page** — the plan, the ordered curriculum with checkboxes and blocked states, links to every session.
- **Goals** — a `kind: learn` step may carry `topic:` and links straight to the curriculum; the validator rejects `topic` on a `do` step or a direction.
- Registry entry (`learn`, sidebar between Jobs and Guide), Guide step `hasTopic`, `template/learn/` seed.

## Checks

`npm test` 292 passed / 22 files (baseline on main in the same worktree: 261 / 21), `npm run typecheck` clean, `npm run build` clean (17 routes, was 14).

**Out of scope, deliberately:** spaced repetition. `/teach`'s session history is the data a later SRS would need, so it stays a clean future addition.

Closes #79

body:
## Resumo

Corrige o achado do teste físico: "Usuários" não aparece no menu de `admin.html`, confirmado fisicamente pelo usuário.

**Causa raiz — não é um bug de código, é reachability.** A gestão de usuários (PR #596) foi implementada corretamente em `central-atendimento.html` — página separada de `admin.html`, com RBAC própria e sessão real (mesmo padrão já usado por "Vendedores", que também só existe ali, desde antes da #596). Confirmado ponto a ponto:

- A rota `GET /api/painel/usuarios` e as demais 7 rotas da PR #595 existem, com `exigir_perfil("adm")`.
- O RBAC no frontend (`abaUsuarios.hidden = sessaoUsuario.perfil !== "adm"`) funciona corretamente.
- O frontend publicado no GitHub Pages contém o HTML/JS/CSS da #596 tal como mergeados — `scripts/minify-assets.mjs` usa uma lista de **exclusão**, não inclusão; `central-atendimento.*` nunca foi excluído.
- `admin.html` migrou para o mesmo `POST /api/auth/login` usado por `central-atendimento.html` (`site-config.js:373`) — a sessão do ADM logado em `admin.html` já é a mesma sessão real que autoriza `/api/painel/usuarios`.

`admin.html` nunca teve nenhum link apontando para `central-atendimento.html`.

## Correção (refinada a pedido do usuário após a primeira revisão)

Um link **"Usuários"** no header do `admin.html` apontando para **`central-atendimento.html#usuarios`** (deep link, não só a página). `central-atendimento.js` passou a honrar esse hash no carregamento: abre a aba Usuários **automaticamente** (sem exigir um segundo clique), sempre que o hash pedir e a aba estiver de fato visível para o perfil da sessão — nunca abre uma aba que o RBAC acabou de esconder; sem `adm`, cai no comportamento padrão de sempre (aba fila).

Nenhuma duplicação de UI: reaproveita 100% a implementação existente das PRs #595/#596. RBAC continua 100% no backend (`exigir_perfil("adm")`) e na própria aba (`abaUsuarios.hidden`) — o link em `admin.html` não decide autorização nenhuma, só leva para o lugar certo.

## Tipo de mudança

- [ ] Documentação
- [x] Visual
- [x] API — nenhuma rota alterada, só uso de hash de navegação no frontend
- [x] Testes
- [x] Correção pequena

- [x] Conferi o diff.
- [x] Rodei os testes quando aplicável — `tests/e2e/admin-usuarios-link.spec.js` (7 testes: link existe; clique abre a Gestão de Usuários já ativa; refresh direto na URL com hash; voltar do navegador; navegação por teclado; deep link nunca abre a aba para vendedor, API continua 403; deep link não quebra Fila/Minhas conversas/Todas/Vendedores). Suíte completa (`admin-usuarios-link` + `central-atendimento-usuarios` + `admin-navegacao-abas` + `frame-guard-clickjacking`, desktop+mobile) — **134/134 passando**, sem regressão. `detect-secrets` sem achados novos.
- [x] A mudança é pequena e isolada.

## Observações

- O clique no link do header em viewport mobile usa `{ force: true }` no teste — reproduzido que essa sobreposição já existe hoje no link pré-existente "Atendimento — Automações" (não é uma regressão desta PR, é uma fragilidade de layout já presente no header do `admin.html`, fora de escopo aqui).

author: stefan-burke
body:
The follow-up to #2083, and then the job it left behind.

## Part one: the comments in `src/shared/db/client.ts`

**357 lines across 100 comments, now 296**, longest down from 20 lines to 14.
Nothing the file does has changed.

A smaller cut than the last file got, and that is the honest result. Most of the
prose here is genuinely useful — it explains how the database client stays safe
when the database is busy or the network hiccups, which a reader cannot work out
from the code. Deleting it would make the file worse.

The real problem was repetition. **One rule was written out in full in four
places:** a write is never retried after a gateway error, because the reply may
arrive after the write already landed, and repeating it would apply it twice. For
a booking system that means charging someone twice. It now lives in one place and
the other three point at it. The copies had already drifted — one had lost the
reason and simply asserted the behaviour.

Three things were also wrong:

- **The file's opening description was out of date.** It said four named
  functions each time their own calls and record the SQL. They do not: two hand
  the work to a shared helper, and the timing happens once, low down, for
  everything. Somebody reading it would add logging that already exists.
- **A link named a function that does not exist** — `syncListingPrices`, where the
  real one is `syncListingPricesForIds`.
- **One comment had been mangled by an edit** and no longer parsed as English.

## Part two: the four other dead links

A scan of the whole `src/` tree found four more `{@link}` targets, out of 523,
naming something that exists nowhere. Each needed reading the surrounding code
rather than a plausible guess:

- **`EditForm`** was a sibling in `site-content.tsx` — heading, error flash,
  fields, save button — deleted when the tabbed editors landed. There is nothing
  left to point at, so the comparison goes and the reason the panel draws no
  heading stays.
- **`handleGroupEditGet`** is now the entity page's Edit tab. `loadGroupEditPanel`
  is what loads the listings and package prices the comment describes.
- **`writeChildEdges`** never existed under that name. `validateChildEdges` strips
  self-edges and unknown ids, and `persistListingJoins` writes what survives.
- **`ListingActionNav`** went when listings moved onto the entity-pages
  framework. This one was also a comparison against an old implementation, which
  `AGENTS.md` says to delete rather than repoint — and `group-page.ts` carried the
  same stale framing, so both now state the rule that actually holds: each entry
  repeats the gate its target enforces, so no forbidden link is ever shown.

## Part three: so it stops happening

A one-off sweep of something that rots is not a fix, so `check:comments` now
fails on a `{@link}` naming something the tree does not contain.

`deno doc --lint` was tried first, as the note asked: it reports type-visibility
and missing-annotation diagnostics, not dangling links, and already fires on our
tree, so it cannot serve as this gate.

The new rule collects every name the tree mentions outside a link, then flags a
link naming nothing in that set. It is deliberately permissive — a name still
mentioned anywhere counts, so only a target with no home at all is reported,
which is why all 520 remaining links pass untouched. Names are cut out of their
own links first; otherwise a dead link would vouch for itself and nothing could
ever be caught. It reports the link's own line inside a block, as the width rule
does, and it covers the files the length limits exempt, because a broken link in
the published documentation is worse than one in ordinary source.

It was verified the only way that means anything: by putting the exact
`handleGroupEditGet` link back and watching the check name it at `groups.ts:263`.

## What checking claims turned up

Three times on this branch, testing a claim instead of trusting it changed the
outcome — which is the case for doing one file at a time.

**A comment I was about to correct was right.** It says an empty id list runs
`IN ()` and matches nothing. Another test in the codebase is named "never invalid
`IN ()`", so I expected the database to reject it. It accepts it and returns no
rows. Confirmed against a real database; the sentence is untouched.

**A mutant I nearly filed as unkillable was a real gap.** I had attributed it to
a migration path prefix; it was the exemption's `endsWith("/")`. Under that
change a file called `doc.tsx` would be wrongly exempted from the limits. It is
now killed by a test, along with five other assertions that pass came out of the
same review.

**jscpd was right about the new rule.** It flagged the dead-link rule against the
length rule, because both walked a file's comments. `eachComment` now takes a
rule about one comment and returns a rule about a whole file, so there is one
walk and every check reports in source order.

## Checks

`deno task precommit` passes in full — all eight steps, including the complete
test suite with coverage. Mutation testing on the changed scripts is at 100%
with no survivors; the four suppressed mutants are recorded with proofs that no
input can distinguish them.

Part one is provably comments-only: the repo's own `codeShape` helper, added in
#2081 for this exact question, reports the code byte-identical either side of
that commit.

body: ## Summary Promotes the second-pass review (already merged into `dev` via #38) up to `main`. See PR #38 for the full breakdown. **Tests:** 163 passing (384 assertions). author: andrehahm
body:
## Summary

Scopes `marketplace-ci.yml`'s `pull_request` `labeled` trigger so only the `codex-review-bypassed` label re-triggers the workflow — any other label (e.g. a review bot's own auto-classification labels) now no-ops the whole run instead of spending a full CI pass.

## Type of Change

- [ ] feat — new feature
- [x] fix — bug fix
- [ ] docs — documentation only
- [ ] refactor — code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
- [ ] perf — performance improvement
- [ ] test — adding or fixing tests
- [ ] chore — build process, tooling, dependencies
- [ ] experiment — experimental change

## Related Issue

N/A

## Changes

- `.github/workflows/marketplace-ci.yml`: added `if: github.event.action != 'labeled' || github.event.label.name == 'codex-review-bypassed'` to every job (`hygiene`, `python-quality`, `marketplace-parity`, `fork-unsupported`, `codex-review`), ANDed with each job's existing condition where one already existed. `publish` needed no change — its existing `needs.codex-review.result != 'skipped'` check already correctly no-ops once `codex-review` is skipped.
- `docs/ci.md`: updated the opening paragraph to state the `labeled` trigger is now scoped to the bypass label only, so the docs stay accurate.

## Testing

Root-caused live on PR #47: CodeRabbit applied 2 of its own classification labels after finishing its review, and since `labeled` was unconditional in the trigger's `types:`, that re-triggered the entire workflow twice (one run was cancelled by the `concurrency` group).

Two things were verified before implementing, not assumed:
- Confirmed via GitHub's own context-availability docs that the `env` context is **not** available in `jobs.<job_id>.if` (only `github`/`needs`/`vars`/`inputs` are) — a first-draft workflow-level `env:` var would have silently broken the gate; switched to inlining the condition per job.
- Confirmed a custom job-level `if:` **replaces**, not ANDs with, the default needs-must-succeed gate — so the condition had to be added to every job individually rather than relying on skip-cascading through `needs:` from just one of them.

Validated with `actionlint` (zero new findings — the two shellcheck warnings it reports are pre-existing, on an unrelated line) and a Python `yaml.safe_load` parse confirming each job's final `if:` string is exactly as intended.

## Checklist

author: sungwoong-noh
body:
## 무엇을

공개범위(`visibility`) 기반 조회 인가와, 그것을 성립시키는 팔로우 API의 스펙. `docs/specs/2026-08-17-visibility-authorization.md`, AC 46개(`AC-FOLLOW` 18 · `AC-VIS` 28), `status: 초안`.

문서만 추가한다. 코드·스키마 변경 없음.

## 왜

`recipes.visibility`·`brew_logs.visibility` 컬럼은 이미 있지만 값이 저장만 되고 판정에 전혀 쓰이지 않는다. 지금은 `PUBLIC`이어도 소유자가 아니면 403이라, 아키텍처 문서(`docs/design/2026-08-14-architecture.md:253`)의 핵심 시나리오 "여자친구 계정으로 로그인해 FRIENDS 레시피 조회"가 실행되지 않는다.

더 근본적으로 **팔로우 관계를 만들 방법이 서버에 없다.** `follows` 테이블·`Follow` 엔티티·`FollowRepository.existsMutualFollow`가 V1부터 있는데 이를 쓰는 컨트롤러가 하나도 없어, 실사용자는 SQL을 직접 치지 않는 한 상호 팔로우 상태에 도달할 수 없다. 브루잉 로그에서 `user_grinders`가 같은 상태였고 착수 후에야 발견했다. 같은 실패를 반복하지 않으려고 팔로우 API를 이 스펙에 함께 넣었다.

포크보다 먼저 다룬 이유: 무엇이 공개인지 정의되지 않으면 "남의 공개 레시피를 복제한다"의 AC를 리터럴로 쓸 수 없다.

관련: `docs/design/2026-08-14-architecture.md`(공유 모델·FRIENDS 판정)
후속 계획: 없음 — 다음 세션에서 작성

## 주요 결정

- 거부는 **403 `FORBIDDEN`** 유지. 404로 숨기는 안은 기존 AC 7개를 고쳐야 해 기각
- **인증 필수.** `PUBLIC`이어도 토큰 없으면 401
- `FRIENDS` = **상호 팔로우**, 요청 시점 실시간 판정(캐시·스냅샷 없음)
- `owner_user_id`가 null이면 소유자 통과만 못 하고 `visibility`로 판정 — CURATED 시드 레시피가 여기 걸린다
- 레시피와 브루로그의 `visibility`는 **독립**. `PRIVATE` 레시피를 참조하는 `PUBLIC` 로그가 허용된다
- 팔로우는 **멱등** — 중복 등록·미존재 해제 모두 204
- **새 `ErrorCode` 없음. 스키마 변경 없음**

## 비목표

목록 조회(피드), 브루잉 로그 수정 API, 포크, 원두 재고·카탈로그, 비로그인 접근, 팔로워/팔로잉 목록.

## 어떻게 확인했나

- [x] `./scripts/check-spec-coverage.sh` 통과 — 새 스펙은 `초안`이라 정상 건너뜀, 기존 5건 192개 그대로 초록
- [x] 스크립트의 AC 패턴(`AC-[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*-[0-9]+`)이 한 파일의 두 접두사를 모두 잡는 것을 확인 (46개 인식)
- [ ] 코드 검증 — 해당 없음(설계 세션, `backend/` 무변경)

## 남은 것

구현 계획(`docs/plans/`) 작성. 팔로우 API가 선행 태스크여야 한다 — FRIENDS 관련 AC 9개가 상호 팔로우 상태를 전제로 하는데, 팔로우 API 없이는 테스트 픽스처를 컨트롤러로 만들 수 없다.

author: owenyuwono
body:
**Description**

Unlike GLSL, WGSL spells the builtin `faceForward()` with a capital `F`. TSL's `faceForward()` is backed by `MathNode.FACEFORWARD = 'faceforward'`, and `WGSLNodeBuilder`'s `wgslMethods` table has no correction entry for it, so the GLSL spelling is emitted verbatim. Any TSL shader calling `faceForward()` therefore fails to compile on a WebGPU backend:

```
Error while parsing WGSL: :39:28 error: unresolved call target 'faceforward'
  DiffuseColor = vec4<f32>( faceforward( vec3<f32>( 1.0, 0.0, 0.0 ), vec3<f32>( 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ), normalLocal ), 1.0 );
                            ^^^^^^^^^^^
```

Minimal repro:

```js
const material = new THREE.MeshBasicNodeMaterial();
material.colorNode = faceForward( vec3( 1, 0, 0 ), vec3( 0, 0, 1 ), normalLocal );
```

The failure is silent from JS: `render()` does not throw and nothing is catchable, the pipeline is simply dropped and the object does not appear. `faceforward()` is a documented TSL function (`docs/TSL.md`), and the WebGL backend is unaffected because `faceforward` is the correct GLSL spelling.

The PR adds the missing entry to `wgslMethods`, mirroring the existing `inversesqrt: 'inverseSqrt'` line directly above it. No polyfill is needed: WGSL's `faceForward( e1, e2, e3 )` has the same argument order and sign convention as GLSL's `faceforward( N, I, Nref )`.

For what it is worth, `examples/jsm/transpiler/WGSLEncoder.js` already carries this exact mapping (`'faceforward': 'faceForward'`, adjacent to `'inversesqrt': 'inverseSqrt'`) - only the node builder was missing it.

**Verification**

Rendered against `src/` on a WebGPU backend before and after the change. Before: the error above. After: emits `faceForward( ... )` and renders with no console errors.

Semantics confirmed by pixel readback on both branches, to check the alias is correct and not merely compiling:

| case | expected | got |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dot( Nref, I ) < 0` -> `+N` | `rgb(255,0,0)` | `rgb(255,0,0)` |
| `dot( Nref, I ) > 0` -> `-N` | `rgb(0,0,0)` | `rgb(0,0,0)` |

`npm run test` passes: lint clean, 1333 unit, 40 addons, 0 failures.

author: make-tuned-unit
body:
Four safety guards could pass while inspecting an empty subject. Each was mutated to prove it now fails; each mutation was reverted. A fifth finding is a production defect that one of the guards surfaced by being honest about its own vacuity.

## The money guard was held up by an accident

`finance::no_tool_can_place_an_order` has five assertions, all negative — "no tool named `place_order`/`buy`/`sell`/`submit_order`/`trade`". An empty tool list satisfies all five.

Mutating `get_tools()` to `return Vec::new()` did turn it red, but on **none of those five**. It failed on a sixth line, `assert!(names.contains("record_trade"))`, which had been written to pin that the safe recording tool exists — a different concern entirely. The money-safety property was resting on an incidental neighbour, and anyone removing that line as redundant would have disarmed the guard with the suite still green.

## Blast radius, and real defence-in-depth

Rather than only asking whether one test went red, the mutated binary was run against the whole lib suite. Four tests caught it:

| test | why |
|---|---|
| `finance::every_tool_is_described` | the new floor — the fix has teeth |
| `finance::no_tool_can_place_an_order` | the accidental catch above |
| `self_knowledge::descriptor_prose_names_only_real_tools` | prose names now-phantom tools |
| `self_knowledge::tool_descriptions_name_every_callable_tool` | the inverse direction |

The last two are structural: the self-knowledge registry cross-checks descriptor prose against the live tool list, so gutting *any* tool list is caught somewhere regardless of local vacuity. Worth knowing that exists before concluding a surviving guard is weak.

## A distinct shape: the branch checks the safe case

`self_knowledge::confirm_checks_only_on_queryable_signals` stated a prohibition in its doc and checked the permitted case in its body:

```rust
if let Some(ConfirmCheck::MemoryRecallable(p)) = step.confirm {
    assert!(!p.is_empty());
}
```

The forbidden case fell through the `if` and passed. The arm *does* execute, so "did the assertion run" detection is blind to this.

Rewritten as an exhaustive match — which immediately failed on `persona`, and **that turned out to be the rule's fault, not the code's**. `state_source` gates `worker_live_state_for`, which only `HasScheduledJob` and `LibrarianDescribedAtLeastOne` read from; `PersonaConfigured` reads the always-rendered "You are <name>" line and is fine for a `Static` feature. The rule is narrowed to what is actually true, and the match is exhaustive so the next variant can't be added without deciding here whether it can be read back.

## The product defect

`observe_settings_never_emits_secret_values` failed ~1 run in 4 in the full suite and passed in isolation. Not the test: `providers()` returns an unordered list and `observe_settings` truncates to `LIST_LIMIT`, so **which five configured providers reached the page changed every call**. An agent observing `settings` twice got a different arbitrary subset with no way to distinguish that from a real change.

Fixed at the cause — sort by name before truncating — which fixes the surface and the flake together. The guard now asserts only what is deterministic, and an `if p["name"] == "openai"` branch was **deleted** from it: with ordering fixed, that provider sorts off the bounded page and the branch could never fire again, making it the same defect in waiting.

## What is deliberately not done

The agents roster is **not** pinned to `WORKER_DESCRIPTORS.len()`. Visibility is filtered by live feature flags (6 of 9 on this host), so a count pin fails on host config rather than on the property — the same class of bug just fixed above — and re-deriving the filter to compare against would assert only that the function equals a copy of itself. It floors non-empty and checks every returned id is a real descriptor id.

## Verification

- `permagent --lib`: 3031 passed / 0 failed
- six consecutive full runs clean, where the flake previously reproduced at ~1 in 4
- `permagent-daemon`: 608 passed / 0 failed
- `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean on both crates
- each of the four fixes independently mutated → RED → reverted

author: gassaan
body:
## The face

Space Grotesk draws a **bare vertical stroke for `1`**, so a run like `1111` reads as a picket fence — precisely where the repeated digits are the thing being sold. Archivo gives the `1` a flag and the whole set sturdier, wider forms, and at weight 800 it carries the presence the number deserves as the product on the card.

Chosen from a rendered specimen of real Maldivian numbers rather than from description — Archivo, Manrope, Sora, Figtree, JetBrains Mono and the incumbent Space Grotesk, all at the size they'd actually appear. Sora wrapped to two lines in the specimen, which was a useful early warning about width. Figtree was the close runner-up; Archivo won on digit differentiation.

Tabular figures stay, so runs remain in register.

## The sizes step around the grid, not simply up

Cards are at their **narrowest at `sm`**, where the grid goes to two columns — the number has *less* room there than on a phone, not more. That is the trap in this layout.

My first attempt used `text-5xl` (48px) at `sm` and filled the card to the pixel: **264px of content in a 264px card**, leaving the copy icon flush against the edge. It technically "fit" and would have broken on any device whose font metrics rounded differently.

Measured across 320 / 390 / 640 / 768 / 1024 / 1280:

| width | size | number + icon | card inner | slack |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 320 | 41.6px | 235px | 254px | 19px |
| 390 | 41.6px | 235px | 324px | 89px |
| 640 | 44px | 247px | 264px | 17px |
| 768 | 44px | 247px | 328px | 81px |
| 1024 | 52px | 287px | 456px | 169px |

No horizontal page overflow at any width.

Every number is the same width — seven tabular digits in a fixed 3+4 grouping — so that worst case is exact, not a sample.

## Scope

The face is loaded alongside the existing two and applies only to the card number. The smaller numbers in the cart and the admin tables already used the body font with tabular figures and are untouched, so nothing becomes inconsistent.

The heavier weight also gives the gold premium treatment more surface for its gradient, which reads better than it did at 700.

## Verification

Built and served under the `/gassandev/` subpath, driven with Playwright:

- `document.fonts.check('800 40px Archivo')` asserted true — the webfont genuinely loads, not a silent fallback
- number width vs card width measured at six viewport widths, with `scrollWidth` overflow and page-level horizontal overflow both checked
- both themes rendered and inspected, including the gold premium card

`tsc -b && vite build` and `oxlint` both clean.

## Summary
- Adds an optional `matterServer` sidecar running `ghcr.io/matter-js/matterjs-server:stable` (the Open Home Foundation's rewrite, successor to the archived `python-matter-server`) inside the main Home Assistant pod.
- Deliberately a sidecar, not a separate Deployment: it needs the pod's host network for Matter/Thread mDNS discovery. author: byunchangill
body:
## 왜

다른 PC에서, 그리고 앞으로의 데스크탑 배포에서 그대로 돌게 만든다.

지금은 두 방식 다 깨진다 — 설정에 절대경로를 박으면 **그 PC에서만** 도는 앱이 되고,
이름만 두면 **PATH에 없는 PC에서** 통째로 막힌다.

실제로 오늘 이 저장소에서 났다: 가상환경이 켜진 셸에서 서버를 띄웠더니 `py`·`python`·`python3`가
셋 다 그 환경을 가리켜, **멀쩡히 깔린 글자 검출기를 두고 "없음"**이 됐다. 같은 PC에서 셸만 바꿔
✅ → ⚠️ 로 뒤집혔다. VSR은 설정에 `vsrPath` 항목이 없어서 저장소가 자리에 있는데도 ⚠️ 였다.

## 무엇을

**설정에는 `ffmpeg` 같은 이름만 두고, 실제 경로는 실행하는 PC에서 그때 찾는다.**

`server/src/util/toolPath.ts` (신규) 의 탐색 순서:

| 순위 | 자리 | 뜻 |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | `tools/bin` · Electron `resources/bin` | 배포판이 들고 다니는 것. **ffmpeg·yt-dlp를 싸 넣을 자리를 미리 뚫어뒀다** |
| 2 | `PATH` | 사용자가 직접 깐 것 |
| 3 | 저장소 안 가상환경 (`.venv-inpaint` 등) | 설치 문서가 안내하는 자리. 상대 경로라 PC가 바뀌어도 맞는다 |
| 4 | 표준 설치 자리 | winget Links · scoop shims · chocolatey · homebrew · `/snap/bin` |

- 탐색은 `run()`·`checkTool()` **안에서** 일어난다. 파이프라인 호출부 20여 곳은 손대지 않았고,
  앞으로 새 서브프로세스를 붙일 때도 할 일이 없다
- **경로가 적힌 값은 손대지 않는다.** 사용자가 특정 설치본을 지목한 것인데 우리가 다른 것을
  고르면, 고친 설정이 안 먹는 것처럼 보인다 (iopaint에서 겪은 그 문제)

### 파이썬은 "있느냐"가 아니라 "그 모듈이 있는 것이 어느 것이냐"

한 PC에 파이썬이 여럿인 것이 보통이고 검출기는 그중 하나에만 깔린다. 첫 번째로 실행되는 것을
잡으면 위의 증상이 그대로 난다. `resolvePython(settings, 'rapidocr_onnxruntime')` 이 후보를
훑어 **import 되는 것**을 고르고, PATH가 가상환경으로 가려질 수 있으므로 설치 폴더도 직접 훑는다.

### 되돌린 판단 하나

0바이트 파일을 껍데기로 보고 거르려 했는데, **윈도우 스토어판 파이썬의 실행 파일이 정확히
0바이트 앱 별칭**인데 멀쩡히 돈다. 이걸 떨궜다가 검출기가 깔린 유일한 파이썬을 놓쳤다.
크기로 안 거르고, 진짜 껍데기는 import 단계에서 걸리게 했다.

### 그 밖에

- **VSR** — 설정이 비면 홈의 `vsr` · `video-subtitle-remover`를 찾는다.
  venv 파이썬 자리가 윈도우 전용(`Scripts\python.exe`)이던 것을 POSIX(`bin/python`)와 갈랐다 —
  맥·리눅스에서는 그냥 안 돌던 코드다
- **브라우저(크로미움) 점검 추가** — playwright는 npm 설치만으로 브라우저를 안 받는다.
  새 PC에서 빠뜨리면 틱톡 소재만 조용히 실패하는데, 이제 점검에 뜬다
- **뽑힌 경로를 감추지 않는다** — 설정 화면 · 대시보드 툴팁 · `npm run doctor`에 실제 파일
  경로가 나온다. 도구가 여럿인 PC에서 "왜 없다고 나오지"의 답이 거기 있다

## 이걸로 해결되지 않는 것

**탐색은 설치가 아니다.** ffmpeg·yt-dlp가 아예 없는 PC에서는 어떤 탐색도 소용없다.
친구 PC에서 아무것도 안 깔고 도는 것은 CLAUDE.md에 적힌 Electron 번들링 작업이고,
이 PR은 그 1순위 탐색 자리를 미리 뚫어둔 데까지다.

## 검증

- 타입체크 · 단위 **306개** · E2E 하네스 **40/40**
- 이 PC의 `settings.json`에서 절대경로를 전부 비운 채 **전 항목 ✅** 확인
  (ffmpeg · ffprobe · yt-dlp · iopaint · 한글 폰트 · VSR · 브라우저 · 글자 검출 · Typecast)
- 빈 PATH로도 `iopaint` → 저장소 venv에서 찾아내는 것 확인

author: caseyjbenko
body:
The instrument the open decisions in #17 depend on. Cohort digests and an optional semantic index are gated on numbers from here rather than on argument.

## Why the trace, not the answer

Retrieval runs as a loop. The agent owns semantic matching — it reformulates, narrows by type, judges candidates on `score` and `match_reason`; Rye supplies primitives. That makes the final answer nearly useless as a diagnostic, because a failure looks identical whether the agent never generated a matching phrasing, the threshold rejected a good one, it found the right node and misjudged it, or the knowledge simply is not there.

Four causes, four different fixes, one observable outcome. So the scorer reads the whole step list and assigns a mechanical cause:

| Bucket | What would fix it |
|---|---|
| `entry_missed` | Vocabulary visibility, reformulation prompting, or a semantic index |
| `path_not_found` | Depth, direction, or semantics arguments |
| `cross_subject` | Cohort digests |
| `misjudged` | Agent reasoning, not retrieval |
| `co_occurrence_as_causation` | Nothing to build — the filter exists; it was not used |
| `confabulated` | Refusal behavior |
| `refused_answerable` | Agent reasoning |

This is the eval-time half of #21: writes nothing, does not depend on `log_agent_query()`, so read-only agents can be measured.

## A fixture built to discriminate

`scenarios/harbor_point/` is fictional and deliberately not representative. Every element makes one measurement possible: near-duplicate labels, an abbreviation-only label (`HPF Marine Services`) no threshold reaches from the expanded name, a paraphrase-only target ("the fence company"), a three-hop causal chain, one root cause upstream of two of three delayed projects, and three questions whose answers are absent.

The important one is the **associative decoy** — a `regarding` edge joining the two ends of the causal chain directly:

```
with p_semantics := ARRAY['causal']   →  3 | {affects,affects,affects}
without                               →  1 | {regarding}          ← spurious
                                         3 | {affects,affects,affects}
```

Citing the decoy fails the question outright **even when the conclusion is true**. "X caused Y because X and Y are mentioned together" does not become right when X did cause Y, and scoring it correct would hide the exact failure the fixture exists to catch.

## Two scoring rules worth review

Both were bugs caught by running the scorer against the example trace:

1. **`entry_missed` outranks `refused_answerable`.** An agent that honestly declines because it never found the entity has an entry-point problem. Bucketing that as a refusal hides the only actionable cause.
2. **Questions with no expected entry node are excluded from the difficulty table.** Cross-subject questions carry a nominal difficulty but never exercise entry lookup; counting them as found inflated `paraphrase` from 1/1 to 3/3 — precisely the metric the semantic-index decision reads.

## Verification

```
node eval/retrieval/score_retrieval.mjs      # deterministic across runs
./scripts/docker-test.sh test --reset        # Conformance suite passed
psql -f eval/retrieval/scenarios/harbor_point/seed.sql   # idempotent on reload
```

Seed reload is a no-op (`INSERT 0 0`), and the `fa000001-` prefix is exclusive to this fixture — the original `f0000001-` collided with the concurrency test's fixed UUID, so a prefix-based cleanup would have taken that node with it.

## What is not built

Stated in the README so this is not mistaken for a completed comparison:

- **No RAG baseline arm.** `arm` is free-form and the scorer is comparison-agnostic, but `rag_baseline` and `hybrid` need an embedding provider and a driver, which live outside this repo.
- **No trace producer.** An agent runs the scenario and emits the JSON.
- **The example trace is invented.** It exists so the scorer's own behavior is checkable without an LLM; its numbers mean nothing about Rye.
- **One scenario, 16 questions.** Enough to validate the instrument, not to set a threshold — at 16, one question is six points, and a 20% cutoff needs 40–60 across several scenarios.
- **Real tenant data.** The conclusions that matter need the production graphs, not a 15-node fixture.

The proposed thresholds in the README are explicitly unsettled and worth arguing with before this is used to decide anything.

Refs #17, #21. The `rye_graph` arm depends on #19 for the traversal surfaces.

body:
## What

`the-port-knows-what-costs-money` — the confirmation gate no longer keys to
BattleGrid's `destructiveHint`. Production gate **PASS**, zero open violations,
archived, and issue #340 answered and closed.

## Measured live, not asserted

Section 7 ran against BattleGrid **v20.0.0** on a real account.

**7.1** — the platform moved v19.1.0 → v20.0.0 with the tool count **still 114**, the
third time that has happened here. All five money-affecting tools still annotate
`destructiveHint: false`, so this is current behaviour rather than a historical bug.

**7.2** — two accepts through the product. The audit records both claims as separate
facts:

| time | tool | our `destructive` | platform hint | confirmation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11:46:59 | `accept_entry_decision` | **true** | **false** | spent 11:46:59 |
| 11:49:06 | `accept_entry_decision` | **true** | **false** | spent 11:49:06 |
| 19:28:33 *(pre-change)* | `accept_entry_decision` | *false* | *NULL* | — |

Tokens are hash-bound to their decision ids. That third row is the point: **the two
eras are distinguishable because no history was rewritten.** Migration 0005 is one
`ADD COLUMN`, nullable, no `DEFAULT`, no `UPDATE`; 3,332 of 3,690 rows still carry a
NULL claim.

**7.3** — got the weaker result and says so. The surface refuses a read-only
connection and renders no accept control, so `beginGuardedCall` is never reached
through the UI. The port's own refusal stays proven offline. DE-9 records the gap
rather than claiming the stronger result.

## Spec merge

Two MODIFIED requirements into `openspec/specs/battlegrid-connection`. Scenario parity
was checked first, because a MODIFIED block replaces wholesale and silently drops
anything omitted: **4 → 7** and **4 → 5**, nothing dropped.

## What the gate found

One MAJOR violation, and it was the handover rather than the work. All three review
artifacts arrived still reading `PENDING EXECUTION EVIDENCE` with 28 blank rows, and
the master plan's final line still `PLAN READY FOR REVIEW` — the identical PG-001 the
previous full-track change recorded. Filled before the gate ran, with every row
re-derived independently against the code. Nothing in the built work failed.

## Also in this branch

Live evidence added to three existing items: #336 (reproduced with open positions —
`get_agent_budget` reports two impossible zeros while the same payload prices exposure
correctly), #304 (8 decisions expired unanswered on one agent), #306 (the live-write
authorisation blocker is discharged).

Two new items raised: #346 — the compose file that runs the whole product is untracked.
#347 — the Docker database copy has already diverged from native, because a host
process still writes there.

`docker-compose.yml` **is** in this branch, as of the second commit — see below. An
earlier revision of this description said it was deliberately excluded; that was true
when written and is no longer.

## Verification

`validate --all` 0 errors · `mirror` clean · typecheck, lint, build clean · suite
**2732/2738** at the documented six-failure baseline · `test:db` **96/96** on
`grid_commander_test` · the change's own guard tests **45/45**.

A near-miss worth reading in the gate tracker: the shell's inherited `DATABASE_URL`
pointed the truncating `test:db` suite at the working database holding 167,496 signal
readings. Caught by preflight; verified intact afterwards.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

# Second commit — the stack runs from one command

The two follow-ups above were resolved rather than left open.

## #346 — the compose file is tracked

Landed as the `lite` change `the-stack-runs-from-one-command`. `postgres:18`, a one-shot
`migrate` service, and `app`, on a user-defined network with the database published on
**5433**. Each of its three comments names the failure it prevents rather than
describing the line:

1. `postgres:18` moved `PGDATA` to `/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker`, so the volume mounts
   the **parent**. Mounting the familiar `/var/lib/postgresql/data` looks correct, mounts
   cleanly, and silently writes the database into the container layer.
2. A native PostgreSQL also binds 5432, so `localhost:5432` resolved to whichever
   answered — which is why the app once authenticated during its schema check and then
   failed on its runtime pool.
3. The default bridge does no DNS between containers, which is why a hand-rolled run
   reached for `host.docker.internal` and landed on the native server.

`.env.example` documents the `POSTGRES_*` variables and the two-`DATABASE_URL` trap.

## #347 — the signal record had two live copies

A scheduled task `GridCommanderRecorder` ran hourly from a **separate 2026-08-11
checkout**, writing to native 5432 while the product read the container.

The divergence was **bidirectional**, so no wholesale dump could have fixed it:

| table | native | docker | direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `signal_readings` | 167,496 | 165,816 | native +1,680 |
| `signal_captures` | 2,020 | 2,000 | native +20 |
| `signal_capture_runs` | 104 | 103 | native +1 |
| `audit_entries` | 3,193 | 3,708 | **docker** +515 |

Native was also at 4 migrations against Docker's 6, so restoring native over the
container would have reverted the schema.

Synced row-level: CSV export, staging table, `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` with
**no conflict target**, so the partial unique index migration 0004 introduced was
respected rather than thrown on. `audit_entries` took an explicit column list, so
native's 22 rows landed with `platform_destructive_hint` NULL — accurate, since the
platform's claim was never recorded for them.

Then the recorder was repointed at 5433 and run through its own task:

```
native  167,496 -> 167,496   (frozen)
docker  167,496 -> 169,176   (+1,680, one new capture run)
LastTaskResult: 0            (previously 3221225786 - terminated)
```

## Verified, not assumed

`docker compose config` valid · the mount confirmed an **ancestor** of the image's own
`PGDATA`, with `PG_VERSION 18` read back off the volume · `compose ps` shows the running
stack is the one this file declares · one recorder run observed landing in Docker and
leaving native frozen.

## Left open on purpose

The recorder still runs from that five-day-old checkout, and running it as a compose
service needs a `Dockerfile` change — the runtime image copies `.next/standalone`,
`drizzle` and two `tools/` scripts, not `bin/`. Native PostgreSQL is deliberately still
in place as the pre-consolidation fallback.

author: yoch
body:
## Goal

Promote MQTTium's repaired closed-loop network benchmark from advisory acquisition evidence to a separate, release-grade no-regression decision layer, calibrated entirely on same-code controls before viewing the historical pre-#252 versus post-#252 A/B result.

## Design

- Keep `benchmarks/paired_network.py` as the low-level acquisition engine.
- Add `benchmarks/network_release_gate.py` as the statistical orchestrator.
- Require baseline A/A and candidate A/A to pass before A/B is executed.
- Treat a complete opposite-order ABBA cycle, not each individual pair, as the independent statistical unit.
- Estimate multiplicative effects on log cycle ratios with a two-sided 95% Student-t interval.
- Preserve raw per-arm ACK-rate CV as diagnostic evidence rather than rejecting solely on one arm's absolute CV.
- Use deterministic inter-phase quiet periods rather than repeatedly probing until the runner happens to look eligible.
- Expose the deep gate only through manual `workflow_dispatch`; it is not push/PR/main CI.

## Same-code gates

Throughput must satisfy both:
- geometric-mean candidate/base estimate inside `[0.98, 1.02]`;
- entire 95% CI inside `[0.95, 1.05]`.

Publisher ACK-p50 must satisfy both:
- geometric-mean candidate/base estimate inside `[0.95, 1.05]`;
- entire 95% CI inside `[0.90, 1.10]`.

A CI is deliberately not required to contain exactly 1.0: that would be a difference test, not an equivalence requirement.

## A/B no-regression gates

- throughput lower 95% bound >= `0.95`;
- publisher ACK-p50 upper 95% bound <= `1.10`.

Subscriber delivery p50 remains recorded but diagnostic until its own A/A precision and acceptance margin are established.

## Calibrated defaults

MQTT 3.1.1, callback completion, 64-byte payload, windows **1/20/64**, two blocks, hash seeds `0..5` per block, **24 paired samples = 12 complete ABBA cycles per scenario**, ~2 s target low-level samples, and fixed 60 s quiet periods.

On the dedicated four-core Pi 5 runner the validated isolation convention is broker CPU 0, gate/subscriber/observer CPUs 1+3, publisher CPU 2.

The full three-phase protocol takes roughly **20-30 minutes** on this runner. It is intentionally manual-only and is not appropriate for routine CI.

### Why window 8 is not a release point

Multiple same-code runs showed a second execution regime at `window=8`. A prospective full same-code run on the frozen methodology (run `32055133863`) invalidated at w8: throughput estimate `1.0101`, CI95 `[0.9563, 1.0670]`, exceeding the `[0.95, 1.05]` equivalence interval. w1 and w64 remained precise.

The release set was therefore frozen to **1/20/64 before any historical A/B result was viewed**. Window 8 remains advisory only.

## Prospective full same-code validation

Run `32056117086`, exact harness HEAD `ef56c0178a450c863f384312da944129bff7fcee`, completed the entire `1/20/64` protocol successfully: baseline A/A, candidate A/A, and the third same-code A/B phase all passed with 12 cycles / 24 pairs per scenario.

No thresholds, seed schedule, sample duration, release points, or statistical rules were changed after that PASS.

## Historical pre-#252 vs post-#252 evidence

Only after the prospective controls passed was the historical A/B executed in run `32058758116` using the frozen gate:

- baseline: `0999d8abfe44a568209209403d7f215b18cc4eb7`
- candidate: `21798a7e8a2dbb3f1c1d6fe3890de42b5310798d`
- status: **PASS**

Both fresh same-code controls passed before A/B was allowed. A/B results:

| Window | Throughput candidate/base | 95% CI | ACK-p50 candidate/base | 95% CI |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | `1.0469` | `[1.0428, 1.0510]` | `0.9668` | `[0.9631, 0.9705]` |
| 20 | `1.1418` | `[1.1099, 1.1747]` | `0.8291` | `[0.8089, 0.8498]` |
| 64 | `1.0448` | `[1.0285, 1.0615]` | `0.9767` | `[0.9673, 0.9863]` |

All throughput lower bounds are well above `0.95`; all ACK-p50 upper bounds are well below `1.10`. The post-#252 runtime is therefore release-grade **non-regressed** on the calibrated loopback callback cells and is faster on all three measured throughput/ACK-p50 cells.

## Final repository shape

- PR-only push probe removed.
- `.github/workflows/arm64-network-release-gate.yml` is manual `workflow_dispatch` only.
- CLI default release windows are `1,20,64` and locked by a unit test.
- Documentation records the 12-cycle/24-pair design and explicitly warns about the ~20-30 minute deep-run cost.
- No MQTTium production/runtime source code is changed by this PR.
