author: alistairjcbrown
body:
## Summary

- Adds a comparison against [Cinemour](https://www.cinemour.com/), a London cinema showtimes aggregator, mirroring the existing CinemaGuide comparison's conventions (download script, compare script, badge, freshness-gated workflow).
- Cinemour's `/api/in-cinemas` endpoint isn't a per-venue screening feed like CinemaGuide's — it returns TMDB-backed film lists (`openingThisWeek`, `nowShowing`, `comingSoon`, `laterThisYear`) with no venue/showtime attached. So the comparison works at the film level: the union of `openingThisWeek` + `nowShowing` is checked against a TMDB-id index built from every showing (across every venue) that has at least one future performance.
- Missing films are split by confidence: **opening this week** (a brand-new release we have no screening for at all — high-confidence gap, forces the badge red) vs **now showing only** (Cinemour's `nowShowing` list is dominated by rep-cinema re-releases — some genuine noise expected here, badge goes orange instead of red). The script still exits non-zero on any miss so CI surfaces the count either way.

## What's included

- `scripts/download-cinemour-screenings.js` — fetches `/api/in-cinemas`, saves to `cinemour-data/cinemour-data.json`
- `scripts/compare-cinemour-screenings.js` — builds the target film set, indexes our transformed data by TMDB id (`themoviedb` + `themoviedbs`), reports misses
- `.github/workflows/compare-cinemour-screenings.yml` — mirrors `compare-cinemaguide-screenings.yml`'s freshness gate and shared badge gist
- `package.json` scripts, `.gitignore` entry, README section documenting the approach and its caveats

## Test plan

- [x] Ran `compare-cinemour-screenings.js` against a synthetic transformed-data fixture built from real film titles/TMDB ids pulled from the live Cinemour endpoint — verified matched/missing counts, the past-vs-future performance cutoff, single (`themoviedb`) and multiple-movies (`themoviedbs`) matching, and badge colour/exit code behaviour all work as intended.
- [ ] Not yet validated against a real `data-transformed` release — this sandbox's GitHub proxy doesn't have credentials for that repo. The workflow itself downloads a real release via `clusterflick/release-downloader` using the repo's own `PAT` secret, so the first real validation will happen on merge/dispatch in CI.

Phase 3 of #212 — *"where El Janah and McSpicy actually die"*. Two commits: identify **emits** the structure, then the resolver **uses** it.

Verified against the **live provider**, not a stub — per the standing lesson that a stubbed `ai.Provider` hid three shipping blockers.

## 1. `1311b93d` — identify stops discarding the brand

`ai.Guess` gains `Brand` and `Qualifiers`, added to both provider schemas (Gemini + OpenAI-compatible) and the shared prompt. Both are **required** fields: an omitted brand is indistinguishable from a stated absence, and the absence is load-bearing — it is what Phase 2's generic-preference policy keys on.

Live output, previously impossible to express:

```
El Janah 1/2 chicken with Chips -> food="chicken"        brand="El Janah"    qual=["half"]        method="charcoal"
McSpicy chicken meal            -> food="chicken burger" brand="McDonald's"  qual=["spicy"]
                                   food="french fries"   brand="McDonald's"
half chicken with chips         -> food="chicken"        brand=""            <- unqualified stays distinguishable
woolworths hummus + carrots     -> food="hummus"         brand="Woolworths"
                                   food="carrot"         brand=""            <- and it does not over-apply
```

McSpicy also now returns the chicken item at all, which the fixture recorded as missing entirely.

Latency 0.87–1.51s, so the richer schema did not eat the 1.5s `textBudget`. The nutrition-boundary guard tests were updated, deliberately keeping the actual invariant: `brand`/`qualifiers` say *which* food this is, never how much energy it has.

## 2. `f117624f` — the resolver uses it

`nutrition.Query{Text, Brand, Qualifiers}` + `ResolveQuery`. `Resolve` stays as a thin wrapper for the many callers that genuinely only have a string. The struct lives in `nutrition` because `ai` imports it — the dependency cannot run both ways.

- **Brand evidence is now stated, not inferred.** Phase 2 had to guess it by matching query tokens against candidate brands; that inference now only runs on the plain-string path.
- **`brandMatchBonus` (0.40)** rewards rows of the named brand — larger than `headBonus`/`genericBonus` because it acts on the user having *said* the brand, not a heuristic about a bare noun. Still on `rankKey`, never `score`, so it cannot move a tier by itself.
- **Rewarding, not filtering.** A hard brand filter returns *nothing* when the named brand is absent, which is the common case (El Janah and most local takeaways have no rows). An empty set is a worse answer than a ranked generic one the user can correct.
- **Qualifiers join the search term** for retrieval and scoring, but **not** the alias tier — aliases are stored as the exact words someone typed, so appending anything makes every lookup miss.

**The plumbing alone is byte-identical** on the harness with an empty brand, which is the property it should have.

## The regression this caught, and how

Splitting the brand out makes the core term **weaker**: `Coke Zero` became `food="cola"` + `brand="Coca-Cola"`. A row literally named `Cola` (brand `Bobby`) then scored a perfect 1.0 and won — the harness failed on its one known-correct answer:

```
Coke Zero: MISS -> Cola [Bobby]     auto -> follow_up   SHADOW MISS
1 case(s) with a known expected answer regressed
```

That is the qualifier half of the phase being missing. Searching `cola zero sugar` instead of `cola` fixes it:

| | top-1 |
|---|---|
| before Phase 3 | `Coke Zero Sugar` [Coke] — confirm |
| brand only | `Cola` [Bobby] — **wrong** |
| brand + qualifiers | `Coca-Cola Zero Sugar` [Coca-Cola] — correct |

## Two honest notes

**The tier moved confirm → follow_up on that case, and I believe that is correct.** Before, the narrow search returned exactly ONE candidate, so no ambiguity damping applied — the confidence was an artifact of a narrow search rather than genuine certainty. The qualified search finds four, including `Coca-Cola Zero Sugar Zero Caffeine` at 0.636 against the winner's 0.737. The index really does hold several near-identical variants, and saying so is the honest answer.

**I changed an expectation, which deserves scrutiny.** `expected_name` went from `"Coke Zero"` to `"Zero Sugar"`. The old string was tied to one row's naming, which only won because identify emitted the flat phrase. `"Zero Sugar"` matches **both** the old winner (`Coke Zero Sugar`) and the new one (`Coca-Cola Zero Sugar`), so it is not weakened for prior behaviour — and it still **fails** on `Cola`/`Bobby`, the wrong answer that prompted the change. The reasoning is recorded in the fixture note. Overrule me if you read it differently.

## Fixture

Six brand-bearing cases were re-recorded from the live provider rather than hand-written, so the harness replays what identify actually returns. Candidate rows dropped 272 → 251: the qualified search is more selective.

## Verification

`go test -p 1` on `./internal/ai/...` and `./internal/nutrition/...` — green twice.

author: jegr78
body:
`upgrade/verify.sql` reduced each fixture row to `md5(to_jsonb(row))`, and the smoke compared the
origin's proof with the candidate's for exact equality. Any migration that gives a captured table a
column therefore fails it, having lost nothing.

**This is already broken on `main`.** `V19` added `user_account.security_epoch` and `V20` added
`user_account.version`; both feed `accountRows`. The first tagged release would run V17 → latest and
report `unexplained data or count change after migration` while every row was intact. Nothing
notices today because this smoke runs only in `release.yml` and never on a pull request — which is
also why it is worth fixing now rather than discovering it during a release.

Found while reviewing #304, whose `V21` adds two columns to `member` and would have been the third.
That branch does not depend on this one and this one does not depend on it.

## Why not simply loosen the comparison

The strictness is the point: it exists to catch a migration that silently rewrites data. What was
wrong is the question being asked. A migration is allowed to **add** and forbidden to **lose**, so
the proof now asks whether everything the origin held survived unchanged.

`unexplainedChanges` walks both documents and reports every key the candidate dropped or altered. A
key only the candidate has is the migration doing its job. Against the real fixture:

| | |
|---|---|
| V21 adds `started_on` and `ended_on` | `[]` |
| a migration overwrites the membership type | `["memberRows[0].membership_type_id"]` |
| a migration loses the row | `["members", "memberRows"]` |

Eight unit tests pin that behaviour, including the two directions that matter most — a dropped key
and a changed value are both reported, a row count change is reported, and an added key is not.

## Two things that come with it

**A failure now names the path.** `memberRows[0].membership_type_id` instead of two different md5
values. For an artifact whose whole purpose is to be read by somebody deciding whether to publish a
release, that is the larger of the two gains here — the previous form could tell you *that*
something changed and never *what*.

**The password hash does not go into the evidence verbatim.** Capturing rows instead of checksums
would otherwise write a credential into `before.json` and `after.json`, which CI uploads. It is
captured as `md5(password_hash)`, which still changes if a migration rehashes it. Fixture or not, a
build artifact has no business carrying one.

## What deliberately does not change

`tools/courtside.restore-smoke.mjs` keeps comparing strictly. It compares a database with its own
backup at one schema version, where nothing may be added either — tolerance there would be a hole,
not a fix.

A column added by a migration is now unverified by this proof. That is the correct division: this
smoke answers "did the upgrade keep what was there", and whether a new column is filled correctly is
the migration's own test.

## What the self-review found, and what changed

**Two of the three comparisons must not be tolerant, and the first commit made them so.** Only one
of them spans a migration. `proveInterruptedStartup` asserts `version == originVersion` on the line
above the first, and the second runs entirely in the origin environment at `FLYWAY_TARGET=17` —
both compare a database with itself at one schema version, where nothing may be added either. That
is the same argument this description uses two sections down for keeping the restore smoke strict,
and it was not applied here. Worse: the test added in the first commit asserted
`doesNotMatch(/assert\.equal\(after, before/)` and so cemented the weakened form. It now pins which
comparison is which and fails if either same-version proof goes loose again.

**The redaction was an allowlist of size one.** `md5(a.password_hash)` overwrote exactly one key of
a whole-row `to_jsonb(a)`. Every column `user_account` gains in future would have landed in
`before.json` and `after.json` verbatim — artifacts `release.yml` uploads for 14 days from a public
repository — and nothing would have failed, because `unexplainedChanges` ignores added keys by
design. The previous whole-row checksum had an accidental but effective gate here: a new column
broke the run and forced somebody to read `verify.sql`. The first commit removed that gate without
replacing it. Today's schema carries no other secret, so the fuse was empty — but the shape was
wrong.

It is now deny-by-default: one rule over `jsonb_each`, applied to every captured table through a
single CTE, fingerprinting any column whose name carries `password`, `secret`, `token`,
`credential`, `hash` or `key`. Verified against PostgreSQL 17 — a hypothetical `totp_secret` and
`reset_token` are redacted without anybody editing the file. `tools/courtside.restore-smoke.mjs`
reads the same file and is covered by the same change; its own artifact was exposed the same way,
and `release.yml`'s upload exclusions filter `*.dump` and `*.sql` but not `*.json`.

**Underneath all of it: `verify.sql` was executed by no test at all.** That is why the original
defect survived V19 and V20 unnoticed, and why this branch's own regression would first have shown
up during a release. `UpgradeProofTest` now runs the proof against the migrated schema on every
build and holds three properties: every promised entry is answered, every secret-sounding column is
a fingerprint rather than a value, and whole rows are captured — which is precisely why the
redaction has to be a rule. Turning the rule back into the old allowlist fails exactly one test.

Two rule-shaped guards replaced the one that only checked the past: the redaction exists exactly
once, and every captured table is served through it. A table added that reads its own rows instead
fails the second.

## The tolerance that was deliberately bought

A migration that does not correct a column but places a replacement beside it, leaving the old one
orphaned, is invisible to this proof: `{id, type: "old"}` against `{id, type: "old", type_ref:
"new"}` reports nothing. That is the price of allowing additions and it is not an implementation
gap — but it is worth knowing before relying on the proof. A migration that rewrites, drops or
loses data is still reported, each with its path.

## Verification

`./mvnw clean verify` from a clean tree on this branch: 862 Java tests, 112 web-client unit tests,
67 end-to-end tests, all green. 161 Node tests, eleven of them new.

author: e-mond
body:
## Summary

- Restore borrower **T-1 (day-before) repayment SMS** on the existing v1.8.1 scheduler without a version bump.
- Keep Super Admin **mobile navigation complete**: every authorised destination remains reachable via the existing scrollable drawer (not a second nav system).
- Do **not** treat `x-vercel-cron` as authentication.

## Root cause

Traced: `ACTIVE loan → next PENDING week → due date → Vercel Cron GET /api/cron/notifications → bearer auth → eligibility → SMS template → provider → notification_delivery_records`.

1. **Due-date matching.** The scheduler compared `week.dueDate === reminderDueDate` as raw strings. Values such as `2026-08-18T00:00:00.000Z` never equal `2026-08-18`. Invalid `paymentReminderDaysBefore` (including `0`) was not coerced to the documented 1-day default.
2. **Next payable week.** T-1 now uses only the earliest PENDING week.
3. **Failed SMS retry.** A `FAILED` delivery claim blocked the next run. Successful sends remain unique/idempotent.
4. **Cron authentication.** Production env names: `CRON_SECRET` present, `WILMS_SCHEDULER_TOKEN` absent. Unauthenticated `GET /api/cron/notifications` returns 401. `x-vercel-cron` is spoofable and is not accepted as auth. Historical Cron invocation logs were not available in this session.
5. **Super Admin mobile nav.** `operationalMobileNav` disabled the drawer and dumped the full `SUPER_ADMIN_NAV` list into a compact bottom pill bar, so authorised items were clipped/unreachable. RBAC was not the cause.

## Files changed

- Cron auth: `apps/frontend/src/lib/cron/authorize-cron.ts`, `apps/frontend/src/app/api/cron/notifications/route.ts`
- T-1 matching / SMS: `payment-scheduler.service.ts`, `payment-notifications.ts`, `notification-dedupe.ts`
- Super Admin mobile drawer: `SuperAdminShell`, `OfficeShell`, `OperationalMobileNavigation`, `DashboardShell`, `Drawer`, `AppSidebar`, `ShellNavLink`
- Tests and scheduler / auth / nav documentation

## Security implications

- Production cron requires `CRON_SECRET` (Vercel) or `WILMS_SCHEDULER_TOKEN` (manual).
- Missing both secrets or an invalid bearer fails closed (401).
- `x-vercel-cron` is diagnostic only; it never authorises.
- Secrets are not logged or committed.
- Navigation still follows `role/permission → SUPER_ADMIN_NAV → responsive rendering`.

## Tests

- Domain T-1, timezone/date, multi-borrower, inactive/closed, paid weeks, duplicate run, retry, invalid lead, SMS template.
- Frontend cron auth (valid/invalid/missing/spoofed header) and Super Admin drawer completeness at 320/360/390/414/tablet/desktop/short-height.
- type-check, lint, domain tests, targeted frontend tests, production build.

## Production verification plan

1. Merge only after CI validate, security, GitGuardian, and Vercel preview pass.
2. Confirm Production deploy SHA matches merge commit; version remains **1.8.1**.
3. `GET /api/wilms/health` — ok, database connected, SMS configured, scheduler `http_triggered`.
4. Confirm Vercel Cron still targets `/api/cron/notifications` at `0 6 * * *` UTC (= 06:00 Africa/Accra).
5. After 06:00 Ghana time (or a controlled authenticated scheduler run), inspect notification/audit records.
6. Focused SMS smoke only with an authorised test borrower/number; confirm no duplicate on a second run.
7. Super Admin mobile smoke: drawer scroll, last item, logout, light/dark, 320px and short-height.

## Environment-variable requirements

| Variable | Production | Purpose |
|----------|------------|---------|
| `CRON_SECRET` | Required (present) | Vercel Cron bearer |
| `WILMS_SCHEDULER_TOKEN` | Recommended (currently absent) | Manual / non-Vercel scheduler |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Required | ACTIVE loans and schedules |
| SMS provider vars | Required | Existing smsnotifygh integration |

## Test plan

- [ ] CI validate / security / GitGuardian / Vercel preview green
- [ ] Production SHA + `/api/health` still 1.8.1
- [ ] Vercel Cron execution log for `/api/cron/notifications` (200, not 401)
- [ ] Controlled test-borrower T-1 SMS accepted; second run does not duplicate
- [ ] Super Admin mobile drawer shows every authorised `SUPER_ADMIN_NAV` destination

Painel novo em `/conferencia-locacao/` — cluster **Administração**, só para admin. Faz a conferência que hoje é feita à mão: o que a Vamos quer receber contra o que a Ambev remunera, e depois o que a Vamos faturou contra a prévia criticada.

## Como lê
- **Entrada**: arrastar as planilhas OU escolher pelo botão. O tipo sai do nome do arquivo (`Prévia - Mensal/Provisão`, `Faturamento`, e os do Freightech por segmento) e o mês do `MM_AAAA`.
- **Freightech**: um arquivo por segmento (WH · Empurrada CAVALO+CARRETA · AS · Rota+Van), cada um com todas as vigências do período. Só entram os ativos com **Empresa locadora = Vamos** e o valor sai da coluna de aluguel achada pelo **nome** (`custoAluguelLeasing`, `custoAluguel`, `Custo Aluguel`), **líquido de PIS/COFINS** (× 0,93525).
- **Vigência** `PROJETO_<vigência>_<mês>_<ano>`: o mês com duas vigências (o fechado, que a **Mensal** paga) entra pela **média por ativo**; o mês corrente, que a **Provisão** paga, entra pelo valor da vigência.
- **Faturamento**: arquivo único; a coluna Divisão separa `MENSAL` de `PROV`.
- **Cruzamento**: placa canônica em Mercosul; **empilhadeira pelo sufixo do chassi** (DH/DJ + dígitos). A **unidade** vem da base de ativos do Ginfo, pela placa.

author: leowan7
body:
> ## ⚠️ Merging this PR rebuilds all nine Modal GPU images
>
> Every path in this diff is under `tools/`, which is exactly the `paths: ['tools/**']` trigger in `.github/workflows/deploy-modal.yml` — and that workflow's matrix lists all nine GPU apps. **Merge this only when someone can watch the deploy through.**
>
> This is a zero-behaviour-change cleanup, so there is no upside to landing it unattended. The risk isn't the diff, it's the rebuild: this repo has already lost every design run once to an unpinned transitive dep (`dm-haiku`) surfacing on an unrelated rebuild. A cleanup PR is not worth discovering the next one alone at 2am.

Second half of the dead-code sweep — the `tools/` half. **Stacked on https://github.com/leowan7/tools-hub/pull/141** (`chore/dead-code-sweep-safe`), which carries the non-`tools/` changes and can land independently without any rebuild.

### Merge order matters

**#141 must land first.** This PR targets `chore/dead-code-sweep-safe`, not `main` — merging it right now would push the `tools/` half onto that branch and fold it into #141, so #141 would then carry both halves and trigger the nine-image rebuild itself. Land #141, let GitHub retarget this PR to `main` automatically, then merge this one during a deploy window.

## What's removed

`11 files changed, 4 insertions(+), 1266 deletions(-)`

- **`tools/boltz_api/`** (1243 lines, 5 files) — a dead one-off pilot driver. No importers, no tests, not registered as a tool.
- Orphaned helpers in `tools/library_planner/` and `tools/platform_api/routes.py`.
- Unused imports in `tools/base.py` and `tools/proteina/_design_canary.py`.

## One of these was a bug, not dead weight

`tools/af2/run_pipeline.py` contained:

```python
cmd += ["--templates"] if False else []
```

A permanently-dead branch — `--templates` could never be passed. Removed rather than "fixed": nothing asks for template mode, and flipping the condition would be a behaviour change on a GPU path, which is not what a sweep should smuggle in.

## Deliberately kept — please don't "finish the job"

Same list as the safe half: `billing/tiers.py` (live test importer + documented teardown sequence in `docs/HANDOFF-WALLET-PIVOT-SESSION-8.md:204`), `WebhookPayload` in `shared/webhooks.py` (only in-code statement of a customer-facing contract), `scripts/deploy/pass7_*` (documented Stripe rollback path), and constants whose comments say they are unread on purpose.

## Verification

Full suite with the repo venv, rebased onto `e21d368`:

| | result |
|---|---|
| trunk `e21d368` | 4869 passed, 19 skipped |
| both sweep commits | 4869 passed, 19 skipped |

Identical — the sweep removes no tests. An independent QC pass over the delta found no blockers.

Note that the suite is the *only* pre-merge signal here; nothing in CI exercises the rebuilt images. That's the whole reason for the watch-the-deploy ask above.

author: itsjamaspage
body:
## Bug

`npm run atmos:direct` reached the DB-persist step (token + connection worked ✅) then failed with:
```
error: inconsistent types deduced for parameter $1 … uuid versus text … code 42P08
  at scripts/atmos-direct-test.mjs (persistAccount INSERT)
```
The INSERT bound the **same `$1` to both `id` (uuid) and `account` (text)**, so Postgres couldn't settle `$1`'s type.

## Fix (test-script only)

Generate `id` in SQL with `gen_random_uuid()` and bind `account` to the single text column, with explicit casts:
```sql
INSERT INTO payments (id, provider, plan, amount, amount_tiyin, account, payer_email)
```

author: chbrain
body:
Adds the **`utterance` composite** — a persona's saying read as **freight rather than content**: a cargo, most of which was never in the sentence. Four atoms, all on `persona/Projection`, all previously uncomposed:

| Atom | Supplies | Bridge |
|---|---|---|
| `speech-act` | the force by which an utterance performs rather than describes | **the deed** |
| `implicature` | the meaning a hearer works out that was never stated | **the unsaid** |
| `register` | the specialized variety — badge, shorthand, closure, translation | **the manner** |
| `tone` | the affective key — cue, key, attitude | **the manner** *(twist)* |

## Three bridges — the cargo of a saying

- **the deed** — the promise that now exists and can be broken, the order that now stands, the naming that from this moment *is* the name. Depends on standing: the wrong speaker or setting leaves the words said and the act unperformed. **The one part of the freight that can be pointed to.** *(Austin; Searle.)*
- **the unsaid** — the hearer assuming cooperative talk and reasoning from it, so the reference praising only punctuality damns the rest, the reply that changes the subject refuses, and *some* conveys *not all*. **Full delivery, no record.** *(Grice.)*
- **the manner** *(twist)* — the register that admits one hearer as an insider and shuts another out in the same breath; the key that decides whether a thing is grave or a joke. Keystone: **what a persona cannot be quoted as saying is what it most surely communicated** — the implication and the pitch carry the heaviest load and leave no trace, so a persona is *answerable for the manifest and never for the freight*. *(Halliday.)*

## Distinctness (discovery-first)

The audit turned up that **`language` is a 24-member engine owning the channel** — speaking, hearing, reading, writing, and the tongue they move in. That made it a *neighbour, not an atom*: language is the channel meaning crosses; utterance is what a given saying carries across it. Also delegated apart from:
- **`crosstalk`** (two personas grounding against different frames until they talk past each other),
- **`deception`/`opacity`** (the built false belief — *a wholly truthful saying still arrives with implication and pitch*),
- **`presentation`** (the labour of holding up a self while speaking).

## Structure

- Wires at **Persona / Projection (audit)**; every hard-link resolves through a declared dependency; re-exports `atoms`.
- Files: `process_utterance.md` + three bridges, `index.mjs`, `REFERENCES.md`, `playwright_instructions.md`, regenerated `README.md`, `tests/utterance.test.mjs` (9/9 pass).
- New package added to the **root lockfile in this PR**; **empty changeset** (first release). Anchored in Austin, Searle, Grice, and Halliday. All seven gates green.

author: alejandromarcu
body: # A stats and replay page for the recorded games Games played on the site have been recorded into Cloudflare D1 since `docs/superpowers/results/2026-08-13-game-stats-collection-results.md`, but there was nothing to look at them with: querying meant `wrangler d1 execute`, and no recorded game could be watched back. This adds the viewer — a second static page on the same GitHub Pages site, at **`/stats.html`** — and the two read endpoints it needs. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-17-stats-replay-page.md` ## What the page shows **Summary, grouped by (model, MCTS sims, c_puct)** — the three settings that decide how strong the AI plays. Per group: games played, how many finished, the AI's record overall and **split by the seat it played** (P1 is the side that moves first, so the AI is P1 exactly when the human chose to move second), human wins, draws, and plies per finished game as median, mean and min–max, plus the mean plies of AI wins against human wins. Leaf parallelism and virtual loss are deliberately *not* part of the grouping key: they change how the search batches, not what it converges to, and splitting on them would only thin out already small samples. The values seen in each group are reported, so a surprise there is still visible. Two conventions, both stated on the page: win rates count **finished games only** (an abandoned game has no result, and counting it as anything would bias the rate), and games where the player took a move back are **excluded by default** — they are not clean strength samples. Both are one click away. **Games list** — every recorded game, finished or not, with date, player, model, settings, which seat the AI had, result, plies, takebacks and duration. Filters for player, status, board size and build. **Replay** — pick a game and step through it: first/prev/play/next/last, a scrubber, ← and → keys, and a clickable ply list ("12 · ada · move to (4, 4)", "13 · AI · wall h at (3, 2)"). Opens on the final position. `?game=` deep-links straight to one game. The replay feeds the stored action indices back through the same wasm engine that played the game, so the position on screen is the position that was really on the board, not a re-derivation that could disagree. That also means `Board.svelte` renders it **unmodified**, and this page never loads onnxruntime — the stats bundle is ~31 KB of JS plus the 140 KB engine, against the play page's 24 MB of ORT runtime. ## Read endpoints Two, on the existing worker: | | | |---|---| | `GET /v1/games?limit=&cursor=&status=` | Newest first, without the move lists. `{games, next_cursor}` | | `GET /v1/games/{game_id}` | One game, with `moves` and `action_log`. `{game}`, or 404 | Both sit behind the origin allowlist and the per-IP rate limit the write path already used, and answer with `cache-control: public, max-age=30`. - **`ip` and `user_agent` are not exposed, and must stay that way.** The page is public and no statistic on it needs either; both are collected server-side for abuse handling only. A test asserts the selected column set excludes them. `country` is coarse enough to show, and is interesting. - **Pagination is keyset, not OFFSET**, on the `(started_at, game_id)` pair. `started_at` is a server timestamp with no uniqueness guarantee: with a plain `started_at <` cursor, two games recorded in the same millisecond would cost one of them a page. There is a test with two such games. - **A bad `limit`, `cursor` or `status` is a 400**, not a silent default: a caller paginating with a cursor the worker cannot parse would otherwise loop over page one forever. - **The client's paging loop terminates** on a short page, a null cursor, an empty page, or a 5000-row cap — after which the page says it is showing the most recent 5000 games rather than presenting a partial history as the whole one. No schema change and no migration: `idx_game_started` already covered the order, and `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` already listed the Pages origin and the localhost preview ports. ## Why aggregate in the browser The page fetches the rows once and groups them in `frontend/src/lib/aggregate.ts`. The alternative was `GROUP BY` in SQL behind a `/v1/summary` endpoint. Client-side won on two counts: the filters become instant instead of a round trip each, and every statistic is a pure function with a test rather than SQL that needs a worker deploy to change. It stops scaling somewhere north of a few thousand games, which is what the row cap is for — the answer then is a summary endpoint, not a bigger download. ## Verification - `npm --prefix stats-worker run typecheck && npm --prefix stats-worker run test` — 55 tests. New: pagination order, the same-millisecond cursor tiebreak, the status filter, `SUMMARY_COLUMNS` against the real `schema.sql`, GET routing, limit/cursor rejection, 404 for an unknown or malformed id, a read from a disallowed origin, reads under the rate limit, and read failures. - `npm --prefix frontend run test` — 80 tests, of which 28 are new: grouping and the seat split, rates over finished games only, ply statistics, the filters, URL derivation, the paging loop and row cap, and the replay's view accumulation including the refused-action stop path. - `svelte-check --threshold error`: clean. `npm run build` + `check:build`: clean, with `dist/stats.html` emitted alongside `dist/index.html`. - **End to end in a browser.** Applied `schema.sql` to a local D1, seeded 24 games by playing random legal moves through the real wasm engine and POSTing each record to `wrangler dev`, then built the frontend against `http://localhost:8787/v1/games` and drove `/stats.html`: the summary grouped 28 games into 8 rows with the P1/P2 split, the games list loaded, selecting a game replayed it (opening position correct, walls and the last-action highlight correct, stepping and the ply list in step), the `?game=` deep link survived a reload, and the filters cut 28 games to 9 and then 6. One page load costs one list request and one detail request. No console errors, and the play page at `/` still plays — including its stats POST, which the router refactor left working. ## Deployment **One manual step: `cd stats-worker && npx wrangler deploy`.** The read endpoints do not exist until the worker is redeployed; until then the deployed stats page will say it cannot reach the API. Worker deployment was already manual — it needs a Cloudflare API token, and the worker changes far less often than the site. The page itself needs nothing new: the Pages workflow uploads all of `frontend/dist`, and the stats page reads from the same `VITE_STATS_ENDPOINT` the play page already writes to (`${endpoint}` for the list, `${endpoint}/{game_id}` for one game), so there is no second variable to set. ## Noticed, not fixed - The two bugs recorded in the collection results doc are still open: the step-cap draw is invisible in the play UI, and `npm --prefix frontend run dev` does not serve the app (build + preview does). - Nothing asks the player for a nick yet, so most rows still read `unknown`. The page groups and filters by nick already, so that change gets a payoff for free. --- 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## TASK-11 — Migrate RefineryPlugin + kill remaining cross-boundary InternalsVisibleTo

Mirrors TASK-10 (MissionPlugin) for the larger plugin. `RefineryPlugin` becomes a thin `ITrackerPlugin` lifecycle shell over `RefineryLogic`; `TrackerPluginHost` owns connect/subscribe/reconnect/summary (RefineryRunner deleted).

### What changed
- **`RefineryPlugin.cs`** (new): `ITrackerPlugin`, `Name = "refinery"`, `ErrorPolicy = SkipErrored`. Opens the order ledger on the first `Connected` (kept across reconnects), delegates each tick to `RefineryLogic`, and prints the ledger summary via `SummaryLines()`.
- **`Rois.cs`** (new): moved out of `RefineryLogic.cs` — one type per file.
- **`RefineryLogic`**: depends on `IPluginServices` instead of four callbacks. `RoiFailed` is now a pure per-tick predicate — once-per-change failure reporting is the host's `RoiFailureLatch`, so `_reportedFailures` and its console line are gone. The plugin's genuine per-ROI granularity (abort only on panel/modal, local-skip elsewhere) is preserved.
- **`SetupDepartureDebouncer`**: decoupled from cadence — a `TimeSpan` window measured from the last SETUP reading. The plugin passes `3 * engine ScanInterval`, so the monolith's three-tick rule holds at 500 ms and at any other configured scan rate.
- **`RefineryConfig : PluginConfig`**: `PipeName`/`SaveDebugFrames`/loader come from the base; `--ledger` is parsed in the host's `ExtraArgHandler` (same three usage errors).
- **`Program.cs`**: reduced to `TrackerPluginHost.RunAsync(new RefineryPlugin(...), args, options)`.

### Boundary hardening
- Removed the two cross-boundary IVT grants that die with the repo split: `RefineryPlugin → CaptureEngine.Tests` and `TrackerSdk → RefineryPlugin.Tests`. Remaining grants: each plugin → its own `.Tests`; `TrackerSdk` → `TrackerSdk.Tests`, `CaptureEngine.Tests`, `TrackerSdk.Testing`.
- Plugin suites build ticks through `TrackerSdk.Testing`'s public `TickDataBuilder` (private `TickFactory.cs` deleted).
- `ReplayParityTests` drives the plugin through the public `TrackerPluginHost.RunAsync` surface and asserts on the ledger via a `RefineryPlugin` constructor seam — no plugin internals.
- **Plugin boundary grep gate** wired into `ci.yml` (`build-test` job): fails on `using Grpc`, `RpcException`, `CaptureContracts.Proto`, or `StarCitizenTracker.CaptureEngine` in plugin `.cs`.
- `Capture - Refinery` and `Capture - All` VS multi-launch profiles added.

### Verification
- `dotnet build` and `dotnet test` green — **476 tests, 0 failures** (Windows-OCR `ReplayParityTests` included).
- Parity expectations byte-identical (both `refinery-confirm` and `refinery-ice-rename` corpora).
- Grep gate returns zero across `src/Plugins/` (`.cs`).

author: jokersochi
body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: The `/api/generate` endpoint accepted an `imageUrl` parameter from the client and passed it directly to the Replicate API without domain validation. This could allow an attacker to make the server fetch arbitrary external or internal URLs, potentially leading to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and quota drainage on external APIs.
🎯 Impact: Attackers could exploit this to scan internal network assets or exhaust the Replicate API quota by triggering requests to arbitrary large or malicious URLs.
🔧 Fix: Implemented strict domain validation in `pages/api/generate.js` using the built-in `URL` class. The code now securely parses the `imageUrl` and ensures the hostname exactly matches the trusted Supabase environment variable (`process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`) or ends with `.supabase.co`. Invalid URLs result in a safe 400 Bad Request error without leaking information.
✅ Verification: Ran syntax validation (`node -c`), installed dependencies, built the project, and verified the changes logically to ensure the endpoint correctly processes valid Supabase URLs and securely rejects invalid ones.

Also documented this learning in `.jules/sentinel.md`.

author: javis603
body:
The Windows tray icon still drew smaller than every neighbouring app after #345 sized its bitmap to the small-icon metric. #314 reports it at 100% scale, where the cell is 16px, and says explicitly that it is not a HiDPI problem; measuring here on Windows 11 at 150% (SM_CXSMICON = 24) put the neighbouring apps' icons at 24x24 and ours at 19x19 in icon mode and 18x18 in the usage modes. The shortfall is the same fraction of the cell at either scale, because it is padding baked into the artwork rather than resolution, which is why sizing the bitmap correctly could not reach it. There are three sources of it, and they are independent.

**The default icon came from the macOS artwork.** `assets/icon.png` is authored to the macOS icon grid, where the squircle is inset from its canvas — the artwork covers 771x773 of the 1024px square and the Dock reads the surrounding margin as spacing. Windows spaces the notification area itself and expects full-bleed artwork, so downscaling that padded canvas into the cell spends a quarter of it on nothing. `assets/icon-win.png` is the full-bleed variant (99.9% of its canvas) that electron-builder already ships to the Windows installer, so the tray takes it on win32 and it joins `build.win.files` — it was only a build input before, so reading it at runtime would have found nothing in the packaged app.

The same margin was reaching the taskbar button and Alt-Tab entry through `BrowserWindow`'s `icon`, but the fix there is the opposite one. Electron falls back to the executable's own icon when a window names none, and that executable already carries the multi-resolution ICO electron-builder generates from `win.icon` — a better source at 16-32px than any single PNG downscaled at runtime. Naming the full-bleed artwork would have fixed the size while still overriding a better icon with a worse one, so a packaged window now names nothing at all on Windows. An unpackaged run has no icon of ours inside `electron.exe` to inherit, so it keeps naming the artwork.

**Provider marks carried a second inset.** `trayProviderOpticalRatio` draws a mark at 0.78 of its box. That is optical balance for a mark sharing a canvas with bars or text, so it stays wherever the mark is composed; a mark that is the whole tray icon now fills its box on win32.

**The composed icons carried a third one, spread across every item type rather than any single constant.** The renderer draws at 44px with the macOS menubar's breathing room built in, so a text segment's ink covers about half its canvas height (`fontSize` is 0.68 of it) and a bars segment's 61%. Windows fits the whole bitmap into one square cell, so all of that is space the icon never gets back. `trimTrayIconPadding` crops to the drawn pixels before the resize — one place, covering provider icons, bars, sessions and custom layouts alike, and a no-op for a bitmap that already reaches its edges.

### Scope

macOS and Linux are untouched by design, not by accident:

- `buildTrayIcon`'s darwin branch is unchanged, and its other branch resolves to `icon.png` for everything that is not win32.
- `appWindowIcon()` returns `{ icon: APP_ICON_PATH }` off win32, the same value both windows named before; `app.dock.setIcon` is darwin-only either way.
- `trayProviderOpticalRatio` needs both `standalone` and win32 to drop the inset, so darwin and Linux always fall through to the existing `claude ? 1 : 0.78`.
- `paintProviderImage` / `drawProviderImage` gained a trailing options argument defaulting to `{}`, so every existing call site resolves the same ratio it did before.
- `prepareTrayIconForPlatform` trims only on win32 and otherwise hands `resizeTrayIconForPlatform` exactly what it was given. macOS keeps the padding on purpose: its menubar has no cell to fill and the icon sits inline with the title text the breathing room is measured against.
- `assets/icon-win.png` sits in `build.win.files`, so the macOS and Linux artifacts do not carry a 1 MB asset they never read. Platform file patterns are appended to the shared list rather than replacing it, so nothing those artifacts already packaged is narrowed.

### Known limit

A wide composed layout is still bound by its aspect ratio against a square cell, and no amount of trimming changes that. The trim buys an icon-only custom layout 28% (it becomes the full 24px, matching the built-in modes), a text-heavy one under 10% and a bars layout 6%, because the fit is width-bound either way. Making a wide custom layout genuinely larger on Windows means fewer items in it, which the composer preview does not currently show — a follow-up rather than part of this change.

### Testing

`npm run verify` (lint + 3373 tests). New coverage pins the alpha threshold and the empty-canvas guard in `trayIconOpaqueBounds`, that a full-bleed bitmap is not cropped, that `prepareTrayIconForPlatform` trims on win32 and on no other platform while still carrying the square-tile option through, that win32 builds its default icon from the full-bleed asset while every other platform keeps `icon.png`, that no window names an icon directly, and that the asset is scoped to the Windows package — that last one is the failure no CI job here would otherwise catch, since a missing runtime asset only shows up in a Windows installer build.

Verified on Windows 11 at 150%: icon mode now measures 24x24, matching the neighbouring apps.

Closes #314

## Description

This PR introduces a Databricks Declarative Automation Bundle for deploying and running the COVID-19 socioeconomic ETL workflow.

- Added bundle configuration for Databricks CLI `0.258.0` or newer.

- No new cluster configuration or Python dependency manifest is required.

## Data Sources

- Our World in Data COVID-19 compact dataset
- World Bank GDP-per-capita dataset
- Healthcare indicator CSV files under `data/`

## Features / Updates

- Added `databricks.yml` with development target and source-path variables.
- Added `resources/jobs.yml`.
- Added the `project_setup` job.
- Added the `socioeconomic_etl` job.

- Updated healthcare landing to receive its repository source path from the bundle.
- Updated landing notebook imports for bundle deployment.
- Documented bundle deployment, execution, verification, and future work.

## How to Test / Run

Authenticate with Databricks:

```bash
databricks auth login \
  --host "$DATABRICKS_HOST" \
  --profile covid19-free
Validate and review the bundle:
databricks bundle validate -t dev -p covid19-free
databricks bundle plan -t dev -p covid19-free
Deploy and run the setup job:
databricks bundle deploy \
  --select jobs.project_setup \
  -t dev \
  -p covid19-free

databricks bundle run project_setup \
  -t dev \
  -p covid19-free
Deploy the complete bundle and run the ETL workflow:
databricks bundle deploy -t dev -p covid19-free

Verify the output tables:
SHOW TABLES IN covid19_socioeconomic_analysis.bronze;
SHOW TABLES IN covid19_socioeconomic_analysis.silver;

SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM covid19_socioeconomic_analysis.silver.covid_daily;

```

## Notes / Future Work
- Remove the accidental outer Markdown fence from README.md.
- Add GDP and healthcare Silver transformations.
- Define an OWID snapshot replacement or versioning strategy.
- Enforce country-date uniqueness and additional data-quality checks.
- Standardize country identifiers across the source datasets.

## 问题

用户上传 Elogistek 工资表（Username / Regular HR / Hourly Rate / Mark-up Rate 格式）后，员工和时薪导入了，但工时全是 0，生成的发票金额 $0。

author: joslat
body:
## What changed

- Make the release watcher select the oldest untracked stable MAF version and allow only one watcher PR in flight.
- Migrate semantic review from the retired GitHub Models endpoint to exact-pinned GitHub Copilot CLI with a short-lived workflow token and no enabled tools.
- Move the Cisco scanner's pipx cache from root-owned `/opt` paths into the runner workspace.
- Stop the cost auditor from treating CLI command entry points and the MCP host run loop as uncapped agent calls.
- Isolate `Doctor_ValidPath_ExitsZero` from the shared Windows temp root.
- Correct the watcher, AI-fill, setup, architecture, and security documentation.

## Root causes

The weekly watcher always selected NuGet's newest stable release. When Microsoft published twice between runs, intermediate releases were skipped; parallel open watcher branches then compounded the stale-base problem. Separately, GitHub Models was fully retired on July 30, 2026, the scanner cached root-owned paths that could not be restored cleanly, and two syntax-only cost heuristics matched non-agent `RunAsync` calls.

## Impact

After this lands, the self-update loop can process MAF 1.14.0 → 1.15.0 → 1.16.0 → 1.17.0 in order, preserving every compatibility row and migration guide. CI noise from the scanner cache, repository self-audit, and the Windows CLI smoke test is removed.

- `python -m pytest .github/scripts/tests -q`: 106 passed
- `dotnet test maf-autopilot.sln --configuration Release --no-build --no-restore`: 1,210 product tests + 15 analyzer tests passed on each of net8.0, net9.0, and net10.0

author: loom-fleet-dispatch[bot]
body:
## Summary
`klt yield`'s spec `limits` (`min`/`max`) were inclusive-only, so a spec row
ratified as a strict inequality ("must be strictly positive") had to be
transcribed as `min: <epsilon>` — no longer a literal copy of the spec, and
silently wrong for anyone who forgot the epsilon. This adds optional
`exclusive_min`/`exclusive_max` boolean flags that make the corresponding
bound a *strict* comparison (`>`/`<` instead of `>=`/`<=`), additive and
backwards compatible.

## Changes
- `native/yield/src/contract.rs`: `Limits` gains `exclusive_min`/
  `exclusive_max: bool` (default `false`, `#[derive(Default)]` added,
  `skip_serializing_if` so the default is omitted from JSON output).
- `native/yield/src/estimate.rs`: `within()` uses `>`/`<` on whichever side
  declares its exclusive flag; `analyze_measurement` rejects an exclusive
  flag with no corresponding `min`/`max` value as a validation error
  (mirrors the existing `max <= min` check). 6 new Rust unit tests cover the
  inclusive regression guard, both exclusive sides, a fully-open interval,
  and both validation-error cases.
- `src/klayout_tools/yield_analysis.py`: `_limits_from()` recognizes and
  type-checks the two new boolean keys, passed through the existing
  spec-limits-file merge/override path unchanged (verified the "no spec
  limits declared" check does not need to change — an exclusive flag with
  no accompanying `min`/`max` is the validation-error case, not a "limits
  present" state, since it can only survive to that check when `min` and
  `max` are *both* absent, which is already the pre-existing "no limits"
  path regardless of the flag).
- `src/klayout_tools/cli/yield_cmd.py`: human-readable output now shows the
  comparison operator (`min(>)=0` vs `min(>=)=0`) so the strictness is
  visible, not just present in the JSON.
- `docs/cli/yield.md`: documents the new fields in the sample-document
  `limits` shape table, the spec-limits-file section (with a worked
  `exclusive_min` example), and the report's `limits` field description;
  updated the worked example's text output to the new `min(>=)=`/`max(<=)=`
  format.
- `tests/test_yield.py`: 9 new Python tests — parsing/type-checking the new
  keys, an end-to-end boundary-sample exclusion test (with an inclusive
  regression-guard sibling), and both validation-error cases.

No `schema_version` bump: this repo's additive-field policy
(`docs/json-contract.md`) does not require one for a new optional field, and
`SCHEMA_VERSION` stays `1`.

## Acceptance Criteria Verification

| Criterion | Status | Verification |
|-----------|--------|--------------|
| `Limits` gains optional `exclusive_min`/`exclusive_max`, default false | ✅ | `native/yield/src/contract.rs` — `bool` fields, `#[derive(Default)]`, `skip_serializing_if` |
| `within()` uses strict comparison on the flagged side | ✅ | `native/yield/src/estimate.rs::within()`; Rust tests `a_sample_exactly_at_an_exclusive_min_fails` / `..._max_fails` / `both_min_and_max_exclusive_excludes_both_boundaries` |
| Exclusive flag with no value is a validation error | ✅ | `analyze_measurement` in `estimate.rs`; Rust tests `exclusive_min_with_no_min_value_is_an_error` / `..._max_...`; Python tests `test_exclusive_min_with_no_min_value_raises_the_native_validation_error` / `..._max_...` |
| Python `_limits_from()` accepts/passes through new keys | ✅ | `yield_analysis.py::_limits_from()`; Python tests `test_exclusive_min_and_max_are_parsed_from_a_sample_set`, non-boolean-value tests |
| Spec-limits merge path's "no limits declared" check unaffected | ✅ | Re-verified during implementation: the check only fires when `min` and `max` are both absent, in which case a dangling exclusive flag is inherently the "no limits" case, not a distinguishable one — confirmed by manual trace, no code change needed |
| Exclusive flags echoed in `measurements[].limits` | ✅ | Falls out of `limits: m.limits` (a `Copy` struct); confirmed via `uv run klt yield ... --format json` on the worked example with `exclusive_min` set |
| `docs/cli/yield.md` updated (shape table + report field description) | ✅ | Both sections updated; worked example's text output regenerated and confirmed against a live run |
| `schema_version` bump confirmed unnecessary | ✅ | Re-checked `docs/json-contract.md`'s additive-field policy as of this PR; `SCHEMA_VERSION` unchanged at `1` |

## Test Plan
- `cargo test` in `native/yield/`: 63 passed (57 pre-existing + 6 new), 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt`: clean.
- `uv run pytest tests/test_yield.py`: 64 passed (55 pre-existing + 9 new), 0 failed/skipped (native extension built via `uv sync --extra dev --group yield`).
- `npm run check:ci` (ruff format/check + full repo `pytest`): lint clean; full suite 4002 passed, 79 skipped, 24 failed — all 24 failures are in `tests/test_gallery_signals.py` and `tests/test_techmap_equiv_gate.py` (a pre-existing local `cargo build` timeout for the unrelated `klt-techmap` native crate and fixture issues), confirmed pre-existing/out of scope via `git diff --stat origin/main` showing this PR touches only the 6 files listed above.
- Manual verification: ran the worked example (`examples/yield/mc-samples.json` + a copy of `spec-limits.json` with `vref.exclusive_min` set) — human-readable output showed `min(>)=1.15`, and `--format json` echoed `"exclusive_min": true` in `measurements[0].limits`.
- Edge case (both sides exclusive): covered by the Rust test `both_min_and_max_exclusive_excludes_both_boundaries`.

TDD: yes — Rust tests in `native/yield/src/estimate.rs` (e.g. `a_sample_exactly_at_an_exclusive_min_fails`) and Python tests in `tests/test_yield.py` (e.g. `test_an_exclusive_min_spec_row_excludes_a_boundary_sample`) were written alongside the `within()`/`_limits_from()` changes and verified to fail before the strict-comparison logic existed, then pass after.

Closes #1083

author: luscaswolf
body:
## Summary

Adds a **"Trust boundaries (security note)"** subsection to the Retain docs,
clarifying that the `context` string is **caller-supplied and unauthenticated**
— a disambiguation hint, not a provenance assertion — and recommending that
untrusted content be retained into a **separate bank** (bank isolation being the
reliable trust boundary).

## Motivation

Relates to #3558 (the security evaluation) and #3562 (the hardening proposal).
The `context` field is currently documented as a speaker-disambiguation feature,
but not as a trust consideration: any caller who can invoke `retain()` can
supply a misleading `context` (for example `context="security_review_note"`) for
content that did not come from that source. This documents the boundary so
integrators don't treat `context` as evidence of provenance.

## Change

- One new subsection in `hindsight-docs/docs/developer/retain.md` (docs-only, no
  code changes).
- Cross-links to the existing "Memory Defense and Source Provenance" section.

This is the docs-first step of the hardening work tracked in #3562; the code
changes (context namespacing, dedup, provenance tiering) are follow-ups.

author: johnayodele1
body:
### Root Cause
1. The Provider Studio dashboard calculated period earnings by blindly summing all positive completed `CreditTransaction` records (`amount > 0`), which incorrectly included non-earning positive transactions such as credit purchases, promo bonuses, and refunds.
2. The "Your Earnings" detailed report used `providerProfile.totalEarnings` (lifetime accumulated earnings) regardless of the selected `dateRange` parameter ("Today", "This Week", "This Month").
3. The frontend `ProviderEarnings.tsx` reverse-engineered gross earnings and platform fees using `totalEarned / 0.85` instead of referencing stored transaction accounting values.
4. Dashboard and Detailed Earnings endpoints used slightly different date boundary calculations for "This Week".

### Solution
1. Created `backend/src/shared/earnings.ts` defining canonical `PROVIDER_EARNING_TYPES` (`tip_received`, `cam_tip`, `tip`, `call_earning`, `service_payment_received`, `gift_received`, `paid_media_earning`, `paid_media_unlock`, `spin_earning`, `spin_wheel`), `getDateRangeBounds`, and `calculateProviderEarnings`.
2. Updated `getProviderDashboard` and `getProviderEarnings` in `providerOnboarding.controller.ts` to use `PROVIDER_EARNING_TYPES` and `getDateRangeBounds`. Period earnings now sum completed earning transactions within the date range, returning identical provider net totals across both endpoints.
3. Kept `providerProfile.totalEarnings` strictly as lifetime accumulated provider earnings used for withdrawable payout balance (`pendingCredits`).
4. Reused `PROVIDER_EARNING_TYPES` in `payout.controller.ts` and `admin.controller.ts`.
5. Updated `ProviderEarnings.tsx` to display `grossEarned` and `platformFee` returned from stored transaction data.
6. Expanded integration tests in `backend/src/tests/provider.earnings.test.ts` proving consistency between dashboard and detailed earnings, date boundary filtering, non-earning transaction exclusions, and platform fee calculations.

author: blysspeak
body:
# v2.0.1

Два бага, найденных в бою на живой памяти, плюс третий, вскрывшийся по дороге.

## Поиск требовал все слова сразу

Пробел между словами в FTS5 означает `AND`, поэтому `memory_search("телеграм алертов")` не находил ничего: слова «алертов» в индексе нет, есть «алерта». Пустая выдача при этом читалась как «знания нет» — то есть отправляла в разведку за тем, что в памяти уже лежало.

Слова соединяются через `OR`, порядок наводит ранжирование: сначала записи, где совпало больше слов запроса, внутри группы — по релевантности bm25. Неудачная форма слова портит порядок, а не результат. Явный оператор заглавными (`a AND b`) исполняется как написан — намерение важнее умолчания.

## Выдача была отсортирована от худшего к лучшему

`ORDER BY rank … DESC`, а `rank` в FTS5 — это bm25: отрицательное число, где меньше значит релевантнее. Самое подходящее уходило в хвост и обрезалось лимитом. Нашлось при разборе первого бага: пока выдача была AND-узкой, порядок внутри неё почти не был виден.

## «Не нашлось» и «запрос не сработал» выглядели одинаково

Состояний три, а не два, и путать их дорого:

| Что вернулось | Что это значит |
|---|---|
| нашлось | — |
| часть слов не встретилась в индексе | дело в форме слова — спроси иначе |
| ни одно слово не встретилось | знания нет — иди и выясняй |

`memory_search` возвращает `unmatched_terms` и `query_hint`, `au search` печатает строку диагноза.

## Проба валила measured на импортах по алиасу

Из текста извлекаются путеподобные токены и проверяются на диске. `@/config/env.js` превращался в `/config/env.js`, которого нет и быть не может: алиас разворачивается сборщиком (`@/*` → `src/*`), а расширение в ESM-импорте не совпадает с расширением на диске (`.js` против `.ts`). Любая запись, цитирующая импорт, была обречена провалить пробу. Токены после `@` и `~` пробами больше не становятся.

## Провал пробы больше не понижает confidence

Понижение прожило один день и успело обесценить то, ради чего вводилось: все записи одного проекта разом прочитались как `unverified`. Проба — улика слабая по устройству: путь в прозе, машина другая, репозиторий чужой. `evidence` с командой и кодом возврата — улика сильная. Слабая не имеет права перебивать сильную. Провал остаётся в `probe_warnings` как замечание, а не как приговор.

## Улики

- `cargo test --workspace` — 146 тестов зелёные; `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — чисто
- на живой базе (758 узлов): `au search "провенансов релиз"` → 7 результатов вместо нуля плюс «ни одного попадания у слов: провенансов … (попробуй прове*)»
- `au search "зурбаган лисс"` → «ни одно слово запроса не встречается в памяти — похоже, этого знания здесь просто нет»
- `memory_add` с `@/config/env.js` в тексте: `confidence: measured`, `probe_warnings: []` — против прежних `unverified` и провалившейся пробы

## Чего здесь нет

Морфология не решена. `OR` с ранжированием снимает основную боль, но «алертов» и «алерт» для индекса остаются разными словами. Trigram-токенайзер, снежковый стеммер или семантический поиск — отдельная работа с перестройкой индекса.

---

## Хвосты, найденные в бою после первого прогона

**Подсказка утверждала больше, чем знала.** На пустую выдачу по «воркеры» она отвечала «похоже, этого знания здесь просто нет» — утверждение о мире, которого у поиска на руках нет: «~20 воркеров» лежало в трёх узлах, не совпала одна словоформа. Ложное успокоение дороже молчания — читатель идёт делать заново уже сделанное. Теперь текст говорит ровно про строку поиска:

```
ни одно слово запроса не встречается в памяти в этой форме («воркеры») —
возможно, дело в словоформе: попробуй другую или короче (ворке*).
Поиск не утверждает, что знания нет, — только что совпадений по этой строке нет
```

**Ранжирование не смотрело на заголовок.** bm25 считает по всему документу, поэтому длинная сессионная запись, где слова рассыпаны по простыне, обходила запись, состоящую из этих слов почти целиком. Совпадение взвешивается по полю: `label` ×3, `claim` ×2, `note` ×1. На живой базе запрос «горячая перезагрузка флагов алерты модули» теперь ставит первой запись с этим заголовком, а не сессионные итоги.

148 тестов зелёные, clippy чист.

author: lemuelvdm
body:
### Summary of Changes

Continues the `Interpretation` extraction into the linked-view cluster. A linked admin view renders another view's list inside an edit tab; this moves its table body out of the legacy helper.

**`Architecture/LinkedView/ListBody`** + **`JoomlaThree/LinkedView/ListBody`.** Only one thing differs between Joomla targets — how the user who has an item checked out is looked up. Joomla 3 asks the global factory by id; later targets resolve a user factory from the container. That is the single extension point, so Joomla 3 is the only target with a class of its own and Joomla 4, 5 and 6 share the base.

**The four publish-state blocks now share one parameterised builder.** They were near-identical copies differing only in the published value, the sort value, the status class and the language key. Because de-duplication is exactly the kind of change that can silently alter generated output, `testThePublishStatesMatchTheLegacyMarkup` rebuilds the complete expected markup for all four states — the way the legacy helper assembled it, including the double space in `<td class="center"  data-value="1">` — and asserts the generated body contains it verbatim, for both Footable releases.

**Two seams gained interfaces:** `ListItemBuilderInterface` and `ListLinkInterface`. Both concrete classes are `final` and sit on top of dependency chains that reach into the compiler container, so a unit test cannot construct or double them. Depending on the abstraction is what lets the linked view body be built and tested in isolation, and it matches how the codebase already treats seams like `HeaderInterface`.

Also in this branch, already merged upstream and included here for context of the running total: the admin edit view body, the Footable asset loader, the edit-view custom tabs and tab layout fields, and the linked view table head.

### Testing Instructions

```
composer --working-dir=libraries/vendor_jcb/tests install
composer --working-dir=libraries/vendor_jcb/tests test
```

To confirm the publish-state de-duplication is faithful, change any one of the four state descriptors in `ListBody::getPublishStates()` and re-run — `testThePublishStatesMatchTheLegacyMarkup` fails on the exact byte.

### Expected result

The blocking suite passes.

### Actual result

2694 tests, 30255 assertions, 1 failure — `FieldCreatorTest::testFieldAsStringNormalizesBothRendererBackends`, which asserts libxml emits `type="text" />` with a space. It reproduces unchanged on `6.x` without this branch and is a libxml build difference in the local runtime, not a regression from these changes. `git diff --check`, `check-php-style.php` and `check-test-ownership.php` are all clean over the change range.

### Documentation Changes Required

None beyond what is already in `docs/architecture/system-map.md` — this branch follows the target-class rule documented there, and adds no new pattern.

author: thomas-geraghty
body:
## 0.4.0

A tidy-up of the authoring surface - the GOV.UK utility wrappers are real components
now, `createForgePackage()` is mandatory and stamps provenance on every node so errors
point at the line in your code that defined the offending definition, and everything
the engine throws is one exported family of `Forge*` error classes with author-first
stack rendering. The code generator is reworked on top of a typed IR too - compiled
functions now read like hand-written JavaScript, runtime errors point straight back at
the line in your journey definition, and you can even drop breakpoints in your
definitions and step through them. Steps can also ask the same question in more than
one place now - same-code field copies gated by `dependentWhen` behave as one field,
with error summary links that land on the right copy.

### Added

- The `Forge*` error classes are exported from core - catch and narrow with
  `instanceof`, and a single `instanceof ForgeBaseError` check answers "did Forge
  throw this" ([#229])
- `ForgeAuthoringError` for authoring API misuse caught while builders are still
  assembling the definition, and `ForgeInternalError` for states the engine should
  make impossible - seeing one is a bug in Forge ([#229])
- `Defined at:` lines on every author-facing error, pointing at the builder call that
  defined the offending node ([#209], [#210])
- List items can be blocks - `GovUKList` items may mix strings with child blocks, and
  each block renders inside its own `<li>` ([#203])
- `Format()` takes a resolvable template - a reference or any string-valued expression
  works: `Format(Answer('template'), ...)` ([#210])
- Source maps on every compiled function - a runtime error's stack lands on the line
  in your journey definition that defined the failing node, not in generated code,
  and the published package ships its sources so the maps resolve inside consuming
  apps ([#247])
- Breakpoints in your journey definitions - set one on a builder call and the
  debugger stops there when the compiled function evaluates it. Still a bit rough
  around the edges ([#247])
- Compiled functions are their own scripts in debugger panels - named
  `forge:compiled/<phase>/<journey>.<step>...js` and content-fingerprinted, so an IDE
  never reuses stale generated source after reconnecting to a restarted process
  ([#247])
- Same-code field variants - one question can appear as several copies on a step,
  each nested under a different parent option via `dependentWhen`. The first active
  copy in declaration order owns preparation, formatters, parsers, defaults and
  validation; when no copy is active the answer clears once. Duplicate literal field
  codes without `dependentWhen` on every copy are rejected at registration ([#248])
- `errorAnchor` on field components - a component whose rendered control ids can
  differ from the field code declares where an error summary link should land
  (`errorAnchor: props => props.idPrefix ?? props.code`), and the engine falls back
  to the field code when it's not declared. `fieldValidationErrors` entries carry the
  failing instance's `anchor`, and `getErrorSummaryList` links it over `blockCode`
  ([#248])

### Changed

- The GOV.UK utility wrappers are real registered components written in the
  experimental JSX API - `GovUKList`'s `type` prop is now `style`, and the standalone
  `GovUK*Props` interfaces are gone ([#203])
- `createForgePackage()` is mandatory - registration rejects anything that hasn't
  passed through it, and `journey` also accepts a JSON string ([#209])
- The engine's errors follow one `Forge`-prefixed naming scheme on a shared
  `ForgeBaseError` base class ([#229])
- A failure thrown by one of your functions during a request surfaces as a
  `ForgeRuntimeEvaluationError` with your error untouched on `cause` - previously
  forge appended its diagnostics prose to your error's own `stack`. The wrapper's
  message carries yours (`Failed to evaluate compiled Forge hooks function: <yours>`)
  and HTTP `status`/`statusCode` are mirrored from the cause, so express error
  handling picks the same response code. Breaking only if a host error handler
  matched on the thrown instance - match on `error.cause` instead ([#247])
- Runtime error stacks read author-first - your frames render as-is, each run of
  forge-internal frames folds to one summary line (`FORGE_FULL_STACK=1` expands it,
  and the unfolded original stays on a non-enumerable `rawStack`), the definition
  site renders as `at [defined]` frames that error trackers ingest as clickable
  in-app frames, and the `Node:` row is gone from the diagnostics block (`nodeId`
  stays on the error object) ([#247])
- The runtime `definedAt` is a chain now, and callsite capture is deeper (15 frames,
  up from 5) - if you wrap forge builders in your own utilities, the chain reads past
  the wrapper file to the line in your code ([#247])
- `core/framework` is types-only - the path utilities are no longer exported, so copy
  the ones you used into your adapter; they're a few lines each ([#212])
- Generated code reads like hand-written JavaScript - blocks, validation rules, and
  hooks compile to named function units, static route metadata and field inventories
  are plain literals, reachability cascades are labelled if/else chains, and every
  generated function opens with a header saying what it does and when it runs ([#247])
- Generated hook functions are only `async` when their bodies actually await ([#247])

### Removed

- The field-level `multiple` flag - it overlapped with the flag that array-shaped
  components like checkboxes already declare on their registry entry, so keeping every
  posted value is solely the component's decision now. Setting `multiple` on a field
  block is a type error; just remove it ([#206])
- The expression builder classes and the granular condition variant types from the
  authoring exports - the factories (`Conditional()`, `Match()`, ...) were always the
  intended surface, and `ConditionalExpr` covers the variant types.
  `PredicateTestExprBuilder` is deleted outright; it was dead code ([#208])
- Error codes and the error `toString()` implementations - the class is the
  discriminator now ([#229])

### Fixed

- Sharing a partially built `Conditional()`/`Match()` chain no longer
  cross-contaminates - each chain step returns a fresh builder ([#208])
- Builders are detected by a `nodeKind` marker instead of `'build' in value`
  duck-typing, so an authored object that happens to have a `build` property can't be
  mistaken for a builder and swallowed during finalisation ([#209])
- The two validation rules missing the `formattedPath` fallback now default it to
  `unknown` like the rest ([#210])
- The deprecated `defineFunction` helpers never stamped callsites on the handles they
  build, so their errors lacked a `Defined at` line - they stamp now ([#210])
- Error summary links land on the rendered control when a GOV.UK field has a custom
  `id` or `idPrefix` - previously the link was always `#<code>`, which matched
  nothing. Date inputs link to their first inner input (`#<id>-day`) instead of the
  wrapper id no element carries ([#248])

### Details

#### GOV.UK wrappers as real components

Previously `GovUKBody`, `GovUKHeading`, `GovUKList`, `GovUKGridRow`,
`GovUKSectionBreak` and `GovUKButtonGroup` were authoring functions that expanded into
generic `html`/`template` blocks. They now register and render like every other
component, with their renders written in the experimental JSX API. Builder names and
props are unchanged, with one exception: `GovUKList`'s `type` prop is now `style`
(`type` is the engine's structure discriminator on real components). The standalone
`GovUK*Props` interfaces are gone - each component's single interface (`GovUKBody`,
`GovUKList`, ...) is both the props and the block type. If you registe

author: tamarawguy
body:
Onboarding doc for anyone handed the repository link.

## Sections

| Section | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Getting it running | `blade server init` → deploy → `/web/devcon/home` |
| What is here | The three client extensions, the site tree, the object model |
| Build log | One entry per PR (#1–#7): what was built and why |
| Things that cost us time | The dead ends, with the actual error messages |
| How to change things | The three-way sync between git, artifacts, and the database |

## Why the pitfalls section is the longest

None of those are documented where you would look for them, and several are
actively contradicted by the reference cards in `.workspace-rules/rules/`. The
ones most likely to catch the next person:

- **`BUILD SUCCESSFUL` only means a file was copied.** It does not mean the
  extension works, its assets are present, or provisioning ran — and a deploy
  against a *stopped* Tomcat is a silent no-op that looks identical to success.
- **`assemble` is project scoped, not entry scoped**, and whether it's needed
  differs per CET type (`globalCSS` yes, `batch` yes, `siteInitializer` no).
  Nested inside an entry it is ignored with no error.
- **A wrong password reads as a broken auth verifier** — `403` with an empty
  `{ }` body on every `/o/` endpoint.
- **Feature-gated endpoints fail with `400`**, and `openapi.json` returns `200`
  either way, so `/o/api` cannot tell you whether a flag is on.
- **Optional references must be absent, not empty** — an unlinked relationship
  exports as `""` and cannot be re-imported.

Each is recorded with the error text that actually appeared, so it's greppable
when someone hits it again.

## Note on accuracy

Everything factual was checked against the running portal rather than the
reference cards — endpoint paths, identifier types per module, field types, and
which CET types need `assemble`. Where a card is wrong, the README says so and
points at Liferay's own code in `liferay-portal/workspaces/`.

body: Port Namco Pole Position and Pole Position II for dsp-cpp. ## Screenshots Attract mode after the Z80 ↔ Z8002 handshake (nearest-neighbour 3×). **Pole Position** — Fuji Speedway map and in-game attract: **Pole Position II** — title billboard and start grid: ## Hardware - New unsegmented Z8002 CPU (`dsp::z8002_device`) from MAME `z8000` - Z80 + dual Z8002 at 3.072 MHz, 256×224, ~60.6 Hz - Shared 16-bit video RAM (sprites, road, alpha, view) with Z80 seeing low bytes - LS259 latch, scanline IRQs, Pole Position II IC25 multiply - Z8002 NVI only latches on a line change, matching MAME `execute_set_input` - Z8002 register file uses MAME's little-endian overlay (byte/word/long XOR 7/3/1) so RH/RL, RR, and MULT/DIV agree - PP2 `pp4_7`/`pp4_8` load into Z8002#2 at `$4000`; Z8002#1 `$4000–$5fff` is IC25 ## Audio and I/O - Fujitsu MB88xx core (MB8843/MB8844) - Real Namco 51xx MCU for coins/DIPs/start - Real Namco 53xx MCU for steering + DSWA (replaces the high-level stub) - Namco 52xx/54xx MCUs driving 4-bit DACs - Pole Position WSG (8 voices, wavetable PROM `pp1-5.3b`) with 52/54 mux - Engine sample player with the three analog filters from MAME `audio/polepos.cpp` - 06xx pulses chip-select/IRQ into all four custom MCUs Attract after IOSEL/CLSON: 51xx and 53xx PCs leave reset on both games and the mixed audio path is non-silent. Pole Position II now passes the IC25 `MULT RR0` check, completes the `$4048` mailbox handshake, and releases Z8002#2. ## ROMs Use MAME 0.221 merged parents `polepos` / `polepos2` from https://archive.org/download/mame-0.221-roms-merged The 51xx–54xx MCU dumps (`namco51.zip` … `namco54.zip`) come from that same archive. The driver loads them from next to the game zip, from `/tmp/roms`, or downloads them if they are missing. ``` ./build/dsp --game polepos /path/to/polepos.zip ./build/dsp --game polepos2 /path/to/polepos2.zip ```

body:
Operator review of v1 reshaped the feature in three ways:

**Parley is the channel.** The standalone treaty action is gone; a `treaty` field rides a parley message. A proposal is a real message that announces itself in the transcript with signing instructions; signatures and dissolutions land there too — negotiation and ink in one place.

**Two typed pacts.** `non_aggression`: broken only when one side **sinks** the other's ship (ships fire automatically on adjacency, so v1's damage trigger made every pact a time bomb — the hook moved to the combat-sink path). `border`: an agreed x/y line, each side keeping its own coordinates — broken only when a signer **sees** the other's ship beyond it, at the fresh-sighting moment in `_update_contacts`. Fog applies: an unseen crossing is deniable. Guards: a border a flagship already violates is refused; `contact_ttl=0` matches refuse borders outright.

**Tiles instead of the link line.** The flagship link line covered the board. Standing pacts now render as tiles at the top of the Parley panel (parties, type, conditions), and an active border treaty draws its agreed line on the chart — dashed, dim, the one treaty visual that is the treaty. Vocabulary is type-aware everywhere; `fx.treaty/treatyEnd` groups are gone; audio keeps treaty slots via `AUDIO_KIND_CFG`.

`tests/test_treaties.py` rewritten: 24 assertions including damage-does-not-break, sighted vs unseen crossings, and the flagship-side guard. Golden manifest regenerated (the rules briefing changed).
