author: tatemeyer
body:
**Arc 2, Phase 1.** A phone scans the TV's QR, trades a one-time code for a per-person token, and its heartbeats keep that person on the roster. Events can finally say *who*.

Rust tests **75 → 132**. Gate green.

## What landed

- `store.rs` → a `store/` module (`mod`/`events`/`people`) — the split #9 flagged and `CLAUDE.md` now permits
- `people` gains `token` and `joined_ms`, migrated in place for an existing Arc 1 database
- One-time join codes, in memory only, rotating every 60s with a 15s grace window
- `GET /api/join/qr.svg`, `POST /api/join`, `GET /api/me`, `POST /api/heartbeat`
- A bearer-token extractor applied *only* where an action needs an actor — reads stay open and `POST /api/events` stays the open ingest port
- `Presence`, feeding Arc 1's existing `Roster` projection

## Decisions worth a look

**Presence reuses `Roster` rather than inventing a second roster.** Phones heartbeat; SESH records `presence.arrived`/`presence.left` on **transitions only**, so a phone beating all evening leaves two rows, not hundreds. When BLE lands later it becomes a second producer of the same two kinds and nothing downstream changes.

**Presence is seeded from the rebuilt roster at startup.** Without this, every restart — every config reload, every crash under `Restart=always`, every power cut — would append a `presence.arrived` for someone who never left. The log is append-only, so each one is permanent. That is the exact shape of the Arc 1 dangling-launch bug, caught before it could happen.

**`Room` grew delegating people methods instead of exposing its `Store`.** Handing out the store would put `append` within reach of every caller and quietly retire the "`Room::record` is the only write path" invariant.

**`Person` has no `token` field at all.** Not omitted from responses — unreachable. It is the type handed to handlers and serialized to clients, and a test asserts the token never appears in the log, which is append-only and served unauthenticated, so a leak there could not be walked back.

**The name is validated before the code is spent**, so a typo doesn't cost a guest their scan and send them back to the TV.

## Dependencies: two, both justified

- `getrandom = "0.2"` — already in the lockfile transitively, so this adds **no** compiled code. `rand` would pull a whole PRNG stack to fill sixteen bytes.
- `qrcode` — renders the QR server-side. A JS QR library would be the first runtime dependency in a deliberately framework-free surface, and the kiosk has no CDN.

## Verified on the Pi

Real binary, spare port, throwaway database — the live log was never touched. Full record in `docs/arc2-phase1-verification.md`.

The QR was **decoded from the served SVG with `zbarimg`** — the same bytes a camera reads. That check earns its keep: the join URL is the one thing unit tests cannot cover, because the TV fetches the QR over `127.0.0.1` and a QR built from the `Host` header would send every phone to its own loopback. It decoded to `http://192.168.40.195:7474/join?c=…`, the Pi's Ethernet address.

Reused code → `403`. Bad token → `401`. Repeat heartbeat → no new events. Restart → roster rebuilt, token still valid, **no spurious arrival**.

```
 1  person.joined      actors=["marcus"]  {"name":"Marcus"}
 2  presence.arrived   actors=["marcus"]  {}
```

## One amendment, flagged rather than quietly reinterpreted

Phase 1's Definition of Done asked for verification "with a real phone camera". That depended on Phase 5 — the join screen and the on-TV QR live there, and there is no `/join` page for a camera to land on yet. The camera check moves to Phase 5 where it tests the screens; everything else was verified as written. Noted in the plan.

author: curiousjc
body:
Two changes that rhyme: one narrows a grammar that had grown three jobs, and the other writes the grammar the last collected thing never had. The first is code and is measured; the second is design only and builds nothing.

## A combo is a damage multiplier and nothing else

A combo used to be a **hand** counting copies of a card, crossed with a **mix** counting distinct colours, plus a reward vocabulary that could bank action points or take actions off the opponent's next turn. It is now one number.

The ladder wears poker's names because it asks poker's question — High Card, Pair, Two Pair, Three of a Kind, Full House, Four of a Kind. IDs renumbered 1–6 in ladder order, safe because no profile exists yet to have recorded the old ones; **multipliers carried through unchanged**, so the size of the hole is readable before anything is retuned.

Three fields left `data/combos.json`:

- **`mixes`** — colour now buys *statuses* and no damage at all. `Blow.Elements` and the attacker's ring decide what lands, exactly as before.
- **`effect`** — nothing a hand forms buys anything but damage. `StaggerAll` and `BankAP` went with it, unused by any shipped combo.
- **`scope`** — `formsBlow` already decided this more narrowly (it also excludes recoil), so the field could never change what was counted and only invited an entry to claim otherwise.

**Stagger goes as a word and as a second mechanic.** `Duelist.Staggered` was deleted rather than renamed: with combos no longer granting one, nothing wrote it, so a chill reads straight off the Ice status. `KindStaggered` → `KindChilled`. `flightStaggerPer` is untouched — that is animation delay-offsetting, a different word entirely.

### Measured, both sides

`tools/balance` against a worktree at the previous commit: **74 walls out of 96 becomes 84.** Every one of the ten is a hand posture — `trips` lost eleven wins, `cheap-trips` five, and the four coloured postures lost none. **The stolen action was doing the work, not the colour multiplier**, which flipped no outcome in the sample at all. Worth knowing before retuning, since it points at the hand ladder rather than at the elements.

## Rings get a grammar

Designed in full, **built not at all**. `MECHANICS.md` carries the argument, `.claude/skills/rings/SKILL.md` the vocabulary, `TODO.md` a six-step build order.

A ring needs three parts where the card language needs two, because **a ring is the only collected thing that is never played** — it has to say when it wakes up. `When` / `If` / `Then`, and a ring holds a *list* of rules rather than one, forced by a stat ring that accumulates at one moment and applies at another.

**Seven moments, and only four are in `internal/combat`.** The rest fire in `session` and on the post-battle screen, which is what makes a ring a *run* concept the rules consult rather than a combat one — so `rings.json` will be parsed in `internal/session`, beside the worms and for the same reason. `Card.Cost`, `Card.Damage` and `Card.Amount` are already methods on the card from the worm work, so three of the four combat seats are a line each.

**Statuses become their own collection** and stop being the same thing as an element — what a lightning ring applying two statuses forces. This holds the 2026-08-16 position rather than reversing it: statuses being free is what left rings with nothing to be. It re-indexes `Duelist.Statuses` from element to status, moves `effectKeys` with it, and puts `cards.MaxEffects` in question, since it is 4 *because* there are four elements.

**Vitae gains propagation** — +1 per 5 held after a fight, capped at +5 — because the Banker ring scales it, and a ring may only bend a rule the game already has.

## Left open, deliberately

Two decisions, each blocking one ring, recorded where they bite:

- Whether propagation's +5 cap binds **Banker** as well. Absolute means the ring is dead past 25 held.
- Which effect a **growing ring's** accumulator feeds when the ring holds more than one.

## Also

`CLAUDE.md` gains a **skill index** — one table of every skill and what trips it, above the sections explaining why each exists, so a skill is not missed by nobody having read to the bottom of a long file. A new skill is a row in it.

Seed and posture names lost their combo vocabulary: `strike-flurry` and `strike-barrage` named hands that no longer exist under those names, so they say what they deal — `three-strikes`, `four-strikes`, `three-smashes`. All five catalogue entries re-checked with `tools/seeds`.

## Checks

`gofmt -l .` silent; `go vet`, `go build` and `go test` green under plain, `debugtrace`, `idleexit` and `demoplay`. Scripted demo run and read.

author: alexandriax
body:
Follow-up to #40, working through the field report: desktop switching apparently dead, show desktop flaky, the pointed wiggle firing clicks, thumb signals near-inert.

## Root causes found

**Desktop left/right.** The action layer itself works — verified live with `--action-eval desktopRight/Left` on this machine (SkyLight switch + verification both fine). Two real problems around it:
1. The space ring from `SLSCopyManagedDisplaySpaces` mixes user desktops with **full-screen app spaces**. Stepping blindly, "desktop right" could land on someone's full-screen window — which looks exactly like "selecting or doing something with different windows". `neighborDesktop` (pure, selftest-covered) now skips full-screen spaces both ways and exits from one to the nearest desktop.
2. The gestures bound to it mostly never fired (below) — and misdetections clicked around instead.

**Thumb signals.** The natural thumbs-up faces its knuckles at the camera. Foreshortening projects the curled chains as straight lines, the angle-band `isFist` never matches, and engagement almost never happened. The fist is now also read by its collapsed fingertips (`isClosedHand`: openness ≤ 0.15, thumb excluded) — a read no orientation can fake — on both engage and hold sides. Show desktop's flakiness falls out of the same fix: the bound hold either didn't fire or fired twice across a refractory (fn+F11 toggles, so the second fire "undoes" the first).

**Pointed wiggle vs. click.** Off-beat drumming swings the index-vs-middle tap differential exactly like a deep index dip. The engine now keeps a debounced pointed-pose park: while your hand is pointed at the screen (tips below the knuckle line), the cursor holds still and neither button may engage — presses already down still drag and release. Clicks are again something only an upright open hand can produce. The pointed pose also stands the hold family down (its collapsed tips + sideways thumb read as a phantom thumbs-left otherwise).

## New: hold countdown in the pill

Any hold-for-a-beat gesture (thumb signals, shaka) now paints a live countdown into the pill from the moment it engages — `🐾 Thumbs up · hold… 0.2 s` — refreshed per frame, cleared when the pose is dropped, replaced by the fire confirmation at zero. Holding is finally visible.

## Testing

- `swift test`: 468 tests, 0 failures (new: knuckles-on thumb signal engages, pointed hand can't phantom a thumb signal, drumming never clicks and parks the cursor, raised hand recovers the cursor, hold progress counts down and clears).
- `make app` + `--selftest`: 98 checks OK (new `spaces.*` picker rows).
- `--action-eval desktopRight/desktopLeft/showDesktop` run live on macOS 26: all switch/toggle correctly, round-trip verified against the actual space ids.

author: daniel812
body:
## Summary
- The service worker (`public/sw.js`) cached `index.html` on install and served that exact copy forever, with no revalidation. After a new deploy changes Vite's content-hashed asset filenames, the frozen shell kept pointing at now-deleted files, producing a blank page on normal load/refresh — only a hard refresh (which bypasses the service worker) picked up the current build.
- The app shell (`/`, `/index.html`) is now **network-first**: every load fetches the latest build from the network and only falls back to the cached copy when actually offline, which is what fixes the reported bug while preserving offline/PWA use on your phone.
- Content-hashed build assets (`assets/index-<hash>.js/css`) stay **cache-first** — safe since identical filenames always mean identical content.
- Added an `activate` handler that purges old cache versions, plus `skipWaiting()`/`clients.claim()` so an updated service worker takes over immediately.
- Excluded `/api/*` and cross-origin requests (Supabase, Telegram, Gemini) from service worker handling entirely — those always hit the network live.
- Added matching `Cache-Control` headers to the Express static server (`server.ts`) as defense in depth for any self-hosted deployment path.

## Test plan
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` passes
- [x] `vite build` succeeds; confirmed Vite emits content-hashed asset filenames (`assets/index-<hash>.js/css`), matching the assumption the cache-first strategy relies on
- [x] Confirmed `sw.js`/`manifest.json` are still copied into `dist/` correctly
- [ ] Please verify on your phone: install/open the PWA, confirm it still works offline, and confirm a normal reload after a new deploy no longer requires a hard refresh

## Note
While testing the production Express path I found a pre-existing, unrelated bug: `app.get('*', ...)` in `server.ts` crashes at startup under Express 5 (`path-to-regexp` no longer accepts a bare `'*'`). It's dormant today because the app is deployed on Vercel, which handles SPA fallback via `vercel.json` rewrites rather than `server.ts` — so it only matters if `npm start` is ever used to self-host. Not fixed here since it's out of scope for this change; flagging separately.

author: casey-allard
body:
## What

Implements #655-D1 per `docs/serving_release_packaging_655_d.md` (D0,
PR #774): a pure, additive helper that builds a `ReleaseBundleManifest`
by digesting an already-compiled R4G1 bundle's real files on disk. No
filesystem write yet, no compile/cover/score stage run or routed
through -- it only reads files the existing CLI pipeline already
produces.

## Why

C1c (PR #773) added a loader that verifies an optional
`release-bundle.json` sidecar, but nothing produces that sidecar yet.
D0 mapped the real bundle layout against `ReleaseBundleManifest`'s
fields; D1 is the first slice that turns that mapping into working code,
without yet wiring it to any CLI surface (that's D2).

## What it does

`package_release_bundle(physical_root, inputs) -> Result<ReleaseBundleManifest, PackageBundleError>`
blake3-hashes `graph/score.r4g1`, `tless_artifacts.bin`, `tokenizer.bin`
(optional), `graph/score_report.json`, and `graph-cover/cover_report.json`
(the `compile_report` mapping D0 decided), fills `abi` from
`AbiVersion::current()`, and takes `model_id`/`capability`/`uor_matmul`/
`tokenizer_adapter`/`provenance_note` as caller-supplied input via
`PackageInputs` -- confirmed via follow-up research this session that
none of those five fields has an on-disk producer in `physical_root`
(notably `tokenizer_adapter`: a bundle's `tokenizer.bin` is a different
format from the HF `tokenizer.json` a `TokenizerAdapter` is derived from,
and deriving one needs the original HF source snapshot, never present in
a compiled bundle directory). The result is validated before returning
-- `Ok` never carries a structurally invalid manifest.

## Why the `#![allow(dead_code)]`

Nothing calls `package_release_bundle` outside its own tests yet (D2 is
the CLI subcommand that will). Every item in the module is therefore
unreachable from any live root in a non-test build, which clippy
correctly flags -- confirmed empirically (12 `-D warnings` errors without
the allow, one per item, since dead-code reachability doesn't propagate
through an already-dead caller). A single module-level allow with a
comment was more honest than a dozen per-item ones. This mirrors how
`release_bundle.rs` (#655-C0) and `release_bundle_loader.rs` (#655-C1c)
each landed before their own consumer existed.

## Verification

Full ladder run locally in the worktree, all green: `cargo fmt --all --
--check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --
-D warnings`, `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p
uor-r4-wasm-router --lib`, `cargo test --workspace` (zero failures).
8 unit tests (full bundle, absent optional tokenizer, each of the four
required files missing individually, invalid caller input, and
`InstructionChat` capability correctly rejected without a real tokenizer
adapter). One additional `#[ignore]`d, environment-gated test
(`UOR_R4_RELEASE_BUNDLE_PATH`, mirrors `crates/uor-r4-api/tests/api.rs`'s
own `UOR_R4_API_E2E_SOURCE` convention) run manually against the real
local bundle at `.uor-models/compiled/smollm2-135m-instruct/` -- passed,
confirming this isn't just synthetic-fixture-shaped code.

`just vv-register` was not runnable in this environment (`just` not
installed) -- same documented gap as PR #773; CI's own register
conformance job covers it.

## Next

Follow-up PR: D2 (a thin CLI subcommand that calls this helper and
writes `release-bundle.json` next to `physical_root`), then D3 (a golden
test confirming C1c's `verify_release_bundle_sidecar` returns `Some`
end-to-end against a real packaged bundle).

author: rianjs
body:
## Summary

Implements issue #39: a resumable, account-bound native “Last.fm importer” window that snapshots complete Last.fm history page-by-page, matches it to Spotify, and supports durable review before applying content, historical counts, metadata, timestamps, exclusions, fuzzy resolution, and partial/Accept All progress.

Highlights:
- Fixed `user.getRecentTracks` snapshot boundary, sequential checkpointing, compact source variants, retry/resume, account binding, quarantine, atomic persistence, and 100 MB guard.
- Independent persisted content/history intents, whole-album versus selected-track semantics, target-scoped fuzzy count modes, search-term preference, and exact album/track entity counting.
- Shared Spotify client/request gate and extracted reusable save operations; whole-album writes send only the album URI, while selected-track writes send only track URIs.
- Three-region importer UI with download/matching progress, queue sorting/status, accessible dialogs and pickers, fuzzy disclosure, exclusion/ignore/skip decisions, durable page advancement, light/dark themes, resize support, and Last.fm attribution.
- Updated owning architecture documentation for library, Spotify, persistence, and the importer boundary.

The approved plan was posted to [issue #39](https://github.com/open-cli-collective/Retune/issues/39). Closes #39.

## Architecture and safety

- Retune core remains deterministic; importer session state lives in the desktop boundary at `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lastfm_import.rs`.
- Session state is persisted atomically at `lastfm-import.json`, owner-only on Unix, bound to both Last.fm username and Spotify account ID, and excluded from normal backup/restore.
- Raw Last.fm responses are not retained. Page checkpoints persist compact aggregates, unique page source IDs, matching/decisions/options, next-page state, retryable errors, and session-level preferences.
- Spotify requests use the existing shared client/request gate. Membership-critical operations are gated without monopolizing the gate during long matching searches.
- Local counts, timestamps, ratings, and genres are applied only after successful upstream membership writes and through one atomic local mutation.

## Automated evidence

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo test --workspace`: passed; desktop 314 passed/1 ignored, Spotify 55 passed, retune-core 27 passed, audio suites 4 + 6 + 3 passed, doc tests 0.
- Focused Last.fm importer suite: 23 passed, 0 failed.
- `npm test`: 42 passed, 0 failed.
- `npm run lint`: exit 0; seven existing exhaustive-deps warnings outside the importer.
- `npx tsc -b`: passed with no errors.
- `npm run build`: passed.
- Documentation checks: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Pre-merge empirical gate

No native app was launched and no connected Spotify or Last.fm state was mutated in this phase. Root owns the remaining live gate: exhaustive control-by-control comparison with the always-open Edge design mock; app-data/export backup and restore checks; account and per-URI membership baseline; real single-track and whole-album tests; live Accept All/cancel verification; cleanup and restoration; and confirmation that Last.fm scrobbles were not polluted.

author: chrislawcodes
body:
## What changed and why

[#687](https://github.com/chrislawcodes/hoard-hurt-help/pull/687) removed the `static.rules` key from the agent turn payload, because the rulebook was being sent twice every turn — once as `rules`, and again inside `base_prompt`.

That key was also the **only** production caller of the "fat" rules text (the game rules plus the connector's JSON response protocol). So since #687 merged, that whole second builder has been unreachable except from tests. This PR deletes it, leaving exactly one rules-text builder.

### Removed

| Symbol | Where |
|---|---|
| `GameModule.rules_text` | `app/games/base.py` (protocol) |
| `GameModule.rules_text_for_match` | `app/games/base.py` (protocol) |
| `BaseGameModule.rules_text` | `app/games/base.py` (raising default) |
| `BaseGameModule.rules_text_for_match` | `app/games/base.py` (wrapper) |
| `HoardHurtHelp.rules_text` / `.rules_text_for_match` | `app/games/hoard_hurt_help/game.py` |
| `make_rules_text` | `app/games/hoard_hurt_help/rules.py` |
| `RULES_TEXT` constant | `app/games/hoard_hurt_help/rules.py` |
| `LiarsDice.rules_text` | `app/games/liars_dice/game.py` |
| `make_rules_text` | `app/games/liars_dice/rules_text.py` |

### Kept — this is now the one rules text

`semantic_rules_text` / `semantic_rules_text_for_match` / `make_game_rules_text` / `GAME_RULES_TEXT`. It is what `agent_base_prompt` embeds and what the MCP path serves through `get_instructions`.

### Checked before removing

Swept `app/`, `mcp_server/`, `scripts/`, `tests/`, plus templates and dynamic `getattr` lookups. Every remaining caller was a test. The three live rules paths all read the survivor:

- `app/engine/agent_play_reads.py:229` → `agent_base_prompt_for_match` (HTTP turn payload)
- `app/routes/web_games_catalog.py:103` → `agent_base_prompt` (public agent-instructions page)
- `mcp_server/mcp_tools.py:142` → `semantic_rules_text_for_match` (MCP `get_instructions`)

## Proof this changes nothing an agent sees

Hashed the agent-facing text on this branch and on `main`, for **both** games. All six match byte-for-byte:

| Game | Surface | SHA-256 (first 16) | Length |
|---|---|---|---|
| hoard-hurt-help | `semantic_rules_text_for_match` | `6d1644a792aa76f7` | 2132 |
| hoard-hurt-help | `agent_base_prompt_for_match` | `a50a4ef7173253e8` | 3030 |
| hoard-hurt-help | `agent_base_prompt` (bare) | `7e2bf54b6988758a` | 3024 |
| liars-dice | `semantic_rules_text_for_match` | `bdf3a55be85d7532` | 3405 |
| liars-dice | `agent_base_prompt_for_match` | `3f19840f095d8c4a` | 3953 |
| liars-dice | `agent_base_prompt` (bare) | `d5c171061cb51bb2` | 3944 |

## Tests — rewritten, not deleted

Every test that named a removed symbol was pointed at the survivor. Two got genuinely stronger:

**`tests/test_end_to_end.py`** — the static-prefix test read:

```python
snapshot = RULES_TEXT
assert RULES_TEXT is snapshot   # same object, no rebinding
```

That compares a name to itself one line after assigning it. No code change could ever fail it. It now builds the prefix the serving path actually sends and pins that two builds come out byte-identical — which is the thing that matters, since prompt caching keys on that prefix.

**`tests/test_mutual_help_modes.py`** — `test_rules_text_for_match_off_drops_decay` checked the mode-to-text mapping through `rules_text_for_match`. Repointing it at `semantic_rules_text_for_match` would have made it an exact copy of the test directly above it. Instead it now covers the **count-based** entry point — the no-Match-row path the public `/agent-instructions` page renders, which no other test in that file reached.

**`tests/test_rules_single_source.py`** — dropped to the two surfaces that remain. Its module docstring described the deleted `static.rules` key, so that was corrected too.

Also: `tests/test_game_registry.py` and `tests/test_liars_dice_rules_text.py` now assert against `semantic_rules_text`, and the two stub games (`test_stub_game.py`, `test_hidden_state_isolation.py`) implement `semantic_rules_text`.

### Mutation-verified

Both rewrites were checked against a deliberately broken build, then reverted:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Made `make_agent_base_prompt` vary between calls | ✅ `test_static_prefix_is_byte_identical_across_builds` failed |
| Dropped the `mode=` argument in `HoardHurtHelp.semantic_rules_text` | ✅ `test_count_based_rules_text_off_drops_decay` failed |

## Docs

`docs/writing-a-game-module.md` told anyone adding a new game to implement `rules_text()` — a hook nothing would have called. Fixed, along with two stale mentions in `docs/platform/AGENT_LUDUM_ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## The fail-quiet this removal exposed — fixed here too

Deleting `rules_text` uncovered a bug one layer down.

`BaseGameModule.semantic_rules_text` returned `""` when a game didn't override it. That was fine while `rules_text` was the loud one — it raised `NotImplementedError`, so a game with no rules text failed at the door.

With `rules_text` gone, that empty string sat on the **only** remaining rules path. A future game module that forgot its rules would have:

- served a **blank rulebook** over MCP `get_instructions`, and
- embedded a blank one in `base_prompt`,

with nothing raising, nothing logging, and the agent simply told nothing about the game it was playing.

It now raises, matching the sibling hooks in `BaseGameModule` that already fail loud for exactly this reason — `action_names`, `default_move`, `next_actor`, `build_replay_view`, `viewer_fragment`.

**Blast radius is zero.** The full suite passed unchanged the moment the raise went in, so no stub and no module ever relied on that empty string. It was latent risk, never exercised.

That also meant nothing pinned the new behaviour, so `tests/test_rules_single_source.py` gains a guard: it builds a rules-free `BaseGameModule` subclass and asserts **both** entry points raise — the bare one and the `_for_match` wrapper that real serving actually goes through.

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Restored `return ""` in `BaseGameModule.semantic_rules_text` | ✅ `test_a_game_that_supplies_no_rules_fails_loud` failed |

Worth flagging: none of the five sibling fail-loud hooks has a test of its own. This is the first.

## Validation

Full Preflight Gate, run from the repo root after rebasing onto `origin/main` (`0ecdb147`):

```
python3 -m ruff check .        → All checks passed!
mypy app/ mcp_server/          → Success: no issues found in 211 source files
pytest -q                      → 1886 passed, 570 warnings in 17.81s
```

Not the small-change lane — this touches the `GameModule` protocol and both game modules — so the full suite ran, not the fast lane.

Diff: **−81 lines of production code** (`app/`: 18 added, 99 removed). Tests are net +43 — two rewritten tests gained real assertions, and the fail-loud guard is new.

author: rbuergi
body:
## Measured first

On a live **33-partition** database, before any change:

| trigger | present | missing |
|---|---|---|
| `mesh_node_notify` on `mesh_nodes` | **1** | **32** |
| `*_notify` on satellite tables | 231 | 0 |
| `mesh_node_copy_to_history` | 33 | 0 |

The **one** schema carrying `mesh_node_notify` is `public` — which AGENTS.md documents as **empty by design**. So in practice **no node write in that database had ever emitted `pg_notify`.**

## Root cause

Three schema scripts created the trigger like this:

```sql
IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_trigger WHERE tgname = 'mesh_node_notify')
```

`pg_trigger` is a **database-global** catalog; trigger names are unique **per table**. The first schema provisioned therefore satisfied the predicate for the entire database, and every schema created afterwards silently skipped installing its own. Nothing failed — each schema concluded the work was already done, because somewhere else it was.

This is the **identical** defect [V44](../blob/main/memex/aspire/Memex.Database.Migration/Migrations/V44_FixMeshNodeHistoryTriggerPerSchema.cs) repaired for the sibling trigger `mesh_node_copy_to_history` — in one of the same methods (`GetVersionedPartitionDdl`). That repair fixed one trigger and left its neighbour.

## Why it stayed hidden

Two independent reasons, which is why it lasted:

- **Satellites were never affected.** `GetSatelliteTableScript` always used the per-table form, so a partition's `_Access` / `_Thread` / `_Activity` writes notified while that *same partition's* `mesh_nodes` writes did not. The asymmetry makes the symptom look selective rather than systemic.
- **The in-process `IStorageAdapter.Changes` feed still carries same-process writes**, so only a notification that had to cross a process boundary was lost — and it was lost silently, with the write reporting success.

## The fix, both halves

- **Source**: the three scripts now use the per-table `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS … ON <table>; CREATE TRIGGER …` form that the other ~20 triggers in the file already use. New schemas are correct by construction.
- **V54**: installs the trigger on existing schemas that lack it. It touches **only** schemas genuinely missing it — `CREATE`/`DROP TRIGGER` takes an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock and this loop runs over every partition on the server, so re-applying an identical definition would buy nothing and cost a lock per partition. It reports **how many were missing**, not merely that it finished.

`mesh_node_copy_to_history` gets **no data repair** — measured 33/33 already present, because V44 covered every existing schema. Its source-side guard in `GetMeshSchemaScript` is fixed alongside so a *new* schema cannot regress.

## 🚨 The third site was found by the test, not by eye

The test rejects the **shape** — any trigger created under a guard that checks only a name without constraining the table — rather than this one trigger. On its first run it immediately flagged a live instance I had not fixed: `mesh_node_copy_to_history` in `GetMeshSchemaScript`, still on the global guard. A targeted fix would have shipped that regression forward into every newly created schema.

It also carries a **negative control** (the real guard must still be flagged) and its complement (a properly table-scoped probe must still be *allowed*), so it forbids the defect rather than the catalog and cannot quietly become vacuous. `WithoutComments` exists because the scripts document this anti-pattern in their own comments — the first run flagged that prose, which is itself evidence the scanner reads what it claims to.

## Verification

- `dotnet build -c Release -warnaserror` clean: `MeshWeaver.Hosting.PostgreSql`, `Memex.Database.Migration`, `MeshWeaver.Documentation`.
- `Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 9`.
- `DbVersion.Latest` 53 → 54, registered in `MigrationRegistry`.

author: colinshepard
body:
On Windows, asyncio defaults to the proactor event loop, which implements no add_reader() - the call pyzmq's asyncio sockets are built on. Every long-lived process here polls ZeroMQ from asyncio: the engine's aggregator, and the command and telemetry servers inside every hardware driver. Each one raised "Proactor event loop does not implement add_reader family of methods required for zmq" on its first poll and then once per poll after that, so the engine came up, logged that it was recording, and recorded nothing.

protocol/asyncio_compat.run() starts the coroutine on a selector loop there and defers to asyncio.run() everywhere else. It lives in protocol/ because it is about being able to speak the shared transport at all, and every process on that transport already imports protocol/.

The loop has to be chosen as it is created, so this replaces asyncio.run() at each entry point rather than being set up inside the process wiring they share.

What the proactor loop offers over the selector loop is asyncio subprocesses, which nothing here uses - a testbed starts driver processes with subprocess.Popen, not from an event loop.

The win32 branch is covered by forcing it, since the suite runs on machines where sys.platform is not win32.

author: rockorama
body:
## Summary

A full run at `-n 12` produced failures that all passed in isolation — 7 on the pre-merge tree where the defect was first found, and **2 at this PR's merge base** (`df12e29`), both in `test_endaoment_funds.py`. That the count moves with test population and partition is itself the signature of the defect. **The number this PR should be judged on is 2 → 0**; see [the measurement comment](https://github.com/Ripe-Foundation/ripe-protocol/pull/180#issuecomment-5331331612). The cause was Titanoboa's diagnostic dictionaries (`sstore_trace`, `sha3_trace`), which are **not** covered by its EVM anchor, so stale entries from earlier tests crashed Boa's revert renderer. Three test files had each worked around this locally; one carried a comment saying the correct fix belonged in `tests/conftest.py`. This PR puts it there and removes the three copies.

With that fixed, it also hoists the deployments in the three most setup-heavy files from function to module scope.

**No production contract is changed by this PR.**

## Claims corrected after review

Thanks @mickhagen — three things in the original description were overstated and are fixed here:

- **"No test logic changed" was wrong.** The workflow-health suite was rewritten, `.tool-versions` added, and the deleverage `sstore_trace` workaround removed. Those are test-logic changes.
- **"Order-independent" was too strong.** `--dist loadfile` keeps every file on one worker in file order, so `-n 8` vs `-n 12` varies only *which files share a worker* — it never reorders within a file. What is demonstrated is robustness across two file→worker partitions. `loadfile` remains load-bearing and is now asserted by a test.
- **The suite-wide numbers were not an isolated A/B.** `760b734` vs `48eef81` spans rh's own contract and test growth. Those numbers are withdrawn and replaced by a clean re-measurement, [posted as a comment](https://github.com/Ripe-Foundation/ripe-protocol/pull/180#issuecomment-5331331612). Note `2985e73` — the base I originally named for it — is the **base-branch tip**, not an ancestor of this head; the **merge base** is `df12e29`, across which there are zero contract changes.
- **"7 order-dependent failures → 0" was not this PR's number.** The 7 was measured at `760b734`, before the rh merge. At the real base it is **2 → 0** (`test_transfer_blacklist_token_when_endaoment_blacklisted` and `..._when_vault_blacklisted`, both in `test_endaoment_funds.py`, both among the original 7).

## What changed

**Isolation** — `4eaf345`
Global autouse fixture in `tests/conftest.py` clearing the two diagnostic traces; three local workarounds removed.

**Fixture scope** — `1cf17c6`, `b9517ea`, `841c79f`, `426313e`, `43c242c`
The teller fixture could not be widened wholesale: it rewrites seven core RipeHq registry entries to mock sinks, and Boa holds a fixture anchor open until finalization, so tests in that module which never request it would have run against a mocked credit engine. Only the deployments moved; every registry rewrite, config and permission grant stays function-scoped. `43c242c` also drops `mock_auction_house`, which had no consumers and never belonged in the speedup story.

**CI** — `9ce09db`, `9ffda2c`, `d2c1cc3`
`9ce09db` originally skipped validation jobs on `push`. That was wrong — the integration branches are unprotected, and `2985e73` (a direct push to `rh` touching `AuctionHouse.vy`) would have been validated by a single test. `d2c1cc3` restores full validation on `push` — **the double-run cost returns**. `9fa61e5` then deletes `warm-boa-cache` entirely: every lean shard's restore-keys already falls back to the same `boa-<os>-py312-lean-<hash>-` prefix that job wrote to, and since `ripe_hq` is an autouse session fixture, any shard's own save is a content superset of it (HQ baseline plus that shard's extras). GitHub returns the newest prefix match, so the warm entry could never beat a real shard cache — it could only be ignored, or picked *instead of* a richer one — while still costing a runner job per push and an immutable entry against the 10 GB LRU budget. Re-gating `push` is only safe once `master` is on `pull_request`/`merge_group` **and** all three branches reject direct pushes; both preconditions are recorded inline.

`test_python_workflow_health.py` (505 lines) hardcoded the shard map in 20+ assertions. Replaced with `tests/test_lean_shard_coverage.py` (24 tests), which **derives** everything from the workflow: file→shard assignment, matrix-vs-`case` scheduling, event routing at both job *and step* level, `rh-pr-gate` wiring, credential `unset` parsing, exact `-m` marker expressions for snapshot-gas and deployment-controls, `loadfile`, action SHA pins, cache-key shape and restore-key **order**, `fetch-depth`, per-job timeouts, concurrency group and `cancel-in-progress`, `permissions`, dispatch lane options, `fail-fast`, unknown-shard `exit 2`, and branch lists.

**Tooling** — `54c529f`
A fresh clone resolved whatever Python asdf defaulted to, so `pytest` rejected `-n --dist loadfile`. `.python-version` (pyenv) and `.tool-versions` (asdf) are read by different tools and do not contend.

## What this does NOT fix

**The local single-test loop is unchanged by this PR**, and that was verified same-node on both sides rather than assumed: `df12e29` → `10f1210` measures 63.7s → 63.0s on a test that pays only the `ripe_hq` bootstrap, and 70.0s → 70.3s on one that also builds the hoisted teller fixture. The landed hoists contribute ~0s here by construction — a module-scoped fixture is built once per module either way when you run a single test, so the −98.2% is amortisation across 98 tests: real for CI and full-file runs, invisible in the dev loop.

Where a focused run actually goes (paired back-to-back runs, one node, same box):

| phase | cost | share |
|---|---|---|
| collection | 1.0s | 2% |
| `ripe_hq` bootstrap (setup) | 35.5s | 61% |
| **the test itself** | **0.01s** | **0.02%** |
| interpreter finalization, after the last test has passed | 22.2s | 38% |

The finalization cost is measured, not inferred: injecting a `pytest_sessionfinish` hook that calls `os._exit(0)` takes the same node from **58.3s/58.5s to 36.4s/35.9s** across two alternating pairs — the interpreter spends ~22s tearing down the py-evm/boa object graph after the result is already known. Absolute seconds drift with machine load (we have measured this phase at 21–27s across sessions); the stable figure is the share, ~38%.

So the two remaining levers are worth ~58s of a ~58s run, and neither is reachable by fixture scoping. 126 files depend on that autouse fixture, so it is a refactor, not a scope change. The bootstrap is also growing — 494.6s → 551.9s across 12 workers in the rh merge alone.

## Test plan

- `-n 12` and `-n 8`, both `--dist loadfile`: **0 failures** on the merge tree, across two file→worker partitions rather than one layout repeated — but see the narrowed claim above. Measured against this PR's merge base `df12e29`, the isolated result is **2 failures → 0**; fixture setup in the three affected files is **332.1s → 40.9s** on identical node sets.
- `test_green_ref_pool.py` eval-writing tests verified in file order, reverse order, individually, and as a full file.
- Scheduling guard verified against the reviewer's mutation: moving `tests/core/endaoment` into an unscheduled `core-d` arm leaves exactly-once green and fails the new guard.
- Shard-coverage guard absorbed rh's 8 new test files with no edits.

Every guard is verified by an independent negative mutation rather than a compound edit: each of the reviewer's six suggested mutations fails its own dedicated test when applied alone, and 13 regressions are covered in total. One gap surfaced that way — the `fetch-depth` guard covered only the `test` job, so shortening `deployment-controls`' checkout passed everything; `6a275ae` derives both depths from the workflow instead. Full history is load-bearing: `tests/config/test_defaults_robinhood.py` pi

author: tylerwhitlock50
body:
## What changed

**Freshness stamp now shows two dates.** `v_data_freshness` gains an `orders_through` column (newest `order_date`), and the portal stamp renders **"Invoiced through Aug 13 · Orders through Aug 17 · Loaded today"** instead of the ambiguous "Data through Aug 13". The orders date is elided when it matches the invoiced date, so on a caught-up night the stamp stays short.

**ETL logs its own wall clock.** `push_to_supabase.py` prints a start timestamp, a finish timestamp with total elapsed (`4m 53s` style, "(with failures)" suffix on a dirty run), and per-statement timing on the `post_load_sql` steps — the rollup/scoring calls previously ran untimed, so most of a run's wall clock was invisible.

## Why

Today's stamp read "Data through Aug 13 · Loaded today" on an Aug 17 load, which looks like a four-day-stale warehouse. Tracing it showed the pipeline was current — ERP **billing** stopped posting Aug 13 while shipments continued through Aug 17. One date cannot distinguish an ETL problem from a billing lag; two can.

## Notes for review

- `data_through` deliberately keeps its meaning (newest non-memo invoice date): MCP `whoami`, the AI brief prompt, and goal-pace math all document it as the revenue horizon. Only the portal label changed.
- The view is an owner-rights exception (024 says not to widen its column list without re-justifying); the migration re-justifies — output is still nothing but warehouse-wide timestamps.
- The view change is already applied to the live database (create-or-replace, replay-safe for `deploy_migrations.py`).
- Frontend typecheck passes; rendered stamp not eyeballed (login wall) — worth a glance when signed in.

author: mckelveygreg
body:
Follows #85. Read off EliteControl 1.2 beside the pedal, 2026-08-17.

## Gate Release — confirmed, fixed

Noon reads **261.4 ms**. That is `10 + 990·(64/127)² = 261.41` — the square prediction to the decimal,
against the log law's 101.8. Same endpoints and same law as the compressor's Release, so it moves to
`sqMap` alongside it.

That's two of the three time constants now confirmed square, which makes it look like the pedal has
one shared law for time parameters.

## Compressor Attack — left DISPUTED on purpose

The same reading put **Attack's noon at 261.4 ms as well**. That isn't just a different taper: **it is
outside the 1–100 ms range** `units.ts` records for Attack. So one of the two is wrong about the
*endpoints*, and a midpoint reading cannot say which.

261.4 ms is also exactly a square taper over 10–1000 ms — i.e. the same law and range as both Release
controls. "All three share one law" is the obvious reading, and it is probably right. It is also
exactly the kind of inference that produced the bug #85 fixed, so changing a **range** on the strength
of a single midpoint would be repeating the two-point mistake in the other direction.

`compAttackMs` therefore keeps its current law with the dispute documented in place, and a test pins
only the endpoints we still believe — so nobody can quietly change the range without a reading.

**To settle it:** Attack's **min and max** off EliteControl. If they read 10 ms and 1000 ms, it's the
shared square law and it's a one-line change.

`npm run check` green — lint, format, both typechecks, 412 tests, Fallow.

Substantive changes:

- Adds the platform thesis as the comparison frame: separated tools that compose into a full text-processing platform with OOTB RAG, native gRPC, and multiple agentic protocols.
- Corrects the accounting with an honest ledger table: most Cube capabilities have a shipped counterpart here (model governance, serving surfaces, masking, metadata, MCP), several stronger; the genuine gaps are the aggregate compiler, time-grain queries, and pre-aggregations.
- Reframes the agentic column: the workflow workbench (check, record, replay, promote with proto-validated requests and replies) plus MCP/ACP is the counter to Analytics Chat, certified queries, and evals, not out-of-scope chrome.

author: mousebrains
body:
Phase 1 of [docs/design/control_engine.md](docs/design/control_engine.md): the substrate a control engine sits on. **No engine yet** — this is the layer an engine will consume, landed alone because it is testable alone.

## Multi-glider from the first commit

Deliberate, and the reason to do this layer first. A formation controller exists to make decisions *across* gliders, and the merge is where that is either easy or impossible; retrofitting it later would touch everything downstream.

So `Event.glider` is **required, not optional**. A single-glider engine can ignore it, but making it optional would mean every formation engine opens with a `None` check that can only ever be dead code.

One queue, one thread, all gliders — which is what lets an engine hold fleet state in ordinary attributes with no locking.

## Split so the interesting half needs no I/O

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `EventMerge` | Pure. Knows nothing about SFMC or sessions. All ordering and drop accounting. |
| `FleetStream` | Wires N `GliderSession` objects in. The only part touching the network. |

The phasing plan asked for *"two fake sessions, assert tagging, ordering within a pair, and drop accounting"* — that is what the tests do. 35 new tests, 98% coverage on the module.

## Decisions worth reviewing

**Bounds are per (glider, source), not global.** One glider surfacing and dumping a mission's worth of dialog must not evict the connection events of the gliders still in the water. The default of 2048 is set against a measurement rather than a guess: a real surfacing on osusim delivered **437 lines inside ten milliseconds**, so a smaller bound would drop during normal operation rather than only when an engine is genuinely too slow.

**Drops are counted and reported, never silent.** This is the direct lesson from a live run that sat through a surfacing and looked byte-identical to one still waiting. Drop-oldest keeps the newest data; one notice per burst carries the whole count; and because a pair that never drains would otherwise never report, a further queue's worth of loss forces a notice mid-burst.

**`received_at` is named for the clock it uses** — the host's. Glider time appears inside dialog text and the two differ by 48 minutes on osusim, so an unqualified `timestamp` would have been a bug generator.

**Gliders join and leave at runtime**, because a formation changes.

## Not in this phase

`BaseControlEngine`, `on_event`, `request`, replay, writes. Those are phases 2 and 3.

author: nmorabowen
body:
Implements **ADR 0098 Amendment 1** (the pane host) plus S3's other two
halves: per-view scope and the four INV-MESH-4 style buttons. Two
commits — the implementation, and a wording-only ADR follow-up that
changes no decision.

## What lands

**The host** (`viewers/session/_host.py`). Root `QSplitter(Horizontal)`
of columns, each a `QSplitter(Vertical)` of rows, depth exactly two,
one `QtInteractor` per mesh pane — the geometry
`test_pane_host_probe.py` proved on both oracles. `T(N)` is a pure
function of the pane count (`C = ceil(sqrt N)`, row-major fill in
`session.panes` order). The ratio law resets **only** the splitter
whose child list changed; everything else keeps its dragged sizes.

Panes are **moved, never rebuilt**. A host that tore down and rebuilt
would satisfy the cell arithmetic while silently destroying every
camera — backend state, not session state, so nothing downstream would
catch it. Criterion 4 asserts object identity for exactly that reason,
and criterion 18's reparent test is the GL half of the same claim.

**The A1.1 seam.** On the session path the shell builds **no** central
interactor: `central_interactor=False` + `set_central_widget` /
`set_plotter_provider` on `ViewerWindow` / `ResultsWindow`, additive
and opt-in. Every GL context in the window belongs to a pane, which is
what makes sixteen of the twenty-four criteria honest in the default
offscreen lane with injected backends instead of paying the xvfb lane
for the whole suite. Toolbar camera / fit / screenshot act on the
active pane. `results_viewer.py` and `_dispatch.py` are **not in the
diff** (criterion 24 + the plan's standing risk).

**Style buttons realize** — they are not just records. `mesh` is
`show_edges` of whichever layer IS the one surface (the substrate, or
the contour when it occludes — INV-MESH-2 + INV-MESH-4); `outlines` is
a feature-edge layer of the same cell set, so hiding a cell takes its
outline with it (INV-MESH-3); `nodes` / `gauss` are glyph clouds, and
the Gauss button stands down when the `gauss` slot is occupied — "they
must not draw two clouds". Three new icon-factory glyphs + four ADR
0087 Appendix A rows. View clips realize too (0083 machinery,
view-owned).

**Per-view scope** joins the outline as its second §9 job: checkboxes
on one composition axis, switching axis rather than intersecting.
`materials` renders present-but-disabled — no element→material index is
published yet, and offering it enabled would promise a picture the
realize layer refuses. The Add gate (A1.4) disables "New mesh view" /
"New plot" with the required width in the tooltip; it constrains
creation only, so a script or an S5 restore is tiled anyway.

**The three named S2 defects are fixed, not managed.** Inspector pages
are evicted and disposed with their pane (caution 9 — they only ever
grew, and each holds a live session subscription). A reconciler *bound*
to a pane id whose view is gone paints **nothing** (caution 10 — the
first-mesh-view fallback would repaint view 1 into a dying backend).
First-fit camera moved onto the pane (caution 11).

**Criterion 12 is a gate, not a hope.** Each reconciler keeps a
pane-level signature over `(instant, scope, pose, style, overlay,
clips, slots, legends)` — all frozen records, so `==` is exact and a
hash collision cannot paint a stale picture. One slot fill in a
four-pane session costs exactly one realize and one `render()`; a theme
change forces all four past the guard.

## Open sub-questions

Took the recommended defaults for 1 (seam spelling), 2 (the signature —
built and gated), 4 (no reorder / no explicit split in S3) and 5
(`font_scale` stays the user's knob). **Sub-question 3 — shared
tessellation via `ShallowCopy` + per-pane ghost array — is NOT
implemented**: each pane realizes from its own `build_fem_scene`, which
is what S1 already did per realize. It is a measurement question at
18.6 M cells, not a correctness one, and nothing in the criteria pins
it. Flagging it rather than claiming it.

## Two things a reviewer should look at

**Caution 2's "legends are safe" is wrong, and the first fix
no-opped.** `ScalarBarSpec` carries geometry and font *sizes* — no
colour — so a bar's title and labels take `plotter.theme.font.color`,
which `viewer_window.py` sets to white on the global theme. On `paper`
that was white text on a light pane. The fix is an explicit per-pane
theme (caution 2's own "or construct panes with an explicit theme"),
and it initially did nothing because `pv.global_theme.copy()` does not
exist on the shipped pyvista and the `except` swallowed the
`AttributeError`. Now `deepcopy`, verified in the review-bar shots.
The same latent defect exists in the old window on light themes;
fixing that is a 0090 question, not S3's.

**S2 test assertions that S3's laws genuinely change.** The boot
picture is now `{substrate, outlines}` — two layers, because `mesh` and
`outlines` are two different pictures (INV-MESH-4). The two
`render_results` parity stills now set the style buttons off so they
compare like with like (`render_results` has no feature-edge pass and
`ContourStyle.show_edges` defaults False), and a new
`test_outlines_button_adds_ink` covers the other half so the parity
pins do not quietly become vacuous. These are behaviour changes, not
mechanical edits — worth reading rather than accepting.

**G-QSS-SYNC now scans `viewers/session/**`.** The pane host's styled
widgets live there; without it every new QSS block reads as dangling.
That widens the guard's reach — no budget moved (criterion 16).

## Testing

| Lane | Result |
|---|---|
| Offscreen `tests/viewers` (default lane) | 2443 passed, 5 skipped |
| Full repo, default lane | 13994 passed, 115 skipped, 1 xfailed |
| `-m qt`, per file, **Windows GL** | probe 7 · new host-window 10 · session-window 2 · widgets 1 |

New: `tests/viewers/test_pane_host.py` (the sixteen `[off]` criteria)
and `tests/viewers/test_pane_host_window_qt.py` (criteria 18–20 on real
GL, beside the probe). `test_pane_host_probe.py` stays green unchanged
(criterion 17).

**Criterion 22 — mutation tests, in the file, each naming what it
breaks:** column-major fill → criterion 3; dropped
`childrenCollapsible` → criterion 5; panes rebuilt instead of moved →
criterion 4 (the cell arithmetic still passes, only the identity assert
catches it); two panes on one backend → criterion 11.

**Criterion 21 — screenshot review bar.** 24 captures (1 / 2 / 4-pane +
one at the 240 px width floor, in `catppuccin_mocha`,
`neutral_studio`, `paper`, both densities), generated by
`scratchpad_shots/take_pane_host_shots.py`. Headers are legible and
unclipped at the floor; caution 6 is visible as predicted — the legend
eats about half a 240 px pane.

## What is NOT verified here

**Windows/GPU green proves nothing for Mesa.** Criteria 17–21 need the
`qt-window-tests` xvfb lane in CI before this slice is really verified;
the local qt runs above are Windows desktop GL. The composited review
shots also show intermittent blocky artefacts *inside* pane interiors —
that is Windows front-buffer `screenshot()` capture, not render: the
same panes came out clean under `QScreen.grabWindow`.

## What changed
- use the stable Whop App API key for product reads and writes after a business installs SCL Marketplace
- keep per-user OAuth tokens only as a backwards-compatible fallback
- add safe retrieve helpers for Whop companies and products
- add a guarded, reversible production E2E workflow limited to a product explicitly named as an SCL sync test

## Why
Whop App API keys are the server credential intended for companies that installed an app. Requiring a user OAuth token made the sync expire and prevented an already-authorized app install from functioning as the durable integration.

## Validation
- 934 repository tests
- 3 production release tests
- TypeScript clean
- ESLint: 0 errors (3 unrelated existing warnings)
- Next.js 16.2.9 production build (53 routes)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how production Whop API credentials are chosen for all storefront sync and push paths; the optional live workflow mutates production Whop products and DB rows but is tightly scoped to test products and restores state in a finally block.
> 
> **Overview**
> Whop storefront **import and push** now authenticate with the **installed-app server key** (`WHOP_APP_API_KEY`) when present, instead of requiring a capper OAuth access token. Per-connection OAuth tokens remain a **fallback** for older links; OAuth refresh runs only when the app key is absent.

> `syncWhopStorefront` and `pushPackageToWhop` resolve credentials via new **`whopStorefrontApiKey`**, and connection errors no longer insist on a user token when a Whop business ID is already linked. **`retrieveWhopCompany`** and **`retrieveWhopProduct`** support single-resource reads for tooling.

> A **manual Production GitHub workflow** runs **`scripts/verify-live-whop-sync.ts`**: a guarded, reversible live test (dedicated “SCL Sync Test” product only) that exercises Whop→SCL sync, hide→deactivate, SCL→Whop push, then restores Whop and DB state.

author: merlinlabs-automation[bot]
body:
## What

Three things, found and fixed together while closing out this session's live-probe sweep:

**1. `one billing` removed entirely** — `one billing current-account`, `one billing usage-export`, `one doctor billing`, and the billing probe inside `one doctor discover`.

Live evidence: `GET /v4/open-api-spec` (172 paths, probed twice this session) contains zero billing, usage, credit, license, or quota routes. Unlike the `/plans/v1`/`/scheduling/v1` case this PR's base fixed, there's no wrong path to repoint here — billing simply has no public API. The spec is not entitlement-filtered (this tenant lacks the Plans entitlement, yet 22 `/v4/plan*` paths still appear in its own spec), so the absence is real, not tier gating the old `--help` text guessed at ("requires an enterprise-tier workspace"). Same treatment as the 0.13.0 removal of `one auto-insights`/`one desktop-exec`: removed rather than shipped as commands that can only fail. The research stays on record in `docs/one-endpoint-matrix.md` and `docs/one-api-surface-audit.md`.

**2. An 18th endpoint with the identical defect** — found live-verifying the removal above. `telemetry permissions workflows`/`summary` dispatched a dead `/iam/v1/workspaces/{id}/people` path since inception. It was invisible to the base PR's 17-endpoint audit because it's deliberately carved out of the `one`-surface inventory (`NON_ONE_SURFACE_ENDPOINTS` — it's a `telemetry` command, not a `one` command), and every path-correctness gate in this repo is built from that inventory. Repointed to the real `/v4/workspaces/{id}/people`; the carve-out itself stays, since the command is still legitimately non-`one`-surface. Live-verified: `workflows` went from a hard `error_code: not_found` to real data (18 members); `summary`'s `workspace_member_count` went from a silently-swallowed `null` to `18`.

**3. Corrected `outside_spec_namespace`/`stale[]` doc-comment claims in `coverage.rs`**, which asserted rows there were "real, working commands" — false for 12 of 25 rows before this PR. This framing was reviewed adversarially (codex, `gpt-5.6-luna`, high effort) against a "the bucket becomes homogeneous after removal, so a correction is all that's needed" argument. The review correctly refuted relying on homogeneity as durable — the next dead sibling-service endpoint would land in the same bucket — so the fix here instead narrows the doc comments to state plainly that liveness is a separate, unverified axis, and points at `docs/one-endpoint-matrix.md`'s `Live status` column as where that evidence actually lives.

Also closes the corresponding open items in `docs/one-api-surface-audit.md` and `docs/roadmap/api-surface-and-observability.md` — striking two roadmap bullets that restated the same tier-gating misdiagnosis the base PR disproved, and two that were already delivered (workflow DELETE live-verification, `workflows list --all` completeness warning).

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | clean |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo nextest run --workspace --locked` (isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `AYX_CONFIG_HOME`) | 849/849, 22 skipped |
| `cargo nextest run -p ayx-rs --locked command_surface` / `catalog`, default + `--features ui` | all pass (CI's "Command surface source-of-truth" job, run locally) |
| `cargo run -q -p xtask -- refresh-command-surface --check` | fresh |
| `grep -rniI billing` full-tree sweep | only historical/reference mentions and immutable shipped release notes remain |
| Live: `ayx one billing` / `ayx one doctor billing` | `error: unexpected argument 'billing' found` — fully removed |
| Live: `telemetry permissions workflows --workspace-id 91946` | real data (18 members), was `error_code: not_found` |

## Summary

Resolves the merge conflict that made #6300 (`mergeable_state: dirty`) unmergeable against `main`, plus a few more review-comment fixes from the same round.

### Merge conflict

`main` merged #6652 ("Replace hand-rolled poller in agent-studio-persona with pollWhile"), refactoring `AgentStudioPersonaComponent.startPolling()`'s polling mechanism (interval + switchMap + a separate immediate fetch → the shared `pollWhile` helper) — unaware of this PR's in-flight elapsed-time-preservation work (resume across audit navigation, freeze at terminal, restart detection), so it also reset `startPolling` to unconditionally zero `elapsedSec` and inline a fresh ticker.

**Resolution:** merged `main`'s `pollWhile`-based poll mechanism (drops the hand-rolled `interval`/`switchMap` poller and the redundant separate immediate-fetch subscribe — `pollWhile`'s `immediate: true` default already covers that) while keeping this PR's elapsed-time resume/freeze logic intact: the conditional `startElapsedTicker()` call, `endedAtMs`-seeded `elapsedSec`, and all of `freezeElapsedAtTerminal`/`reseedElapsedAfterRestart` are unchanged.

**Test fallout:** `pollWhile`'s immediate poll fires via a (fake) `timer(0)` rather than synchronously — `main`'s own spec updates already account for this (`vi.advanceTimersByTime(0)` after `launch()`), but four PR-6300-only tests predate that convention and needed the same flush added: `shows View full audit after a run exists…`, `resumes an in-progress run after the component is recreated`, `caps elapsed time at the run's updated_at when it finished while unmounted`, and `restores a completed run after the component is recreated`.

### Review comments

- **Brittle route-order assertion:** `app.routes.spec.ts` asserted an exact-order array equality on the Studio children paths; replaced with `expect.arrayContaining([...])` + a length check, since the `find()`-based assertions below already verify each child's own properties.
- **Direct `setPersonaLiveRunId(null)` test:** the clear-on-null behavior was only verified indirectly (via `setTeamId`'s team-change test). Added a focused test calling it directly.

author: lexfrei
body:
New plugin: taguchi. When a debugging plan has 3+ candidate factors and every run is expensive (CI round-trip, flaky repro, hardware cycle), an orthogonal array covers every pair of factor levels in a few runs: 12 instead of 2048 for 11 binary factors. The skill triggers at that point, picks the smallest array that fits (L4/L8/L9/L12/L18), renders a run sheet, ranks suspects by column-wise main effects, and requires accusation and acquittal confirmation runs before any root-cause claim. If effects come out confounded, it falls back to a full factorial on the top two suspects.

All five embedded arrays are verified pairwise-balanced with a script before embedding. The plugin README asks the same of any array added later.

author: stephane-segning
body:
## 1. Summary

This PR changes:

- Adds `## 0.8.3` and `## 0.8.2` sections to `dart-packages/cratestack_cbor/CHANGELOG.md`.
- Removes the stale "Not yet published to pub.dev" line from the `## 0.8.0` section.

It solves:

- pub.dev reporting **0/5 points: Provide a valid CHANGELOG.md** for `cratestack_cbor` (#563).

---

## 2. Intent

The intent of this PR is:

> To stop losing 5 pub.dev points because the package's changelog has no entry for the version being published.

The file had a single `## 0.8.0` section while 0.8.0, 0.8.2 and 0.8.3 are all published, and still claimed the package was unpublished — untrue for three releases.

Entries are derived from the actual diffs between published versions, not written from memory:

```
git diff 7126006 v0.8.2 -- dart-packages/cratestack_cbor/
  -> README.md and pubspec.yaml only; no code changes

git diff v0.8.2 v0.8.3 -- dart-packages/cratestack_cbor/
  -> one line (the version bump)
```

So 0.8.2 is described as metadata-only and 0.8.3 as no functional change. Anything more impressive would have been invention.

---

## 3. Scope

### In Scope

- The package's own `CHANGELOG.md` content.

### Out of Scope

- **Wiring the package changelog into the seed/check tooling.** See below — a real gap, but a process decision rather than a bug fix.
- The root `CHANGELOG.md`, whose `changelog (no unedited seeds)` check is separately failing on main.

---

## 4. Verification

I verified this change by:

- [ ] Running automated tests
- [x] Running manual tests
- [ ] Checking logs
- [ ] Checking metrics
- [ ] Testing error cases
- [ ] Testing permissions/security behavior
- [ ] Testing rollback or failure behavior, if relevant

```text
headings after the change:  ## 0.8.3, ## 0.8.2, ## 0.8.0
"Not yet published" occurrences: 0
published versions on pub.dev:   0.8.0 0.8.2 0.8.3
```

Every published version now has a section, and the content matches the recorded diffs above.

**This does not fix the score for the already-published 0.8.3.** The CHANGELOG is baked into each published archive, so the effect lands on the next publish. Worth being explicit about, because "fixed the changelog" naturally reads as "fixed the score".

---

## 5. Screenshots / Evidence

Diff output quoted above.

---

## 6. Risk Assessment

Risk level:

* [x] Low
* [ ] Medium
* [ ] High

Potential risks:

* **It will go stale again on the next release** — see below. This PR fixes today's content, not the mechanism.

Mitigation:

* The mechanism gap is documented here and on #563 rather than left to be rediscovered from a score drop.

### Why this will recur, and what would stop it

Neither `.ci/changelog-seed.sh` nor `.ci/changelog-check.sh` knows this file exists. Both default to:

```bash
CHANGELOG_FILE="${CHANGELOG_FILE:-CHANGELOG.md}"
```

— the **root** changelog — and neither mentions `dart-packages`. So each release seeds a section in the workspace CHANGELOG and CI verifies a human edited it, while the package's own changelog silently falls behind and costs 5 points again.

Both scripts already accept `CHANGELOG_FILE` as an environment variable, so wiring the package changelog into the seed and check is a small change to `prepare-release.yml`, not new tooling. Left out deliberately: it adds a second section for a human to edit on every bump, which is a process decision for whoever cuts releases.

---

## 7. AI Usage Declaration

AI was used for:

* [x] Understanding existing code
* [ ] Generating code
* [ ] Generating tests
* [x] Drafting documentation
* [x] Reviewing the diff
* [ ] Not used

Written by Claude Opus 5 after the maintainer spotted the 0/5 score on pub.dev. The changelog entries were derived by diffing the published tags rather than recalled, and the recurrence cause was traced to the seed/check scripts' default `CHANGELOG_FILE`.

Human verification:

* [ ] I understand every meaningful change in this PR
* [ ] I checked generated code manually
* [ ] I checked generated tests manually
* [ ] I removed unsupported AI assumptions
* [ ] I accept responsibility for this PR

---

## 8. Reviewer Focus

Please focus your review on:

* [ ] Correctness
* [ ] Architecture
* [ ] Security
* [ ] Performance
* [ ] Tests
* [x] Maintainability
* [x] Product intent

Specifically: whether the 0.8.2 and 0.8.3 entries say enough for a consumer. They are deliberately modest because the diffs are modest, but you know the audience better than the diff does.

author: patrickserrano
body:
`dependabotUpdates()` emitted a `swift` entry for every `ios` component, at that
component's own directory, on the reasoning that a project with no SPM
dependencies has nothing for Dependabot to find and the entry is therefore
harmless. Both halves were wrong, and both were failing in production:

- Dependabot does not no-op, it **aborts the whole job** — "Error during file
  fetching; aborting: Repo must contain a Package.swift configuration file or an
  .xcodeproj/.xcworkspace directory with a Package.resolved file" — taking the
  repo's github-actions updates down with it. Queueify and rail, twice each.
- The manifest is not always at the component root: windsock has one at
  `WindsockKit/Package.resolved` while its entry pointed at `/`.

An `ios` component is detected by an `.xcodeproj`, which is not a dependency
manifest. Every other ecosystem here is safe to derive from the manifest alone (a
`web` component was detected BY its package.json), so only `swift` changes.

## Approach

The project root, recorded on `config.Config` by `config.Load` rather than
threaded through `tokens.Values`. `Values(cfg, prefix)` has ~15 call sites across
`internal/{assets,sync,audit}` and the tests, and `assets.MissingTokens`/`Plan`
would have needed a root argument of their own to pass one along. `Load` is
already handed `<project>/.lacquer.toml`, so the root is a property of the
manifest that was read: the two cannot disagree, no call site changes, and
`internal/fleet` — which loads many projects in one process — gets the right root
for each for free.

`detect.IndexSwiftManifests` then asks **git**, not the filesystem, what the
repository contains. That distinction is the fix: rail has a `Package.resolved`
on disk at exactly the path Steps has one, and the difference between the working
repo and the aborting one is a `*.resolved` line in `.gitignore` (Queueify's is
`*.xcworkspace`). A filesystem walk would have confirmed both broken entries as
correct. It also excludes `DerivedData/` and `.build/` for free — a checkout of
Steps carries nine `Package.resolved` files belonging to RevenueCat's test
fixtures.

The rules are read off this fleet's actual runs, not off documentation:

| repo | committed manifest | swift PRs today | rule it establishes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Steps | `Steps.xcodeproj/…/Package.resolved` | yes | a bundled resolved at the entry works |
| kit | `Kit/Kit.xcodeproj/…/Package.resolved`, entry `/` | yes | bundles are found **recursively** below the entry |
| windsock | `WindsockKit/Package.{swift,resolved}`, entry `/` | none, ever | a bare package is **not** found from above |
| rail, Queueify | nothing committed | none | with nothing to fetch, the job aborts |

A component with nothing readable now gets **no** entry, and an unknown root or a
non-git directory yields none either. A missing entry stops watching dependencies
quietly; a wrong one fails a job every day and silences the other ecosystems in
the same file. Prefer nothing.

## Result, end to end

`lacquer sync` run against local clones of all five repos:

| repo | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Steps | `/` | `/` (unchanged) |
| kit | `/` | `/` (unchanged) |
| windsock | `/` (aborting) | `/WindsockKit` |
| rail | `/` (aborting) | no swift entry |
| Queueify | `/ios` (aborting) | no swift entry |

`github-actions` and `npm` are untouched.

## Tests

`internal/shipped/dependabot_test.go` builds throwaway **git repositories** —
tracked files committed, untracked ones only written — because what makes a
manifest real here is that the repository contains it. Every case above has one,
plus a sibling-directory case (`iosSupport` is not inside `ios`) and one that
renders from a manifest actually loaded off disk.

Each was verified by mutation — broken, watched fail, restored:

| mutation | caught by |
| --- | --- |
| always emit at the component dir (the old behaviour) | the 3 no-entry/nested cases + the no-root case |
| count untracked files too | `IgnoresManifestsTheRepoDoesNotContain` |
| drop the nested-package search | `PointsSwiftAtANestedPackage` |
| require the bundle exactly at the component dir | `KeepsTheComponentDirWhenTheBundleIsDeeper` |
| let `Package.swift` alone qualify | `IgnoresManifestsTheRepoDoesNotContain` |
| `Load` stops recording the root | `ResolvesManifestsForALoadedProject` |
| `within()` loses its path separator | `DoesNotAcceptASiblingDirectory` |
| render the root as `/.` | 3 cases |

Two mutations that fail nothing are documented rather than papered over:
outermost-vs-innermost bundle selection is behaviourally inert (only ancestors are
consulted), and the comment now says so.

## Not verified

- That windsock's `/WindsockKit` entry succeeds — only its next Dependabot run can
  show that. It satisfies the fetcher's own stated criteria (`Package.swift` plus
  `Package.resolved`, both committed).
- Whether a `Package.swift` with no committed `Package.resolved` would work. No
  entry in this fleet has been observed to, so rail's `RailCore`/`RailData` get
  nothing rather than two guesses. Worth knowing: rail and Queueify are one
  `.gitignore` line away from being watchable at all — `*.resolved` and
  `*.xcworkspace` respectively keep their resolved files out of the repo.

author: klomkling
body:
coord #0085 reported that 0.16.0 crash-loops a consumer whose `data_protection_keys`
predates Themia running its own migration — 42P07 on CREATE TABLE, production API down,
reverted to 0.15.0. propertiezy has since retracted the mechanism (they could not
reproduce it either), and ezy-assets is running 0.16.0 in production. Neither the
reported state nor the concurrency hypothesis reproduces here.

Both tests come out of that investigation. Neither changes shipping code — 0.16.0
already behaves correctly in both cases; nothing was pinning it.

## `ConsumerOwnedTableUpgradeTests` (48c2e22)

The reported production state, seeded against a real PostgreSQL: the consumer's
`VersionInfo` carrying 202607260001 (the collision that skipped our migration under
0.15), their own `data_protection_keys` with a key row in it, and no Themia ledger.
The migration adopts the table, the row survives, and the version is recorded so the
next boot has nothing pending.

`Applying_twice_is_safe` could not have caught this class either way: there the table
comes from *our* migration, so a guard that merely agrees with what we just did passes.
Here it predates Themia entirely and carries a consumer's shape.

## `PendingCheckInsideLockTests` (347fe20)

coord #0085's remaining hypothesis: if `RunCore` decides which migrations are pending
*before* `MigrationLock.RunExclusive` takes the advisory lock, two instances both read
an empty ledger, serialize, and the second applies DDL the first already committed —
which produces the reported trace and a ledger row that was never written.

`Run_AppliesEachMigrationOnce_WhenInstancesBootSimultaneously` covers the same ground
with six racing instances, but it can only fail when the interleaving lands, so its
green run is not evidence. This one holds the window open: an external holder takes the
lock, the run under test parks on it (having already resolved `IMigrationRunner`, which
is where a stale read would be taken), and the probe table and its ledger row are
created while it waits. A decision made before acquiring the lock is then guaranteed
stale. It is not.

`ProbeMigration` is the subject because it is **unguarded**. All eighteen shipping
migrations check for what they create, which would have masked a stale read behind the
guard and returned a green test that proved nothing.

## Test plan

- `dotnet test tests/Themia.Migrations.ReplayTests --filter ConsumerOwnedTableUpgradeTests` — green
- `dotnet test tests/Themia.Data.Migrations.IntegrationTests --filter PendingCheckInsideLockTests` — green
- Both are new files; no existing test or source file is touched. Full integration suites left to CI.

## Related

- coord #0085 — answered `needs_info`; the one open question is the resolved version of
  `Themia.AspNetCore.DataProtection` (the core package) in the build that crashed.
- coord #0088 — a separate defect found while failing to reproduce this one: migrations
  resolve to `public` while the Dapper stores follow `search_path`.

author: dcajal
body:
## Summary

- apply the OSP projection associatively without materializing the square projection matrix
- document the mathematical rationale next to the optimized multiplication
- bump Biosigpy to 0.3.2 and add the release notes to the authoritative changelog

## Why

`hrv.osp` previously formed an `(N - D + 1) × (N - D + 1)` projection matrix for every HRV window. Applying `(V G+ V.T) m` as `V (G+ (V.T m))` preserves the defined decomposition while avoiding that quadratic intermediate.

## Impact

The scientific model, adaptive delay, Gram pseudoinverse threshold, outputs, and public API remain unchanged. The projection step now uses linear memory in the signal length for fixed subspace order and is substantially faster for five-minute windows sampled at 4 Hz.

## Validation

- 220 pytest tests against Biosiglib commit `9f2370451c6b77296c2714f719132edb7fa034c0`
- strict MkDocs build
- wheel and source distribution build
- `twine check` on both distributions
- clean wheel and source-distribution installs with `pip check` and version/import smoke tests
